Sū. 3-4-92 as read]; *guṇa* and *av*-substitution; no *guṇa* of the root vowel since the *vikaraṇa* acts as *ṅit*; *nighāta* accent); *arātīyataḥ* (*na vidyate rātir dānam asmin* — *arātiḥ*, 'enemy'; *arātim ivācarati*, *upamānād ācāre* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-97 as read]; *aṭ*; *sip* by *sib bahulaṃ leṭi* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-34 as read]; *guṇa*; *raparatva*; *nighāta*); *durgāṇi* (*duḥkhena gamyate eṣu*, root *gam*; *ḍa* by a vārttika under Pā. ## Sūkta 100

**ನೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು** — *nūraneya sūktavu*, "the hundredth Sūkta" *(Kannada heading)*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 100 (Sanskrit in Kannada script; doubtful places [?]):**

> स यो वृषेत्येकोनविंशत्यृचं सप्तमं सूक्तम् । अत्रानुक्रम्यते । स यो वृषैकोना वार्षागिरा ऋज्राश्वाम्बरीषसहदेवभयमानसुराधस इति । वृषागिरो महाराजस्य पुत्रभूता ऋज्राश्वादयः पञ्च राजर्षयः सहेदं सूक्तं ददृशुः । आत्रस्येऽस्य सूक्तस्य ऋषयः [?] । उक्तं ह्यार्षानुक्रमण्याम् । सूक्तं स यो वृषेत्येतत्पञ्च वार्षागिरा विदुः । नियुक्ता नामधेयैः स्वरैरपि चैत[?]त्त्वदिद्य[?]टि [?] । अनादेशपरिभाषया त्रिष्टुप् । इन्द्रो देवता । दशरात्रस्य षष्ठेऽहनि मरुत्वतीये इदं सूक्तम् । तथा च सूत्रितम् । यं त्वं रथमिन्द्र स यो वृषेन्द्र मरुत्व इति तिस्र इति मरुत्वतीयम् । आ. ८-१ [?] इति ॥
> *sa yo vṛṣety ekonaviṃśatyṛcaṃ saptamaṃ sūktam | atrānukramyate | sa yo vṛṣaikonā vārṣāgirā ṛjrāśvāmbarīṣasahadevabhayamānasurādhasa iti | vṛṣāgiro mahārājasya putrabhūtā ṛjrāśvādayaḥ pañca rājarṣayaḥ sahedaṃ sūktaṃ dadṛśuḥ | ātrasye 'sya sūktasya ṛṣayaḥ [?] | uktaṃ hy ārṣānukramaṇyām | sūktaṃ sa yo vṛṣety etat pañca vārṣāgirā viduḥ | niyuktā nāmadheyaiḥ svarair api caita[?]ttvadidya[?]ṭi [?] | anādeśaparibhāṣayā triṣṭup | indro devatā | daśarātrasya ṣaṣṭhe 'hani marutvatīye idaṃ sūktam | tathā ca sūtritam | yaṃ tvaṃ ratham indra sa yo vṛṣendra marutva iti tisra iti marutvatīyam | Ā. 8-1 [?] iti ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada):** "*Sa yo vṛṣā* is the seventh sūkta in the fifteenth anuvāka. It has nineteen Ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said '*sa yo vṛṣaikonā vārṣāgirā ṛjrāśvāmbarīṣasahadevabhayamānasurādhasa iti*'. Five royal sages — Ṛjrāśva, Ambarīṣa, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna and Surādhas, sons of the great king Vṛṣāgira — together saw this sūkta. In the Ārṣānukramaṇikā it is said — *sūktaṃ sa yo vṛṣety etat pañca vārṣāgirā viduḥ | niyuktā nāmadheyaiḥ svarair api caitat…* [the last words clotted, [?]] — The metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Indra. On the sixth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, this sūkta is applied for the recitation of the mantras of the Marutvatīya *śastra*: so it is set down in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra by the aphorism *yaṃ tvaṃ ratham indra, sa yo vṛṣendra marutva iti tisra iti marutvatīyam* (*Ā.* 8-1 [as read])."

"Indra, who is the showerer of desires, who is *samokāḥ* — completely united, joined — with the powers (*vṛṣṇyebhiḥ*, 'the powers that belong to the vigorous'); the supreme ruler of the great heaven, the world of the sky, and of the earth, the widely-spread land; *satīnasatvā* — *satīna* is a name of water; one who makes water sit [descend], who sends it forth; *havyaḥ* in battles, in wars — to be called by all the praisers; such an Indra, accompanied by the Maruts — may he be for our protection."

**Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized, with the cited sūtras where read)**

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*yaḥ* — which Indra; *vṛṣā* — the one who showers desired objects; *vṛṣṇyebhiḥ* — with (all) powers; *samokāḥ* — together-dwelling [united with them]; *mahaḥ* — of the very vast; *divaḥ* — of the heavenly world; *pṛthivyāḥ ca* — and of the earth also; *samrāṭ* — the sole sovereign; *satīnasatvā* — the one who sends water; *bhareṣu* — in battles; *havyaḥ* — the one to be called (by all, for help); *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *saḥ indraḥ* — that Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"May Indra, who fulfils the desired objects of his devotees, who is endowed with all powers, the sole lord of the very vast heavenly world and of the earth, the sender of water, he who is called by all for help in battles — may he, together with the Maruts, be for our protection."

### Page 168 (PDF 188)

*(Running head: left 168; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**English Translation (as printed)**

> May he who is the showerer of desires, who is co-dweller with (all) energies, the supreme ruler over the vast heaven and earth, the sender of water and to be invoked in battles ; may Indra, associated with the Maruts be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.1 (Kannada)**

"*Vṛṣā* — *kāmānāṃ varṣitā*: the one who showers [grants] desired objects.

*Vṛṣṇyebhiḥ* — *vṛṣṇi bhavair vīryaiḥ*: with the powers that reside in the vigorous one. The two words *vṛṣā* and *vṛṣṇyebhiḥ* are both formed from the root *vṛṣ*. [Of the two roots *vṛṣu secane* and *vṛṣa śaktibandhane*:] the first word, *vṛṣā*, is from the root *vṛṣ* that gives the sense of sprinkling, showering; the second word, *vṛṣṇyebhiḥ*, from the root that gives the sense of strength and capacity — so it is derived, as is to be understood from the explanations that the bhāṣya-author gives in this context. But since the epithet *vṛṣan*, and the other epithets derived from it, are used at every step in the Ṛksaṃhitā, these words cannot be limited to the one fixed meaning: in each context the sense has to be given that fits that context. Let us therefore note, carefully, in which senses the word *vṛṣan* is chiefly used, and then examine what its special sense is when it is used here as an epithet of Indra.

The word *vṛṣan* is used in many places in the sense of *pumān*, 'a male, capable of sprinkling [seed]'. As an indicator of the masculine gender, this word is used either as a synonym of *puruṣa* ('man') or as a synonym of the males of horses and other animals."

> ये ते इन्द्र ददुषो वर्धयन्ति महि क्षत्रं स्थविरं वृष्ण्यं च ।
> *ye te indra daduṣo vardhayanti mahi kṣatraṃ sthaviraṃ vṛṣṇyaṃ ca |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-5[?]-8 as read [?])

"— here, for the word *vṛṣṇyam*, 'bullhood, manhood' (*vṛṣatvam*, *puṃstvam*); and in"

> स्तुत [?] श्रवस्यन्नवसोप मद्रिग्युक्त्वा हरी वृषणा योह्यर्वाङ् ।
> *stuta [?] śravasyann avasopa madrigyuktvā harī vṛṣaṇā yohy arvāṅ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-1[7?]6-1 as read [?]; the first word and *madrig-* clotted in print, not completed from memory)

"— here *vṛṣaṇā* means *yuvāsā* [as printed, ?]; and"

> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-30-10 as read [?])

"— here it may be inferred to be a synonym of Indra. But it is also the cause of doubt in many places, as to which deity is meant. Sometimes even Sāyaṇācārya, in explaining this epithet, has not reached a firm decision."

> वृषा छन्दुर्भवति हर्यतो वृषा क्षेमेण धेनां मघवा यदिन्वति ।
> *vṛṣā chandur bhavati haryato vṛṣā kṣemeṇa dhenāṃ maghavā yad invati |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-[3?]5-4 as read [?])

"In this Ṛk, for the word *vṛṣā* he first says '*vṛṣā — haviṣāṃ varṣayitā yajamānaḥ*' — the sacrificer who makes the oblations 'shower'; and then '*yadvā vṛṣā — indraḥ*' — and so leaves room for doubt. Thus, since it is used in various meanings, in each context the sense that fits it must be understood. In explaining this pregnant word, Max Müller, the English commentator, has told the depth of the ideas expressed by this word as follows:"

> In Vrishan we have one of those words which it is almost impossible to translate accurately. It occurs over and over again in the Vedic hymns and if we once know the various ideas which it either expresses or implies, we have litte [sic] difficulty in understanding its import in a vague and general way, though we look in vain for corresponding terms in any modern language … … … and we shall see how difficult it would be to translate such terms without losing either the key-note that was still sounding, or the harmonies which were set vibrating by it in the minds of the poets and their listeners.
> (F. Max Muller, *The Sacred Books of the East*, Vol. XXXII, pp. 138–139) *(English in the original.)*

"Since the word *vṛṣan* is used chiefly in the senses of *vīrya* and *parākrama* ('valour, prowess'), in this present Ṛk also *vṛṣṇyebhiḥ* means 'endowed with prowess', and so points to Indra. The point that, among gods or men, none can be equal to Indra in prowess, and that all are astonished at seeing Indra's deeds of valour, is told in many places. For example —"

> अस्येदु भिया गिरयश्च दृळ्हा द्यावा च भूमा जनुषस्तुजेते ।

"[— the quality of Indra who sends down water] is told. *Satīnasatvā*, *satīnamanyuḥ* mean 'one endowed with the intention of showering water', that is, 'one whose mind is bent on sending down the water in the form of rain'.

*Bhareṣu havyaḥ* — *bhara* is a name for battle (*Ni.* [?]) — '*bharater vā, harater vā*' (*Ni.* 4-24 as read [?]): the Nirukta-author shows the derivation of the word *bhara* — either from the root *bhṛ* with the sense 'to carry, bear', or from the root *hṛ* with the sense 'to take away, seize'. *Bhareṣu* — in battles; *havyaḥ* — *stotṛbhir āhvātavyaḥ* — he who is to be called by the praisers: Indra, who is called for help by all his devotees at the times of war. That Indra is the god of war is shown even at the time of his birth:"

> उपस्थाय मातरमन्नमैट्ट तिग्ममपश्यदभि सोममूधः ।

> *jajñānaḥ somaṃ sahase papātha pra te mātā mahimānam uvāca | endra paprāthorv antarikṣaṃ yudhā devebhyo varivaś cakartha ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* [3?]-4[9?]-3 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "Standing by [his] mother he sought food; he saw the sharp [Soma] over the udder of Soma [plant]… he went about driving others away, the many-faced one did great things"; "Born, you drank Soma for strength; your mother proclaimed your greatness; you, O Indra, filled the wide mid-air; in battle you made room for the gods".)*

"— as in many places, Indra on being born drank Soma, for the increase of his strength and as the helper for the preparation for war; and in battle he won the victory and made room for the movement of the gods: so he is praised. And therefore his devotees too call upon Indra for help at all times of war."

> यं क्रन्दसी संयती विह्वयेते परेऽवर उभया अमित्राः ।
> *yaṃ krandasī saṃyatī vihvayete pare 'vara ubhayā amitrāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-12-8 as read [?])

> त्वां वृत्रेष्विन्द्र सत्पतिं तरुत्रं त्वां चष्टे मुष्टिहा गोषु युध्यन् ।
> *tvāṃ vṛtreṣv indra satpatiṃ tarutraṃ tvāṃ caṣṭe muṣṭihā goṣu yudhyan |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-3[3?]-3 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "Whom the two roaring [hosts] when they meet call upon, the far and the near, both [sets of] foes"; "You, Indra, the lord of the good in the battles, the carrier across — you the fist-smiter calls on, fighting for cattle".)*

"— and so on: since he is called upon in times of war, there is the epithet *bhareṣu havyaḥ*.

*Marutvān* — the eternal companionship between Indra and the Maruts is well known in the Śruti. The relation of ruler and subjects between Indra and the Maruts, the offering of oblations jointly to Indra and the Maruts in the principal sacrificial acts, and the help the Maruts give Indra when he fights against the demon Vṛtra, are praised in many places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. A story of old, which tells how Indra, together with the Maruts, stood apart from the other gods, can be seen in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa."

"Formerly, when the gods had performed the *ātithya* rite, each — out of rivalry, unwilling to be outshone by another's splendour [as the sense seems; the print's words are clotted] — formed four groups and separated: Agni with the Vasus, Soma with the Rudras, Varuṇa with the Ādityas, Indra with the Maruts, and Bṛhaspati with the Viśvedevas formed separate groups. In this story, Indra's companionship with the Maruts, and the close relationship held with them, are stated. Besides this, in many places Indra is said to be the lord and the Maruts the subjects. "— and from Ṛks such as these there is the invocation, and the offering of oblation, to Indra and the Maruts together. Because there is such companionship, here too he has the epithet *marutvān*. Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *vṛṣṇyebhiḥ* (the word *vṛṣan*; *yat* in the sense 'born in, belonging to' by *bhave chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 4-4-110 as read, ?]; *bha*-designation before *yat* by *yaci bham* [Pā. Sū. 1-4-18]; loss of the *a* of *an* by *ālloponaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-134 as read]; the rule *ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-168 as read] — which would keep the stem unchanged — is said not to apply here, by a line of reasoning to be accepted; the instrumental plural *bhis*, kept as *bhis* and not *ais* by *bahulaṃ chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; *e* by *bahuvacane jhaly et* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-103 as read]; accent on the first syllable by *yato 'nāvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 as read]); *mahaḥ* (root *mah pūjāyām*, *kvip* by *kvip ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read]; or from *mahat* with Vedic loss of the *at*; the ending acute by *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 as read]); *divaḥ* (*ūḍidaṃpadādi* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); *pṛthivyāḥ* (*udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-174 as read]); *samrāṭ* (root *rājṛ dīptau*, *kvip* by *kvip ca*, total loss of the affix; *mo rāji samaḥ kvau* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-25 as read], so that the *m* of *sam* stays *m*; the accent of the finite-participle-like compound member by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; *ṣatva* of *j* by *vraścabhrasja…*; *ḍ* for the word-final; *ṭ* as the optional pause-form *cartva*); *satīnasatvā* (root *padḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*; *satīnaṃ* = 'rain-water that settles in the clouds', formed with the Uṇādi *īna*, *d* → *t*; or *satī mādhyamikā vāk*, 'the middle-region speech', *satī inā īśvarā yasya tat satīnam*, with the masculine-like form by *vyatyayo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 4-[1?]58 as read, ?]; *satīnasatvan*, with the accent of the first member since it belongs to the *marudvṛdh…* list; lengthening of the penult before *su*; loss of *n*); *marutvān* (*maruto 'sya santi*; *matup* by *tad asyāstyasmin* [Pā. Sū. 5-2-94 as read]; *m* → *v* by *jhayaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-10 as read]; lengthening by *atvasantasya* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-14 as read]; *num* because of the marked affix; the loss of the final consonant of the cluster is treated as not having taken place [*asiddha*] so *n* is not dropped); *ūtī* (*ūtiyūtijūti…* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 as read], a *ktin*-ending noun with the accent fixed; dative singular, with *supāṃ sulug…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read] and the single substitute that is the preceding homogeneous long vowel). *yasya | anāptaḥ | sūryasya-iva | yāmaḥ | bhare-bhare | vṛtra-hā | śuṣmaḥ | asti | vṛṣan-tamaḥ | sakhi-bhiḥ | svebhiḥ | evaiḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.2)**

> यस्येन्द्रस्य यामो गतिरनाप्तः परैरप्राप्तः [?] सूर्यस्येव । यथा सूर्यस्य गतिरन्यैर्न प्राप्तुं शक्यते तद्वत् । स्वेभिरात्मीयैरेवैर्गमनशीलैः सखिभिर्मित्रभूतैर्मरुद्भिः सह वृषन्तमोऽतिशयेन कामानां वर्षिता । भरे भरे सर्वेषु संग्रामेषु वृत्रहा शत्रूणां हन्ता शुष्मः सर्वेषामसुराणां शोषकः । एवंभूतो य इन्द्रोऽस्ति विद्यते स मरुत्वानिन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥
> *yasyendrasya yāmo gatir anāptaḥ parair aprāptaḥ [?] sūryasyeva | yathā sūryasya gatir anyair na prāptuṃ śakyate tadvat | svebhir ātmīyair evair gamanaśīlaiḥ sakhibhir mitrabhūtair marudbhiḥ saha vṛṣantamo 'tiśayena kāmānāṃ varṣitā | bhare bhare sarveṣu saṃgrāmeṣu vṛtrahā śatrūṇāṃ hantā śuṣmaḥ sarveṣām asurāṇāṃ śoṣakaḥ | evaṃbhūto ya indro 'sti vidyate sa marutvān indro no 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖*

"Of whom, Indra, the speed (*yāmaḥ*), the going, is unattainable (*anāptaḥ*) — not to be reached by others — like the sun's: as the sun's going cannot be overtaken by others, so is his. With his own, [swift]-going friends, the Maruts, *vṛṣantamaḥ* — most abundantly the showerer of desires; *bhare bhare* — in all battles, *vṛtrahā* — the slayer of foes; *śuṣmaḥ* — the withering of all the Asuras: such an Indra who exists — may that Indra with the Maruts be for our protection."

**Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized)**

> यामः । या प्रापणे । अर्तिस्तुसुहुसृधृक्षिक्षुयाभा… इत्यादिना [?] भावे मन्प्रत्ययः । निस्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । शुष्मः । शुष शोषणे । अविसिविसिशुषिभ्यः कित् । उ. १-१४३ [?] । इति मन्प्रत्ययः । निस्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अस्ति । यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । वृषन्तमः । वृषन् इति तकारात् [?] उत्तरस्य तमपो नाद्यस्य । पा. ८-२-१८ [?] इति नुट् । एवैः । इण् गतौ । इण्शीङ्भ्यां वन् [Uṇ.] ॥
> *yāmaḥ | yā prāpaṇe | artistusuhusṛdhṛkṣikṣuyābhā… ity ādinā [?] bhāve manpratyayaḥ | nistvād ādyudāttatvam | śuṣmaḥ | śuṣa śoṣaṇe | avisivisiśuṣibhyaḥ kit | U. 1-143 [?] | iti manpratyayaḥ | nistvād ādyudāttatvam | asti | yadvṛttayogād anighātaḥ | vṛṣantamaḥ | vṛṣan iti takārāt [?] uttarasya tamapo nādyasya | Pā. 8-2-18 [?] iti nuṭ | evaiḥ | iṇ gatau | iṇśīṅbhyāṃ van [Uṇ.] ‖*

*(Characterized: the root* yā *'to reach', the affix* man *in the sense of the action;* śuṣmaḥ *from* śuṣ *'to dry up', with* man *by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. Sū. 1-143, as read, ?]; the verb* asti *keeps its accent because of the relative that governs it;* vṛṣantamaḥ *with the augment* nuṭ*;* evaiḥ *from* iṇ *'to go' with* van*. **॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*yasya* — of which Indra; *yāmaḥ* — the speed of movement (swift going); *sūryasya iva* — like the sun's speed of movement; *anāptaḥ* — unsurpassable by anyone (and which Indra); *svebhiḥ* — his own; *evaiḥ* — those whose nature is to go; *sakhibhiḥ* — with the Maruts who are his friends; *vṛṣantamaḥ* — the one who abundantly showers the desired objects; *bhare bhare* — in all battles; *vṛtrahā* — destroyer of enemies; *śuṣmaḥ* — one with the power that makes the Rākṣasas waste away; *asti* — is; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — that Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra, whose speed of movement, like the sun's, can be overtaken by no one, who is swift in going; who, together with his friends the Maruts, showers desired objects abundantly; who is the destroyer of enemies in all battles and the one who makes the Rākṣasas waste away — may that Indra, together with the Maruts, be for our protection."

"From the descriptions in Ṛks such as these it is understood that the speed of Indra's movement is [that of] an incomparable power.

*Evyaiḥ sakhibhiḥ* — *gamanaśīlair mitrabhūtair marudbhiḥ saha*: with the Maruts, who are always of a moving nature, and who are Indra's friends. The friendship of Indra and the Maruts and their companionship were told in the explanation of the previous Ṛk. The true nature of these Maruts is known here by the epithets *evyaiḥ* and *evāsaḥ*. For example —"

> आ ये रजांसि तविषीभिरव्यत प्र व एवासः स्वयतासो अध्रजन् ।
> *ā ye rajāṃsi taviṣībhir avyata pra va evāsaḥ svayatāso adhrajan |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-166-5 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the word *evāsaḥ* [Sāyaṇa] has said: '*marutsambandhinaḥ aśvaviśeṣāḥ*' — 'particular horses belonging to the Maruts' is what it comes to; the sense is: swift-going horses. Besides —"

> प्र वो महे मतयो यन्तु विष्णवे मरुत्वते गिरिजा एवयामरुत् ।
> *pra vo mahe matayo yantu viṣṇave marutvate girijā evayāmarut |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-87-1 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, and in all the remaining Ṛks of the sūkta 5-87 [as read], the nature of the Maruts can be known from the epithet *evayāmarut* also. (According to one view, however, *Evayāmarut* here is the name of the ṛṣi.) In the fourth *khaṇḍa* of the [sixth, as read, ?] chapter of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, the mantra called the *Acchāvāka-śastra*, *evayāmarut*, is addressed to the Maruts; it is said that, when a sacrifice is being done for Indra, a mantra concerned with the Maruts disregards Indra; and Bulila [as printed], the Acchāvāka priest, was reproached on that account, and the Acchāvāka's reply too is described there. The telling of that story is unnecessary here. Chiefly when oblations and the like are offered addressed to the Maruts, and when praise is made, the epithets *evāsaḥ*, *evyaiḥ*, *evayāmarut* are used mostly. The sense is: Maruts who are always of a moving nature. In the same sense —"

> कथा दाशेम नमसा सुदानूनेवया मरुतो अच्छोक्तौ प्रश्रवसो मरुतो अच्छोक्तौ ।
> *kathā dāśema namasā sudānūn evayā maruto acchoktau praśravaso maruto acchoktau |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-41-16 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk also *evayāmarut* is described.

*Vṛṣantamaḥ* — *atiśayena kāmānāṃ varṣitā*: one who showers desired objects in abundance. The special meanings of the word *vṛṣan* were told in the explanation of the previous Ṛk."

### Page 179 (PDF 199)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 9 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 179.)*

"*Bhare-bhare vṛtrahā* — *sarveṣu saṃgrāmeṣu śatrūṇāṃ hantā*: 'in all battles the slayer of enemies'; here they have given the word *vṛtra* the sense 'enemy'. Looked at literally, the word *vṛtrahan* comes to mean 'the killer of the one named Vṛtra'. According to the Paurāṇika tradition, the word *vṛtra* is well known as the title-name of a certain Rākṣasa. But in the Ṛksaṃhitā this word has various meanings; chiefly 'Rākṣasa, enemy', and so on. In the Ṛksaṃhitā there are many separate passages for each of these two meanings. Taken together, the meaning 'enemy' is said to be the ancient one. This enemy may be in various forms. In the contexts of Indra's battles, the word is used in two senses, *Ārya-vṛtra* and *Dāsa-vṛtra* —"

> यया दासान्यार्याणि वृत्रा करो वज्रिन्त्सुतुका [as printed] नाहुषाणि ।
> *yayā dāsāny āryāṇi vṛtrā karo vajrin sutukā [as printed] nāhuṣāṇi |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-22-10 as read [?])

> त्वं ताँ इन्द्रोभयाँ अमित्रान्दासा वृत्राण्यार्या च शूर ।
> *tvaṃ tāṃ indrobhayāṃ amitrān dāsā vṛtrāṇy āryā ca śūra |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-33-3 as read [?])

> हतो वृत्राण्यार्या हतो दासानि सत्पती ।
> *hato vṛtrāṇy āryā hato dāsāni satpatī |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-60-6 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "By which [might], O thunderbolt-bearer, you make the Dāsa and the Ārya [foes], the descendants of Nahuṣa, [yours]"; "You, O Indra, [subdue] both the foes, the Dāsa and the Ārya enemies, O hero"; "You two lords of the good have slain the Ārya foes and the Dāsa foes".)*

"In various contexts such as these, 'Vṛtra', that is, the enemy — whether in the groups of Āryas or in the groups of non-Āryas — who gives trouble to the sacrificer must be fought with and destroyed: so Indra is besought. Likewise, whenever trouble has come to the people's life, it is Indra's nature to obtain the protection of the deity of the realm (*rāṣṭra*). The destruction of this evil power is described in the Saṃhitā as, above all, the most important of Indra's very valorous deeds. These evil powers are of many forms; among them, the one that is most violent in nature is understood to be Vṛtra.

This word *vṛtra* has arisen from the root *vṛ*; *vṛ* has the senses of 'to obstruct, to cover, to conceal'. This matter is explained in detail in *Ṛ. Saṃ.* part 3, page 123 [as printed, in the Kannada original series]. Because of such a nature, enemy-destroyer of the obstructing kind, the epithet *vṛtrahan* has become very famous for Indra.

*Śuṣmaḥ* — since *ojaḥ, pājaḥ* and the like are read among the names of strength, *śuṣma* means strength (*Ni.* 2-9 as read [?]): '*śuṣmam iti balanāma śoṣayatīti sataḥ*' [as printed, ?] (*Ni.* 2-[2?]3 as read [?]). Here it is an epithet of Indra as 'the strong'. *Sarveṣām asurāṇāṃ śoṣakaḥ* — 'one who makes all the enemies wither': the sense is, one who has the strength that makes them waste away."

"Of which Indra the paths, the rays (*panthāsaḥ*), milking out (*dughānāḥ*) the waters of rain (*retasaḥ*) — pouring down — go, issue forth, spread out from the heavenly world hither and thither. **॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*yasya* — of which Indra; *śavasā* — endowed with strength; *aparītāḥ* — (by enemies) not to be approached; *panthāsaḥ* — rays of splendour; *divo na* — like the rays of the shining sun (which make rain), from the sky [like the rays of the sun going out from the sky]; *retasaḥ* — the waters of rain; *dughānāḥ* — pouring; *yanti* — spread from the world of heaven in all directions; *taraddveṣāḥ* — one who overcomes such enemies, [and]; *pauṃsyebhiḥ* — [with his] prowess; *sasahiḥ* — victorious in fighting [with enemies]; *marutvān* — one joined with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may [he] be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"May Indra — whose rays of splendour, joined with strength and not to be approached by enemies, pour down the waters of rain like the rays of the shining sun, and spread from the heavenly world to every side — who overcomes such enemies, and is victorious in battle with enemies by his prowess, and who is joined with the Maruts, give us protection."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> May he, whose rays, powerful and unattainable, issue forth like those of the sun, milking (the clouds) ; he who is victorious over is [sic] adversaries triumphant by his manly energies ; may Indra, associated with the Muruts [sic] be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.3 (Kannada)**

"In explaining this Ṛk, between Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya there is a difference in the order of construction (*anvayakrama*) and in the explanation of the meaning, but the main intention is the same. In Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya, for the word *panthāsaḥ* is given '*raśmayaḥ*' — 'rays'; Skandasvāmin has *mārgāḥ* — 'paths'" *(continues on p. 183)*

### Page 183 (PDF 203)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 10 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 183.)*

"[— 'paths'] and so explains. From this difference of meaning there is a difference in the construction too. As in the first explanation:

*Yasya* — *indrasya*; *panthāsaḥ* — *raśmayaḥ*, 'rays'; *retasaḥ* — *vṛṣṭyudakāni*, 'waters of rain'; *dughānāḥ* — *pravarṣantaḥ*, 'pouring'; *yanti* — *nirgacchanti dyulokād itas tataḥ prasaranti*, 'they issue forth, they spread from the heavenly world hither and thither' — that is, the sense is that they spread in all directions from the heavenly world. *Divo na* — '*yathā dyotamānasya sūryasya kiraṇā vṛṣṭiṃ kurvanto nabhaḥsthalān nirgacchanti tadvat*': as the rays of the shining sun, making rain, go out from the sky — that is, 'as these go out from the sky and spread to all the world', this is said as a simile showing the capacity for splendour of Indra and of the sun. Then the two words *śavasā* and *aparītāḥ* are adjectives to *panthāsaḥ*: *śavasā* is 'endowed with strength', and *aparītāḥ* is 'not to be approached by enemies'.

According to the second explanation: '*diva iti pañcamī | na śabdaḥ upariṣṭād upacāraḥ*' [as printed, the second clause doubtful [?]]: '*dyulokāt yasyendrasya balena retasaḥ vṛṣṭilakṣaṇāny udakāni | dughānāḥ kṣarantaḥ | panthāsaḥ vṛṣṭipatanamārgāḥ | yanti pṛthivīṃ prati gacchanti*': by Indra's power the paths of the falling of rain go from the world of the gods towards the earth, pouring out. In this, *divaḥ* means 'from the world of the gods', in the fifth case; and *na* is understood with the sense of *saṃprati* — 'now', 'in the present case' — and not only as a particle of comparison. In this construction *śavasā* means *indrasya balena*, 'by Indra's strength', and *aparītāḥ* means *vṛṣṭipratibandhakarair asurādibhir aprāptāḥ* — 'not approached by the Asuras and the like that hold back the rain'; and it serves as an adjective to *panthāsaḥ* as well.

*Retasaḥ* — since *ārṇaḥ, kṣodaḥ, kṣadma* and the like are read among the names of water (*Ni.* [1-?]3 as read [?]), *retasaḥ* means 'rain-waters'.

*Taraddveṣāḥ* — *dveṣāṃsi śatrūn taran jitaśatrukaḥ iti arthaḥ*: one who has crossed [overcome] the enemies, the sense is, one who has conquered enemies.

*Pauṃsyebhiḥ* — since *ojaḥ, pājaḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-eight names of strength (*Ni.* 2-9 as read [?]), and also among the [forty-six, as read, ?] names of battle, such as *raṇaḥ, vivāk, vikhādaḥ*, the word has the two senses 'strength' and 'battle'. Here it means 'by strengths'; 'prowess endowed with manly capacity' is the sense. This epithet is used very often of Indra —"

Sū. 4-[?]10 [?]] with the augment *tuṭ*; *guṇa* of the root vowel; acute on the first syllable by *ñnityādir nityam*; the *jas*-substitute for *śas* by the statement *supāṃ suluk…*, read in the print as *supāṃ suṣo bhavanti* [?]); *dughānāḥ* (root *duh prapūraṇe*; *śānac* for *laṭ* in the active; *luk* of *śap* by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ*; *gh* for *h* by *vyatyayo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read], even though no cause for it is present; the final acute that the *c*-marked affix would give is replaced by the first-syllable acute, since *vṛṣa* etc. is an open list [*ākṛtigaṇa*], by *vṛṣādīnāṃ ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-203 as read]); *panthāsaḥ* (*patanti iti panthāno raśmayaḥ*; root *patḷ gatau*; *ini* by *pateṣṭh ca* [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]]; the word *pathin*; *jas*: *a* for *i* by *pathimathyṛbhukṣām āt* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-85 as read]; the augment *asuk* by *ajjhaser asuk* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 as read]; or, in the Vedic manner, *n* → *s* by letter-interchange; *th* → *nth* by *tho nthaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-87 as read]; *s* → *ru* → visarga; acute on the first syllable by *pathimathoḥ sarvanāmasthāne* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-199 as read]).

The grammar of Rik 100.3 continues: *yanti* (root *iṇ gatau*, *adādi*; *laṭ*, third person plural, *jhi*; *anta* by *jho 'ntaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-81 as read]; no *nighāta*, because of the relative [*yad*] before it; the verb being *adyudātta* by its affix); *taraddveṣāḥ* (root *dviṣ aprītau*; *asun* of the Uṇādi class; *dveṣāṃsi taran yaḥ saḥ taraddveṣāḥ* — the member that is the object is placed last because the compound belongs to the *rājadantādi* class); *sasahiḥ* (root *ṣah abhibhave*; *ki* by *ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-171 as read] by the rule *utsargaś chandasi*, even without a cause for it; doubling as if *liṭ* followed; *ādihalśeṣa* in the reduplicative; lengthening of the reduplicative syllable by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 as read]; final acute by the affix); *pauṃsyebhiḥ* (*puṃsaḥ bhāvaḥ pauṃsyam*; *ṣyañ* in the sense of 'state' under the heading *strīpuṃsābhyām* [Pā. Sū. 4-1-87 as read]; *vṛddhi* by *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ*; since the affix is *ñit*, acute on the first syllable; *bhis* follows, and *ais* does not appear because of *bahulaṃ chandasi*). *saḥ | aṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ | aṅgiraḥ-tamaḥ | bhūt | vṛṣā | vṛṣa-bhiḥ | sakhi-bhiḥ | sakhā | san | ṛgmi-bhiḥ | ṛgmī | gātu-bhiḥ | jyeṣṭhaḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.4)**

> स इन्द्रोऽङ्गिरोभिः । अङ्गन्ति गच्छन्तीत्यङ्गिरसो गन्तारः । तेभ्योऽप्यङ्गिरस्तमोऽभूत् । अतिशयेन गन्ता भवति । वृषभिर्वृषा वर्षित्रभ्योऽप्यतिशयेन वर्षिता । सखिभिः समानख्यानेभ्यो मित्रभूतेभ्योऽपि सखातिशयेन हितकारी । एवंभूतः सन् ऋग्मिभिरर्चनीयेभ्योऽपि ऋग्मी अर्चनीयो भवति । गातुभिर्गातव्येभ्यः स्तोतव्येभ्योऽपि ज्येष्ठोऽतिशयेन स्तोतव्यः । एवंगुणविशिष्टो मरुत्वानिन्द्रो रक्षणाय भवतु ॥
> *sa indro 'ṅgirobhiḥ | aṅganti gacchantīty aṅgiraso gantāraḥ | tebhyo 'py aṅgirastamo 'bhūt | atiśayena gantā bhavati | vṛṣabhir vṛṣā varṣitrabhyo 'py atiśayena varṣitā | sakhibhiḥ samānakhyānebhyo mitrabhūtebhyo 'pi sakhātiśayena hitakārī | evaṃbhūtaḥ san ṛgmibhir arcanīyebhyo 'pi ṛgmī arcanīyo bhavati | gātubhir gātavyebhyaḥ stotavyebhyo 'pi jyeṣṭho 'tiśayena stotavyaḥ | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭo marutvān indro rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖*

"That Indra — *aṅgirobhiḥ*: those who move, go (*aṅganti*), are *aṅgirasaḥ*, 'goers'; he became *aṅgirastamaḥ* even among them, that is, the one who is the greatest goer. *Vṛṣabhiḥ vṛṣā* — among the showerers, the greatest showerer. *Sakhibhiḥ* — among those of equal standing, who are friends, the friend who does good to the highest degree. Being such, *ṛgmibhiḥ ṛgmī* — he is worshipful even among the worshipful ones. *Gātubhiḥ jyeṣṭhaḥ* — even among those who are to be praised, to be sung, he is the most excellent, to be praised most. Indra, thus endowed, accompanied by the Maruts — may he be for our protection."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*saḥ* — Indra; *aṅgirobhiḥ* — among those who go about (swiftly); *aṅgirastamaḥ* — the one who goes about most swiftly; *bhūt* — was; *vṛṣabhiḥ* — among those who shower desired objects; *vṛṣā* — the giver who is the most generous of desired objects; *sakhibhiḥ* — among friends; *sakhā san* — being a friend (the most beneficent); *ṛgmibhiḥ* — among the worshipful; *ṛgmī* — (the most praiseworthy) the worshipful one; *gātubhiḥ* — among all those who deserve to be praised; *jyeṣṭhaḥ* — the most excellent; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"May Indra — who among those who go swiftly goes most swiftly; among those who shower desired objects is the most generous giver of the desired; among friends is the most beneficent friend; among the worshipful is the most worshipful; and among those worthy of praise is the most excellent — together with the Maruts be for our protection."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> He is the swiftest among the swift, most bountiful amongst the bountiful, a friend with friends, venerable among those who claim veneration, and pre-eminent among those deserving of praise : may Indra associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.4 (Kannada)**

"*Aṅgirobhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ* — *aṅganti gacchantīti aṅgiraso gantāraḥ, tebhyo 'py aṅgirastamaḥ — atiśayena gantā*: 'among those who go about, he who goes about most swiftly' — Sāyaṇa has given this meaning. This way of explaining is also acceptable in one respect. For, in the explanation of the second Ṛk of this same sūkta, quoting Śruti sentences in praise of the speed of Indra's movement, it was shown how horses swifter than the speed of the mind carry his chariot; and the above meaning, which describes such swift movement of Indra, is also borne out from that point of view. But Skandasvāmin says:"

> स इन्द्रोऽङ्गिरोभिः ऋषिभिः अङ्गिरस्तमः । सोऽयमङ्गिरोभिः सम्बन्धादङ्गिरःसम्बन्धिस्यमङ्गिरःशब्दोऽत्र द्रष्टव्यः [?] । अतिशयेन अङ्गिरसां स्तुत्यतया सम्बन्धी भवति ॥
> *sa indro 'ṅgirobhiḥ ṛṣibhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ | so 'yam aṅgirobhiḥ sambandhād aṅgiraḥsambandhisyam aṅgiraḥśabdo 'tra draṣṭavyaḥ [?] | atiśayena aṅgirasāṃ stutyatayā sambandhī bhavati ‖*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read; the middle clause clotted [?])

"[— that is: 'among the Aṅgiras seers Indra is the most Aṅgiras'; here the word *aṅgiras* is to be seen as 'connected with Aṅgirases'; he is connected, to the highest degree, with the Aṅgirases by being praiseworthy.] In the first" *(continues on p. 188)*

### Page 188 (PDF 208)

*(Running head: left 188; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

"[In the first *aṅgirobhiḥ*] the word *aṅgiras* means the seers called Aṅgirases; in the second *aṅgirastamaḥ* the word *aṅgiras* is used in the sense 'he too is one [of them]' — just as, in showing an extremely close relation by identity (*tādātmya*), here too, because of extreme worthiness of reverence, he is said to be one very near to the Aṅgirases: thus [Skandasvāmin] has given the meaning. Who the Aṅgiras seers are, what their greatness is, and what the relation is between Agni and the Aṅgirases — all these matters were explained in the *Ṛgvedasaṃhitā*, part 1, pp. 641–642 [as printed in the Kannada original series]. Continuing that explanation, let us here learn what relation Indra has with the Aṅgirases; or whether Indra can be addressed as 'Aṅgiras'.

The word *Aṅgiras* is a title-name; it is also the name of a line of seers; and it is also the name of a group of deities; in three places this word has [separate] application.

First: the title-name *Aṅgiras* is used as the name of a single person, and in many places his power is described. For example —"

> अङ्गिरस्वन्महिव्रत [print: …न्नमहिव्रत, ?] प्रस्कण्वस्य श्रुधी हवम् ।
> *aṅgirasvan mahivrata [print: …nnamahivrata, ?] praskaṇvasya śrudhī havam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-[4?]5-3 as read [?])

> तमु त्वा वाजसातममङ्गिरस्वद्धवामहे ।
> *tam u tvā vājasātamam aṅgirasvad dhavāmahe |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-[7?]8-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛk sentences such as these, calling to mind Aṅgiras, we too ask in the same way: the request is, 'hear our prayer too'. In the same way in the Upaniṣads also Aṅgiras is a seer who knew the truth of the Self, and there is a story that he taught Śaunaka the knowledge of fire (*agnividyā*):"

> शौनको ह वै महाशालोऽङ्गिरसं विधिवदुपसन्नः पप्रच्छ । कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति ॥
> *śaunako ha vai mahāśālo 'ṅgirasaṃ vidhivad upasannaḥ papraccha | kasmin nu bhagavo vijñāte sarvam idaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavatīti ‖*
> (*Muṇḍakopaniṣad* 1-1-3 as read [?])

"— but who this human person Aṅgiras is will be explained later.

Second: it is the name of a line of seers. That the seer Aṅgiras, who was born in the very first Agni, and that lineage grew from him, is also hinted at in the Ṛksaṃhitā:"

> त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अङ्गिरा ऋषिर्देवो देवानामभवः शिवः सखा ।
> *tvam agne prathamo aṅgirā ṛṣir devo devānām abhavaḥ śivaḥ sakhā |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-31-1 as read [?])

"This story is also described in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa."

Here, since we need to know what relation Indra has with the Aṅgirases, how it grew, and how this epithet *aṅgirobhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ* arises for Indra, that matter is briefly told with examples from the Śruti. In former times the seven seers named Aṅgirases went to seek the cows hidden in the cave of a mountain; and, meditating then on Indra with devotion, [it is described in the Ṛksaṃhitā how] Indra became their deity of worship:"

> वीळौ सतीरभि धीरा अतृन्दन्प्राचाहिन्वन्मनसा सप्त विप्राः ।
> विश्वामविन्दन्पथ्यामृतस्य प्रजानन्नित्ता नमसा विवेश ।
> विदद्यदी सरमा रुग्णमद्रेर्महि पाथः पूर्व्यं सध्र्यक्कः ।

*(Gloss, mine and tentative and only in outline: "The wise seven seers pierced the firm [places], they impelled [it] forward with the mind; they found the whole path of the Law; knowing it, he entered with homage. When Saramā found the cleft of the rock, she made the great ancient way her own; she led the way of the syllables, first knowing, she went toward the sound. The wisest came, wishing friendship; the rock gave up its embryo for the good-doer. The mortal won it with the youths, [wishing for] the sacrifice, and then he became Aṅgiras, honouring at once.")*

### Page 190 (PDF 210)

*(Running head: left 190; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 100.4, continued from p. 189 (Kannada)**

"[…Indra too, becoming the chief among the Aṅgirases, when fighting] split the mountain, the cows and the waters were released: so it is described in the form of a story, that Indra stood foremost, most worthy of reverence among all the Aṅgirases. Therefore the expression *aṅgirobhiḥ aṅgirastamaḥ* is fitting.

*Ṛgmibhiḥ ṛgmī* — *arcanīyebhyo 'pi arcanīyo bhavati*: 'he is worshipful even among the worshipful': the sense is, the most excellent worshipful one among all those who are worthy of worship."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.4)** *(grammar pages, pp. 190–191, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *aṅgirobhiḥ* (*aṅganti gacchantīti aṅgirasaḥ*; the roots *agi, ragi, lagi* in the sense of going; the Uṇādi affix *asun*, fixed by the rule *aṅgirā apsarāḥ* [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]-[?] as read, ?]; the word *aṅgiras*; before *bhis*, *s* → *ru* → *u* with *guṇa*; since the affix is *nit*, acute on the first syllable; the instrumental in the sense of the ablative in this mantra); *aṅgirastamaḥ* (*atiśayena aṅgirāḥ*; *tamap* by *atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau* [Pā. Sū. 5-3-55 as read]; being *pit*, unaccented); *bhūt* (*luṅ* in the sense of the present in the Veda by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 as read]; loss of the *i* of *tip* by *itaś ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-100 as read]; *luk* of *sic* by *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 2-4-77 as read]; the *aṭ* does not come, by *bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 as read]; *nighāta*); *vṛṣā* (root *vṛṣu secane*; the Uṇādi *kanin*; acute on the first syllable, the affix being *nit*); *ṛgmibhiḥ* (root *ṛc stutau*; *kvip* by the class *sampadādibhyaḥ* [vārttika, as read [Pā. 3-3-108, ?]]; the form *ṛc*; *mini* in the possessive sense; *c* → *k* by *coḥ kuḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-30 as read] since the word has *pada* status; *g* by *jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-39 as read]; *ṛgmin*; final acute by the affix; instrumental); *gātubhiḥ* (root *gā stutau*; *tu* in the passive by *kamimanijani…* [Uṇ. Sū. 1-73 as read, ?]; final acute by the affix).

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.5)**

> सूनुभिर्न पुत्रैरिव रुद्रेभिः रुद्रपुत्रैर्मरुद्भिर्युक्तः ऋभ्वा महान् एवंभूतः स इन्द्रो नृषाह्ये नृभिः पुरुषैः सोढव्ये संग्रामेऽमित्रान् शत्रून् सासह्वानभिभूतवान् । अपि च सनीळेभिः समाननिलयैर्मरुद्भिः सह श्रवस्यानि श्रव इत्यन्ननाम । तद्धेतुभूतान्युदकानि तूर्वन् मेघात्प्रच्यावयन् मरुत्वानिन्द्रोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥
> *sūnubhir na putrair iva rudrebhiḥ rudraputrair marudbhir yuktaḥ ṛbhvā mahān evaṃbhūtaḥ sa indro nṛṣāhye nṛbhiḥ puruṣaiḥ soḍhavye saṃgrāme 'mitrān śatrūn sāsahvān abhibhūtavān | api ca sanīḷebhiḥ samānanilayair marudbhiḥ saha śravasyāni srava ity anna­nāma | taddhetubhūtāny udakāni tūrvan meghāt pracyāvayan marutvān indro 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖*

*(The print's* srava *is read as* śrava *[?].)*

"As if with sons, *rudrebhiḥ* — with the Maruts, the sons of Rudra — joined, *ṛbhvā* — great: such an Indra, in the battle (*nṛṣāhye*) that is to be endured by men, overcame (*sāsahvān*) the enemies, the foes. And also, with the Maruts who dwell in the same abode (*sanīḷebhiḥ*), *śravasyāni* — *śrava* is a name of food; the waters that are the cause of it — *tūrvan* — making them fall from the cloud: such an Indra, with the Maruts — may he be for our protection."

**Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized, partly transcribed)**

> नृषाह्ये । षह मर्षणे । शकिसहोश्च । पा. ३-१-९९ [?] । इति कर्मणि यत् । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायां धात्वकारस्य दीर्घत्वम् । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तत्वे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । सासह्वान् । षह अभिभवे । लिटः क्वसुः । आभ्यासदीर्घत्वं छान्दसम् । अमित्रान् । मित्राण्येषु न सन्तीत्यमित्राः । नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सनीळेभिः । समानं नीळं येषां ते सनीळाः । समानस्य छन्दसीति सभावः ॥
> *nṛṣāhye | ṣaha marṣaṇe | śakisahoś ca | Pā. 3-1-99 [?] | iti karmaṇi yat | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyāṃ dhātvakārasya dīrghatvam | yato 'nāva ity ādyudāttatve kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | sāsahvān | ṣaha abhibhave | liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | ābhyāsadīrghatvaṃ chāndasam | amitrān | mitrāṇy eṣu na santīty amitrāḥ | nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | sanīḷebhiḥ | samānaṃ nīḷaṃ yeṣāṃ te sanīḷāḥ | samānasya chandasīti sabhāvaḥ ‖*

*(Characterized: the form* nṛṣāhye *(*ṣah *'to endure' with* yat *by* śakisahoś ca *[Pā. Sū. 3-1-99, as read [?]]; lengthening of the* a *of the root in the Saṃhitā, 'as seen in others also'; acute on the first syllable by* yato 'nāvaḥ*, together with the accent of the last member of a compound ending in a* kṛt*);* sāsahvān *(root* ṣah 'to overcome', *kvasu* for *liṭ*; Vedic lengthening of the reduplicative syllable);* amitrān *(*na* + *mitra*; acute on the second member by *nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ*);* sanīḷebhiḥ *(*sa* for *samāna* by *samānasya chandasi*).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*sūnubhir na* — (his own) as if together with sons; *rudrebhiḥ* — with the Maruts, sons of Rudra; *ṛbhvā* — the great one; *saḥ* — Indra; *nṛṣāhye* — in the battle that is to be faced by men; *amitrān* — the enemies; *sasahvān* — he who overcame [them]; (and) *sanīḷebhiḥ* — together with the Maruts who dwell in the same abode with him; *śravasyāni* — the waters that are the root cause of food; *tūrvan* — causing [them] to pour down from the clouds; *marutvān* — joined with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may [he] be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"The great Indra, joined with the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, as if with his own sons, with pride, overcame his enemies in the battle that is to be faced by men, and protected his devotees, men. And, making fall from the clouds the waters that are the root cause of food, together with the Maruts who dwell with him in his own abode — may that Indra, together with the Maruts, be the one who brings about our protection."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Mighty with the Rudras, as if with his sons, victorious in battle over his enemies, and sending down with his co-dwellers (the waters which are productive of) food ; Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

"*Rudrebhiḥ* — *rudraputrair marudbhiḥ*: with the Maruts who are the sons of Rudra. That the Maruts are the sons of Rudra is well known from the Śruti."

> रुद्रो यद्वो मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसो वृषाजनि पृश्न्याः शुक्र ऊधनि ।
> *rudro yad vo maruto rukmavakṣaso vṛṣājani pṛśnyāḥ śukra ūdhani |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-34-2 as read [?])

"— as said in this Ṛk, the story that the Maruts were born to Rudra as sons, in Pṛśni, is well known; so, whenever they are addressed, this epithet is used most often. In explaining this Ṛk, Sāyaṇācārya tells another story as well:"

> पृश्निर्नानावर्णा इयं भूमिः पुरा गोरूपधरासीत् । तस्यां महेशो वृषो भूत्वा मरुत उत्पादयामासेत्याचक्षते ॥
> *pṛśnir nānāvarṇā iyaṃ bhūmiḥ purā gorūpadharāsīt | tasyāṃ maheśo vṛṣo bhūtvā maruta utpādayām āsety ācakṣate ‖*
> (Sāyaṇa's commentary on *Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-34-2)

"— that this many-coloured earth formerly took the form of a cow, and Maheśa [Rudra], becoming a bull, begot the Maruts in her: so Sāyaṇa has shown the relation of father and sons between Rudra and the Maruts. And the story told in the Ṛk 2-34-2 above is also told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā; so he has cited the sentence from there:"

> पृश्न्यै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः ।
> *pṛśnyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ |*
> (*Tai. Saṃ.* 2-2-11-4 as read [?])

"— and for this reason in many places the Maruts are addressed as Rudra's sons. For example —"

> प्र ये शुम्भन्ते जनयो न सप्तयो यामन्रुद्रस्य सूनवः सुदंससः ।
> *pra ye śumbhante janayo na saptayo yāman rudrasya sūnavaḥ sudaṃsasaḥ |*

> इदं पित्रे मरुतामुच्यते वचः स्वादोः स्वादीयो रुद्राय वर्धनम् ।

> *idaṃ pitre marutām ucyate vacaḥ svādoḥ svādīyo rudrāya vardhanam | rāsvā ca no amṛta martabhojanaṃ tmane tokāya tanayāya mṛḷa ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-114-6 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "Who adorn themselves like women [or: like steeds], the sons of Rudra, the skilful, on their way"; "This word is spoken for the father of the Maruts, sweeter than the sweet, a [word] that strengthens Rudra: and give us, O immortal, mortals' food; be gracious to ourselves, our child, our offspring".)*

> […कामय]मानातपसा [read: कामयमाना तपसा] भर्तुः सकाशाद्गर्भं लेभे । इमं वृत्तान्तमवगच्छन्निन्द्रो वज्रहस्तः सन् सूक्ष्मरूपो भूत्वा तस्या उदरं प्रविश्य तं गर्भं सप्तधा बिभेद । पुनरप्येकैकं सप्तखण्डमकरोत् । ते सर्वे गर्भैकदेशायोर्निर्गत्य [?] आरुदन् । एतस्मिन्नवसरे लीलार्थं गच्छन्तौ पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ इमान् ददृशतुः । महेशं प्रति पार्वती एवमुवाच । इमे मांसखण्डा यथा प्रत्येकं पुत्राः सम्पद्येरन्नेवं त्वया कार्यं मयि चेत्प्रीतिरस्तीति । स च महेश्वरस्तान् समानरूपान् समानवयसः समानालंकारान् पुत्रान् कृत्वा गौर्यै प्रददौ केवेमे [?] पुत्राः सन्तीति । अतः सर्वेषु मारुतेषु सूक्तेषु मरुतो रुद्रपुत्रा इति स्तूयन्ते । रौद्रेषु च मरुतां पिता रुद्र इति ।
> *[…kāmaya]mānā tapasā bhartuḥ sakāśād garbhaṃ lebhe | imaṃ vṛttāntam avagacchann indro vajrahastaḥ san sūkṣmarūpo bhūtvā tasyā udaraṃ praviśya taṃ garbhaṃ saptadhā bibheda | punar apy ekaikaṃ saptakhaṇḍam akarot | te sarve garbhaikadeśāyor [?] nirgatya āruadan | etasminn avasare līlārthaṃ gacchantau pārvatīparameśvarau imān dadṛśatuḥ | maheśaṃ prati pārvatī evam uvāca | ime māṃsakhaṇḍā yathā pratyekaṃ putrāḥ sampadyerann evaṃ tvayā kāryaṃ mayi cet prītir astīti | sa ca maheśvaras tān samānarūpān samānavayasaḥ samānālaṃkārān putrān kṛtvā gauryai pradadau keveme [?] putrāḥ santīti | ataḥ sarveṣu māruteṣu sūkteṣu maruto rudraputrā iti stūyante | raudreṣu ca marutāṃ pitā rudra iti |*
> (Sāyaṇa's commentary on *Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-114-6)

*(Reading note:* āruadan *above stands for the print's* āruden*, i.e.* arudan *'they wept' [?]; the words* garbhaikadeśāyor *and* keveme *are clotted in print.)*

"Once in former times Indra conquered the Asuras. Then Diti, the mother of the Asuras, wishing to obtain a son able to kill Indra, performed austerities and, by the favour of her husband, conceived. Indra, learning of this, took the thunderbolt in his hand, became of subtle form, entered her womb, and split the embryo into seven parts; and again he made each one into seven pieces. They all came out from one part of the womb and wept. At that time Pārvatī and Parameśvara, who were going about in sport, saw them; and Pārvatī, moved with compassion, begged Maheśvara to make all of them into children. Then Īśvara made them all of one form, of one age, with the same ornaments, as sons, and gave them to her, saying 'these are your sons'. Therefore in all the Marut-sūktas the Maruts are praised as sons of Rudra, and in the Rudra-sūktas Rudra is spoken of as father of the Maruts: so Sāyaṇa tells this story.

*Sūnubhir na* — 'as if together with his own sons': so the love between Indra and the Maruts is suggested. The nature of the established companionship between Indra and the Maruts was explained in detail in the explanation of the first Ṛk of this sūkta.

*Ṛbhvā* — for the word *ṛbhvan* the Nirukta-author, explaining *Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-120-6 (*Ni.* 11-31 as read [?]), says '*urubhūtam mahattvāt svarūpavat*' [as read, ?] — 'one who has the nature of vastness'; Sāyaṇa too gives the meaning *mahān*, 'great': the sense is, the great Indra. This epithet has also been used where the sense 'shining exceedingly' is to be given. For example —"

### Page 195 (PDF 215)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 195.)*

> दक्षं महे पाययते हिरण्ययं रथमावृत्या हरियोगमृभ्वसम् ।
> *dakṣaṃ mahe pāyayate hiraṇyayaṃ rathaṃ āvṛtyā hariyogam ṛbhvasam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-56-1 as read [?])

"— in contexts such as these, for the word *ṛbhvasam* the sense is *urubhāsamānam*, 'shining greatly, exceedingly'. In sum, the meaning is 'the great one'.

*Nṛṣāhye* — *puruṣaiḥ soḍhavye saṃgrāme*: in the battle that is to be endured by men; that is, in a battle that shows the power to withstand the onsets of enemies, by men.

*Sanīḷebhiḥ* — since *gayaḥ, kṛdaraḥ, garta* and the like are read among the twenty-two names of house (*Ni.* 3-[?]3 as read [?]), the word *nīḷa* means 'house'. Since the Maruts always dwell together, the sense is, 'those who have one abode'. This epithet is generally used when the Maruts are addressed. For example —"

> कया शुभा सवयसः सनीळाः समान्या मरुतः सं मिमिक्षुः ।
> *kayā śubhā savayasaḥ sanīḷāḥ samānyā marutaḥ saṃ mimikṣuḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-165-1 as read [?])

> क ईं व्यक्ता नरः सनीळा रुद्रस्य मर्या अधा स्वश्वाः ।
> *ka īṃ vyaktā naraḥ sanīḷā rudrasya maryā adhā svaśvāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-3[3?]-1 as read [?])

"— in all such Ṛks the dwelling of the Maruts in one abode is described by '*sanīḷāḥ*'. *Sanīḷebhiḥ* means 'with the Maruts who dwell in one abode'.

*Śravasyāni* — *śrava* is a name for food [as the print's *srava ity anna nāma* is read, ?]; *taddhetubhūtāny udakāni*: the waters that are the cause of food and are of the form of rain.

*Tūrvan* — *meghāt pracyāvayan*: making [the waters] pour from the cloud."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.5)** *(grammar pages, pp. 195–196, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *rudrebhiḥ* (*rudra* + *bhis*; the substitution *ais* does not come, by *bahulaṃ chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; *e* by *bahuvacane jhaly et* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-103 as read]; *s* → *ru* → visarga); *nṛṣāhye* (root *saha marṣaṇe*; *ṣ* for the initial *s* by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-64 as read]; *yat* in the passive by *śakisahoś ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-99 as read]; lengthening of the root's *a* in the Saṃhitā by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 as read]; *nṛbhiḥ sāhyaḥ nṛṣāhyaḥ*; the acute on the first syllable that *yato 'nāvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-213 as read] would give is replaced by the accent of the last member of a *kṛt*-ended compound with a *kāraka* first member, by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; locative singular).

### Page 196 (PDF 216)

*(Running head: left 196; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

The grammar of Rik 100.5 continues: *sāsahvān* (root *ṣah abhibhave*; *kvasu* for *liṭ* by *kvasuś ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-107 as read]; doubling of the root; *ādihalśeṣa*; Vedic lengthening of the reduplicative syllable; acute on the affix; before *su* lengthening of the penult by *atvasantasya* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-14 as read]; *num* because the affix is *ugit*, by *ugidacāṃ sarvanāmasthāne 'dhātoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-70 as read]; the loss of the final consonant of the cluster is treated as not having happened, so *n* is not lost); *amitrān* (*mitrāṇi eṣu na santi*; the acute on the second member by *nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-116 as read]); *sanīḷebhiḥ* (*samānaṃ nīḷaṃ yeṣāṃ te sanīḷāḥ*; *sa* for *samāna* by *samānasya chandasy amūrdhaprabhṛtyudarkeṣu* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-84 as read]; *ais* does not arise, by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *e*); *tūrvan* (root *turvī hiṃsārthe*, *bhvādi*; *śatṛ* in the sense of the present; the penult lengthened because it ends in *r*; *śap*; the single substitute *a* by *ato guṇe* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-97 as read]; the *lasārvadhātuka* accent being the low one after a root with *a*-initial *upadeśa*, by *tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 as read], the root keeps its own accent; *num* before the nominative *su* since the affix is *ugit*, and, as before, the loss of *t* is treated as not having happened so that *n* is not lost; the form *tūrvan*). The Rik is closed with *‖ 5 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

*sa manyumīḥ samadanasya kartāsmākebhir nṛbhiḥ sūryaṃ sanat | asminn ahan satpatiḥ puruhūto marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖ 6 ‖*

### Page 197 (PDF 217)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 197.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 100.6)**

> सः । मन्युऽमीः । सऽमदनस्य । कर्ता । अस्माकेभिः । नृऽभिः । सूर्यम् । सनत् ।
> अस्मिन् । अहन् । सत्ऽपतिः । पुरुऽहूतः । मरुत्वान् । नः । भवतु । इन्द्रः । ऊती ॥ ६ ॥

*saḥ | manyu-mīḥ | sa-madanasya | kartā | asmākebhiḥ | nṛ-bhiḥ | sūryam | sanat | asmin | ahan | sat-patiḥ | puru-hūtaḥ | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.6)**

> शत्रुभिरपहृतासु गोषु तैः सह युद्धार्थं विनिर्गता ऋज्राश्वादयोऽनेन सूक्तेनेन्द्रमस्तुवन् । स इन्द्रो मन्युमीर्मन्योः कोपस्य निर्माता [?] । यद्वा । अभिमन्यमानस्य शत्रोर्हिंसकः । अपि च समदनस्य संग्रामस्य कर्ता । सत्पतिः सतां पालयिता । पुरुहूतो बहुभिर्यजमानैराहूतः । एवंगुणविशिष्टः स अस्मिन्नहन् अस्मिन् दिनेऽस्माकेभिरस्मदीयैर्नृभिः पुरुषैः सूर्यं सूर्यप्रकाशं सनत् सम्भक्तं करोतु । शत्रुपुरुषैस्तु वृष्टिनिरोधकमन्धकारं संयोजयतु । स च मरुत्वानिन्द्रोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥
> *śatrubhir apahṛtāsu goṣu taiḥ saha yuddhārthaṃ vinirgatā ṛjrāśvādayo 'nena sūktenendram astuvan | sa indro manyumīr manyoḥ kopasya nirmātā [?] | yadvā | abhimanyamānasya śatror hiṃsakaḥ | api ca samadanasya saṃgrāmasya kartā | satpatiḥ satāṃ pālayitā | puruhūto bahubhir yajamānair āhūtaḥ | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭaḥ sa asminn ahan asmin dine 'smākebhir asmadīyair nṛbhiḥ puruṣaiḥ sūryaṃ sūryaprakāśaṃ sanat sambhaktaṃ karotu | śatrupuruṣais tu vṛṣṭinirodhakam andhakāraṃ saṃyojayatu | sa ca marutvān indro 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖*

"When their cows had been carried off by enemies, Ṛjrāśva and the others, having set out to fight those [enemies], praised Indra with this sūkta. That Indra is *manyumīḥ* — the one who brings about [or: measures out] wrath; or, the destroyer of an enemy who is behaving with arrogance (*abhimanyamāna*). And he is the maker (*kartā*) of *samadana*, of battle; *satpatiḥ* — the protector of the good; *puruhūtaḥ* — called by many sacrificers. Being endowed with such qualities, *asminn ahan* — this day — may he make *sūryam*, the light of the sun, to be shared (*sanat*) by our men (*asmākebhiḥ nṛbhiḥ*); but may he join the enemy men to the darkness that holds back rain [print's wording, as read]. And may that Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be for our protection."

**Bhāṣya's grammatical tail (characterized, partly transcribed)**

> *manyumīḥ | manyuṃ mināti iti manyumīḥ | mīñ hiṃsāyām | kvip | samadanasya | saha mādyanty asminn iti samadanaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ | madī harṣe | adhikaraṇe lyuṭ | sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām | Pā. 6-3-78 [?] | iti sabhāvaḥ | asmākebhiḥ | tasminn aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau [?] … asmacchabdasyāsmākādeśaḥ | saṃjñāpūrvakasya vidher anityatvād aisyaiṣyabhāvaḥ [?] | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisabhāvaḥ | [clotted citation] ity udāhṛtaḥ | sanat | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | ahan | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā luk | satpatiḥ | patyāvaiśvarye iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam ‖*

*(Characterized: the stem* manyumī *('one who destroys wrath/the arrogant', root* mī *'to injure', with* kvip*);* samadana *(*saha mādyanty asmin*, 'where they rejoice together', = battle; root* mad *'to rejoice' with* lyuṭ *in the locus;* sa *for* saha *by* sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām *[Pā. ### Page 198 (PDF 218)

*(Running head: left 198; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha of Rik 100.6, concluded from p. 197 (Kannada)**

"[*sūryam* —] the light [of the sun]; *sanat* — may he join [it] (may he give us light and make darkness for the enemies' share); *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"May Indra — who makes his fierce anger manifest and destroys his enemies, who is the maker of battle, the protector of the good, the one called for help by many sacrificers — on this day give the light of the sun to all who are with us, and make darkness for the share of our enemies; and, together with the Maruts, be for our protection."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> May he, the repressor of (hostile) wrath, the author of war, the protector of the good, the invoked of many, share with our people on this day the (light of the) sun : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.6 (Kannada)**

"*Manyumīḥ* —"

> मन्युर्मन्यतेर्दीप्तिकर्मणः क्रोधकर्मणो वधकर्मणो वा ।
> *manyur manyater dīptikarmaṇaḥ krodhakarmaṇo vadhakarmaṇo vā |*
> (*Ni.* 10-29 as read [?])

"— from the root *man*, the word *manyu* acquires the meanings 'to shine', 'to be angry', or 'to kill'. [Sāyaṇa gives for] *manyumīḥ*: '*manoḥ kopasya nirmātā*, *abhimanyamānasya śatror hiṃsakaḥ*': 'one who makes anger manifest, or one who destroys an enemy who is in a rage'. Skandasvāmin says:"

> अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । प्रजापतेः पुत्रो मन्युर्नाम । तं प्रजापतिः सेनापत्ये नियुक्तवान् । तेन सहेन्द्रो निजघान इति ।
> *atrétihāsam ācakṣate | prajāpateḥ putro manyur nāma | taṃ prajāpatiḥ senāpatye niyuktavān | tena sahendro nijaghāna iti |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: here they tell the tale: the son of Prajāpati, named Manyu; Prajāpati appointed him as commander; with his help Indra slew the foes.] Thus he tells the story, and explains *manyumīḥ* as 'one who killed with the help of Manyu'. [The Śruti itself shows that] Manyu, who is the son of Prajāpati, stands in a most close relation to Indra; the story of Manyu, how he was changed into Rudra, is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:"

> प्रजापतेर्विस्रस्ताद्देवता उदक्रामन्त्स्मैक एव [?] देवो नाजहान्मन्युरेव सोऽस्मिन्नन्तर्वर्तितोऽतिष्ठत्सोऽरोदीत्तस्य यान्यश्रूणि प्रास्कन्दंस्तान्यस्मिन्नो [?] प्रत्यतिष्ठत् [?] स एव शतशीर्षा रुद्रः समभवत् सहस्राक्षः शतेषुधिः ।
> *prajāpater visrastād devatā udakrāman smaika eva [?] devo nājahān manyur eva so 'smin antarvartito 'tiṣṭhat so 'rodīt tasya yāny aśrūṇi prāskandaṃs tāny asminno [?] pratyatiṣṭhat [?] sa eva śataśīrṣā rudraḥ samabhavat sahasrākṣaḥ śateṣudhiḥ |*
> (*Śat. Brā.* 9-1-1-6 as read [?]; several words clotted in print [?])

### Page 199 (PDF 219)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 199.)*

"When Prajāpati had become weak, all the other deities abandoned him; only the deity named Manyu did not leave him but stayed with him, close beside him. Then Prajāpati wept; and when the tears fell on Manyu, he became Rudra with a hundred heads, a thousand eyes and a hundred quivers: so the story goes. By this it is known that Manyu is bold and valorous in battle. (But it does not say that he is a son of Prajāpati.) The close relation between this deity called Manyu and Indra is known from a sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā —"

> इन्द्राश्रयस्तु पर्जन्यो रुद्रो वायुर्बृहस्पतिः । वरुणः कश्च मृत्युश्च देवश्च ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ॥
> मन्युश्च विश्वकर्मा च मित्रः क्षेत्रपतिर्यमः ।
> *indrāśrayas tu parjanyo rudro vāyur bṛhaspatiḥ | varuṇaḥ kaś ca mṛtyuś ca devaś ca brahmaṇaspatiḥ ‖ manyuś ca viśvakarmā ca mitraḥ kṣetrapatir yamaḥ |*
> (*Bṛ. De.* 8-93–95 as read [?])

"— so the Bṛhaddevatā says that Manyu and the other deities [listed] are *indrāśraya*, 'resting in Indra'. Quoting this Ṛk-saṃhitā sentence [*sic*, as printed], [the Nirukta-author] has followed the sentence of the Nirukta-author (*Ni.* 10-29 as read [?]) that gives the derivation of the word *manyu*. The Nirukta-author, citing the Ṛk"

> त्वया मन्यो सरथमारुजन्तो हर्षमाणासो धृषिता मरुत्वः ।
> तिग्मेषव आयुधा संशिशाना अभि प्र यन्तु नरो अग्निरूपाः ॥
> *tvayā manyo sarathām ārujanto harṣamāṇāso dhṛṣitā marutvaḥ | tigmeṣava āyudhā saṃśiśānā abhi pra yantu naro agnirūpāḥ ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-84-1 as read [?])

"— has shown that Indra and the other deities conquered their enemies with the help of Manyu. In the present context also *manyumīḥ* means 'one who destroyed enemies with Manyu's help'.

*Samadanasya* — since *raṇaḥ, vivāk, vikhādaḥ* and the like are read among the [forty-six, as read, ?] names of battle (*Ni.* 2-[?] as read [?]), the meaning is 'of battle'. When the Nirukta-author derives the word *samat*, citing the Ṛk"

> चित्रो यदभ्राट् श्वेतो [print: छ्वेतो] न विक्षु रथो न रुक्मी त्वेषः समत्सु ।
> *citro yad abhrāṭ śveto [print: chveto] na vikṣu ratho na rukmī tveṣaḥ samatsu |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-66-6 as read [?])

"— he has said that the word *samat* has the meaning 'battle'. The word *samadana* is a synonym of the word *samat*. Because Indra, even at his birth, manifested the aspects of the war-deity, and afterwards fought and destroyed all the Asuras, he is praised as the maker of battle."

"*Sūryaṃ sanat*" —

> *sūryasya hi yāgādikarmanivṛttiḥ phalam | asmadīyaiḥ ṛtvigbhiḥ saha devatātmatvam āpannaḥ indraḥ sūryodayaphalabhūtam asmadīyaṃ yogaṃ nirvartayatv ity arthaḥ |*
> (as printed, a short Sanskrit gloss; read as given [?])

"— the completion of the sacrificial acts, the *yāga* and the rest, is indeed the fruit of the [rising of the] sun. [The sense is:] may Indra, who has attained the nature of a deity together with our priests, bring about for us that sacrifice which has the sunrise as its fruit. For the performance of the *yāga* and the other acts is the result of the sun's rising, and so, for the completion of those rites, the prayer is that Indra give us the light of the sun and bring our rites to completion with all their parts."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.6)** *(grammar pages, pp. 200–201, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *manyumīḥ* (*manyuṃ mināti*; root *mīñ hiṃsāyām*; *kvip* by *kvip ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read]; since the first member is a *kāraka*, the accent of the last member by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; nominative singular); *samadanasya* (*saha mādyanty asmin iti samadanaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ*; root *madī harṣe*; *lyuṭ* in the locus; *ana* for *yu* by *yuvoranākau* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; *sa* for *saha* by *sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-78 as read]; the syllable before the affix is acute because the affix is *lit*, by *liti* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 as read]; genitive); *kartā* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *tṛc* in the agent; final acute by *citaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]); *asmākebhiḥ* (*asmākaṃ sambandhinaḥ asmākāḥ*; *aṇ* in the sense of 'connected with'; *asmāka* for *asmad* by *tasmin aṇi ca yuṣmākāsmākau* [Pā. Sū. 4-3-2 as read]; the *vṛddhi* that *aṇ* would cause does not arise, since a rule that depends on a name is not invariable [*saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*, Paribhāṣā 93 as read]; *asmāka* + *bhis*: *ais* does not come, by *bahulaṃ chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; the accent rule for this is stated at the place *prāsmākāsaś ca sūrayaḥ* [*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-97-3 as read [?]]); *sanat* (root *vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau*; *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; loss of the final *i* by *itaś ca lopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-97 as read]; *aṭ* by *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; *nighāta*); *ahan* (the locative ending dropped by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]).

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.7)**

> तमिन्द्रं शूरसातौ शूरैर्वीरपुरुषैः सम्भजनीये संग्रामे ऊतयो गन्तारो मरुतो रणयन् । रमयन्ति । यद्वा प्रहर भगवो जहि वीरयस्वेत्येवंरूपं शब्दमिन्द्रमुद्दिश्य कुर्वन्ति । अपि च क्षितयो मनुष्यास्तमिन्द्रं क्षेमस्य रक्षणीयस्य सर्वस्य धनस्य त्रां त्रातारं रक्षितारं कृण्वत । कुर्वन्ति । देवतान्तरादस्य कोऽतिशय इति चेदुच्यते । स इन्द्रो विश्वस्य सर्वस्य करुणस्याभिमतफलनिष्पादनरूपस्य कर्मण एकोऽसहाय एवेशे । ईष्टे । अन्यत्पूर्ववत् ॥
> *tam indraṃ śūrasātau śūrair vīrapuruṣaiḥ sambhajanīye saṃgrāme ūtayo gantāro maruto raṇayan | ramayanti | yadvā prahara bhagavo jahi vīrayasvety evaṃrūpaṃ śabdam indram uddiśya kurvanti | api ca kṣitayo manuṣyās tam indraṃ kṣemasya rakṣaṇīyasya sarvasya dhanasya trāṃ trātāraṃ rakṣitāraṃ kṛṇvata | kurvanti | devatāntarād asya ko 'tiśaya iti ced ucyate | sa indro viśvasya sarvasya karuṇasyābhimataphalaniṣpādanarūpasya karmaṇa eko 'sahāya eveśe | īṣṭe | anyat pūrvavat ‖*

"Him, Indra, in the *śūrasātau* — in the battle in which heroic men take part — the Maruts, who come as helpers (*ūtayaḥ*, 'those who go'), *raṇayan* — delight; or they utter, addressing Indra, cries of the kind 'strike, Lord! kill! show your valour!'. And the people, *kṣitayaḥ* — men — make that Indra *trām* — the protector, the guardian — of *kṣemasya*, of all wealth that is to be preserved. If it be asked what excellence he has over another deity, it is answered: that Indra *viśvasya karuṇasya* — of all work, which consists in bringing about the fruit that is wished for — alone, without a helper, is lord (*īśe*, 'he rules'). The rest is as before."

*(Characterized: the stem* ūti *from the root* av *'to go', with* ktin *in the agent by* kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam*, the augment* iṭ *barred, and* ūṭ *for the* v *and the penultimate syllable by* jvaratvara…*, the accent fixed by* ūtiyūtijūti…*; or with* ktic*;* raṇayan *(root* ram *with the causative* ṇic*, the Vedic* laṅ *in the present sense; or from the root* raṇ *'to sound');* trām *(root* trai *'to protect', with* kvip*, which applies even without a prefix by the word* ca *drawing in* dṛśi*);* karuṇa *(root* ḍukṛñ *with* unan *by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. **॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*taṃ* — that Indra; *śūrasātau* — at the time of battle fought with heroes; *ūtayaḥ* — the Maruts who go about for help; *raṇayan* — [they] rejoice, with sounds that suggest victory; *kṣitayaḥ* — men; *taṃ* — that Indra; *kṣemasya* — of their wealth that is to be protected; *trām* — as the protector; *kṛṇvata* — have made [him]; *saḥ* — that Indra; *viśvasya karuṇasya* — (of the rites that bring about the desired objects) of all rites; *ekaḥ* — he alone; *īśe* — is lord; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"At the time of fighting with heroes, the Maruts, who go along with that Indra for his help, make sounds that suggest victory and rejoice. Men make that Indra the protector of their wealth. That Indra alone is the lord of all the rites that bring about the desired objects. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

### Page 203 (PDF 223)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 203.)*

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Him, his allies, the Maruts, animate in battle ; him, men regard as the preserver of their property ; he alone presides over every act of worship : may Indra, associated with the Maruts be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.7 (Kannada)**

"*Śūrasātau* — *śūrair vīrapuruṣaiḥ sambhajanīye saṃgrāme*: in a battle in which heroic men take part; that is, a battle that heroic men enter into with eagerness.

*Ūtayaḥ* — the Maruts, who have come to help.

*Raṇayan* — *ramayanti*: they delight, they cause delight; or they make a sound that suggests exultation. On the basis of the root meaning 'delightful', the word *raṇa* is also a synonym for battle. Even there, the idea that, when Indra and the Maruts, helping one another, enter the battlefield together, it must be delightful, is shown by the Ṛk"

> मरुत्वाँ इन्द्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय ।
> *marutvāṃ indra vṛṣabho raṇāya pibā somam anuṣvadhaṃ madāya |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-47-1 as read [?])

"— and for the word *raṇāya* in this Ṛk, [Sāyaṇa] has given *ramaṇīyāya saṃgrāmāya*, 'for the delightful battle': an apt meaning for the word. That the Maruts, whether in the sacrificial house or in the field of battle, make their delightful sounds is described in many places. For example —"

> रराणता मरुतो वेद्याभिर्नि हेळो धत्त वि मुचध्वमश्वान् ।
> *rarāṇatā maruto vedyābhir ni heḷo dhatta vi mucadhvam aśvān |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-171-1 as read [?])

> कृते चिदत्र मरुतो रणन्तानवद्यासः शुचयः पावकाः ।
> *kṛte cid atra maruto raṇantānavadyāsaḥ śucayaḥ pāvakāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* [5?]-52-3 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "Rejoice, O Maruts, with the altar-offerings; set down [your] wrath, unyoke the horses"; "Here, at the rite, O Maruts, the blameless, bright, purifying ones rejoice".)*

"— in many Ṛks like these the Maruts are described as showing their joy, in the sacrificial house, by their delightful sound. In the same way —"

> मरुतो ह वै क्रीडिनो वृत्रं हनिष्यन्तमिन्द्रमागतं तमभितः परिचिक्रीडुर्मर्हयन्तस्तथो एवैतं पाप्मानं द्विषन्तं भ्रातृव्यं हनिष्यन्तमभितः परिक्रीडन्ते ।
> *maruto ha vai krīḍino vṛtraṃ haniṣyantam indram āgataṃ tam abhitaḥ paricikrīḍur marhayantas tatho evaitaṃ pāpmānaṃ dviṣantaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ haniṣyantam abhitaḥ parikrīḍante |*
> (*Śat. Brā.* 2-5-3-10 as read [?])

*(Gloss, mine and tentative: "The Maruts, the playful, played all around Indra, who had come to slay Vṛtra, honouring him; so, indeed, they play around the one who is about to slay this evil, the hating rival".)*

### Page 204 (PDF 224)

*(Running head: left 204; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

"— so, at the time of the slaying of Vṛtra, the Maruts, being Indra's companions, showed their joy and played; and in the same way it is described that they do so in the sacrificial house. This kind of *raṇana* ('sounding in joy') is natural to the Maruts, and so the same is described here.

*Kṣitayaḥ* — *manuṣyāḥ*: since *naraḥ* and the rest are read among the twenty-five [as read, ?] names of man, the sense is 'men' (*Ni.* 2-[2?] as read [?])."

> अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋतावा ।
> *agnir netā bhaga iva kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ deva ṛtupā ṛtāvā |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-20-4 as read [?])

"— in such places, to show the difference between men and the subjects connected with the gods, by the word *kṣiti* it is suggested that the subjects of the earth are men.

*Karuṇasya* — since *apaḥ, apnaḥ, daṃsaḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-six [as read, ?] names of action (*Ni.* 2-1 as read [?]), the sense is 'of action'. Since Indra is the lord in all actions, protection of the action is asked of him; since, at every step, obstacles come to the action from the Asuras and the like, and by destroying those Asuras he is himself the chief protector in carrying the action through."

> इन्द्रो वै यज्ञस्य देवता ।
> *indro vai yajñasya devatā |*
> (*Śat. Brā.* 1-4-1-[3?]2 as read [?])

> इन्द्राय विमृधेऽनुनिर्वपति सेन्द्रो मे यज्ञोऽसदिति सर्वो वै यज्ञ इन्द्रस्यैव ।
> *indrāya vimṛdhe 'nunirvapati sendro me yajño 'sad iti sarvo vai yajña indrasyaiva |*
> (*Śat. Brā.* 11-1-3-4 as read [?])

"— in many places such as these Indra is praised as the chief lord of the sacrifice. Not only by the destruction of the Asuras: since the rain, so essential to the sacrifice, must be obtained by Indra's favour, Indra is the chief lord of the sacrifice. Skandasvāmin explains this point: '*sarvakarmaṇāṃ vṛṣṭinibandhanatvāt vṛṣṭeś ca kevalendrāyattatvāt*' [as read, ?] — since rain is the basis of all rites, and rain depends on Indra alone, [the carrying out of] all rites must come by rain, and since Indra himself is the one who makes rain, he alone is lord of the rites."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.7)** *(grammar pages, pp. 204–205, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *ūtayaḥ* (a *ktin*-ending noun fixed by *nipātana*, with its accent, by *ūtiyūtijūti…* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 as read]; the root *av rakṣaṇe*, used here in the sense of going; *ktin* in the agent by *bahulam* under *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-113 as read]; the prohibition of *iṭ* [a rule beginning *śri-…*, as read, Pā. Sū. 7-2-[9?]]; the root's *v* and its penultimate vowel become *ūṭ*, by *jvaratvarasrivyavimavām upadhāyāś ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-20 as read], giving *ūti*; or *ktic* in the agent by *ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-174 as read], with the advantage that no appeal to *nipātana* is needed; acute on the last syllable because the affix is *cit*; nominative plural).

Sū. 6-4-92 as read]; the Vedic *laṅ* in the present sense by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-6 as read]; third person plural, *jhi* replaced by *anta* [ending]; loss of the *i* by *itaś ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-100 as read]; *śap* the *vikaraṇa*; *guṇa* of *ṇic* and the *ay*-substitution; loss of the final *t* of the ending by *saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-23 as read]; no *aṭ*, by *bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 as read]; the *ṇ* for the *m* of the root is Vedic; or the root *raṇa śabdārthe* with *ṇic* and *laṅ* as before; *nighāta* accent); *śūrasātau* (*śūraiḥ sātiḥ*, in it; the first member keeps its accent in the compound with a third-case first member by *tṛtīyā karmaṇi* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; nominative plural); *kṛṇvata* (root *kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayoś ca*; Vedic *laṅ* in the present sense; third person plural, *jhi*; the *ātādeśa* by *ātmanepadeṣv anataḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-5 as read]; the *vikaraṇa* *u* by *dhinvikṛṇvyor a* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-80 as read]; *a*-ending of the root; loss of the *a* by *ato lopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; *yaṇ* for the *u*; *nighāta*; no *aṭ*, by *bahulaṃ chandasi*); *trām* (root *traiṅ pālane*; *trāyata iti trāḥ*; *kvip* by *kvip ca* [Pā. *(Running head: left 206; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

The grammar of Rik 100.7 concludes: *trām* (*ā* for *e* by *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-45 as read]; accusative singular); *karuṇasya* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; the affix *unan* in the sense of the action by *kyavṛtyādāribhya unan* [Uṇ. Sū. 3-53, read in print as 3-[?]3, ?]; *guṇa* of the root vowel because of the affix; *raparatva* by *uraṇ raparaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 1-1-51 as read]; the *ṇ* of the affix by *āṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi* [Pā. Sū. 8-4-2 as read]; the first-syllable acute that *nit* gives is made to stand by *vyatyayo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read], in the print's words, 'if another accent were attained'); *īśe* (root *īśa aiśvarye*, *adādi*; *laṭ*, third person singular, *ta*; *e* by *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-79 as read]; loss of the *t* of the ending in the Veda by *lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-41 as read]; the form *īśe*; *nighāta* accent because it follows a non-verb). The Rik is closed with *‖ 7 ‖* and a rule of dashes.
