**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.8)**

> नरो नेतारः स्तोतारः शवसो बलस्य सम्बन्धिष्वुत्सवेषु संग्रामेषु नरं जयस्य नेतारं तमिन्द्रमप्सन्त । आप्नुवन्ति । किमर्थम् । अवसे । अन्नार्थं रक्षणार्थं वा । तथा धनाय धनार्थं च तमिन्द्रं प्राप्नुवन्ति । यस्मात्स इन्द्रस्तमसि दृष्टिप्रतिबन्धकेऽन्धे चित् आध्यानरहिते [?] चित्तव्यामोहकरेऽपि संग्रामे ज्योतिर्विजयलक्षणं प्रकाशं विदत् । लम्भयति । तस्मात्तमेव प्राप्नुवन्तीत्यर्थः । अप्सन्त । आप्ऌ व्याप्तौ । लङि व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । व्यत्ययेन क्नप्रत्ययः [?] । व्यत्ययेन धातोर्[?]त्वम् [?] । विदत् । विद्ऌ लाभे । छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्लिट इति वर्तमाने छान्दसो लुङ् । ऌदित्त्वाच्चेरङादेशः [?] । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः ॥
> *naro netāraḥ stotāraḥ śavaso balasya sambandhiṣv utsaveṣu saṃgrāmeṣu naraṃ jayasya netāraṃ tam indram apsanta | āpnuvanti | kimartham | avase | annārthaṃ rakṣaṇārthaṃ vā | tathā dhanāya dhanārthaṃ ca tam indraṃ prāpnuvanti | yasmāt sa indras tamasi dṛṣṭipratibandhake 'ndhe cit ādhyānarahite [?] cittavyāmohakare 'pi saṃgrāme jyotir vijayalakṣaṇaṃ prakāśaṃ vidat | lambhayati | tasmāt tam eva prāpnuvantīty arthaḥ | apsanta | āpḷ vyāptau | laṅi vyatyayenātmanepadam | vyatyayena knapratyayaḥ [?] | vyatyayena dhātor[?]tvam [?] | vidat | vidḷ lābhe | chandasi luṅlaṅliṭa iti vartamāne chāndaso luṅ | ḷdittvāc ceraṅādeśaḥ [?] | bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pīty aḍabhāvaḥ ‖*

"The men (*naraḥ*) — the leaders, the praisers — in the *utsavas* (battles) of *śavas*, of strength, *apsanta* — approach, obtain — that Indra, the man (*naram*), the leader to victory. For what? *Avase* — for food, or for protection. And likewise for wealth (*dhanāya*) they come to that Indra. Because that Indra, in the darkness (*tamasi*) that obstructs sight, in the blind (*andhe cit*) — even in a battle that is without clear thought, that causes confusion of mind — obtains [for them] *jyotiḥ*, the light that has the character of victory, he makes [them] attain: therefore they come to him alone — that is the sense."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized: the root* āp *'to attain' with the middle voice in the* laṅ *by* vyatyaya*, and two further* vyatyaya*-changes marked [?];* vidat *from the root* vid *'to obtain', with the Vedic* luṅ *in the present sense, and no augment* aṭ *by* bahulaṃ chandasi*. Several words are clotted and marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*saḥ* — Indra; *tamasi* — in the one that causes pitch darkness; *andhe cit* — and the one that causes mental confusion, [even in] a (dreadful) battle too; *jyotiḥ* — light in the form of victory; *vidat* — he causes [them] to obtain; *naraḥ* — the devotee-subjects; *śavasaḥ* — who must show valour; *utsaveṣu* — in battles; *naram* — the one who brings victory; *tam* — that Indra; *apsanta* — approach (take refuge in); *avase* — for food or for protection; *dhanāya* — for wealth also; *tam* — [that] Indra (they take refuge in); *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra, even in the dreadful battle that causes pitch darkness and mental confusion, gives the light that has the form of victory. The subjects who are his devotees approach that Indra who brings victory in battles that call for valour. And for food or for protection, and for wealth too, they take refuge in him. May Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

### Page 208 (PDF 228)

*(Running head: left 208; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**English Translation (as printed)**

> To him, a leader (to victory) his worshippers apply in contests of strength for protection and for wealth, as he grants them the light (of conquest) in the bewildering darkness (of battle) : may Indra, associated with the Maruts be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.8 (Kannada)**

"Two kinds of obstruction, which could not be withstood by the human sacrificers, were created by the Asuras at every step. The first was, by concealing the light of the world, to cause pitch darkness; the second was, by waging deceitful war, to cause confusion of mind in them. The chief thing was that these two came about. In such contexts, in order to help his devotees, Indra, standing straight in front of these deceivers, destroyed them by deceiving them with his own power of illusion, and, by spreading light, benefited the world; and that valorous deed is here described, with a suggestion of gratitude.

*Andhe cit* — *citravyāmohakare 'pi saṃgrāme*: even in a battle that causes confusion of mind; *jyotir vidat* — he grants the light of victory. As the Asuras' power of illusion is extremely strong, it is natural that any warrior, however brave, should be confused. In such contexts it is described, most fittingly, that Indra destroyed those Asuras and also deceived them beyond their own deceit."

> अहोहानम् [?] अप आशयानं प्र मायाभिर्मायिनं सक्षदिन्द्रः [?] ।

> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-30-6 as read [?]; the first word clotted in print, not completed from memory)

"— having overcome Vṛtra, who obstructs the deities and who is exceedingly deceitful, with his own power of illusion; and, when he struck, one fighter after another rose from his body, showing the fury of those who stand against Indra: the context too, in which it is described that even at such hard occasions Indra easily destroyed them all, uprooting them —"

> इन्द्रः स्वर्षा जनयन्नहानि जिगायोशिग्भिः पृतना अभिष्टिः ।
> प्रारोचयन्मनवे केतुमह्नामविन्दज्ज्योतिर्बृहते रणाय ॥
> *indraḥ svarṣā janayann ahāni jigāyośigbhiḥ pṛtanā abhiṣṭiḥ | prārocayan manave ketum ahnām avindaj jyotir bṛhate raṇāya ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-34-4 as read [?])

> स्वर्भानोरध यदिन्द्र माया अवो दिवो वर्तमाना अवाहन् ।
> गूळ्हं सूर्यं तमसापव्रतेन तुरीयेण ब्रह्मणाविन्ददत्रिः ॥
> *svarbhānor adha yad indra māyā avo divo vartamānā avāhan | gūḷhaṃ sūryaṃ tamasāpavratena turīyeṇa brahmaṇāvindad atriḥ ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-40-6 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "Indra, winning the heavenly light, bringing forth the days, conquered the battles with the eager ones; he made the banner of the days shine for man; he found the light for the great battle"; "Then, O Indra, you struck down the illusions of Svarbhānu that were working below the sky; Atri found the sun hidden in darkness with the fourth prayer".)*

"— the brilliance of the sun, which had been concealed by Asuras and others, Indra released, and gave light to all the worlds, earth, mid-air and the rest: so his greatness is praised.

*Utsaveṣu* — *saṃgrāmeṣu*, 'in battles'; *balavatām utsavabhūteṣu saṃgrāmeṣu*: in battles that are festivals for the strong. For the strong, battle itself is a source of enthusiasm: so it is counted as an *utsava*. Skandasvāmin gives one sense for *utsaveṣu* in this way, and another with *abhiṣaveṣu*. Explaining the second meaning, he says:"

> अथवा उत्सवेष्वित्युच्छब्द अभीत्येतस्य स्थाने । बलस्य सम्बन्धिष्वभिषवेषु । बलेन येषु यज्ञेष्वभिषूयन्ते सोमस्तेष्वित्यर्थः ।
> *athavā utsaveṣv ity ucchabda abhīty etasya sthāne | balasya sambandhiṣv abhiṣaveṣu | balena yeṣu yajñeṣv abhiṣūyante somas teṣv ity arthaḥ |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— in the word *utsaveṣu*, the syllable *ut* is in the place of *abhi*: 'in the pressings (*abhiṣava*) connected with strength'; the sacrifices in which Soma is pressed with strength: that is the sense."

*saḥ | savyena | yamati | vrādhataḥ | cit | saḥ | dakṣiṇe | saṃ-gṛbhītā | kṛtāni | saḥ | kīriṇā | cit | sanitā | dhanāni | marutvān | naḥ | bhavatu | indraḥ | ūtī ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.9)**

> स इन्द्रः सव्येन वामहस्तेनैकहस्तेन व्राधतश्चित् हिंसतो महतः शत्रोनपि यमति । नियमयति । तथा स इन्द्रो दक्षिणे दक्षिणपार्श्वस्थेन हस्तेनैकेन यजमानैः कृतानि हवींषि संगृभीता । संगृह्णाति । अपि च स इन्द्रः कीरिणा चित् कीर्तयित्रा स्तोत्रा स्तुतः सन् धनानि सनिता प्रदानशीलो भवति । हविष्मदात्रादामिव स्तोत्रादामपि धनं प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः । शिष्टं स्पष्टम् ॥ यमति । यमु उपरमे । णिच्चेमन्तः शत्संनित्वे [?] मितां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । छन्दस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वाणेरनिटीति णिलोपः । व्राधतः । व्रधु वृद्धौ । अस्मादतिप्रत्ययः । औणादिक आमागमश्च । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । सङ्गृभीता । ग्रह उपादाने । लिटि [?] बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । लिङः सलोप इति सलोपः [?] । ग्रहिज्यादिना सम्प्रसारणम् । हृग्रहोर्भ इति भत्वम् । द्व्यचोऽतस्तिङ इति दीर्घः । सनिता । षणु दाने । ताच्छीलिकस्तृन् । धनानि । न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठीप्रतिषेधः ॥
> *sa indraḥ savyena vāmahastenaikahastena vrādhataś cit hiṃsato mahataḥ śatroṇ api yamati | niyamayati | tathā sa indro dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇapārśvasthena hastenaikena yajamānaiḥ kṛtāni havīṃṣi saṃgṛbhītā | saṃgṛhṇāti | api ca sa indraḥ kīriṇā cit kīrtayitrā stotrā stutaḥ san dhanāni sanitā pradānaśīlo bhavati | haviṣmadātrād āmiva stotrād āmapi dhanaṃ prayacchatīty arthaḥ | śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam ‖ yamati | yamu uparame | ṇicce mantaḥ śatsaṃnitve [?] mitāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam | chandasy ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāṇ ṇer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | vrādhataḥ | vradhu vṛddhau | asmād atipratyayaḥ | auṇādika āmāgamaś ca | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttatvam | saṅgṛbhītā | graha upādāne | liṭi [?] bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | liṅaḥ salopa iti salopaḥ [?] | grahijyādinā samprasāraṇam | hṛgrahor bha iti bhatvam | dvyaco 'tastiṅa iti dīrghaḥ | sanitā | ṣaṇu dāne | tācchīlikas tṛn | dhanāni | na lokāvyayeti ṣaṣṭhīpratiṣedhaḥ ‖*

*(The print's* śatroṇ api *stands for* śatrūn api *[?]. The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the causative of* yam *'to restrain' with shortening of the penult by* mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*, loss of* ṇi *before an* ārdhadhātuka*;* vrādhat *(root* vradh *'to grow', with the affix* ati *and the Uṇādi augment* ām*, acute on the first syllable as belonging to the class* vṛṣādi*);* saṃgṛbhītā *(from* grah*, with the dropping of the* vikaraṇa*, the* samprasāraṇa *of* r *and the change of* h *to* bh*, and the lengthening by* dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ*);* sanitā *(root* ṣaṇu *'to give', with* tṛn *in the sense of habit); and the prohibition of the genitive by* na lokāvyaya*… in* dhanāni*. The words marked [?] are clotted.)*

"That Indra, with his *savyena* — left — hand, with that single hand, restrains (*yamati*, 'holds in check') even a mighty enemy who is harming (*vrādhataḥ cit*). And likewise that Indra, with one hand, the one on the right side (*dakṣiṇe*), *saṃgṛbhītā* — receives — the oblations made by the sacrificers. And also, when praised by the praiser (*kīriṇā cit*, 'by one who proclaims'), that Indra is *sanitā* — disposed to give — *dhanāni*, wealth: he gives wealth even to the praiser, as to a sacrificer who has oblations. The rest is clear."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)** *(begun at the foot of p. 211; continues on p. 212)*

"*saḥ* — that Indra; *savyena* — with the left hand; *vrādhataś cit* — even [an enemy] who is able to do harm, if he is a powerful one; *yamati* — [he] stops, holds back; *saḥ* — that same Indra; *dakṣiṇe* — with the right [hand]; *kṛtāni* — [havis] offered by the sacrificers —"

### Page 212 (PDF 232)

*(Running head: left 212; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

"— *saṃgṛbhītā* — accepts; (and) *saḥ* — Indra; *kīriṇā cit* — by the praiser, the devotee, praised; *dhanāni* — wealth; *sanitā* — becomes the giver; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"However strong the enemy who does harm, Indra stops him with his left hand alone. And with his right hand he accepts the oblations offered by the sacrificers. When he is praised by the devotee, he gives wealth to him. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> With his left hand he restrains the malignant, with his right he receives the (sacrificial) offerings ; he is the giver of riches, (when propitiated) by one who celebrates his praise : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.9 (Kannada)**

> तमूतयो रणयञ्छूरसातौ तं क्षेमस्य क्षितयः कृण्वत त्राम् ।
> स विश्वस्य करुणस्येश एको मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥
> *tam ūtayo raṇayañ chūrasātau taṃ kṣemasya kṣitayaḥ kṛṇvata trām | sa viśvasya karuṇasyeśa eko marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-100-7 as read — this is Rik 7 of the present sūkta, cited by the author)

"— as described in the preceding Ṛk, in the same way the greatness of Indra, who is at one and the same time the deity of war and the deity of sacrifice, is praised here as well. With one hand Indra can stop an enemy, however strong; with the other hand he accepts the oblations offered at the sacrifices; thereafter he gives wealth freely to his devotees: thus the manifold powers of Indra are described.

*Vrādhataś cit* — '*vrādhan*' is read among the names of *mahat*' — *mahato 'pi śatrūn* [Sāyaṇa]: as the bhāṣya-author says, *vrādhan* is read among the names of 'great'. In general the word *mahat* is used in the sense 'worshipful', 'honoured'. But since the epithet *vrādhan* is used mostly with reference to enemies, it comes to mean 'one with exceedingly great power'. It is unusual that this epithet should be applied to deities."

### Page 213 (PDF 233)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 12 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 213.)*

> इमे ये ते सु वायो बाह्वोजसोऽन्तर्नदी ते पतयन्त्युक्षणो महि व्राधन्त उक्षणः ।
> *ime ye te su vāyo bāhvojaso 'ntar nadī te patayanty ukṣaṇo mahi vrādhanta ukṣaṇaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-134-4 as read [?])

"— here the word *vrādhantaḥ*, as an adjective of the bulls of Vāyu, in *mahi vrādhante* means *atiprabhūtaṃ vardhamānāḥ*, 'growing in great abundance'. And —"

> स चन्द्रो विप्र मर्त्यो महो व्राधन्तमो दिवि ।
> *sa candro vipra martyo maho vrādhantamo divi |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-1[4?]0-3 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk it is an epithet that praises the greatness of the man who worships Agni. *Vrādhantamaḥ* — *pravṛddhatamaḥ | itaradevānām api śreṣṭhaḥ*: 'the most grown; the best even among other deities': that is, extremely excellent. Thus, apart from a couple of Ṛks, in all other places it is used as a synonym of 'enemy'."

> स व्राधतो नहुषो दंसुजूतः शर्धस्तरो नरां गूर्तश्रवाः ।
> *sa vrādhato nahuṣo daṃsujūtaḥ śardhastaro narāṃ gūrtaśravāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-1[1?]3-10 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, *hiṃsakān vā mahato 'pi*: 'oppressors, however very strong', is the meaning. And —"

> शत्रूयन्तो अभि ये नस्ततस्रे महि व्राधन्त ओगणास इन्द्र ।
> *śatrūyanto abhi ye nas tatasre mahi vrādhanta ogaṇāsa indra |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-[6?]9-[1?]2 as read [?])

"— in this, *vrādhantaḥ* = *asmān bādhamānāḥ*: 'those who afflict us greatly'. So in some other places likewise, the word is used in the sense of an enemy who is extremely powerful, hard to stop and harming; and so, in the present Ṛk too, the sense is: however great the strength of the enemy, he is able to stop him, even in his left hand [alone].

*Kīriṇā* — *kīrtayitrā stotrā*: by the praiser, the devotee. Since *rebhaḥ, jaritā, kāruḥ* and the like are read among the [names] of the praiser (*stotṛ*) (*Ni.* 3-1[6?] as read [?]), *kīri* means 'praiser'. [Another word:] *sūrayaḥ kīrayo rudrāḥ* [as printed, ?]."

> यो रातहव्योऽवृकाय धायसे कीरेश्चिन्मन्त्रं मनसा वनोषि तम् ।
> *yo rātahavyo 'vṛkāya dhāyase kīreś cin mantraṃ manasā vanoṣi tam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-3[1?]-13 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the words *kīreḥ cit* Sāyaṇa gives '*stotuḥ eva*' — 'of the praiser' [as printed *stutikāra*, ?]; Skandasvāmin too says the same, but [he adds:] *yo dāridryāt na yajate* [as read, ?]" *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

### Page 214 (PDF 234)

*(Running head: left 214; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 100.9, concluded from p. 213 (Kannada)**

"[Skandasvāmin says] *stotraiva* [as read, ?], and gives also a sense that suggests poverty. Oldenberg, the English commentator, supporting this same sense, has rendered it, 'Thou acceptest in thy mind the hymn even of the poor' *(English as printed in the Kannada text)*. Though the word *kīri* does not literally mean 'poor', it may be that the praisers who had not the means for performing sacrifices were mostly poor, and that this prayer, which suggests poverty, was therefore made. In the present Ṛk, too, the sense is that Indra, praised by the praiser, gives him wealth and the like; so Indra is praised."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.9)** *(grammar pages, pp. 214–215, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *yamati* (root *yamu uparame*; since the causative sense is shown, *ṇic* by *hetumati ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-26 as read]; *vṛddhi* of the penult by *ata upadhāyāḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 as read]; the root is called *mit* by the rule *janījṛṣknasurañjo 'mantāś ca* [as read], since it ends in *m*; shortening of the penult by *mitāṃ hrasvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-92 as read]; the *śap* of the *laṭ* counting as *ārdhadhātuka* as well by *chandasy ubhayathā* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-117 as read]; loss of *ṇi* by *ṇer aniṭi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-51 as read]; *nighāta* accent); *vrādhataḥ* (root *vradhu vṛddhau*; the Uṇādi affix *ati* and the augment *ām* after the root's last vowel by *midaco 'ntyāt paraḥ* [Pā. Sū. 1-1-47 as read]; *yaṇ*; acute on the first syllable by *vṛṣādīnāṃ ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-203 as read]; the case is printed as 'accusative plural', as read); *saṃgṛbhītā* (root *graha upādāne*; the third person singular ending in the *liṅ*-like form; loss of the *vikaraṇa* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *suṭ* by *suṭ tithoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-107 as read]; *sīyuṭ* by *liṅaḥ sīyuṭ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-102 as read]; loss of the *s* by *liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-79 as read]; loss of *y* by *lopo vyor vali* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-66 as read]; the affix being treated as *ṅit*, no *guṇa*; *samprasāraṇa* by *grahijyāvayi…* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-16 as read]; the form *gṛhīta*; *bh* for *h* by *hṛgrahor bhaś chandasi* [vārttika]; lengthening by *dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 as read]; *nighāta*).

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 12 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 215.)*

The grammar of Rik 100.9 concludes: *kṛtāni* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *kta* in the passive by *niṣṭhā* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-102 as read]; acute on the last syllable by the affix; accusative plural); *sanitā* (root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *s* for *ṣ* by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-64 as read]; *tṛn* in the sense of habit by *tācchīlyārthe* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-135 as read]; *iṭ* by *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-35 as read]; the word *sanitṛ*, as its affix is *nit*, is acute on the first syllable; nominative singular); *dhanāni* (in *dhanāni sanitā* the genitive would be expected by *kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti* [Pā. Sū. 2-3-65 as read], but, since a word ending in the present-time *tṛn* is joined, it is prevented by *na lokāvyaya…* [Pā. Sū. 2-3-69 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 9 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.10)**

> स इन्द्रो ग्रामेभिर्मरुत्संघैः सह सनिता फलानां प्रदाता भवति । स चाद्यास्मिन्नहनि नु क्षिप्रं विश्वाभिः कृष्टिभिः सर्वैर्मनुष्यै रथेभिरिन्द्रसम्बन्धिभी रथैः कारणभूतैर्विदे । विज्ञायते । अपि च स इन्द्रः पौंस्येभिः स्वकीयैर्बलैरशस्तीरशंसनीयान् शत्रूनभिभूः । अभिभवन् वर्तते [?] । मरुत्वान्स इन्द्रोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ ग्रामेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसभावः । ग्रामादीनां च । फि. २-१४ [?] । इत्याद्युदात्तत्वम् । विदे । विद ज्ञाने । कर्मणि लट् । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्विति तलोपः ॥
> *sa indro grāmebhir marutsaṃghaiḥ saha sanitā phalānāṃ pradātā bhavati | sa cādyāsminn ahani nu kṣipraṃ viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ sarvair manuṣyai rathebhir indrasambandhibhī rathaiḥ kāraṇabhūtair vide | vijñāyate | api ca sa indraḥ pauṃsyebhiḥ svakīyair balair aśastīr aśaṃsanīyān śatrūn abhibhūḥ | abhibhavan vartate [?] | marutvān sa indro 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ grāmebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisabhāvaḥ | grāmādīnāṃ ca | Phi. 2-14 [?] | ity ādyudāttatvam | vide | vida jñāne | karmaṇi laṭ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | lopas ta ātmanepadeṣv iti talopaḥ ‖*

"That Indra, with the *grāmas* — the Maruts' bands — is *sanitā*, the giver of fruits. And he, *adya* — today, *nu* — quickly, by *viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ* — all men — is known (*vide*) by *rathebhiḥ*, his chariots, which are the means [of knowing him]. Also that Indra, by his own *pauṃsya* — strengths — is the conqueror (*abhibhūḥ*) of *aśastīḥ* — the unpraiseworthy enemies; [he lives] overcoming [them] [?]. May that Indra, with the Maruts, be for our protection."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized: the instrumental plural* grāmebhiḥ *with* bhis *and no* ais*, and the acute on the first syllable by* grāmādīnāṃ ca *[Phiṭ-sūtra 2-14, as read [?]];* vide *(root* vid *'to know', the present passive, the* vikaraṇa *dropped, and the loss of the* t *of the ending).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*saḥ* — that Indra; *grāmebhiḥ* — together with his companions the Maruts; *sanitā* — becomes the giver, a benefactor; *saḥ* — he; *adya* — today; *nu* — in haste, quickly; *viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ* — by all men; *rathebhiḥ* — (with his) chariots (as one mounted on his chariot); *vide* — is recognized; *saḥ* — that Indra; *pauṃsyebhiḥ* — by his [own] strengths; *aśastīḥ* — the unworthy enemies; *abhibhūḥ* — he overcomes; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra, together with his companions the Maruts, is exceedingly beneficent to all as the giver of wealth. All men, too, recognize Indra today as the rider of his chariot. By his prowess that Indra overcomes the enemies who are unworthy. May that Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> He, along with his attendants, in [sic] a benefactor ; he is quickly recognized by all men to-day, through his chariots ; by his manly energies he is victor over unruly (adversaries) : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.10 (Kannada)**

"*Grāmebhiḥ* — *marutsaṃghaiḥ*, 'with the bands of Maruts': 'come together with the groups of the Maruts' — here [Sāyaṇa] has given *grāma* the sense of *saṃgha*, 'band'. This word, besides the established meaning 'village' — in which it is used in many Ṛks, such as 1-44-10; 1-1[?]4-1; 10-90-8 [as read [?]] — is used in many places also in the sense of 'band', *saṃgha*."

> यदङ्ग त्वा भरताः संतरेयुर्गव्यन्ग्राम इषित इन्द्रजूतः ।
> *yad aṅga tvā bharatāḥ saṃtareyur gavyan grāma iṣita indrajūtaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-33-11 as read [?])

> नियुत्वन्तो ग्रामजितो यथा नरोऽर्यमणो न मरुतः कबन्धिनः ।
> *niyutvanto grāmajito yathā naro 'ryamaṇo na marutaḥ kabandhinaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-54-8 as read [?])

"— here *grāmajitaḥ* means '*saṃghātmakasya padārthasya vikleṣayitāraḥ*', those who separate a thing that consists of a band, that is, who split apart things joined together; and in the same way —"

> अपश्यं ग्रामं वहमानमारादचक्रया स्वधया वर्तमानम् ।
> *apaśyaṃ grāmaṃ vahamānam ārād acakrayā svadhayā vartamānam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-27-19 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these also the sense is 'band'. In the present Ṛk, too, *grāmebhiḥ* means 'together with the Maruts, who are in the form of a band'.

*Rathebhiḥ vide* — [he] is known along with his chariots. Because he is the rider of a chariot that moves in the mid-air with exceeding speed, that is furnished with thousands of supports [as read, ?], and that draws all to itself, the sense is that, as soon as they know the distinctive quality of his chariot, they recognize him."

> आ यस्मिन्हस्ते नर्या मिमिक्षुरा रथे हिरण्यये रथेष्ठाः ।
> आ रश्मयो गभस्त्योः स्थूरयोराध्वन्नश्वासो वृषणो युजानाः ॥
> *ā yasmin haste naryā mimikṣur ā rathe hiraṇyaye ratheṣṭhāḥ | ā raśmayo gabhastyoḥ sthūrayor ādhvann aśvāso vṛṣaṇo yujānāḥ ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-29-2 as read [?])

> यस्ते रथो मनसो जवीयानेन्द्र तेन सोमपेयाय याहि ।
> *yas te ratho manaso javīyān endra tena somapeyāya yāhi |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-112-2 as read [?])

"— as described in many Ṛks like these, he is recognized by all as the rider of a chariot of great attraction.

*Viśvābhiḥ kṛṣṭibhiḥ* — the word *kṛṣṭi* means 'races of men'. Just as the Nirukta-author, for *pañcakṛṣṭīḥ* in the Ṛk 4-3[8?]-10, gives '*pañcajanān*' (*Ni.* 10-31 as read [?]), including all human races in the meaning, so here also the sense is 'by all men'. (The word *pañcajana* —" *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

### Page 218 (PDF 238)

*(Running head: left 218; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 100.10, continued from p. 217 (Kannada)**

"[The word *pañcajana*] — what the five groups suggested by that word are will be told later, in the explanation of the [thirteenth, as read, ?] Ṛk of this same sūkta). Thus Sāyaṇa's explanation is that Indra is recognized by all men as the rider of a chariot. Skandasvāmin has explained giving a different sense:"

> ग्रामेभिः रथेभिरिति द्वितीयार्थे तृतीया । स ग्रामान् सनिता दाता । स एव रथान् । इत्येवमहं विदे जानामि ।
> *grāmebhiḥ rathebhir iti dvitīyārthe tṛtīyā | sa grāmān sanitā dātā | sa eva rathān | ity evam ahaṃ vide jānāmi |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: in *grāmebhiḥ rathebhiḥ* the third case stands in the sense of the second; 'he is the giver of villages, and of chariots; thus I know']. These two words *grāmebhiḥ*, *rathebhiḥ* are in the third case, but they must be given the sense of the second case: 'I know that Indra gives villages and chariots.' If it is explained thus, the word *grāma* does not have the sense of 'band', but only 'village'. But in this context Sāyaṇa's explanation appears the more fitting.

*Pauṃsyebhiḥ* — the word *pauṃsya* is read among the names of strength and among the names of battle (*Ni.* 2-[9?] as read [?]); here it means 'by strengths'.

*Aśastīḥ* — *aśasaḥ, aśastīḥ*: these are words that are synonyms of 'enemy':"

> शंसन्ति स्तुवन्तीति शसः स्तोतारः । ते न भवन्तीत्यशसः नृशंसाः [?] ।
> *śaṃsanti stuvantīti śasaḥ stotāraḥ | te na bhavantīty aśasaḥ nṛśaṃsāḥ [?] |*

"— those who praise are *śasaḥ*, praisers; those who are not such are *aśasaḥ*, [cruel to men, as read [?]]: enemies who have fallen away from [sacrificial] rites. They may be Asuras, or they may be men fallen away from rites. Such unworthy enemies Indra *abhibhūḥ* — overcomes."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.10)** *(grammar pages, pp. 218–219, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *grāmebhiḥ* (the word *grāma*, instrumental plural, *bhis* following; *ais* does not arise by *bahulaṃ chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; *e* by *bahuvacane jhaly et* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-103 as read]; *s* → *ru* → visarga; acute on the first syllable by *grāmādīnāṃ ca* [Phiṭ-sūtra 2-[?]4 as read, ?]; likewise *rathebhiḥ*); *vide* (root *vida jñāne*; *laṭ* in the passive, third person singular, *ta*; the *vikaraṇa* dropped by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *e* for the *ṭi* of the ending by *ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-79 as read]; loss of the *t* of the ending by *lopas ta ātmanepadeṣu* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-41 as read]; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda no *nighāta*; final acute by the affix); *kṛṣṭibhiḥ* (root *kṛṣa vilekhane*; *ktic* by *ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-174 as read]; acute on the last syllable by *citaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; *ṭ* for the affix's *t* by the *ṣṭutva* rule; instrumental plural); *pauṃsyebhiḥ* (as before, no *ais*; *e*).

The grammar of Rik 100.10 concludes: *aśastīḥ* (root *śaṃsu stutau*; *ktin* in the passive, in the feminine, by *striyāṃ ktin* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-24 as read]; the form *śastiḥ*; *na śastiḥ aśastiḥ*, a negative *tatpuruṣa*; the accent of the first member kept, as it is an indeclinable, by *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-2 as read]; accusative plural); *abhibhūḥ* (*abhi bhavati iti abhibhūḥ*; *kvip* by *kvip ca*; the accent of the last member by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 10 ‖* and a printed ornament.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.11)**

> पुरुहूतो बहुभिर्यजमानैराहूतः स इन्द्रो मीळ्हे संग्रामे । मीळ्हमिति धननाम । तद्धेतुत्वात्संग्रामोऽपि मीळ्हशब्देनोच्यते । जामिभिर्बन्धुभिरजामिभिर्वा बान्धवरहितैर्वा एवैर्मरुद्भिः सह युद्धार्थं यद्यदा समजाति सङ्गच्छते । तेषामुभयविधानामपां [?] इन्द्रं प्राप्नुवतां पुरुषाणां तोकस्य पुत्रस्य तनयस्य च तत्पुत्रस्य च जेषे जयप्राप्तये स इन्द्रो भवति । किमु वक्तव्यमस्माकं स्तोतृत्वमानां जयो भवतीति । अन्यत्स्पष्टम् ॥ समजाति । अज गतिक्षेपणयोः । लेट्यडागमः । जेषे । जि जये । औणादिकः सप्रत्ययः । चतुर्थ्यर्थे सप्तमी । यद्वा । जेषृ [?] गतौ । क्विप् चेति क्विप् । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वम् ॥
> *puruhūto bahubhir yajamānair āhūtaḥ sa indro mīḷhe saṃgrāme | mīḷham iti dhananāma | taddhetutvāt saṃgrāmo 'pi mīḷhaśabdenocyate | jāmibhir bandhubhir ajāmibhir vā bāndhavarahitair vā evair marudbhiḥ saha yuddhārthaṃ yadyadā samajāti saṅgacchate | teṣām ubhayavidhānām apāṃ [?] indraṃ prāpnuvatāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ tokasya putrasya tanayasya ca tatputrasya ca jeṣe jayaprāptaye sa indro bhavati | kimu vaktavyam asmākaṃ stotṛtvamānāṃ jayo bhavatīti | anyat spaṣṭam ‖ samajāti | aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | jeṣe | ji jaye | auṇādikaḥ sapratyayaḥ | caturthyarthe saptamī | yadvā | jeṣṛ [?] gatau | kvip ceti kvip | sāv ekāca iti vibhakter udāttatvam ‖*

"*Puruhūtaḥ* — called by many sacrificers, that Indra, in *mīḷhe* — in battle. *Mīḷha* is a name of wealth; because battle is the cause of it, battle too is called by the word *mīḷha*. *Jāmibhiḥ* — with kinsmen, or *ajāmibhiḥ* — with those without kinsmen, together with the Maruts, 'who go' (*evaiḥ*), whenever he goes forth (*samajāti*) for battle: for the people of both kinds who have reached Indra, for their son (*tokasya*), their grandson (*tanayasya*) and their son's son, for the winning of victory (*jeṣe*) that Indra becomes [the means]. What need to say, then, that victory is for us who are praisers! The rest is clear."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized: the form* samajāti *from the root* aja *'to drive, to cast' with the* leṭ *and* aḍāgama*;* jeṣe *from* ji *'to conquer' with an Uṇādi affix, a locative used for the dative; or from a root* jeṣṛ *[?] 'to go', with* kvip*; accent on the ending by* sāv ekāca*. The word* apām *at the head of the bhāṣya's list is read as printed [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*puruhūtaḥ* — Indra, who is called by many sacrificers; *saḥ* — Indra; *mīḷhe* — in the battle (that is the root cause of wealth); *jāmibhiḥ* — with kinsmen, be it; *ajāmibhiḥ vā* — or with those who are not kinsmen; *evaiḥ* — (those who go to battle) with the Maruts; *yat* — whenever; *samajāti* — [he] joins [them]; *apām* — [all] those who join [him] and obtain [his] protection; *tokasya* — to their sons; *tanayasya* — and to their grandsons; *jeṣe* — he becomes the giver of victory; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra, who is called by many sacrificers for help, in the battle that is the root cause of wealth, whenever he joins his kinsmen, or those who are not his kinsmen, together with the Maruts who go to battle, then, to those who gain Indra's protection, and to their sons and grandsons, he becomes the giver of victory. May Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Invoked by many, he goes to battle with his kinsmen, or with (followers) not of his kindred ; he secures the (triumph) of those who trust in him, and of their sons and grandsons : may Indra associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

### Page 221 (PDF 241)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 10 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 221.)*

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.11 (Kannada)**

"The idea that, for those who gain Indra's protection, victory in battle is assured, whether they are kinsmen or not, is plainly shown in this Ṛk.

*Mīḷhe* — since *raṇaḥ, vivāk* and the like are read among the [forty-six, as read, ?] names of battle (*Ni.* 2-[?] as read [?]), the sense is 'in battle'."

> बाधसे जनान्वृषभेव मन्युना घृषौ मीळ्ह ऋचीषमः ।
> *bādhase janān vṛṣabheva manyunā ghṛṣau mīḷha ṛcīṣamaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-46-4 as read [?])

> असर्जि कलशाँ अभि मीळ्हे सप्तिर्न वाजयुः ।
> *asarji kalaśāṃ abhi mīḷhe saptir na vājayuḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 9-106-13 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, as the word *mīḷhe* has the sense 'in battle', so here too the sense is 'in battle'. According to the classification in the Nirukta this word comes to have the meaning 'battle' directly. Even so, Sāyaṇa has given an explanation showing the sense that has come down by tradition: '*mīḷham iti dhananāma | taddhetutvāt saṃgrāmo 'pi mīḷhaśabdenocyate*' — he has said that, *mīḷha* being a name of wealth, since battle is the cause of wealth the word is also used for battle. In the Nirukta this word is included in both lists, the names of wealth and the names of battle (*Ni.* 2-[?] as read [?]).

*Jāmibhiḥ* —"

> जामीरन्येऽस्यां जनयन्ति जामुपत्वम् [?] । जमतीर्वा स्यान्निगमनप्रायाः भवति [?] ।
> *jāmīr anye 'syāṃ janayanti jāmupatvam [?] | jamatīr vā syān nigamanaprāyāḥ bhavati [?] |*
> (*Ni.* 3-6 as read [?]; clotted in the print)

"— with the idea 'others cause offspring to be born in her', and from the root *jan*, which gives the sense 'to be born', the title *jāmi* is derived in one way; or, with the idea 'she who goes to her husband's house', and from the root *jam*, which gives the sense 'to go', the title *jāmi* is derived in another way. By both explanations, it is known from the Nirukta-author's derivation that the word *jāmi* means 'sister' (*sahodari*). Supporting this meaning —"

> न जामये तान्वो रिक्थमारैक्चकार गर्भं सनितुर्निधानम् ।
> *na jāmaye tānvo rikthām āraik cakāra garbhaṃ sanitur nidhānam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-31-2 as read [?]; the print's *tānvo rikthamāraik* followed as printed)

"— quoting this Ṛk [the Nirukta-author] explains *jāmi* as 'sister'. In the same way —"

> भगस्य स्वसा वरुणस्य जामिरुषः सूनृते प्रथमा जरस्व ।
> *bhagasya svasā varuṇasya jāmir uṣaḥ sūnṛte prathamā jarasva |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-123-5 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "He does not leave the [father's] inheritance to a sister…; the embryo, the deposit of the giver"; "O Uṣas, sister of Bhaga, kin of Varuṇa, O truthful one, speak first!".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 100.11, continued from p. 221 (Kannada)**

"In Ṛks like these also the word *jāmi* has just the sense 'sister'. But in the present Ṛk the sense of *jāmi* is more extended: it means 'kinsmen'. *Jāmibhiḥ, ajāmibhir vā* — with kinsmen, or with those who are not kinsmen: that is the sense. In the same way in many other Ṛks too this extended meaning is seen. For example —"

> जामिः सिन्धूनां भ्रातेव स्वस्रामिभ्यान्न राजा वनान्यत्ति ।
> *jāmiḥ sindhūnāṃ bhrāteva svasrām ibhyān na rājā vanāny atti |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-65-[2/4?] as read [?])

> कस्ते जामिर्जनानामग्ने को दाश्वध्वरः ।
> *kas te jāmir janānām agne ko dāśvadhvaraḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-[2?]3-3 as read [?])

"— in these Ṛks too the sense is 'kinsmen', as in this Ṛk. Besides the above two senses, the word *jāmi* is also used as a synonym of 'fingers'. For example —"

> एष वृषा कनिक्रददशभिर्जामिभिर्यतः ।
> *eṣa vṛṣā kanikradad daśabhir jāmibhir yataḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 9-[3?]9-4 as read [?])

> अंशुर्यवेन पिपिशे यतो नृभिः सं जामिभिर्नसते रक्षते शिरः ।
> *aṃśur yavena pipiśe yato nṛbhiḥ saṃ jāmibhir nasate rakṣate śiraḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 9-68-4 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "Like a brother of the rivers, like [a king consuming forest] of the sisters"; "Who is your kinsman among men, O Agni, who has done the sacrifice for you?"; "This bull, roaring, held by the ten fingers"; "The shoot, adorned with barley, held by men, is joined by the fingers; the head is guarded".)*

"— in Ṛks like these, for the word *jāmi* the meaning is 'fingers'.

*Evyaiḥ* — *yuddhārthaṃ gacchadbhiḥ marudbhiḥ saha*: with the Maruts who go to battle. The special character of the word *evyaiḥ* as used of the Maruts was told in the explanation of the third Ṛk of this sūkta [as read, ?].

*Yat evyaiḥ samajāti* — 'whenever he joins with the Maruts who go for battle': it is said so because, in battle, when the Maruts help Indra, victory is unfailing; hence victory comes easily to all who gain Indra's protection: that is the sense."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.11)** *(grammar pages, pp. 222–223, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *samajāti* (the preverb *sam*; root *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ*; *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; *aṭ* by *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; the form *ajāti*; because the relative *yat* is related to it earlier, the *nighāta* accent is prevented by *yadvṛttān nityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; since *tip* is *pit* it is unaccented, and the root's accent remains; since the finite verb retains an acute, the preverb *sam* gets the *nighāta* accent by the rule beginning *tiṅ ca…* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-71 as read]); *evyaiḥ* (root *iṇ gatau*; *van* by *iṇśīṅbhyāṃ van* [Uṇ. Sū. 1-150 as read]; *guṇa* by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-84 as read]; acute on the first syllable, the affix being *nit*; instrumental plural).

### Page 223 (PDF 243)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 10 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 223.)*

The grammar of Rik 100.11 concludes: *apām* (the word *ap* is always feminine and plural; genitive plural; the ending acute by *ūḍidaṃpadādi* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); *jeṣe* (root *ji jaye*; the Uṇādi affix *sa*; *guṇa* because of the affix; *ṣ* for *s* by *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-59 as read], the *i* being the cause; a locative in the sense of the dative, 'since the *kārakas* arise as the speaker intends'; or from the root *jeṣṛ gatau* [as read, ?] with *kvip* by *kvip ca*, with total loss, the form *jyeṣ*; dative singular, with the ending *ṅe* standing as *e*; acute on the ending by *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 11 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

> स इन्द्रो वज्रभृत् अन्यैर्भर्तुमशक्यस्य वज्रस्य भर्ता । दस्युहा दस्यूनामुपक्षपयितॄणामसुराणां हन्ता । भीमः सर्वेषां भयहेतुः उग्र उद्गूर्णतेजाः सहस्रचेता बहुविधज्ञानः । सर्वज्ञ इत्यर्थः । शतनीथो बहुस्तुतिर्बहुविधप्रापको वा ऋभ्वा उरु भासमानो महान् चम्रीषो न चम्रा चमसे रसात्मनावस्थितः सोम इव शवसा बलेन पाञ्चजन्यः । गन्धर्वा अप्सरसो देवा असुरा रक्षांसि पञ्च जनाः । निषादपञ्चमाश्चत्वारो वर्णा वा । तेषु रक्षकत्वेन भवः । एवंभूतः स मरुत्वानिन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ दस्युहा । बहुलं छन्दसीति हन्तेः क्विप् । भीमः । ञिभी भये । भीमादयोऽपादाने । पा. ३-४-७४ । इत्यपादाने भियः षुग्भा उ. १-१४४ [?] । इति मक् । शतनीथः । नीञ् प्रापणे । हनिकुषिनीरमिकाशिभ्यः क्थन् । उ. २-२ [?] । इति क्थन्प्रत्ययः । चम्रीषः । ईष गतौ । चम्रामीषति गच्छतीति चम्रीषः । इगुपधलक्षणः कप्रत्ययः । वर्णव्यापत्त्या रेफो दीर्घश्च । यद्वा चमेरौणादिक ईषन्प्रत्ययः । पूर्ववद्रेफः । पाञ्चजन्यः । भवार्थे बहिर्देवपञ्चजनेभ्यश्चेति वक्तव्यम् । का. ४-३-५८-१ [?] । इति ञ्यप्रत्ययः । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥
> *sa indro vajrabhṛt anyair bhartum aśakyasya vajrasya bhartā | dasyuhā dasyūnām upakṣapayitṝṇām asurāṇāṃ hantā | bhīmaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhayahetuḥ ugra udgūrṇatejāḥ sahasracetā bahuvidhajñānaḥ | sarvajña ity arthaḥ | śatanītho bahustutir bahuvidhaprāpako vā ṛbhvā uru bhāsamāno mahān camrīṣo na camrā camase rasātmanāvasthitaḥ soma iva śavasā balena pāñcajanyaḥ | gandharvā apsaraso devā asurā rakṣāṃsi pañca janāḥ | niṣādapañcamāś catvāro varṇā vā | teṣu rakṣakatvena bhavaḥ | evaṃbhūtaḥ sa marutvān indro no 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ dasyuhā | bahulaṃ chandasīti hanteḥ kvip | bhīmaḥ | ñibhī bhaye | bhīmādayo 'pādāne | Pā. 3-4-74 | ity apādāne bhiyaḥ ṣugbhā U. 1-144 [?] | iti mak | śatanīthaḥ | nīñ prāpaṇe | hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan | U. 2-2 [?] | iti kthanpratyayaḥ | camrīṣaḥ | īṣa gatau | camrām īṣati gacchatīti camrīṣaḥ | igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kapratyayaḥ | varṇavyāpattyā repho dīrghaś ca | yadvā camer auṇādika īṣanpratyayaḥ | pūrvavad rephaḥ | pāñcajanyaḥ | bhavārthe bahirdevapañcajanebhyaś ceti vaktavyam | Kā. 4-3-58-1 [?] | iti ñyapratyayaḥ | ñittvād ādyudāttatvam ‖*

"That Indra is *vajrabhṛt* — the bearer of the thunderbolt which others cannot bear. *Dasyuhā* — the slayer of the Dasyus, the Asuras who cause destruction. *Bhīmaḥ* — the cause of fear to all; *ugraḥ* — of upraised splendour; *sahasracetāḥ* — of manifold knowledge, that is, all-knowing; *śatanīthaḥ* — much praised, or one who bestows many kinds of things; *ṛbhvā* — shining widely, great; *camrīṣo na* — like Soma that is present in the cup (*camasa*) as juice; *śavasā* — with strength; *pāñcajanyaḥ* — the five peoples: Gandharvas, Apsarases, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; or the four castes with the Niṣāda as the fifth: he is the protector among them. **॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*saḥ* — that Indra; *vajrabhṛt* — the bearer of the thunderbolt weapon (which cannot be borne by others); *dasyuhā* — the destroyer of the Rākṣasas who have the form of robbers; *bhīmaḥ* — the fearful; *ugraḥ* — the one with fierce splendour; *sahasracetāḥ* — the one with manifold knowledge (the all-knowing); *śatanīthaḥ* — the one who is praised in many ways, or the one who makes many kinds of things be obtained; *ṛbhvā* —" *(continues on p. 225)*

"[*ṛbhvā* —] the one of great splendour; *camrīṣo na* — like the Soma-juice that is in the cup (*camasa*); *śavasā* — with strength; *pāñcajanyaḥ* — the one who is the protector of the five groups beginning with the Gandharvas, or of the four castes together with the Niṣāda; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"That Indra holds the exceedingly mighty thunderbolt weapon; is the destroyer of the Rākṣasas who have the form of robbers; is the terrifying one, of fierce splendour; of manifold knowledge; one who accepts many kinds of praise; highly powerful; and, with strength of exceeding excellence like the Soma in the cup, is the protector of all the gods and Asuras, from the Gandharvas on, and also of the people of the five classes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> He is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the slayer of robbers, fearful and fierce, knowing many things, much eulogized, and mighty, and, like the Soma juice, inspiring the five classes of beings with vigour : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.12 (Kannada)**

"In this Ṛk two kinds of power of Indra are described together. The first is the power that is terrifying, of fierce splendour, and that destroys the Dasyus; the second is the power that is highly splendid and that protects the *pāñcajanyas*. Because of this incomparable greatness Indra is praised by the epithets *sahasracetāḥ*, *śatanīthaḥ*, *ṛbhvā* and the like. This twofold power — terrifying toward the wicked and protecting toward the good, and spreading knowledge by dispelling darkness — is described in the Śrutis, Smṛtis and the rest, in all contexts, in words and ideas suited to those contexts. That this twofold greatness and brilliance becomes manifest in Indra alone is described in many parts of the Ṛksaṃhitā; in this Ṛk, too, that point is set out.

*Dasyuhā* — the destroyer of the *dasyu*. *Dasyu* means the Asuras, Piśācas and the like, who cause decay. From the word *deva*, which in that sense has [the senses] expansive, illuminating, giving (*Ni.* 7-15 as read [?]), whatever sense appears — the opposite of all of that: destructive, blind [—" *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

**Special Topics of Rik 100.12, continued from p. 225 (Kannada)**

"[…the opposite of all of that: destructive, blind,] causing darkness, and violent — such senses the word *dasyu* shows. [The Nirukta:] *dasyur dasyateḥ kṣayārthād upadasyanty asmin rasāḥ upadāsayati karmāṇi* (*Ni.* 7-23 as read [?]) [as read, doubtful [?]]: from the root *das* (*upakṣaye*), which gives the sense 'to cause to waste away', the *dasyu* is known as one who makes the groups of cows and the like dry up and who destroys the sacrificial acts and the like. Vṛtra and the other Asuras all belong to this group of *dasyus*. Those who stop the flow of the waters and conceal the light — by their deeds Indra destroyed them, made the waters flow, and spread the light. Therefore Indra is praised in many places as *dasyuhā*. The word *dasyu* is used in many places as a synonym of the Asuras, but in some places this word is also used of men who are without rites (*karmahīna*). For example —"

> त्वं ह नु त्यददमायो दस्यूँरेकः कृष्टीरवनोरार्याय ।
> *tvaṃ ha nu tyad adamāyo dasyūm̐r ekaḥ kṛṣṭīr avanor āryāya |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-18-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, *dasyūn* means 'people without rites'. Because Indra killed both such enemies, Vṛtra and the like, and the *dasyus* who are without rites, Indra has the epithet *dasyuhā*."

> कुवित्सस्य प्र हि व्रजं गोमन्तं दस्युहा गमत् ।
> *kuvit sasya pra hi vrajaṃ gomantaṃ dasyuhā gamat |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-45-24 as read [?])

> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-86-11 as read [?])

> चक्षुः श्रोत्रं [print: श्रोतं] मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः ।
> गन्धर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा ॥
> सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयन्ते ह्यैतरेयिके ।
> *cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ [print: śrotaṃ] mano vāk ca prāṇaś cety ātmavādinaḥ | gandharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitaras tathā ‖ sarpāś ca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyante hy aitareyike |*
> (*Bṛ. De.* 7-7[?] as read [?]; and *Ai. Brā.* 3-[?]1-5 as read [?])

"Eye, ear, mind, speech and breath: these five are the *pañcajanas*, hold the *ātmavādins* [those who speak of the Self, the adhyātma view]; the Gandharvas and the rest are set out in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (*Ai. Brā.* 3-[?]1-5 as read [?]). 'Let such *pañcajanas* too enjoy the oblation': Agni gave this answer to the gods; and in the explanation of the Bṛhaddevatā too differences of opinion were pointed out in this way.

In this Ṛk in question, where Indra is the protector of the *pāñcajanyas*, Indra's greatness is described. Since all the worlds are included in Indra's protection, the word *pāñcajanya* will fit all the opinions given above."

Sū. 1-[1?]43 as read, ?]; *mak* after the root; as the affix is *kit*, no *guṇa* of the root vowel; final acute by the affix); *sahasracetāḥ* (*sahasrāṇi cetāṃsi yasya saḥ*; in the *bahuvrīhi*, the first member keeps its accent by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-135 as read]; in the Veda, by letter-interchange, *r* comes in and the vowel is lengthened; the form *camrīṣa*; since the first member is a *kāraka*, the accent of the last member by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. **॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.13)**

> तस्येन्द्रस्य वज्रः कुलिशः स्मत् भृशं क्रन्दति । शत्रूनाक्रन्दयति । रोदयतीत्यर्थः । य इन्द्रः स्वर्षाः शोभनस्योदकस्य दाता दिवो न दिवः सम्बन्धी सूर्य इव त्वेषो दीप्तः रवथः शब्दस्य गर्जनलक्षणस्य कर्ता शिमीवान् । शिमीति कर्मनाम । लोकानुग्राहकेण कर्मणा युक्तस्तमिन्द्रं सनयो धनस्य दानानि सचन्ते । सेवन्ते । तथा तं धनानि च सेवन्ते । स मरुत्वानिन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ क्रन्दति । कदि क्रदि क्लदि आह्वाने रोदने च । छन्दस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वाण्णेरनिटीति णिलोपः । स्वर्षाः । सुपूर्वात् [?] । सुष्ठु ऋच्छतीति स्वः उदकम् । तत् सनोतीति स्वर्षाः । षणु दाने । जनसनखनक्रमगमो विट् । विड्वनोरनुनासिकस्यात् इत्यात्वम् । सनोतेरनः । पा. ८-३-१०८ [?] । इति षत्वम् । त्वेषः । त्विष दीप्तौ । पचाद्यच् । रवथः । रु शब्दे । शीङ्क्षसिरुगमिवञ्चिजीविप्राणिभ्योऽथः [?] । उ. ३-१०३ [?] । इत्यथप्रत्ययः । गुणावादेशौ । सनयः । सनोतेर्भावे औणादिक इप्रत्ययः ॥
> *tasyendrasya vajraḥ kuliśaḥ smat bhṛśaṃ krandati | śatrūn ākrandayati | rodayatīty arthaḥ | ya indraḥ svarṣāḥ śobhanasyodakasya dātā divo na divaḥ sambandhī sūrya iva tveṣo dīptaḥ ravathaḥ śabdasya garjanalakṣaṇasya kartā śimīvān | śimīti karmanāma | lokānugrāhakeṇa karmaṇā yuktas tam indraṃ sanayo dhanasya dānāni sacante | sevante | tathā taṃ dhanāni ca sevante | sa marutvān indro no 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ krandati | kadi kradi kladi āhvāne rodane ca | chandasy ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāṇ ṇer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ | svarṣāḥ | supūrvāt [?] | suṣṭhu ṛcchatīti svaḥ udakam | tat sanotīti svarṣāḥ | ṣaṇu dāne | janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ | viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt ity ātvam | sanoter anaḥ | Pā. 8-3-108 [?] | iti ṣatvam | tveṣaḥ | tviṣa dīptau | pacādyac | ravathaḥ | ru śabde | śīṅkṣasirugamivañcijīviprāṇibhyo 'thaḥ [?] | U. 3-103 [?] | ity athapratyayaḥ | guṇāvādeśau | sanayaḥ | sanoter bhāve auṇādika ipratyayaḥ ‖*

"The thunderbolt (*kuliśa*) of that Indra *smat* — greatly — *krandati*: makes the enemies cry out, that is, makes them weep. That Indra, who is *svarṣāḥ* — the giver of good water — *divo na* — like the sun that belongs to heaven, *tveṣaḥ* — shining — *ravathaḥ* — maker of a sound that has the character of thunder — *śimīvān* — *śimī* is a name of action; he is joined to action that helps the world: *sanayaḥ*, the gifts of wealth, *sacante* — attend, follow him; and likewise *dhanāni*, riches, attend him. May that Indra, with the Maruts, be for our protection."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the stem* svarṣā *(from* svar *'water' [as read] and* san *'to give', with* viṭ *by* janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ*,* ā *for the nasal, and* ṣ *by a rule given in the print as Pā. Sū. 8-3-108 [?]);* tveṣa *(from* tviṣ *'to shine' with* ac *of the* pacādi *class);* ravatha *(from* ru *'to sound', with the Uṇādi* atha *[Uṇ. Sū. 3-103, as read, ?], with* guṇa *and* av*-substitution);* sanaya *(from* san *with an Uṇādi* i *in the sense of the action). The Uṇādi sūtra's list of roots is clotted [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*tasya* — of that Indra; *vajraḥ* — the thunderbolt weapon; *smat* — greatly; *krandati* — (makes the enemies) weep, makes them wail; (*yaḥ* — that Indra, who is) *svarṣāḥ* — the giver of excellent waters; *divo na* — like the sun that shines in the world of heaven; *tveṣaḥ* — shining; *ravathaḥ* — the one who makes a roaring sound; *śimīvān* — (the cause of benefit to the world) endowed with action; *tam* — that Indra; *sanayaḥ* — liberal gifts; *sacante* — attend; *tam* — him; *dhanāni* — wealth also (attends); *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

### Page 232 (PDF 252)

*(Running head: left 232; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra's thunderbolt weapon makes the enemies weep copiously. That Indra, the giver of waters, who shines like the sun in the world of heaven, makes a roaring sound, and who is endowed with the action that is the cause of benefit to the world — such an Indra is served by wealth and liberal gifts. May such an Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> His thunderbolt draws cries (from his enemies), he is the sender of good waters, brilliant as (the luminary) of heaven, the thunderer, the promoter of beneficent acts, upon him do donations and riches attend : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.13 (Kannada)**

"*Vajraḥ* —"

> वज्रः कस्मात् । व्रजयतीति सतः ।
> *vajraḥ kasmāt | vrajayatīti sataḥ |*
> (*Ni.* [?] as read [?])

"— since it separates the vital breaths from living creatures and drives them forth, it is called *vajra*. It has the power to kill the extremely strong Asuras. The greatness of the thunderbolt weapon, and how Indra obtained it, are described here and there in various ways."

> अस्मा इदु त्वष्टा तक्षद्वज्रं स्वपस्तमं स्वर्यं रणाय ।
> *asmā id u tvaṣṭā takṣad vajraṃ svapastamaṃ svaryaṃ raṇāya |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-32-2 as read [?])

> अनवस्ते रथमश्वाय तक्षन्त्वष्टा वज्रं पुरुहूत द्युमन्तम् ।
> *anavas te ratham aśvāya takṣan tvaṣṭā vajraṃ puruhūta dyumantam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-31-4 as read [?])

"— in many Ṛks like these it is told that Tvaṣṭṛ prepared for Indra the shining thunderbolt weapon. Besides —"

> यं ते काव्य उशना मन्दिनं दाद्वृत्रहणं पार्यं ततक्ष वज्रम् ।
> *yaṃ te kāvya uśanā mandinaṃ dād vṛtrahaṇaṃ pāryaṃ tataksa vajram |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-121-12 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these it is said that it was made by Kāvya Uśanas."

> समुद्रे अन्तः शयत उद्ना वज्रो अभीवृतः ।
> भरन्त्यस्मै संयतः पुरःप्रस्रवणा बलिम् ॥
> *samudre antaḥ śayata udnā vajro abhīvṛtaḥ | bharanty asmai saṃyataḥ puraḥprasravaṇā balim ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-100-9 as read [?])

### Page 233 (PDF 253)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 10 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 233.)*

"— in this and similar places the nature and the power of the thunderbolt weapon are described. [This weapon] lies in the sea, covered with water, and hidden; and with the [Maruts and] friends, the enemies in the field of battle give up their very lives as an offering to it: so the power of the thunderbolt weapon is told. With such a weapon Indra destroyed all the Rākṣasas; and before killing them he made them *smat krandati* — cry out copiously, so that they were overcome. The word *smat* is generally explained by Sāyaṇa in many places as having the senses 'beautiful, auspicious, praiseworthy'; in some places he has shown it as a synonym of *saha*, 'together with'. Here he explains it as *bhṛśam*, 'greatly'."

> अस्मिन्निन्द्र वृजने सर्ववीराः स्मत्सूरिभिस्तव शर्मन्स्याम ।
> *asminn indra vṛjane sarvavīrāḥ smat sūribhis tava śarman syāma |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-91-13 as read [?])

> सिषक्तु माता महीरसा नः स्मत्सूरिभिर्ऋजुहस्त ऋजुवनिः ।
> *siṣaktu mātā mahī rasā naḥ smat sūribhir ṛjuhasta ṛjuvaniḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-41-15 as read [?])

"— in these Ṛks, and likewise in [the Ṛks 3-4?-?; 1-1?-?; 2-?-?; 8-?-? and others, numerals as read [?]], for the word *smat* used there, he has given the sense *suprasasta* — 'very praiseworthy' — or *śobhana*, 'beautiful'. And —"

> उत न ईं मरुतो वृद्धसेनाः स्मद्रोदसी समनसः सदन्तु ।
> *uta na īṃ maruto vṛddhasenāḥ smad rodasī samanasaḥ sadantu |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-186-9 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, [he has given] also the sense *saha*, 'together'; and for the word *smat* used in the Ṛk 1-23-6 [as read [?]] — '*smacchabdo nityaśabdasamānārthaḥ | nityam ūḍhasā yuktāḥ*' [as read, ?] — he has given the sense *nitya*, 'always'.

In the present Ṛk, as in the Ṛk 3-4-9 [as read [?]], he has explained '*saha*, *bhṛśam*, *atiprabhūtam*' — 'greatly, exceedingly': the sense is that he made the enemies wail exceedingly.

*Svarṣāḥ* — *śobhanasya udakasya dātā*: the giver of good water; one who gives waters of excellent quality.

*Śimīvān* — '*śimīti karmanāma | śamayater vā śaknoter vā*' (*Ni.* 2-[?]5 as read [?]): 'from the root *śam*, which gives the sense of toiling, exerting oneself, or from the root *śak*, which gives the sense of being able': the word is thus derived and means 'action' —"

> आपान्तमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिः शिमीवाञ्छरुमाँ ऋजीषी ।
> *āpāntamanyus tṛpalaprabharmā dhuniḥ śimīvāñ charumāṃ ṛjīṣī |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-99-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, as the sense comes, here too it means 'endowed with action'. By such actions as the killing of Vṛtra, by actions of the form of sending rain, and because he is joined to other actions that are means of protecting the world, the epithet *śimīvān* is fitting for Indra."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.13)** *(grammar pages, pp. 234–235, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *krandati* (root *kadi kradi kladi āhvāne rodane ca*; since the causative sense is shown, *ṇic* by *hetumati ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-26 as read]; since the root is *idit*, the augment *num* by *idito num dhātoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-58 as read]; *krand* gets the name of a root by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-32 as read]; *laṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; *śap*; the *śap* counting as *ārdhadhātuka* in the Veda by *chandasy ubhayathā* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-117 as read], loss of *ṇi* by *ṇer aniṭi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-51 as read]; the form *krandati*; *nighāta* accent); *svarṣāḥ* (root *ṛ gatau*; with *su* as the preceding member, *viṭ* [*viC*] by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-75 as read], with total loss of the affix; *suṣṭhu ṛcchati gacchatīti svar udakam* — 'water' [as read, 'that which goes well']; *svar sanotīti svarṣāḥ*, root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *viṭ* by *janasanakhanakramagamo viṭ* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-67 as read]; *s* for the initial *ṣ* by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-64 as read]; *ā* for the nasal of the root by *viḍvanor anunāsikasyāt* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-41 as read]; the *ṣ* of *svarṣā* by *sanoter anaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-108 as read]; the word ends in *ā*; the accent of the last member by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]); *divaḥ* (*ūḍidaṃpadādi* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); *tveṣaḥ* (root *tviṣa dīptau*; since it belongs to the *pacādi* class, *ac* by *nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 as read]; *guṇa* of the penult because of the affix; acute on the last syllable by the affix); *ravathaḥ* (root *ru śabde*; *atha* by *śīṅśapiruguminañcijīviprāṇibhyo 'thaḥ* [Uṇ. Sū. 3-[?]3 as read, ?]; *guṇa* by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-84 as read]; *av*-substitution; the form *ravatha*; the accent of the affix makes the word acute on the middle syllable); *sacante* (root *ṣac sevane secane ca* [print: *paca*, as read, ?], *bhvādi*; *laṭ*, third person plural; *nighāta*).

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*śavasā* — by strength; *yasya* — of which Indra; *ukthaṃ* — the praiseworthy; *mānaṃ* — the measure (or the standard for the strength of others); *rodasī* — heaven and earth; *viśvataḥ sīm* — in all regions; *ajasram* — always; *paribhujat* — he protects completely; *saḥ* — that Indra; *kratubhiḥ* — by the sacrifices (performed by us); *mandasānaḥ* — made glad; *pāriṣat* — may he make [us] free from sin; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"The praiseworthy strength of Indra surpasses the strength of all others in the world, is the standard and the model for them all, and always protects completely all the regions of heaven and earth. May Indra, who has such strength, made glad by the sacrifices we perform, make us free from sin. May that Indra, together with the Maruts, be our protector."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> May he, of whom the excellent measure (of all things), through strength, eternally and everywhere cherishes heaven and earth, propitiated by our acts, convey us beyond (evil) : may Iudra [sic], associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.14 (Kannada)**

"No one can surpass Indra's strength in earth or in sky, either. His strength surpasses all the strength of earth and sky, and is the standard for all strengths. First: his power is praiseworthy, and is the measure for everyone. The excellence of that power can be known from the descriptions in the Saṃhitā."

> नहि नु यादधीमसीन्द्रं [print: …योदधी…, ?] को वीर्या परः ।

"— who can know Indra, who is all-pervading, who dwells in places so deep that men cannot know them, and who is endowed with such ability? Because of this heroism, all the gods made Indra their leader for the performance of heroic deeds and for becoming a support for strength."

> नि षु सीद गणपते गणेषु त्वामाहुर्विप्रतमं कवीनाम् ।

"— he is counted as the most excellent poet among all the poets, who are intelligent and of transcendent mind.

### Page 238 (PDF 258)

*(Running head: left 238; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 100.14, continued from p. 237 (Kannada)**

"[…the Ṛk 8-13-2 says that] Indra upheld heaven and earth both by his power, and, having established them, made them firm and secure [as read, ?]. In this way, because Indra's power, his sovereignty and his work of protection are unmatched —"

> नहि न्वस्य प्रतिमानमस्त्यन्तर्जातेषूत ये जनित्वाः ।
> *nahi nv asya pratimānam asty antar jāteṣūta ye janitvāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-18-4 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 171)

"— [the Ṛk] declares that none, whether among those who have been born or among those who will be born hereafter, can be compared with Indra. These two points alone are set out, in the present Ṛk, as *śavasā yasya ukthaṃ mānaṃ rodasī viśvataḥ sīm ajasraṃ paribhujat*.

*Mandasānaḥ* — *modamānaḥ*, 'rejoicing': *mandater tṛptikarmaṇaḥ* [as read] (*Ni.* 2-[3?]5 as read [?]); the word is derived from the root *mand*, which means 'to attain satisfaction'. *Kratubhiḥ mandasānaḥ*: be satisfied by our sacrifices and the like, and, having obtained that satisfaction, [free] us —

*Pāriṣat* — *duritāt pārayatu*: 'make us pass over sin', is Sāyaṇa's explanation.

Skandasvāmin has made another construction:"

> स पारिषत् — पृ पालनपूरणयोः । पूरयत्यस्मान् । क्रतुभिः प्रज्ञाभिः । अत्यन्तप्रज्ञान् अस्मान् करोतीत्यर्थः । मन्दसानः । मन्दतिरर्चतिकर्मा । स्तूयमानोऽस्माभिः ।
> *sa pāriṣat — pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ | pūrayaty asmān | kratubhiḥ prajñābhiḥ | atyantaprajñān asmān karotīty arthaḥ | mandasānaḥ | mandatir arcatikarmā | stūyamāno 'smābhiḥ |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: *pāriṣat* is from the root *pṛ*, 'to protect, to fill': 'he fills us'; *kratubhiḥ* — with intelligences, the sense is 'he makes us of exceeding intelligence'; *mandasānaḥ*: the root *mand* is a verb of 'honouring'; he who is praised by us]. Since *mand* is read among the [forty-four, as read, ?] names of the *arcati*-verbs [?], *mandasānaḥ* means 'Indra, who is praised by us'. Skandasvāmin explains that the intention is that such an Indra may give us full wisdom. Here Sāyaṇa's meaning appears the more suitable."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.14)** *(grammar pages, pp. 238–239, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *mānam* (root *māṅ māne*; *lyuṭ* in the sense of the action; *ana* for *yu* by *yuvoranākau* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; the syllable before the affix acute by *liti* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 as read]); *uktham* (root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *thak* in the passive by a rule beginning *pātṛtudi…* [as read [?]]; since the affix is *kit*, *samprasāraṇa* by *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-15 as read]; the single substitute by *samprasāraṇāc ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-108 as read]; *k* for *c* by *coḥ kuḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-30 as read]; final acute by the affix; accusative singular).

The grammar of Rik 100.14 continues: *paribhujat* (root *bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ*, with the preverb *pari*; *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; loss of the *i* by *itaś ca lopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-97 as read]; *aṭ* by *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; the *śa*-*vikaraṇa* in place of *śap* by *vyatyayo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read]; since the relative *yasya* has been mentioned earlier, the *nighāta* is prevented by *yadvṛttān nityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read], and the accent of the root remains; the preverb *pari* receives the *nighāta* by *tiṅ codāttavati* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-71 as read]); *viśvataḥ* (in the sense of 'from all', *tasil* by *pañcamyās tasil* [Pā. Sū. 5-3-7 as read]; the preceding syllable acute by *liti* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-193 as read]); *pāriṣat* (root *pāra tīra karmaparisamāptau*; *leṭ*, *tip*; loss of *i*; *aṭ*; *sip* by *sib bahulaṃ leṭi* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-34 as read]; *ārdhadhātukaṃ śeṣaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-114 as read] gives it *ārdhadhātuka* status and *iṭ* by *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-35 as read]; the root belongs to the *curādi* class and so takes *ṇic* in its own sense; though the *iṭ*-initial affix follows, by *vyatyaya* the *ṇic* is dropped; the form *pāriṣat*; *nighāta*); *mandasānaḥ* (root *madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu*; *asānac* by *ṛñjivṛdhimandisahibhyaḥ kit* [Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]4 as read, ?]; *num* by *idito num dhātoḥ*; the form *mandasāna*; final acute, the affix being *cit*, by *citaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]). **॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.15)**

> देवता देवस्य दानादिगुणयुक्तस्य यस्येन्द्रस्य शवसो बलस्यान्तमवसानं देवा वस्वादयो देवगणा नापुः । नाप्नुवन् । तथा मर्ता मनुष्या आपश्च नापोऽपि न प्राप्नुवन् । स तादृश इन्द्रस्त्वक्षसा शत्रूणां तनूकर्त्रात्मीयेन बलेन क्ष्मः पृथिव्या दिवश्च स्वर्गस्य च प्ररिक्वा प्रकर्षेण रेचको भवति । लोकद्वयोदपस्य [?] बलमतिरिच्यत इत्यर्थः । मरुद्भिर्युक्तः स इन्द्रोऽस्माकमूतये रक्षणाय भवतु ॥ देवता । देव इव देवता । देवात्मकेति स्वार्थे तल् । सुपां सुलुगिति षष्ठ्या लुक् । मर्ताः । मृङ् प्राणत्यागे । असिहसीत्यादिना तन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । प्ररिक्वा । रिचिर् विरेचने । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति क्वनिप् । आन्त्यैकारश्छान्दसः [?] । त्वक्षसा । तक्षू त्वक्षू तनूकरणे । असुन् । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । क्ष्मः । क्ष्मेति पृथिवीनाम । [the rest of the tail is on p. 241 and is clotted]
> *devatā devasya dānādiguṇayuktasya yasyendrasya śavaso balasyāntam avasānaṃ devā vasvādayo devagaṇā nāpuḥ | nāpnuvan | tathā martā manuṣyā āpaś ca nāpo 'pi na prāpnuvan | sa tādṛśa indras tvakṣasā śatrūṇāṃ tanūkartrātmīyena balena kṣmaḥ pṛthivyā divaś ca svargasya ca prarikvā prakarṣeṇa recako bhavati | lokadvayodapasya [?] balam atiricyata ity arthaḥ | marudbhir yuktaḥ sa indro 'smākam ūtaye rakṣaṇāya bhavatu ‖ devatā | deva iva devatā | devātmaketi svārthe tal | supāṃ suluk iti ṣaṣṭhyā luk | martāḥ | mṛṅ prāṇatyāge | asihasītyādinā tanpratyayaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | prarikvā | ricir virecane | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti kvanip | āntyaikāraś chāndasaḥ [?] | tvakṣasā | takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe | asun | nittvād ādyudāttatvam | kṣmaḥ | kṣmeti pṛthivīnāma |*

"Of Indra, the deity, endowed with such qualities as generosity, of whose *śavas* — of whose strength — the *antam*, the limit, the gods, the groups of gods, the Vasus and the rest, did not reach; and likewise mortals, men, and the waters [as the print has it, *āpaś ca nāpo 'pi*, ?] have not attained it: such an Indra, by his *tvakṣas* — his own strength that makes his enemies weak — *prarikvā* — greatly surpasses — *kṣmaḥ* — the earth — and *divaḥ* — the heaven; the sense is that his strength exceeds [that of] both worlds. May that Indra, joined with the Maruts, be for our protection."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*devatā* — [Indra,] endowed with qualities such as generosity, of the nature of a deity; *yasya* — of which Indra; *śavasaḥ* — of the strength; *antam* — the limit; *devāḥ* — the gods; *na āpuḥ* — have not reached (nor obtained); *martāḥ* — men; *āpaś cana* — and the water-deities too; *na* — have not reached; *saḥ* — that Indra; *tvakṣasā* — by the strength that makes [enemies] weak; *kṣmaḥ* — of the earth; *divaḥ ca* — and of heaven; *prarikvā* — becomes the excellent illuminator, surpasses; *marutvān* — together with the Maruts; *indraḥ* — Indra; *naḥ* — our; *ūtī* — for protection; *bhavatu* — may he be."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"The power of Indra, who is of the nature of a deity, endowed with such qualities as generosity, exceeds that of all others in the world. Neither gods, nor men, nor the water-deities could reach its limit. That Indra, by his enemy-destroying and majestic power, makes the earth and the heavenly world both shine together. May such an Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, be our protector."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Nor gods, nor men, nor waters, have reached the limit of the strength of that beneficent (divinity), for he surpasses both earth and heaven by his foe-consuming (might) : may Indra, associated with the Maruts, be our protection.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.15 (Kannada)**

"In the previous Ṛk, [the author] described that Indra's power and sovereignty are the standard for the whole universe; in this Ṛk he explains that his power surpasses the power of earth and sky, and the power of gods and men, and that none in the universe could attain to that power. This point is described in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā."

"In Ṛks like these, Indra's greatness surpassed earth and sky both. Neither earth nor heaven could hold this greatness. By descriptions such as 'Indra's influence expanded exceedingly, pervaded all, and grew beyond the universe', it is declared that his influence grew to such a degree that it could not be attained even by the gods — [as in the vow-like declaration]:"

> सत्यमित्तन्न त्वावाँ अन्यो अस्तीन्द्र देवो न मर्त्यो ज्यायान् ।
> *satyam it tan na tvāvām̐ anyo astīndra devo na martyo jyāyān |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-30-4 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these Indra's greatness is described. Just as in these descriptions, so in the present Ṛk also:

*yasya śavasaḥ antaṃ devāḥ na āpuḥ* — the gods could not approach the limit of that Indra's valour;

*martāḥ āpaś ca na* — men and the water-deities could not approach it either; and

*kṣmaḥ divaś ca prarikvā* — he became the illuminator of earth and sky: thus the greatness of the extremely great Indra is praised.

*Tvakṣasā* — since *ojaḥ, pājaḥ* and the like are read among the [thirty-eight, as read, ?] names of strength, *tvakṣaḥ* means 'strength'; *tvakṣasā* means 'by strength'.

*Prarikvā* — *prakarṣeṇa recako bhavati | lokadvayād apy asya balam atiricyata ity arthaḥ*: 'he becomes the one who greatly surpasses; the sense is that his strength exceeds even the two worlds'; by his own strength he makes earth and sky both shine; that is, with his strength he exceeds the two worlds."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.15)** *(grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: *devatā* (*deva eva devatā*; *tal* in the sense of the thing itself by *devāt tal* [Pā. Sū. 5-4-27 as read]; feminine by *talantaṃ striyām* [as read]; the sixth-case ending dropped by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]); *martāḥ* (root *mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*; *tan* by *asihasi…* [Uṇ. Sū.]; *guṇa* of the root vowel because of the affix; *raparatva* by *uraṇ raparaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 1-1-51 as read]; the form *marta*; acute on the first syllable, the affix being *nit*, by *ñnityādir nityam*); *āpuḥ* (root *āp-ḷ vyāptau*; *liṭ*, third person plural; since the relative is related to it, the *nighāta* is prevented by *yadvṛttān nityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; acute on the last syllable by the affix); *prarikvā* (root *ricir virecane*; *kvanip* by *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-75 as read]; preverb *pra*; *rikvan*; *k* for *c* in the Vedic manner; since *vanip* is *pit*, unaccented, the root's accent remains; nominative singular); *tvakṣasā* (root *takṣū tvakṣū tanūkaraṇe*; *asun* by *sarvadhātubhya asun* [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]3 as read, ?]; the word *tvakṣas*; acute on the first syllable by *ñnityādir nityam*; instrumental singular); *kṣmaḥ* (*kṣmā* is a name of the earth; by the splitting of the rule *ato dhātoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-140 as read], the desired result is reached: when the stem ending in *ā* has *bha*-status, before *jas*, the *ā* is dropped; or from the root *kṣmāyī vidhūnane* with *kvip* by *kvip ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read]; loss of *v* by *verapṛktasya* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-67 as read] and of *y* by *lopo vyor vali* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-66 as read]; the form *kṣmā*, a stem by *kṛttaddhitasamāsāś ca* [Pā. Sū. 1-2-46 as read]; the loss of the final *ā* is natural; since the ending is unaccented, the ending is acute by *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-161 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 15 ‖*.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"The line of horses of Indra's chariot — red and dark on its two sides, long-limbed, with beautiful ornaments, dwelling in the world of heaven — carries on its yokes the chariot that has been called, with Indra, to give wealth to the king named Ṛjrāśva; and all the armies belonging to men recognize that line of horses, which gladdens all."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> The red and black coursers, long-limbed, well-caparisoned, and celestial and harnessed, well-pleased, to the yoke of the chariot in which the showerer of benefits is conveyed, for the enrichment of Rijraswa [sic], and is recognized amongst human hosts.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.16 (Kannada)**

"*Sumadaṃśuḥ* — here there are two words, *sumat* and *aṃśuḥ*. As the Nirukta-author has explained:"

> सुमत् स्वयमित्यर्थः ।
> *sumat svayam ity arthaḥ |*
> (*Ni.* 6-22 as read [?])

"— he has given the word *sumat* the sense *svayam*, 'of itself'. Here, too, in *sumadaṃśuḥ*, *sumat* means *svayam*, that is, *svataḥ prāṃśuḥ*, 'tall of its own nature' *(the passage continues on the next page)*

### Page 246 (PDF 266)

*(Running head: left 246; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 100.16, continued from p. 245 (Kannada)**

"[*sumadaṃśuḥ* — 'tall of its own nature'; and] *atidīrghāvayavā*, 'having very long limbs': [Sāyaṇa] has explained it by quoting a Nirukta sentence, since in the whole this is the intended sense: 'having exceedingly long limbs'.

Earlier, in explaining the [thirteenth, as read, ?] Ṛk of this same sūkta, it was shown that Sāyaṇa gave different meanings, in different contexts, to the word *smat* used there; and it was suggested that the word *smat* is a synonym of the words *kalyāṇa*, *śobhana* or *bhadra*. In the same way it cannot be wrong to say that the word *sumat* too is a synonym of the words *kalyāṇa*, *śobhana* or *bhadra*. Just as in *sumadaṃśuḥ*, many other words such as *sumadrathaḥ* and *sumadgaṇaḥ* are found in use; so, if we see in what way Sāyaṇa explains the words used in the Ṛksaṃhitā —"

> अथा मन्दस्व जुजुषाणो अन्धसस्त्वष्टर्देवेभिर्जनिभिः सुमद्गणः ।
> *athā mandasva jujuṣāṇo andhasas tvaṣṭar devebhir janibhiḥ sumadgaṇaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-36-3 as read [?])

"— in the Ṛk he has given, for the word *sumadgaṇaḥ*, the meaning *śobhanagaṇaḥ* ('of splendid retinue'). The sense: the word *sumat* is a synonym of *śobhana*."

> विभावा देवः सुरणः परि क्षितीरग्निर्बभूव शवसा सुमद्रथः ।
> *vibhāvā devaḥ suraṇaḥ pari kṣitīr agnir babhūva śavasā sumadrathaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-3-8 as read [?])

"— here *sumadrathaḥ* means *śobhanarathaḥ*, 'of splendid chariot'. Moreover —"

> आ ते [?] वचोयुजा हरी गृभ्णे सुमद्रथा [?] ।
> *ā te [?] vacoyujā harī gṛbhṇe sumadrathā [?] |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-43-29 as read [?]; clotted in the print, not completed from memory)

"— in this Ṛk, too, [Sāyaṇa] has explained *kalyāṇarathau*. In the same way, for the word *sumadaṃśuḥ* occurring in the present Ṛk also, the sense could be 'having a splendid *aṃśu*', that is, splendid brilliance, or 'having a splendid bridle'. (*samadaṃśu* [as printed] — 'Together with reins or harness': Monier Williams, *Sanskrit-English Dictionary*.) *(English in the original.)*

Skandasvāmin also —"

> सुमच्छब्दोऽत्र स्मच्छब्देन समानार्थः प्रशस्तवचनः । अंशुशब्दो रश्मिवचनः । प्रशस्तरश्मिः ।
> *sumacchabdo 'tra smacchabdena samānārthaḥ praśastavacanaḥ | aṃśuśabdo raśmivacanaḥ | praśastaraśmiḥ |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: 'the word *sumat* here is of the same meaning as the word *smat*, a word of praise; the word *aṃśu* means ray; so 'of excellent ray'']. 'Just as for the word *smat*, so for the word *sumat* too the sense is "praiseworthy".' *Aṃśu* means 'bridle': so he explains that [the horse-line] is 'one having an excellent bridle'.

*Dyukṣā* — *divi dyuloke kṛtanivāsā*: one that has made her dwelling in the heavenly world: that dwells in the world of heaven."

### Page 247 (PDF 267)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 247.)*

"*Ṛjrāśvasya* — *etannāmakasya rājarṣeḥ*: of the royal sage named Ṛjrāśva; or — by the mention of Ṛjrāśva, [his brothers] all five Vārṣāgiras are indicated [as read, the print's Sanskrit clotted [?]]. Ṛjrāśva is the son of Vṛṣāgira. Ambarīṣa and the others are his brothers; their names are told in the next Ṛk. These too are the seers of this sūkta. A story describing a charming occasion in the life of Ṛjrāśva is told in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself:"

> शतं मेषान्वृक्ये चक्षदानमृज्राश्वं तं पिताऽन्धं चकार ।
> तस्मा अक्षी नासत्या विचक्ष आधत्तं दस्रा भिषजावनर्वन् ॥
> *śataṃ meṣān vṛkye cakṣadānam ṛjrāśvaṃ taṃ pitā 'ndhaṃ cakāra | tasmā akṣī nāsatyā vicakṣa ādhattaṃ dasrā bhiṣajāv anarvan ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-116-16 as read [?])

"Once Ṛjrāśva killed a hundred sheep [print: young goats] for a she-wolf and gave them to her; for that his father was angry and cursed him: 'let him not see!' At once the son became blind. Then, by the favour of the Aśvins, the divine physicians, his sight came to him. Thus, to Ṛjrāśva, who had become worthy of the favour of the gods, Indra too appeared in person and gave abundant wealth. This is the sense of the Ṛk: that, when Indra, to give wealth to Ṛjrāśva, harnessed his most excellent horses and came in his chariot, all men recognized Indra.

*Nāhuṣīṣu* — since *manuṣyāḥ, naraḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-five [as read, ?] names of man (*Ni.* 2-2 as read [?]), *nahuṣa* means 'man', and *nāhuṣa* means 'belonging to men'.

*Vikṣu* — Skandasvāmin explains it as *manuṣyajātiṣu*, 'among the races of men', and Sāyaṇa as *senārūpāsu prajāsu*, 'among the subjects who have the form of armies'. They recognized Indra, who came to help in battle. Here, in *nāhuṣīṣu vikṣu*, either [it may be taken]: 'among men, among the subjects who have the form of armies' — one sense, taking *nahuṣa* as the word for man; or, [Skandasvāmin:] *nahuṣanāmno vā rājñaḥ svabhūtāsu vikṣu manuṣyajātiṣu brāhmaṇādikāsu* — 'among the subjects, the races of men, the Brāhmaṇas and the rest, belonging to a king named Nahuṣa' — another sense. Sāyaṇa has given only one sense here. These same words *nāhuṣīṣu vikṣu* occur in the eighth maṇḍala —"

> उत त्यदाश्वश्व्यं यदिन्द्र नाहुषीष्वा । अग्रे विक्षु प्रदीदयत् ॥
> *uta tyad āśvaśvyaṃ yad indra nāhuṣīṣv ā | agre vikṣu pradīdayat ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-6-24 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the words *nāhuṣīṣu vikṣu* [Sāyaṇa gave:] *nahuṣā iti manuṣyanāma tatsambandhinīṣu vikṣu | yadvā | nāhuṣo nāma kaścid rājā | tadīyāsu vikṣu | prajāsu |* — 'for *nahuṣa* is a name for man; among the subjects connected with them; or, there was a king named Nahuṣa; among the subjects belonging to him' — two kinds of" *(the sentence continues on p. 248)*

"[— two kinds of] sense. A story about the king named Nahuṣa is also subtly hinted in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself:"

"— the king named Nahuṣa, wishing to take the initiation and perform a sacrifice for a thousand years, travelled round this earth in one chariot, addressing all the rivers that flow to the sea thus:"

> वहेम भागान् स्वर्वाँस्ते [as printed; read *sarvāṃs te*?] सत्रे वार्षसहस्रके । सरस्वतीं प्रपद्यस्व सा ते वक्ष्यति नाहुष ॥
> *yakṣye vahata bhāgān me dvandvaśo vātha vaikaśaḥ | pratyūcus taṃ nṛpaṃ nadyaḥ svalpavīryāḥ kathaṃ vayam ‖ vahema bhāgān svarvāṃs te [as printed] satre vārṣasahasrake | sarasvatīṃ prapadyasva sā te vakṣyati nāhuṣa ‖*

"— 'I shall sacrifice; carry my portions, two at a time or one by one.' The rivers answered that king: 'We have little strength; how could we carry all your portions in a sacrifice of a thousand years? Resort to Sarasvatī; she will carry them for you, O Nāhuṣa.'"

> तथेत्युक्त्वा जगामाशु आपगां स सरस्वतीम् । सा चैनं प्रतिजग्राह दुदुहे च पयो घृतम् ॥
> *tathety uktvā jagāmāśu āpagāṃ sa sarasvatīm | sā cainaṃ pratijagrāha duduhe ca payo ghṛtam ‖*

"— and so, saying 'So be it', he quickly went to the river Sarasvatī; she received him and gave milk and ghee, as he had wished. Thus, since the story of the king named Nahuṣa is famous in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself, the meaning in the present Ṛk may also be taken as Skandasvāmin has explained it."
