**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 100.17)**

> हे इन्द्र वृष्णे कामानां वर्षित्रे ते तव तृप्त्यादेतदुक्थं स्तोत्रं राधः संराधकं तृप्तिहेतुं वार्षागिरा वृषागिरो राज्ञः पुत्रा ऋज्राश्वादयोऽभि गृणन्ति । अभिमुखेन वदन्ति । वार्षागिरा इत्येतद्विवृणोति । ऋज्राश्वश्चैतन्नामा राजर्षिः पृष्टिभिः पार्श्वस्थैरन्यैर्ऋषिभिः सहेन्द्रमस्तौत् । के ते पार्श्वस्थाः । अम्बरीषादयश्चत्वारो राजर्षयः ॥ वार्षागिराः । तस्यापत्यम् । पा. ४-१-९३ [?] । इत्यण्प्रत्ययः । गृणन्ति । गृ शब्दे । प्वादीनां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । राधः । राध साध संसिद्धौ । राध्नोति सम्यद्धो भवत्यनेनेति राधः । करणेऽसुन् । ऋज्राश्वः । ऋज्रा गतिमन्तोऽश्वा यस्य स तथोक्तः । अम्बरीषः । अबि शब्दे । औणादिक ईषन्प्रत्ययः । उ. ४-२९ [?] । सहदेवः । देवैः सह वर्तत इति सहदेवः । वोपसर्जनस्येति विकल्पेन सभावाभावः [?] । भयमानः । ञिभी भये । अस्माद् अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थाद् व्यत्ययेन शानच् । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लौ [?] रभावः । अदुपदेशाल्लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वर एव शिष्यते । सुराधाः । राध इति धननाम । शोभनं राधो यस्य । सोर्मनसी अलोमोषसी इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥
> *he indra vṛṣṇe kāmānāṃ varṣitre te tava tṛptyād etad uktham stotraṃ rādhaḥ saṃrādhakaṃ tṛptihetuṃ vārṣāgirā vṛṣāgiro rājñaḥ putrā ṛjrāśvādayo 'bhi gṛṇanti | abhimukhena vadanti | vārṣāgirā ity etad vivṛṇoti | ṛjrāśvaś caitannāmā rājarṣiḥ pṛṣṭibhiḥ pārśvasthair anyair ṛṣibhiḥ sahendram astaut | ke te pārśvasthāḥ | ambarīṣādayaś catvāro rājarṣayaḥ ‖ vārṣāgirāḥ | tasyāpatyam | Pā. 4-1-93 [?] | ity aṇpratyayaḥ | gṛṇanti | gṛ śabde | pvādīnāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam | rādhaḥ | rādha sādha saṃsiddhau | rādhnoti samyaddho bhavaty aneneti rādhaḥ | karaṇe 'sun | ṛjrāśvaḥ | ṛjrā gatimanto 'śvā yasya sa tathoktaḥ | ambarīṣaḥ | abi śabde | auṇādika īṣanpratyayaḥ | U. 4-29 [?] | sahadevaḥ | devaiḥ saha vartata iti sahadevaḥ | vopasarjanasyeti vikalpena sabhāvābhāvaḥ [?] | bhayamānaḥ | ñibhī bhaye | asmād antarbhāvitaṇyarthād vyatyayena śānac | bahulaṃ chandasīti śapaḥ ślau [?] rabhāvaḥ | adupadeśāl lasārvadhātukānudāttatve dhātusvara eva śiṣyate | surādhāḥ | rādha iti dhananāma | śobhanaṃ rādho yasya | sormanasī alomoṣasī ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam ‖*

"O Indra, *vṛṣṇe* — you who rain down desires — *te*, for your satisfaction, this praise (*uktha*), *rādhaḥ* — that fulfils, that is the cause of satisfaction — the *vārṣāgirāḥ*, the sons of King Vṛṣāgira, Ṛjrāśva and the others, *abhi gṛṇanti* — speak facing [you]. [The commentator] explains *vārṣāgirāḥ*: the royal sage named Ṛjrāśva, with *pṛṣṭibhiḥ* — the other seers who stand at his sides — praised Indra. Who are those who stand at his sides? The four royal sages beginning with Ambarīṣa."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read:* vārṣāgira *(*aṇ *in the sense of 'offspring of him', [Pā. Sū. 4-1-93, as read [?]]);* gṛṇanti *(root* gṛ *'to sound', with shortening by* pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ*);* rādhas *(root* rādh *'to succeed', 'that by which one is made perfect', with* asun *as instrument);* ṛjrāśva *(he whose horses are swift);* ambarīṣa *(root* abi *'to sound', with the Uṇādi* īṣan *[Uṇ. Sū. 4-29, as read, ?]);* sahadeva *('who is with the gods', with an optional* sa*-substitution by* vopasarjanasya *[as read [?]]);* bhayamāna *(root* ñibhī *'to fear', with a causative sense included, and* śānac *by* vyatyaya*);* surādhas *(*rādhas *is a name of wealth; 'of excellent wealth'; the accent of the last member by* sormanasī alomoṣasī*). Clotted rule-names are marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*vṛṣṇe* — [to you] who shower the desired objects; *indra* — O Indra; *te* — your; *tyat* — the well-known; *etat uktham* — this praise; *rādhaḥ* — [for the satisfaction of you] who are endowed with the best wealth, for your satisfaction; *vārṣāgirāḥ* — the sons of the king named Vṛṣāgira; *ṛjrāśvaḥ* — the royal sage named Ṛjrāśva; *pṛṣṭibhiḥ* — with (his) companions at his side; *ambarīṣaḥ* — Ambarīṣa; *sahadevaḥ* — Sahadeva; *bhayamānaḥ* — Bhayamāna; *surādhāḥ* — and Surādhas; *abhi gṛṇanti* — stand facing [you] and recite."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, giver of desired objects! The sons of the king Vṛṣāgira, the royal sage Ṛjrāśva, together with Ambarīṣa, Sahadeva, Bhayamāna and Surādhas, who are with him, stand before you and recite to you this well-known praise."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Indra, showerer (of benefits) the Varshagiras, Rijraswa and his companions Ambarisha, Sahadeva, Bhayamana and Surdhas [sic], address to you this propitiatory praise.

### Page 252 (PDF 272)

*(Running head: left 252; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100".)*

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.17 (Kannada)**

"*Uktham* — *stotram*: in the explanation [Sāyaṇa] has given only the general meaning, 'hymn of praise'. But since it says '*tyat te uktham*' — 'that *uktha* addressed to you, the well-known' — it is suggested that this *uktha* is one that is directed to Indra and that is also the one recited from earlier times, in the times of sacrifice. This *uktha* that is directed to Indra has an extraordinary distinction.

The nature of the *uktha*, its greatness, its connection with the *śastra*, the *uktha* and the *sāman*, and the subtle differences between them, and also the order in which the Hotṛ and his assistant priests are to recite it at the time of the Soma-pressing — all this was set out in detail in the previous part [of this edition].

Here, because the greatness of Indra is praised through the *uktha*, the power of the *uktha*, and through it the greatness of Indra, is subtly shown, with a former story connected with it. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa there is a story that the power of the *uktha* was extremely great; that the Asuras took refuge in it and so their power also grew; and that then Indra came, was praised, and drove them out."

> ते वा असुरा मैत्रावरुणस्योक्थमश्रयन्त सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्स्यवहा [?] इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्वरुणस्तस्मादैन्द्रावरुणं मैत्रावरुणस्तृतीयसवने शंसतीन्द्रश्च हि तान् वरुणश्च ततो नुदेताम् ॥
> *te vā asurā maitrāvaruṇasyokthamaśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyavahā [?] ity ahaṃ cety abravīd varuṇas tasmād aindrāvaruṇaṃ maitrāvaruṇas tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān varuṇaś ca tato nudetām ‖*
> (*Ai. Brā.*, as printed; the numeral on p. 253 [?])

"The Asuras took refuge in the *uktha* of the Maitrāvaruṇa. Then Indra said, 'Who will help me to drive these Asuras out of this *uktha*?' When he asked, Varuṇa said that he would help him. At that time the Maitrāvaruṇa, the assistant priest to the Hotṛ, at the third Soma-pressing, reciting the sūkta that begins with the Ṛk"

> इन्द्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतम् ।
> *indrāvaruṇā yuvam adhvarāya no viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchatam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-68-1 as read [?])

"— praised Indra and Varuṇa. Then Indra and Varuṇa drove those Asuras out by means of the Maitrāvaruṇa *śastra*."

> ते वै ततोऽपहता असुरा ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन उक्थमश्रयन्त सोऽब्रवीदिन्द्रः कश्चाहं चेमानितोऽसुरान्नोत्स्यवहा [?] इत्यहं चेत्यब्रवीद्बृहस्पतिस्तस्मादैन्द्राबार्हस्पत्यं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी तृतीयसवने शंसतीन्द्रश्च हि तान् बृहस्पतिश्च ततो नुदेताम् ॥
> *te vai tato 'pahatā asurā brāhmaṇācchaṃsina ukthamaśrayanta so 'bravīd indraḥ kaś cāhaṃ cemān ito 'surān notsyavahā [?] ity ahaṃ cety abravīd bṛhaspatis tasmād aindrābārhaspatyaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsī tṛtīyasavane śaṃsatīndraś ca hi tān bṛhaspatiś ca tato nudetām ‖*

"The Asuras driven out from there took refuge in the *uktha* of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin."

From this the power of the *uktha*, and the greatness of Indra, are known. *Tat tye uktham* means 'this *uktha* of such influence'.

For this reason, in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa also —"

"Indra alone is the deity of all the sacrifice; therefore, 'to Indra, [the one] with *bṛhat*, with *vayas*' — 'one endowed with valour' — as is said, 'I take up the [cup] named *uktha*': thus it is said, and thereby he takes him [Indra] up from [or: by means of] the *ukthas*." *(Gloss, mine and tentative; the print's Sanskrit is cited in part [?].)* "Indra alone is the deity of the sacrifice. "[…just as the power of the *uktha* was described at the time of sacrificial acts, so, in the time of teaching spiritual knowledge too, the greatness of this *uktha*, which has the form of a hymn, is praised. In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad —"

"— in the sacrifice that has the form of the Mahāvrata, the *uktha*, the chief *śastra*, is itself the breath (*prāṇa*). From it, indeed, the rising up (*utthāna*) comes about. Therefore the son who has the knowledge of the *uktha* is born [in this world], and obtains equality with it and equal esteem: so the greatness of the *uktha* is told.

*Ṛjrāśvaḥ* — the story of Ṛjrāśva was told in the explanation of the previous Ṛk.

*Ambarīṣaḥ* — the name of Ambarīṣa appears to occur only in this one place; his name is not as famous in the Vedas as it is in the Purāṇas.

*Sahadevaḥ* — Sahadeva's story is told in many places: in the Ṛksaṃhitā, in the Ṛk 4-15-7 [as read [?]], in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (2-4-3-4 as read [?]), and in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa also, the matter of Sahadeva is told.

> *sūktaṃ sa yo vṛṣety etat pañca vārṣāgirā viduḥ | niyuktā nāmadheyaiḥ svarair api caitat tyad ity ṛci ‖*
> (Ārṣānukramaṇī, as printed here [clear on this page; the reading *caitat tyad ity ṛci* settles the clotted words *caitat…* noted in the introduction to Sūkta 100 on p. 165])

"— so these five seers received the vision of this sūkta."

### Page 255 (PDF 275)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 255.)*

The grammar of Rik 100.17 continues: *vārṣāgirāḥ* (*vṛṣāgiraḥ apatyaṃ pumān vārṣāgiraḥ*; *aṇ* after *vṛṣāgira* in the sense of 'son' by *tasyāpatyam* [Pā. Sū. 4-1-92 as read]; since the affix is *ñit*, acute on the first syllable; *vṛddhi* by *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-117 as read]; *raparatva* by *uraṇ raparaḥ*; the form *vārṣāgira*; nominative plural); *gṛṇanti* (root *gṝ śabde*, *kryādi*; since it belongs to the *pvādi* class, shortening by *pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-80 as read]; *laṭ*, third person plural, *jhi* → *anta*; *śnā* by *kryādibhyaḥ śnā* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-81 as read]; since the affix is treated as *ṅit*, loss of the *ā* of *śnā* by *śnābhyastayor ātaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-112 as read]; *ṇ* because of the preceding *ṛ*; *nighāta*); *rādhaḥ* (root *rādha sādha saṃsiddhau*; *rādhnoti samyaddho bhavaty aneneti rādhaḥ*; *asun*, in the instrumental sense, the Uṇādi affix that goes with all roots; the word *rādhas*; acute on the first syllable by *ñnityādir nityam*); *ṛjrāśvaḥ* (*ṛjrāḥ gatimantaḥ aśvāḥ yasya saḥ*; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its accent); *ambarīṣaḥ* (root *abi śabde*; the Uṇādi *īṣan* [Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]4 as read, ?]; *num* by *idito num dhātoḥ*; *r* in the Vedic manner; the accent of the affix stays by *vyatyaya*); *sahadevaḥ* (*devaiḥ saha vartate*; *sa* for *saha* optionally by *vopasarjanasya* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-82 as read], and here it does not apply; the accent of the first member in the *bahuvrīhi*); *bhayamānaḥ* (root *ñibhī bhaye*; since the causative sense is included, the root has the causative meaning; *śānac* in the sense of the present by *vyatyayo bahulam*; *ślu* does not replace *śap* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *guṇa* of the root vowel because of *śap*; *ay*-substitution; *muk* to a vowel-ending stem by *āne muk* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-82 as read]; *bhayamāna*; since the root has *a*-ending *upadeśa*, the *lasārvadhātuka* affix *āna* is unaccented by *tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 as read]; the root's own accent remains).

### Page 257 (PDF 277)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 257. A printer's signature "17 · VOLUME 8" stands at the foot.)*

> […]धकारिणो [?] राक्षसादींश्च हत्वा प्रहृत्य तदनन्तरं शर्वा हिंसकेन वज्रेण नि बर्हीत् । अवधीत् । निबर्हयति वधकर्मा । एवं शत्रून्निरस्य श्वित्न्येभिः श्वेतवर्णैरलङ्कारेण दीप्ताङ्गैः सखिभिर्मित्रभूतैर्मरुद्भिः सह क्षेत्रं शत्रूणां स्वभूतं भूमिं सनत् । समभाश्रित् [?] । तथा वृत्रेण तिरोहितं सूर्यं तस्य वृत्रस्य हननेन सनत् । अभजत प्राप्तवानित्यर्थः । तथा सुवज्रः शोभनवज्रयुक्त इन्द्रो वृत्रेण निरुद्धा अपो वृष्ट्युदकानि सनत् । समभजत ॥
> *[…]dhakāriṇo [?] rākṣasādīṃś ca hatvā prahṛtya tadanantaraṃ śarvā hiṃsakena vajreṇa ni barhīt | avadhīt | nibarhayati vadhakarmā | evaṃ śatrūn nirasya śvitnyebhiḥ śvetavarṇair alaṅkāreṇa dīptāṅgaiḥ sakhibhir mitrabhūtair marudbhiḥ saha kṣetraṃ śatrūṇāṃ svabhūtaṃ bhūmiṃ sanat | samabhāśrit [?] | tathā vṛtreṇa tirohitaṃ sūryaṃ tasya vṛtrasya hananena sanat | abhajata prāptavān ity arthaḥ | tathā suvajraḥ śobhanavajrayukta indro vṛtreṇa niruddhā apo vṛṣṭyudakāni sanat | samabhajata ‖*

"…and, having killed the Rākṣasas and the rest [who are the destroyers?], having struck, thereafter *śarvā* — with the weapon that does harm, the thunderbolt — *ni barhīt*: he killed. [*Nibarhayati* is a word meaning 'to kill'.] Having thus driven off the enemies, together with *sakhibhiḥ*, the friends, the Maruts, *śvitnyebhiḥ* — white-coloured, with limbs shining with ornaments — he *sanat* [divided, took] the *kṣetra*, the land that belonged to the enemies. So also, the sun hidden by Vṛtra he *sanat* — obtained, shared — by the slaying of that Vṛtra. And likewise Indra, *suvajraḥ*, endowed with the splendid thunderbolt, *sanat* — released — the waters, the rain-waters, shut in by Vṛtra."

> दस्यून् । दसु उपक्षये । यजिमनिशुन्धिदसिजनिभ्यो युः । उ. ३-[२?]० [?] । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वम् । शिम्यून् । शमु उपशमे । शमयति सर्वं तिरस्करोतीति राक्षसादिः शिम्युः । औणादिको युप्रत्ययः । वर्णव्यापत्त्या [?] ह्रस्वत्वम् [?] । शर्वा । शृ हिंसायाम् । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति वनिप् । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया डादेशः । सनत् । वन षण सम्भक्तौ । लेट्यडागमः । बहुलं छन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपीत्यडभावः । श्वित्न्येभिः । श्विता वर्णे । औणादिको नक्प्रत्ययः । श्वित्नं शुक्लवर्णमर्हन्तीति श्वित्न्याः । छन्दसि ञेति यः [?] । सुवज्रः । आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् ॥
> *dasyūn | dasu upakṣaye | yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuḥ | U. 3-[2?]0 [?] | vṛṣāditvād ādyudāttatvam | śimyūn | śamu upaśame | śamayati sarvaṃ tiraskarotīti rākṣasādiḥ śimyuḥ | auṇādiko yupratyayaḥ | varṇavyāpattyā [?] hrasvatvam [?] | śarvā | śṛ hiṃsāyām | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti vanip | supāṃ suluk iti tṛtīyāyā ḍādeśaḥ | sanat | vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | bahulaṃ chandasy amāṅyoge 'pīty aḍabhāvaḥ | śvitnyebhiḥ | śvitā varṇe | auṇādiko nakpratyayaḥ | śvitnaṃ śuklavarṇam arhantīti śvitnyāḥ | chandasi ñeti yaḥ [?] | suvajraḥ | ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasīty uttarapadādyudāttatvam ‖*

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the stem* dasyu *(root* dasu *'to waste', Uṇādi* yu*) and* śimyu *(root* śam *'to quiet', Uṇādi* yu*, 'one who quiets, suppresses everything: a Rākṣasa and the like');* śarvā *(root* śṛ *'to injure', with* vanip *by* anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante*, and* ḍā *for the third-case ending by* supāṃ suluk…*);* sanat *(root* van/ṣaṇ *'to share', with* leṭ *and* aḍāgama *and, by* bahulaṃ chandasi*, no augment);* śvitnya *(root* śvit *'to be white', with an Uṇādi* nak*, 'worthy of white colour');* suvajra *(accent on the last member by* ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi*). **॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*puruhūtaḥ* — Indra, who is called by many; *evaiḥ* — together with the moving Maruts; *pṛthivyām* — on the earth; *dasyūn* — the enemies who do harm (the Dasyus); *śimyūn ca* — and the Rākṣasas who kill; *hatvā* — having struck; *śarvā* — with the thunderbolt weapon that does harm; *ni barhīt* — he killed [afterwards]; *śvitnyebhiḥ* — with limbs shining with white ornaments; *sakhibhiḥ* — with the Maruts who are his friends; *kṣetram* — the fields (of the enemies); *sanat* — he divided; *sūryam* — the sun (that was hidden by Vṛtra); *sanat* — he released; *suvajraḥ* — Indra, he of the splendid thunderbolt; *apaḥ* — the rain-waters; *sanat* — he released and made flow."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra, called by many for help, together with the roving Maruts, killed with the thunderbolt all the harmful Dasyus who were on the earth, and the Rākṣasas who do harm. And with his friends the Maruts, bright with white ornaments, he divided the fields of the enemies. He released the sun that Vṛtra had hidden. And Indra, with the splendid thunderbolt, released and made flow the rain-waters."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Indra, who is invoked by many, attended by the moving (Maruts), having attacked the Dasyus and the Simyus, slew them with his thunderbolt ; *(the translation continues on p. 258)*

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.18 (Kannada)**

"*Puruhūtaḥ* — *bahubhir yajamānair āhūtaḥ*: Indra, who is called by many sacrificers.

*Evyaiḥ* — formed from the root *iṇ*, which has the sense of going, the form *eva* results. When it is said, 'one whose nature is to go or to move, and in that, to move swiftly', this epithet has been used in many places, chiefly as an epithet of the Maruts; and how this epithet shows the distinguishing character of the Maruts has been explained in the special topics of the second Ṛk of this very sūkta. Here also *evyaiḥ* means *gamanaśīlair marudbhiḥ*, 'with the Maruts of moving nature'. Since the word is used in contexts that show the sense of movement — as a synonym of 'praise (*stotra*)', as a synonym of 'horse (*aśva*)', as a synonym of 'sacrifice (*kratu*)' — the sense of the word must be given according to each context. For example —"

> सनाद्दिवं परि भूमा विरूपे पुनर्भुवा युवती स्वेभिरेवैः ।
> *sanād divaṃ pari bhūmā virūpe punarbhuvā yuvatī svebhir evaiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-62-8 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk '*evaiḥ*' means '*gamanaiḥ*', 'by [their] movements': it shows, as a general adverb, the eternal going of Night and Dawn."

> भजन्त विश्वे देवत्वं नाम ऋतं सपन्तो अमृतमेवैः ।
> *bhajanta viśve devatvaṃ nāma ṛtaṃ sapanto amṛtam evaiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-68-4 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the word *evaiḥ*, [Sāyaṇa] has given '*tvāṃ gantṛbhiḥ stotṛbhiḥ*' [as printed, ?] — a synonym of 'praisers' (*stotṛ*)."

> उप वामवः शरणं गमेयं शूरो नाज्म पतयद्भिरेवैः ।
> *upa vāmavaḥ śaraṇaṃ gameyaṃ śūro nājma patayadbhir evaiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-158-3 as read [?]; the first words clotted in print [?])

"— in this Ṛk, *evaiḥ* = *aśvaiḥ*, a synonym of horses."

> स सूर्य प्रति पुरो न उद्गा एभिः स्तोमेभिरेतशेभिरेवैः ।
> *sa sūrya prati puro na udgā ebhiḥ stomebhir etaśebhir evaiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-19-3 as read [?])

"— here, for *evaiḥ*, Sāyaṇa has explained *aśvaiḥ*, yet there he has shown a doubtful mind [about it]. Here, since it is natural as a qualifier of *stomebhiḥ*" *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

### Page 259 (PDF 279)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 11 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 259.)*

"[— since it is natural as a qualifier of *stomebhiḥ*, it is] a synonym of *stotra*, 'praise'. Only in the present Ṛk, however, *evaiḥ* means 'with the Maruts, who are always of a moving nature, the friends of Indra'.

*Dasyūn* — it was said earlier, in the special topics of the twelfth Ṛk of this sūkta, that for the word *dasyu* the senses 'Rākṣasas who cause decay' and 'men without rites' arise as separate meanings. Here [Sāyaṇa] gives *upakṣapayitṝn śatrūn*, 'enemies who cause decay': that is the sense.

*Śimyūṃś ca* — *śamayitṝn, vadhakāriṇaḥ rākṣasān ca* [as printed]: 'the Rākṣasas who kill' — so a difference is shown between the two kinds of harmers, *dasyu* and *śimyu*. Though the general meaning of both is 'enemies', a subtle difference is stated here. As it is derived from the root *śim*, which gives the sense of power [*śakti*], the sense is 'enemies endowed with the power to harm'. Indra is entreated to destroy both kinds of harmers. As this word is used here, so —"

> शर्धन्तं शिम्युमुचथस्य नव्यः शासं सिन्धूनामकृणोदशस्तीः ।
> *śardhantaṃ śimyum ucathasya navyaḥ śāsaṃ sindhūnām akṛṇod aśastīḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 7-19-[3/5?] as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk also it is used in the sense of *bādhamāna*, 'oppressing'.

*Śarvā* — *śṛṇāti śatrūn aneneti śaruḥ vajraḥ*: 'with which one harms and destroys enemies', the thunderbolt is named *śaru*; *śarvā* means 'with the thunderbolt weapon'. Though in general *śaru* need not mean the thunderbolt weapon alone, there is no rule."

> यः शश्वतो मह्येनो दधानानमन्यमानाञ्छर्वा जघान ।
> *yaḥ śaśvato mahy eno dadhānān amanyamānāñ charvā jaghāna |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-12-10 as read [?])

> युवं ताँ इन्द्रावरुणावमित्रान् हतं पराचः शर्वा विषूचः ।
> *yuvaṃ tām̐ indrāvaruṇāv amitrān hataṃ parācaḥ śarvā viṣūcaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-68-3 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these, since it is a weapon connected with Indra, *śaru* means the thunderbolt weapon. But —"

> आरे सा वः सुदानवो मरुत ऋञ्जती शरुः ।
> *āre sā vaḥ sudānavo maruta ṛñjatī śaruḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-172-3 as read [?])

"— in places like this, since it is connected with the Maruts and the other deities, the meaning is only 'a weapon that harms enemies'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 100.18)** *(grammar pages, pp. 260–261, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *dasyūn* (root *dasu upakṣaye*; *yu* by *yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuḥ* [Uṇ. Sū. 3-[2?]00 as read, ?]; the form *dasyu*; the accent of the affix would be expected, but by *vṛṣādīnāṃ ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-203 as read] the first syllable is acute; accusative plural); *śimyūn* (root *śamu upaśame*; *śamayati sarvaṃ tiraskaroti iti rākṣasādiḥ śimyuḥ*; the affix *yun*, established in the Uṇādi; *i* for the *a* of the root in the Veda by letter-interchange; acute on the first syllable, the affix being *nit*, by *ñnityādir nityam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 as read]; accusative plural); *hatvā* (root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *ktvā* by *samānakartṛkayoḥ pūrvakāle ktvā* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-21 as read]; since *kit*, loss of the nasal by *anudāttopadeśavanatitanotyādīnām anunāsikalopo jhali kṅiti* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-37 as read]); *pṛthivyām* (*udāttayaṇo hal pūrvāt* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-174 as read]); *śarvā* (root *śṝ hiṃsāyām*; *vanip* by *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-75 as read]; *guṇa* of the root vowel because of the affix; the word *śarvan*; before the instrumental ending, *ḍā* by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]; since *ḍit*, loss of the *ṭi* part (*an*) of the stem; *śarvā*; since *vanip* is *pit*, the root's accent remains); *sanat* (root *vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau*; *leṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; loss of the *i* by *itaś ca*; *śap*; *s* for the initial *ṣ* by *dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*; no *aṭ* by *bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 as read]; since it is at the beginning of the pāda, no *nighāta*; since *śap* is *pit*, unaccented, the root's accent remains).

The grammar of Rik 100.18 concludes: *śvitnyebhiḥ* (root *śvitā varṇe*; the Uṇādi affix *nak*; since *kit*, no *guṇa* of the penult; the form *śvitna*; *śvitnaṃ śuklavarṇam arhantīti śvitnyāḥ*; *ya* in the sense of 'worthy of' in the Veda by *arhārthe chandasi ca* [Pā. Sū. 5-1-67 as read]; loss of the *a* by *yasyeti ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-148 as read]; the form *śvitnya*; *bhis* follows, and *ais* does not arise by *bahulaṃ chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read]; *e* by *bahuvacane jhaly et* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-103 as read]); *suvajraḥ* (*śobhanaḥ vajraḥ yasya saḥ*; the accent on *su* would be expected [*susvara*], but, since the last member has two syllables [*ac*], the last member keeps its acute on the first syllable by *ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-119 as read]; nominative singular). The Rik is closed with *‖ 18 ‖* and a printed ornament.

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*viśvāhā* — at all times; *naḥ* — for us; *indraḥ* — Indra; *adhivaktā* — the one who speaks words of partisanship; *astu* — may he be (and we also); *aparihvṛtāḥ* — leaving the crooked path (staying on the straight path); *vājam* — (abundant) food; *sanuyāma* — may we enjoy; *naḥ* — our; *tat* — that prayed-for desired object; *mitraḥ* — Mitra; *varuṇaḥ* — and Varuṇa; *aditiḥ* — Aditi; *sindhuḥ* — the deity presiding over the sea; *pṛthivī* — the earth; *uta* — and; *dyauḥ* — the heavenly world also; *māmahantām* — may they guard."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"May Indra be, at all times, one who speaks words of partisanship for us. And may we also, staying always on the straight path, enjoy abundant food. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the deity of the sea, the earth and the heavenly world guard that desired object which we have prayed for."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> May Indra be daily our vindicator, and may we, with undiverted course, enjoy (abundant) food ; and may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi,—ocean, earth, and heaven, preserve it to us.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 100.19 (Kannada)**

"*Adhivaktā* — *adhivacanaṃ pakṣapātena vacanam*: 'speaking with partisanship': that is, '[Indra] as one who speaks with pride [or favour]': it asks for Indra's partisanship. But if Indra's partisanship and favour are to be gained, they can be gained only by those who stand on the straight path, that is, those who are not crooked: so the adjective *aparihvṛtāḥ* shows [the need for] purity of conduct.

*Aparihvṛtāḥ* — *akuṭilagatayaḥ santaḥ*: 'those who have left the crooked path, that is, who stand on the straight path'. Or, as Skandasvāmin explains, '*sāmarthyād ahiṃsārthaḥ | āhiṃsitāḥ kenacit*' [as printed]: 'unharmed by anyone'; since the pressure of enemies is exceedingly strong, even though food and the like be given by Indra, enemies may carry it off; so the prayer may be: 'may we be unharmed by the enemies'. Sāyaṇa too, for this word in other places, has given both these two meanings. For example —"

> आ यो विवाय सख्या सखिभ्योऽपरिह्वृतो अत्यो न सप्तिः ।
> *ā yo vivāya sakhyā sakhibhyo 'parihvṛto atyo na saptiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-6-3 as read [?])

> सम्राजो ये सुवृधो यज्ञमाययुरपरिह्वृता दधिरे दिवि क्षयम् ।
> *samrājo ye suvṛdho yajñam āyayur aparihvṛtā dadhire divi kṣayam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-63-5 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "He who has come with friendship to his friends, unobstructed, like a courser"; "The joint-sovereigns, the good increasers, who came to the sacrifice, unobstructed, established their dwelling in heaven".)*

"— in Ṛks like these, for the word *aparihvṛte* used there, '*kenacid asya ahiṃsitāḥ*': Sāyaṇa too has given the meaning 'unharmed by anyone'. In the same way the meaning may be taken in this Ṛk also.

*Vājaṃ sanuyāma* — may we enjoy food; the prayer to Indra is that he make us enjoy food without harm.

*Tan no mitro varuṇaḥ* — this prayer, a prayer to many deities at the end of the sūkta, shows, in the form of a conclusion (*udarka*), the style of the seer Kutsa's works: so it was said earlier in the explanation of the last Ṛk of the ninety-fourth sūkta [as read, ?]. Even though this style is seen in the works of other seers, the distinction of Kutsa's style" *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

## Sūkta 101

**ನೂರೊಂದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು** — *nūrondaneya sūktavu*, "the hundred-and-first Sūkta" *(Kannada heading)*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 101 (Sanskrit in Kannada script; doubtful places [?]):**

> प्र मन्दिन इत्येकादशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तमाङ्गिरसस्य कुत्सस्यार्षम् । अष्टम्याद्याश्चतस्रस्त्रिष्टुभः शिष्टाः सप्त जगत्यः । इन्द्रो देवता । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । प्र मन्दिन एकादश कुत्सश्चतुस्त्रिष्टुबन्तमाद्या गर्भस्राविण्युपनिषत् ॥ दशरात्रस्य नवमेऽहनि मरुत्वतीय एतत्सूक्तम् । विश्वजित इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । प्र मन्दिन इमा उ त्वेति मरुत्वतीयम् । आ. ८-[७?] [?] । इति ॥
> *pra mandina ity ekādaśarcam aṣṭamaṃ sūktam āṅgirasasya kutsasyārṣam | aṣṭamyādyāś catasras triṣṭubhaḥ śiṣṭāḥ sapta jagatyaḥ | indro devatā | tathā cānukrāntam | pra mandina ekādaśa kutsaś catustriṣṭubantam ādyā garbhasrāviṇy upaniṣat ‖ daśarātrasya navame 'hani marutvatīya etat sūktam | viśvajita iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | pra mandina imā u tveti marutvatīyam | Ā. 8-[7?] [?] | iti ‖*

*(Sense, mine, from the Kannada that follows: "The eighth sūkta, of eleven Ṛks, beginning* pra mandine*, is the seer-composition of Kutsa Āṅgirasa; the four beginning with the eighth are Triṣṭubh, the remaining seven Jagatī; the deity is Indra. So the Anukramaṇī: '*pra mandine* — eleven; Kutsa; four Triṣṭubh at the end; the first [Ṛk] is a* garbhasrāviṇī *[a Ṛk for the miscarriage?],* upaniṣad*.' On the ninth day of the Daśarātra this sūkta is used in the Marutvatīya [śastra]; set down in the Sūtra in the section called* Viśvajit*:* pra mandine, imā u tvā *— the Marutvatīya.")*

**Anuvāda (Kannada):** "*Pra mandine* — this sūkta is the eighth sūkta in the fifteenth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa, the son of Aṅgiras. Four Ṛks, from the eighth, are in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining seven Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said '*pra mandina ekādaśa kutsaś catustriṣṭubantam ādyā garbhasrāviṇy upaniṣat*'. On the ninth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra this sūkta is applied for the Marutvatīya mantras: it is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section called *Viśvajit*, by the aphorism *pra mandina imā u tveti marutvatīyam* (*Ā.* 8-[7?])."

"O priests! To Indra, who is *mandine* — who has [the quality of] praise, who is to be praised — offer, *prārcata*, with great force, the *vacaḥ*, the speech which has the character of praise, *pitumat*, accompanied with food that has the character of an oblation. That Indra who, with his friend the king named Ṛjiśvan, *nirahan* — killed — *kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ*: there was an Asura named Kṛṣṇa; his wives, in whom the embryos placed by him were — [Indra] killed them. The sense is that, having killed the Asura Kṛṣṇa, he killed also his pregnant wives, in order that no other offspring should arise [from them] [?]. We, *avasyavaḥ*, who wish for protection, *havāmahe* — call — for the sake of friendship, that *vṛṣaṇam* — the sprinkler of desires — *vajradakṣiṇam* — he who has the thunderbolt in the right hand — Indra, accompanied by the Maruts."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*mandine* — (O priests,) to Indra, who is worthy of praise; *pitumat* — accompanied by food in the form of oblation; *vacaḥ* — words in the form of a hymn; *pra arcata* — recite exceedingly; *yaḥ* — which Indra; *ṛjiśvanā* — together with the king named Ṛjiśvan [his friend]; *kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ* — the pregnant wives of the Asura named Kṛṣṇa; *nirahan* — killed; *avasyavaḥ* — we who wish for protection; *vṛṣaṇam* — the one who showers desired objects; *vajradakṣiṇam* — the one who holds the thunderbolt weapon in his right hand; *marutvantam* — [the one] who is together with the Maruts; *sakhyāya* — to make friendship (with us); *havāmahe* — we call."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O priests, praise, with words of hymn together with oblations, Indra, who is to be delighted by hymns. That Indra, together with his friend the king named Ṛjiśvan, killed the Asura named Kṛṣṇa, and also killed his pregnant wives, and so made it that there should be no Asura progeny. We too, desiring protection, call to us, to be our friend, that Indra who showers desired objects, holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, and is together with the Maruts."

### Page 268 (PDF 288)

*(Running head: left 268; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 101".)*

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Offer adoration with oblations to him who is delighted (with praise), who, with Rijis'wan, destroyed the pregnant wives of Krishna : desirous of protection, we invoke, to become our friend, him, who is the showerer (of benefits), who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, attended by the Maruts.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.1 (Kannada)**

"To show, by the example of the king named Ṛjiśvan, that victory and happiness are sure to come to those who obtain Indra's friendship, the Ṛk prays to Indra, desiring such friendship and also protection.

*Mandine* — *mandī mandateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ* (*Ni.* 4-[3?]1 as read [?]): derived from the root *mand*, which gives the sense of praising, [the word means] one who is worthy of praise: it shows honour. *Mandine* means 'to Indra, who is worthy of reverence, who is worthy of praise'.

Showing the derivation of the word *mandine* in the manner given above, the Nirukta-author quoted this very Ṛk (*Ni.* 4-3[1?]):"

> प्रार्चत मन्दिने पितुमद्वचः ।
> *prārcata mandine pitumad vacaḥ |*
> (*Ni.* 4-3[1?] as read [?])

"— 'to Indra, who is worthy of praise, offer and honour him with words of praise accompanied by food', is the sense.

*Pitumat* — since *andhaḥ, vājaḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-eight [as read, ?] names of food (*Ni.* 2-7 as read [?]), the word *pitu* means 'food'. Here the intention is 'together with food in the form of oblations'." 

> पितुरित्यन्ननाम पातेर्वा पिबतेर्वा प्यायतेर्वा ।
> *pitur ity annanāma pāter vā pibater vā pyāyater vā |*
> (*Ni.* 9-[2?]4 as read [?])

"— from the root *pā*, which gives the sense 'to protect', or from the root *pyai*, which gives the sense 'to grow, to fatten': the word *pitu* is formed and may be a synonym of food: such is the Nirukta-author's derivation. Later, in order to state the right meaning, [the Nirukta-author] again uses this word, in —"

> पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीम् ।
> *pitum nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīm |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-187-1 as read [?])

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.1)** *(grammar pages, pp. 270–271, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *mandine* (root *madi stutimodamadasvapnakāntigatiṣu*; *num* by *idito num dhātoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-58 as read]; the Uṇādi affix *ini*; the word *mandin*; the *i* of the affix acute; dative singular; Yāska says the same: *mandī mandateḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ* [*Ni.* 4-[3?]1 as read]); *pitumat* (*pituḥ asya asti*; *matup* by *hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-176 as read]; in the Veda, since a short vowel precedes, *matup* is acute); *arcata* (root *arca pūjāyām*; *loṭ*, second person plural; since the *ṅit*-ness is wanting, *ta* by *tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-101 as read]; *nighāta* accent); *vacaḥ* (root *vaca paribhāṣaṇe*; *asun*, the affix attached to all roots; *vacas*; the first syllable acute, the affix being *nit*; accusative singular); *kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ* (*kṛṣṇena niṣiktāḥ garbhāḥ yāsu tāḥ*; the last syllable of the first member acute by *parādiś chandasi bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-199 as read]); *ahan* (root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *laṅ*, third person singular; since the relative *yaḥ* is related to it, no *nighāta*; since the augment *aṭ* is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable); *avasyavaḥ* (root *ava rakṣaṇe*; the Uṇādi *asun*, which goes with all roots; the word *avas*; *avaḥ ātmanaḥ icchati* — in the sense 'wishes for protection for himself', *kyac* by *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 as read]; the word gets the name of a root by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-32 as read]; *u* by *kyāc chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-170 as read]; loss of *a* by *ato lopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; the word *avasyu*; the final acute by the affix; *jas*, *guṇa* by *jasi ca* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-109 as read], *av*-substitution; *avasyavaḥ*).

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.2)**

> य इन्द्रो जहृषाणेन प्रवृद्धेन मन्युना क्रोधेन व्यंसं विगतभुजं वृत्रमहन् । अवधीत् । अपि च य इन्द्रः शम्बरमेतन्नामानमसुरं चावधीत् । तथाव्रतं व्रतस्य यागादेः कर्मणो विरोधिनं पिप्रुमेतन्नामानमसुरं च य इन्द्रोऽवधीत् । किंच य इन्द्रोऽशुषं शोषकरहितं शुष्णं सर्वस्य जगतः शोषकमेतन्नामानमसुरं न्यवृणक् । न्यवर्जयत् । समूलं हतवानित्यर्थः । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायोप्ययामहे । व्यंसम् । विगतोंऽसो यस्मात् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । यणि उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः इति परस्यानुदात्तस्य स्वरितत्वम् । जहृषाणेन । हृष तुष्टौ । अत्र वृद्ध्यर्थः । छन्दसि लिट् । लिटः कानज्वेति तस्य कानजादेशः । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायामभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् । चित्त्वादन्तोदात्तत्वम् । अशुषम् । शुष शोषणे । इगुपधलक्षणः कः । शुषाः शोषका न सन्त्यस्येत्यशुषः । परादिश्छन्दसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वम् । अवृणक् । वृजी वर्जने । रौधादिकः ॥
> *ya indro jahṛṣāṇena pravṛddhena manyunā krodhena vyaṃsaṃ vigatabhujaṃ vṛtram ahan | avadhīt | api ca ya indraḥ śambaram etannāmānam asuraṃ cāvadhīt | tathāvrataṃ vratasya yāgāder karmaṇo virodhinaṃ pipruṃ etannāmānam asuraṃ ca ya indro 'vadhīt | kiṃ ca ya indro 'śuṣaṃ śoṣakarahitaṃ śuṣṇaṃ sarvasya jagataḥ śoṣakam etannāmānam asuraṃ ny avṛṇak | nyavarjayat | samūlaṃ hatavān ity arthaḥ | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe [read: hvayāmahe] | vyaṃsam | vigato 'ṃso yasmāt | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | yaṇi udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ iti parasyānudāttasya svaritatvam | jahṛṣāṇena | hṛṣa tuṣṭau | atra vṛddhyarthaḥ | chandasi liṭ | liṭaḥ kānaj veti tasya kānajādeśaḥ | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyām abhyāsasya dīrghatvam | cittvād antodāttatvam | aśuṣam | śuṣa śoṣaṇe | igupadhalakṣaṇaḥ kaḥ | śuṣāḥ śoṣakā na santy asyety aśuṣaḥ | parādiś chandasi bahulam ity uttarapadādyudāttatvam | avṛṇak | vṛjī varjane | raudhādikaḥ ‖*

*(The print's* sakhyāyopyayāmahe *is read as* sakhyāya hvayāmahe *[?].)*

"That Indra who, in swelling wrath (*jahṛṣāṇena manyunā*), killed Vṛtra, who was *vyaṃsa* — bereft of arms (shoulders); and also killed the Asura named Śambara; and likewise killed the Asura named Pipru, who was *avrata*, hostile to the rite, the sacrificial act and the like; and further, who *ny avṛṇak* — cut off, destroyed utterly — the Asura named Śuṣṇa, *aśuṣa*, who was without the dryness [? i.e. who could not be dried up], the withering of the whole world: him, Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, we call to be our friend."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read:* vyaṃsa *(a* bahuvrīhi *with the accent of its first member);* jahṛṣāṇa *(root* hṛṣ *'to be glad', with the Vedic* liṭ *and* kānac*, with lengthening of the reduplicative syllable, final acute because the affix is* cit*);* aśuṣa *(root* śuṣ *'to dry', with* ka *by* igupadha…*, 'one for whom there are no witherers' [as read], accent of the last member);* avṛṇak *(root* vṛj *'to avoid', of the* rudhādi *class).)*

"*yaḥ* — which Indra; *jahṛṣāṇena* — [with] growing; *manyunā* — wrath; *vyaṃsam* — Vṛtra, who was deprived of arms; *ahan* — killed; *yaḥ* — which Indra; *śambaram* — the Rākṣasa named Śambara; (so killed;) *yaḥ* — which Indra; *avratam* — the one who is hostile to rites such as sacrifices; *pipruṃ* — the Asura named Pipru; (killed besides;) *yaḥ indraḥ* — which Indra; *aśuṣam* — [him whom others] could not kill or wither; *śuṣṇam* — [one who withers up the world,] the Asura named Śuṣṇa; *ni avṛṇak* — uprooted completely;" *(continues on p. 273)*

"[*marutvantam* —] that Indra, together with the Maruts; *sakhyāya* — to make friendship (with us); *havāmahe* — we call."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"That Indra who killed Vṛtra, bereft of arms, in wrath growing to the highest degree; and who killed the Rākṣasa named Śambara, and the Asura named Pipru, who was hostile to rites such as sacrifice; and who uprooted completely the Asura named Śuṣṇa, who could not be held back by others, and who had the power to hold back all the world — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship and to help us."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> We invoke to be our friend, Indra, who is attended by the Maruts ; he who, with increasing wrath, slew the mutilated Vritra, and Sambara, and unrighteous Pipru, and who extirpated the unabsorbable S'ushna.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.2 (Kannada)**

"In explaining the sense of this Ṛk, there are differences in some places between Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and Skandasvāmin's bhāṣya.

*Jahṛṣāṇena manyunā vyaṃsam ahan* — to this sentence Sāyaṇa has given the explanation: '*pravṛddhena krodhena vigatabhujaṃ vṛtram avadhīt*': 'by a growing anger he killed Vṛtra, who was bereft of arms'.

Skandasvāmin explained, taking *vyaṃsa* as the name of a certain Rākṣasa, [thus:]"

> जहृषाणेन आत्मार्थं हृष्यता मन्युना मन्युनाम्ना प्रजापतिपुत्रेण सह अहन् ।
> *jahṛṣāṇena ātmārthaṃ hṛṣyatā manyunā manyunāmnā prajāpatiputreṇa saha ahan |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: 'with the Manyu — the son of Prajāpati, named Manyu — who was rejoicing for his own sake, he killed']: so, joined with Manyu, who showed the greatest delight and who was the son of Prajāpati, he killed the Asura named Vyaṃsa — one sense; or:"

> अथवा मन्युरिति क्रोधनाम । आत्मार्थं हृष्यता क्रोधेन । प्रविवेकसता [?] क्रोधेन इत्यर्थः ।
> *athavā manyur iti krodhanāma | ātmārthaṃ hṛṣyatā krodhena | praviveka-satā [?] krodhena ity arthaḥ |*

"— [that is: 'or *manyu* is a name of anger; with anger that rejoices for its own sake'] — 'by the anger that grew exceedingly' is another sense that he has given. According to this second explanation, *vyaṃsa* is a name, a proper noun, and *manyu* has only the sense of 'anger' [and not the person]. But here Skandasvāmin's construction and meaning appear to have no support; Sāyaṇa's explanation is the natural one: the word *vyaṃsa*, which means 'one whose arms have gone', is used in many Ṛks, and is an adjective of Vṛtra and of other Asuras."

*Śambaram (ahan)* — Indra's [killing of] the enemy Śambara is told in the Ṛks 1-[?]-[?], 1-5[?]-[?], 1-1[?]-[?], 1-130-[?], 1-1[?]-[?], 1-1[?]-[?]. In general, his name is found mostly alongside the Asuras Śuṣṇa, Pipru and Varcin."

> अव गिरेर्दासं शम्बरं हन्प्रावो दिवोदासं चित्राभिरूतिभिः ।

'It is uncertain whether he was a demon, according to Roth's view, which is favoured by the use of the word Asura, or a human foe, as Ludwig, Oldenberg and Hillebrandt believe.' *(English in the original.)*

(Vide *Vedic Index of Names and Subjects* by Keith and Macdonell, Vol. I, p. 532.) *(English in the original.)*

But the bhāṣya-author has called him an Asura.

*Aśuṣaṃ śuṣṇaṃ* — [Indra killed] Śuṣṇa, who could not be killed: that is, no one other than Indra could kill him. The Asura named Śuṣṇa dried up all the waters, and, though he was extremely powerful, he was at last killed by Indra. Apart from Vṛtra, this is the foe most harmful [to the world], the Asura who caused drought. After his slaying the earth became full of the abundance of crops and full of fruit."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.2)** *(grammar pages, pp. 276–277, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *vyaṃsam* (*vigataḥ aṃśaḥ yasmāt saḥ vyaṃsaḥ*; in the *bahuvrīhi* the first member keeps its accent by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 as read]; the *i* of *vi* is acute; since *yaṇ* takes its place, the unaccented *a* following it receives the *svarita* by *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-4 as read]).

### Page 277 (PDF 297)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 12 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 277.)*

The grammar of Rik 101.2 concludes: *jahṛṣāṇena* (root *hṛṣa tuṣṭau*, which has several senses, here used in the sense of *vṛddhi*; *liṭ* by *chandasi liṭ* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-105 as read], though *liṭ* is generally expected; for it *kānac* by *liṭaḥ kānac vā* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-106 as read]; doubling of the root; *halādiśeṣa* in the reduplicative; *ur at* by *ur at* [Pā. Sū. 7-4-66 as read]; since *raparatva* comes, again *halādiśeṣa*; since the affix is *kit*, no *guṇa* of the penult of the root; *ṇ* for the *n* of the affix by *āṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye 'pi* [Pā. Sū. 8-4-2 as read], on account of the *ṣ*; the form *jahṛṣāṇa*; lengthening of the reduplicative in the Saṃhitā by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 as read]; since *kānac* is *cit*, final acute by *citaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; instrumental singular); *manyunā* (root *manu avabodhane*; the Uṇādi *yu*; final acute by the affix; instrumental); *ahan* (root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*, *adādi*; *laṅ*, third person singular; because *yaḥ* is related to it, no *nighāta* by *yadvṛttān nityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; since the augment *aṭ* is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable); *aśuṣam* (root *śuṣa śoṣaṇe*; *ka* by *igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-135 as read]; since *kit*, no *guṇa* of the penult; *śuṣāḥ śoṣakāḥ na santy asya iti aśuṣaḥ*; the accent of the second member by *parādiś chandasi bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-199 as read]; accusative singular); *avṛṇak* (root *vṛjī varjane*, *rudhādi*; *laṅ*, third person singular, *tip*; loss of the *i* by *itaś ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-100 as read]; *śnam* by *rudhādibhyaḥ śnam* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-78 as read]; *num* and its *m*-augment after the last vowel by *midaco 'ntyāt paraḥ* [Pā. Sū. 1-1-47 as read]; loss of *t* by *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-68 as read]; *k* for *j* by *coḥ kuḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-30 as read]; since a *ṛ* precedes it, *ṇ* for the *n* of the vikaraṇa; since the relative *yaḥ* is related to it, no *nighāta*, and since the augment *aṭ* is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable). The Rik is closed with *‖ 2 ‖* and a printed ornament.

## Rik 101.3 — printed pp. 278–[281]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.3)**

> यस्य द्यावापृथिवी पौंस्यं महद्यस्य व्रते वरुणो यस्य सूर्यः ।
> यस्येन्द्रस्य सिन्धवः सश्चति व्रतं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ३ ॥

*yasya dyāvāpṛthivī pauṃsyaṃ mahad yasya vrate varuṇo yasya sūryaḥ | yasyendrasya sindhavaḥ saścati vrataṃ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.3)**

> यस्य । द्यावापृथिवी इति । पौंस्यम् । महत् । यस्य । व्रते । वरुणः । यस्य । सूर्यः ।
> यस्य । इन्द्रस्य । सिन्धवः । सश्चति । व्रतम् । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ३ ॥

*yasya | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | pauṃsyam | mahat | yasya | vrate | varuṇaḥ | yasya | sūryaḥ | yasya | indrasya | sindhavaḥ | saścati | vratam | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.3)**

> यस्येन्द्रस्य महद्विपुलं पौंस्यं बलं द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्योरनुवर्तते । यस्य चेन्द्रस्य व्रते नियमरूपे कर्मणि वरुणो वर्तते । वरुणोऽपीन्द्रस्य नियमनं नातिक्रामतीत्यर्थः । अपि च सूर्योऽपि यस्येन्द्रस्य व्रते वर्तते । तथा यस्येन्द्रस्य व्रतं कर्म सिन्धवो नद्यः सश्चति । वचनव्यत्ययः । गच्छन्ति । सश्चतिर्गतिकर्मा । इन्द्रेणानुशिष्टाः प्रवहन्तीत्यर्थः । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायाह्वयामहे ॥ द्यावापृथिवी । द्यौश्च पृथिवी च द्यावापृथिव्यौ । दिवो द्यावेति द्यावादेशः । स चाद्युदात्तो निपातितः । पृथिवीशब्दो जातिष्प्रत्ययान्तोऽन्तोदात्तः । देवताद्वन्द्वे चेत्युभयपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । वा छन्दसीति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥
> *yasyendrasya mahad vipulaṃ pauṃsyaṃ balaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī dyāvāpṛthivyor anuvartate | yasya cendrasya vrate niyamarūpe karmaṇi varuṇo vartate | varuṇo 'pīndrasya niyamanaṃ nātikrāmatīty arthaḥ | api ca sūryo 'pi yasyendrasya vrate vartate | tathā yasyendrasya vrataṃ karma sindhavo nadyaḥ saścati | vacanavyatyayaḥ | gacchanti | saścatir gatikarmā | indreṇānuśiṣṭāḥ pravahantīty arthaḥ | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyāhvayāmahe ‖ dyāvāpṛthivī | dyauś ca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivyau | divo dyāveti dyāvādeśaḥ | sa cādyudātto nipātitaḥ | pṛthivīśabdo jāṣpratyayānto 'ntodāttaḥ | devatādvandve cety ubhayapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | vā chandasīti pūrvasavarṇadīrghaḥ ‖*

"Of that Indra whose great, abundant manly strength is followed by heaven and earth, and in whose *vrata* — in the work that has the form of a [fixed] rule — Varuṇa stays: the sense is that even Varuṇa does not go beyond Indra's regulation. And also the sun stays in the *vrata* of that Indra. And likewise the rivers, the streams, *saścati* [plural, by exchange of number] — go, in the work of that Indra: *saścati* is a verb of going. The sense is that, instructed by Indra, they flow on. Him, that Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* dyāvāpṛthivī *(a dvandva of* dyu *and* pṛthivī*, with* dyāvā *for* div *by* divo dyāvā*, the accent on the first syllable by* nipātana*; the second member ends in* ṅīṣ*/*jāṣ*, acute on the last; the accent of both members stays by* devatādvandve ca*, and the long vowel is of the same class by* vā chandasi*).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)** *(begins on p. 279)*

"*yasya* — of which Indra; *mahat* — exceeding; *pauṃsyam* — the strength; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — [that has pervaded] heaven and earth, both; *yasya* — of which Indra; *vrate* — in the command, which has the form of work; *varuṇaḥ* — Varuṇa (who stands firm, intent on the work to be done), and; *sūryaḥ* — the sun too; *yasya* — of which Indra; (who stand intent on the work to be done in obedience to the command;) *yasya indrasya* — of which Indra; *vratam* — the work of command; *sindhavaḥ* — the rivers too; *saścati* — go on carrying out (they flow); *marutvantam* — Indra, thus together with the Maruts; *sakhyāya* — to make friendship (with us); *havāmahe* — we call."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra whose exceeding strength has pervaded heaven and earth both; in whose command Varuṇa and the sun stand firm, intent on the work to be done; and in whose commanded work the rivers too flow — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> We invoke to become our friend, Indra who is attended by the Maruts ; whose great power (pervades) heaven and earth, in whose service Varuna and Surya are steadfast, and whose command the rivers obey.

"— so, since he has pervaded both heaven and earth, which are difficult to measure and have extensive expanse, and shown his own strength, in this Ṛk also it is described that *yasya mahat pauṃsyaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī* (*saścati*). It is because he has such strength and sovereignty that Varuṇa and the others are obedient to his commands."

> विश्वे ते इन्द्र वीर्यं देवा अनु क्रतुं ददुः ।
> *viśve te indra vīryaṃ devā anu kratuṃ daduḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-6-3 as read [?])

"— that all the gods yield to Indra's valour and prowess; and —"

> यदा सूर्यममुं दिवि शुक्रं ज्योतिरधारयः । आदित्ते विश्वा भुवनानि येमिरे ॥

"— in many places it is praised that, when Indra established the shining sun in the mid-air, all the worlds became subject to him. The same points are described here.

*Vratam* — here *vrata* means 'work'. The rain-like and sacrifice-like works, and the other works as well, are carried out by Indra's command.

*Saścati* — *vartate*. Since *ayate*, *saścati* and the like are read among the twenty-two [as read, ?] names of verbs of going (*Ni.* 2-[?] as read [?]), *saścati* means 'goes'; that is, 'carries out'."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.3)** *(grammar pages, pp. 280–281, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *dyāvāpṛthivī* (*dyauś ca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivyau*; in the compound, *dyāvā* for *div* by *divo dyāvā* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-29 as read]; this substitute is fixed by *nipātana* as acute on the first syllable; the word *pṛthivī*, ending in the affix *ṅīṣ*, is acute on the last; then in the compound the accent of both members is retained by *devatādvandve ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-141 as read]; to it, the dual ending following, the single substitute of the previous homogeneous long vowel comes by *vā chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-106 as read]); *pauṃsyam* (*puṃsaḥ bhāvaḥ pauṃsyam*; *ṣyañ*; as it is *ñit*, *vṛddhi* by *taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ*; acute on the first syllable by *ñnityādir nityam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 as read]); *sūryaḥ* (*sarati ākāśe iti sūryaḥ*; root *sṛ gatau*; *kyap*-ending form fixed by *nipātana* in *rājasūyasūrya…* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-114 as read]; since the affix is *pit*, unaccented, the root's accent remains).

### Page 281 (PDF 301)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 12 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 281.)*

The grammar of Rik 101.3 concludes: *sindhavaḥ* (root *syandū prasravaṇe*; *uṇ* by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]1 as read, ?], with *samprasāraṇa* of the root and *dh* for *d*, by *skandeḥ samprasāraṇaṃ dhaś ca*; the form *sindhu*; in the nominative plural *jas*, *guṇa* by *jasi ca*, *av*-substitution); *saścati* (root *saśca gatau*; *laṭ*, third person plural; the singular *tip* by *vyatyayo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read]; *śap*; because of the relative [*yasya*], no *nighāta*; since *śap* and *tip* are *pit*, unaccented, the root's accent remains). The Rik is closed with *‖ 3 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

## Rik 101.4 — printed pp. 281–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.4)**

> यो अश्वानां यो गवां गोपतिर्वशी य आरितः कर्मणिकर्मणि स्थिरः ।
> वीळोश्चिदिन्द्रो यो असुन्वतो वधो मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ४ ॥

*yo aśvānāṃ yo gavāṃ gopatir vaśī ya āritaḥ karmaṇi-karmaṇi sthiraḥ | vīḷoś cid indro yo asunvato vadho marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.4)**

> यः । अश्वानाम् । यः । गवाम् । गोऽपतिः । वशी । यः । आरितः । कर्मणिऽकर्मणि । स्थिरः ।
> वीळोः । चित् । इन्द्रः । यः । असुन्वतः । वधः । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ४ ॥

*yaḥ | aśvānām | yaḥ | gavām | go-patiḥ | vaśī | yaḥ | āritaḥ | karmaṇi-karmaṇi | sthiraḥ | vīḷoḥ | cit | indraḥ | yaḥ | asunvataḥ | vadhaḥ | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.4)**

> यः इन्द्रोऽश्वानामीशानानां पतिरधिपतिः । तथा य इन्द्रो गोपतिः । न केवलमेकस्या गोः किन्तु सर्वासामित्याह गवामिति । सर्वासां गवामधिपतिर्भवति । वशी अपराधीनः स्वतन्त्र इत्यर्थः । अपि च य इन्द्रः कर्मणि कर्मणि सर्वेषु कर्मसु स्थिरो नैश्चल्येनावतिष्ठमान आरितः स्तुतिभिः प्रत्यृतः प्राप्तो भवति । आरितः प्रत्यृतः स्तोमानिति निरुक्तम् । नि. ५-[३?]२ [?] । यश्चेन्द्रोऽसुन्वतः सुन्वतां योगानुष्ठात्रॄणां विरोधिनो वीळोश्चित् दृढस्यापि शत्रोर्वधो हन्ता तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायोप्ययामहे ॥ गवाम् । न गोश्वन्साववर्णे । पा. ६-१-[१८?]२ [?] । इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वस्य प्रतिषेधः । गोपतिः । पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वम् । आरितः । ऋ गतौ । अस्माण्ण्यन्तात्क्तः । आगमानुशासनस्यानित्यत्वात्पुगागमाभावः । यद्वा । सूचिसूत्रिमूत्र्यृत्यर्तिभ्यश्च [?] । पा. ३-२-[?] । इति विहितस्य यजो यजोऽचि [?] चेत्यत्र चकारेण बहुलग्रहणानुकर्षणादन्येमित्रके लुकि प्रत्ययलक्षणेन सन्यजोरिति …(the line is clotted) … ऋ इत्येतस्य द्विर्वचने उरदत्वहलादिशेषयोः सतो रुग्रिकौ च लुकीति रुक् । ततो निष्ठायां छान्दस इडागमः । ऋकारस्य यणादेशः रो रीत्यभ्यासरेफलोपः । द्र्लोपे पूर्वस्य दीर्घोऽणः इति दीर्घत्वम् । वधः । कृत्यल्युटो बहुलमिति बहुलवचनाद्धनश्च वध इति कर्तर्यप् वधादेशश्च । स चान्तः । अतो लोपे उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण प्रत्ययस्योदात्तत्वम् ॥
> *ya indro 'śvānām īśānānāṃ patir adhipatiḥ | tathā ya indro gopatiḥ | na kevalam ekasyā goḥ kintu sarvāsām ity āha gavām iti | sarvāsāṃ gavām adhipatir bhavati | vaśī aparādhīnaḥ svatantra ity arthaḥ | api ca ya indraḥ karmaṇi karmaṇi sarveṣu karmasu sthiro naiścalyenāvatiṣṭhamāna āritaḥ stutibhiḥ pratyṛtaḥ prāpto bhavati | āritaḥ pratyṛtaḥ stomān iti niruktam | Ni. 5-[3?]2 [?] | yaś cendro 'sunvataḥ sunvatāṃ yogānuṣṭhātṝṇāṃ virodhino vīḷoś cit dṛḍhasyāpi śatror vadho hantā taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe ‖ gavām | na gośvansāvavarṇe | Pā. 6-1-[18?]2 [?] | iti vibhakter udāttatvasya pratiṣedhaḥ | gopatiḥ | patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvam | āritaḥ | ṛ gatau | asmāṇ ṇyantāt ktaḥ | āgamānuśāsanasyānityatvāt pugāgamābhāvaḥ | yadvā | sūcisūtrimūtryṛtyartibhyaś ca [?] | … [the middle is clotted] … vadhaḥ | kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam iti bahulavacanād dhanaś ca vadha iti kartary ap vadhādeśaś ca | sa cāntaḥ | ato lope udāttanivṛttisvareṇa pratyayasyodāttatvam ‖*

"That Indra who is the lord, the sovereign, of the horses, the ruling ones. And that Indra is the lord of the cows (*gopati*): not of a single cow only, but of all; so he says, *gavām* — he is the sovereign of all cows. *Vaśī* — not subordinate to another: independent. And that Indra, in each and every work (*karmaṇi karmaṇi*), *sthiraḥ* — standing without moving — *āritaḥ*, *pratyṛtaḥ* — reached, attained, by praises. [The Nirukta:] *āritaḥ pratyṛtaḥ stomān* [as read (*Ni.* 5-[3?]2 [?])]. And that Indra who is the destroyer (*vadhaḥ*) of the enemy of those who perform sacrifices, the *asunvat*, the one who presses no Soma, even though he is strong (*vīḷoḥ cit*) — him, the Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read:* gavām *(the genitive plural; the prohibition of the acute on the ending by* na gośvansāvavarṇe… *[Pā. Sū. 6-1-[18?]2, as read [?]]);* gopati *(the accent of the first member by* patyāvaiśvarye*);* arita *(root* ṛ *'to go', with the causative* ṇic *and* kta*, no* puk *because the rules of augment-teaching are not invariable; or from* ṛ *with* yaj *…; the middle is clotted and not reproduced [?]);* vadha *(the affix* ap *in the agent with the substitute* vadha *for* han*). The sūtra numerals are small and doubtful.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*yaḥ* — which Indra; *aśvānām* — of horses; *adhipatiḥ* — the sovereign; *yaḥ* — which Indra; *gavām* — of all cows; *gopatiḥ* — the protector of the cows, and; *vaśī* — independent (not subordinate to another); *yaḥ* — which Indra; *karmaṇi karmaṇi* — in every sacrificial act; *sthiraḥ* — standing firm; *āritaḥ* — praised by the praisers, or brought near (reached by all); *yaḥ indraḥ* — which Indra; *asunvataḥ* — those who hate the performers of sacrifices; *vīḷoḥ cit* — even a powerful enemy; *vadhaḥ* — is the killer; *marutvantam* — together with the Maruts, that Indra; *sakhyāya* — to make friendship (with us); *havāmahe* — we call."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Which Indra is the sovereign of all horses and cows; who is independent; who stands firm in every sacrificial act and is praised by the praisers; and who, even if the enemy is mighty, slays him who is without sacrifice and who hates those who sacrifice; that Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

### Page 283 (PDF 303)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 12 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 283.)*

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Who is the lord over all horses and cattle, who is independent, who, propitiated by praise, is constant in every act, and who is the slayer of the obstinate abstainer from libations : we invoke to become our friend, Indra, attended by the Maruts.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.4 (Kannada)**

"*Gavāṃ gopatiḥ* — *na kevalam ekasyā goḥ kintu sarvāsām ity āha gavām iti* | *sarvāsāṃ gavām adhipatir bhavati*: [Sāyaṇa] has explained that, since he is the sovereign of all cows, the repetition in *gavāṃ gopatiḥ* [*go*… *gavām*] is [only apparent]. But Skandasvāmin:"

> गोशब्दोऽत्राप्शब्दवचनः सोमवचनो वा स्तुतिवचनो वा स्तोत्रवचनो वा । पतिशब्दोऽप्यधिपतिवचनः पालयितृवचनो वा । अपां वा सोमस्य वा स्तुतीनां वा स्तोत्र्याणां वा अधिपतिः पालयिता वेत्यर्थः ।
> *gośabdo 'tra apśabdavacanaḥ somavacano vā stutivacano vā stotravacano vā | patiśabdo 'py adhipativacanaḥ pālayitṛvacano vā | apāṃ vā somasya vā stutīnāṃ vā stotryāṇāṃ vā adhipatiḥ pālayitā vety arthaḥ |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read)

"— [that is: here the word *go* is a word for water, or for Soma, or for praise, or for praisers; and the word *pati* is a word for lord or protector: the sense is 'lord or protector of the waters, or of Soma, or of the praises, or of the praisers']. For the word *go* here, any meaning may be given among waters, Soma, praise or praiser: he explains that it means 'lord of water, or of Soma, or of praise, or of praiser'.

*Vaśī* — Skandasvāmin has made the construction *yaś cāśvānāṃ gavāṃ ca vaśī* and given it the meaning that he rules the horses and cows; and for the word *gopati* he has given the above meaning. But Sāyaṇa gives for the word *vaśī* the sense *aparādhīnaḥ svatantraḥ*, 'independent'."

> यस्य ते नू चिदादिशं न मिनन्ति स्वराज्यम् । न देवो नाध्रिगुर्जनः ॥
> *yasya te nū cid ādiśaṃ na minanti svarājyam | na devo nādhrigur janaḥ ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-[?]3-11 as read [?])

> त्वमिन्द्राभिभूरसि त्वं सूर्यमरोचयः । विश्वकर्मा विश्वदेवो महाँ असि ॥
> *tvam indrābhibhūr asi tvaṃ sūryam arocayaḥ | viśvakarmā viśvadevo mahām̐ asi ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-98-2 as read [?])

### Page 284 (PDF 304)

*(Running head: left 284; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 101".)*

"— since in such Ṛks Indra alone is the one who commands the whole universe, it is he who is independent. As is said in the third Ṛk of this very sūkta —"

> यस्य द्यावापृथिवी पौंस्यं महद्यस्य व्रते वरुणो यस्य सूर्यः । यस्येन्द्रस्य सिन्धवः सश्चति व्रतं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥
> *yasya dyāvāpṛthivī pauṃsyaṃ mahad yasya vrate varuṇo yasya sūryaḥ | yasyendrasya sindhavaḥ saścati vrataṃ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-101-3 as read [?]; Rik 3 of the present sūkta)

"— Varuṇa, the sun and all the rivers follow the command of that Indra, and all affairs of the universe go on subject to him. Everything is subject to him; he is subject to nothing. He is truly independent.

*Āritaḥ* — *āgata ity arthaḥ | punaḥ punaḥ sarvayajñeṣv āgatas san ā yajñaparisamāpter aviśālī*: [Skandasvāmin:] 'he who, having come again and again to all sacrifices, remains till the completion of the sacrifice, unmoving' — that is, he who stands in place at every step of the sacrifice until the sacrifice is completed: Skandasvāmin's explanation. Sāyaṇa, quoting the Nirukta sentence *āritaḥ pratyṛtaḥ stomān* (*Ni.* 5-[3?]2 as read [?]), says *stutibhiḥ pratyṛtaḥ prāpto bhavati* — 'he is attained by praises'. This meaning is the more fitting. In the same way —"

> वृतंचयः सहुरिर्विक्ष्वारित इन्द्रस्य वोचं प्र कृतानि वीर्या ।
> *vṛtaṃcayaḥ sahurir vikṣv ārita indrasya vocaṃ pra kṛtāni vīryā |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-1[?]-3 as read [?]; the first word clotted in print [?])

"— in this Ṛk too, for the word *āritaḥ* used there, the sense is *pālakatvena prāpitaḥ*, 'brought near as protector': he was brought near as a protector; the sense is that he came together with all.

*Asunvataḥ* — one who does not press the Soma juice, and does not do sacrifices and the like; or one who hates the performers of sacrifices.

*Vīḷoś cit* — *vīḷayatiś ca prīḷayatiś ca saṃstambhakarmaṇau* (*Ni.* 5-[?]) — the Nirukta-author says that the words *vīḷa* and *prīḷa* are used in the sense of 'hard' or 'firm', and has quoted the Ṛk"

> तद्देवानां देवतमाय कर्त्वमश्रथ्नन्दृळ्हाववदन्त वीळिता ।
> *tad devānāṃ devatamāya kartvam aśrathnan dṛḷhāv avadanta vīḷitā |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-31-[?] as read [?])

"— there, for the word *vīḷitā*, the sense *dṛḍhīkṛtā* is shown; so here also *vīḷoḥ* means *dṛḍhasya*, 'of the firm, hard': in the enemy sense it is construed 'extremely hard, or firm'. 'However strong the enemy may be, however hard, he destroys him,' is the sense. And for the full sense of the word *vīḷa* and the fitting context of its use, also —" *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.4)** *(grammar pages, pp. 285–[286], noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *gavām* (the word *go*; genitive plural; the acute on the ending, which *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 as read] would give, is prevented by *na gośvansāvavarṇarāḍaṅkukrukṣuk…* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-182 as read]); *gopatiḥ* (*gavāṃ patiḥ gopatiḥ*; the accent of the first member by *patyāvaiśvarye* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-18 as read]); *vaśī* (*vaśaḥ asyāsti iti vaśī*; in the possessive sense *ini* by *ata iniṭhanau* [Pā. Sū. 5-2-115 as read]; acute on the affix); *āritaḥ* (root *ṛ gatau*; the causative *ṇic* and *kta* in the sense of the passive by *niṣṭhā* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-102 as read]; though *puk* would be expected by *arttihrīvlī…* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-36 as read] after the *ṇic* ending, the augment does not come, by the statement *āgamānuśāsanam anityam*; *vṛddhi* of the root because of *ṇic*; *raparatva*; *iṭ* for the affix by *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ*; or by the statement *sūcisūtrimūtryaṭyartibhyaś ca* [vārttika, Pā. 3-2-[?]3 as read, ?] the affix *yaj*, which is lost by *yajo yaji ca* [Pā. Sū. 2-4-[?]4 as read, ?]; by *pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam* [Pā. Sū. 1-1-62 as read] the *ṅit*-like effect remains; doubling of the root by *sanyaṅoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-9 as read]; in the reduplicative *a* by *ur at* [Pā. Sū. 7-4-66 as read]; *halādiśeṣa*; *ruk* by *rurikau ca luki* [Pā. Sū. 7-4-[?]1 as read]; *iṭ* for the affix *ta* in the Veda; *yaṇ* for the *ṛ*; with *ar* + *r* + *ita*, loss of the former *r* by *ro ri* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-14 as read]; since the *r* is lost, lengthening of the preceding vowel by *ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-111 as read]; final acute by the affix); *karmaṇi karmaṇi* (doubling by *nityavīpsayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-4 as read]); *asunvataḥ* (root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *śatṛ* in the sense of the present; *śnu*; the form *sunvat*; *na sunvan asunvan*; in the negative *tatpuruṣa* the accent of the first member kept by *tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-2 as read]).

### Page 286 (PDF 306)

*(Running head: left 286; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 101".)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 101.4, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])**

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 101.4 concludes: *vadhaḥ* (by the word *bahulam* in *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-113 as read] and by *hanaś ca vadhaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-76 as read], the affix *ap* in the agent; by its connection, the substitute *vadha* for the root *han*; this ends in *a*; loss of the *a* by *ato lopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; since the affix *ap* is unaccented, and the loss of the acute *a* is made, the affix is made acute by *anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-161 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 4 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

## Rik 101.5 — printed pp. 286–[?]

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.5)**

> *ya indro viśvasya jagato gacchataḥ prāṇataḥ praśvasataḥ prāṇijātasya patiḥ svāmī | yaś ca brahmaṇe brāhmaṇajātibhyo 'ṅgirobhyaḥ prathamo 'nyebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvabhāvī san paṇibhir apahṛtā gā avindat | alabhata | anyebhyo devebhyaḥ pūrvam eva tair asurair yuddhvā gāḥ svayam alabhatety arthaḥ | api ca ya indro dasyūn upakṣapayitṝn asurān adharān nikṛṣṭān stṛtvā [?] avātirat avadhīt | avatiratir vadhakarmā | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe ‖ jagataḥ | gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau | vartamāne pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca | U. 2-84 [?] | ity atipratyayānto nipātito jagacchabda ādyudāttaḥ | prāṇataḥ | śvasa prāṇane ana ca | asmāl laṭaḥ śatṛ | adāditvāc chapo luk | śatur anuma iti vibhakter udāttatvam | ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputreti visarjanīyasya satvam ‖*

"That Indra who is the *pati*, the lord, the master, of the whole world — of all that moves, breathes, draws breath: of the whole race of living beings. And who *brahmaṇe* — for the Brāhmaṇa race, the Aṅgirases — being first (*prathamaḥ*), prior to the other gods, *avindat* — found, obtained — the cows that had been carried off by the Paṇis; that is, before the other gods, himself fought those Asuras and got back the cows. And that Indra who *avātirat* — killed — the Dasyus, the Asuras who cause destruction, *adharān*, the lowly, [having laid them low] [?]. *Avatirati* is a verb meaning 'to kill'. Him, the Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend."

Sū. 2-84, as read, ?], acute on the first syllable);* prāṇat *(root* śvas *'to breathe' with* ana ca *…, then* laṭ *→* śatṛ*,* luk *of* śap*, acute on the ending by* śatur anumo nadyajādī*;* visarga *→* s *by* ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…*).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*yaḥ* — which Indra; *viśvasya* — of the whole; *jagataḥ* — of all moving beings; *prāṇataḥ* — of all creatures that breathe; *patiḥ* — the lord; *yaḥ* — which Indra; *brahmaṇe* — to the Aṅgirases of the Brāhmaṇa race; *prathamaḥ* — first (before the other gods); *gāḥ* — the cows (carried off by the Paṇis); *avindat* — obtained and gave; *yaḥ indraḥ* — which Indra; *dasyūn* — the Asuras who do harm; *adharān* — made low (humble); *avātirat* — killed (such); *marutvantam* — that Indra together with the Maruts; *sakhyāya* — to make friendship (with us); *havāmahe* — we call."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Which Indra is lord of all moving and breathing creatures; who, being before the other gods, fought with the Paṇis and first obtained for the Aṅgirases the cows that had been carried off; and who humbled and killed the Asuras who have the form of Dasyus — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Who is the lord of all moving and breathing creatures, who first recovered the (stolen) cows for the Brahman and who slew the humbled Dasyus : we invoke to become our friend, Indra, attended by the Maruts.

"— thus the all-pervading lordship of Indra is praised.

*Brahmaṇe prathamaḥ gāḥ avindat* — for the word *brahmaṇe*, Skandasvāmin gives *brāhmaṇādīnāṃ caturṇām api varṇānām*: 'he caused [the people of] the four castes, beginning with Brāhmaṇas, to get back the cows carried off by the Asuras'. But Sāyaṇa has given for the word *brahmaṇe* the sense *aṅgirobhyaḥ*, 'to the Aṅgirases'. This meaning also is fitting. For Indra's relation with the Aṅgirases is very close, and Indra's pride in the Aṅgirases is exceedingly great. This subject is told in the Ṛksaṃhitā itself —"

> *vīḷau satīr abhi dhīrā atṛndan prācāhinvan manasā sapta viprāḥ | viśvām avindan pathyām ṛtasya prajānann it tā namasā viveśa ‖ vidad yadī saramā rugṇam adrer mahi pāthaḥ pūrvyaṃ sadhryak kaḥ | agraṃ nayat supady akṣarāṇām acchā ravaṃ prathamā jānatī gāt ‖ agacchad u vipratamaḥ sakhīyann asūdayat sukṛte garbham adriḥ | sasāna maryo yuvabhir makhasyann athābhavad aṅgirāḥ sadyo arcan ‖*

"In former times the cows of the Aṅgirases were carried off by the Asuras called Paṇis, who hid them in a secret place on a mountain. Then the Aṅgirases prayed to Indra that they might get those cows. Indra, to search for them, sent Saramā, the bitch of the gods." *(the passage continues on the next page)*

"[Saramā, going and] finding the cows, and telling Indra the place where they were, Indra went, brought the cows, and gave them to the Aṅgirases; and Indra became their worshipful deity: this tale is told in the Ṛks 10-108 [as read [?]]. In accordance with this, Sāyaṇa's meaning here is also right.

*Yaḥ dasyūn adharān avātirat* — the explanation of the word *dasyu* was given in the special topics of the twelfth Ṛk [as read, ?] of the previous sūkta [Sūkta 100]. The sense is that he overcame all the Asuras, humbling them.

*Avātirat* — *dabhnoti, śṛṇāti* and the like are read among the [thirty-three, as read, ?] names of 'killing' (*Ni.* 2-[?]0): hence *avātirat* means 'killed'."

"— as said in this Ṛk, here too *avātirat* means 'destroyed'.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.5)** *(grammar pages, pp. 289–[290], noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *jagataḥ* (root *gamḷ sṛpḷ gatau*; *ati* fixed by *nipātana* among the words like *pṛṣat, bṛhat, mahat, jagat* by *pṛṣadbṛhanmahajjagacchatṛvac ca* [Uṇ. Sū. 2-[?]84 as read, ?]; the word *jagat* is acute on the first syllable); *prāṇataḥ* (root *śvasa prāṇane*, also *ana*; *śatṛ* in the sense of the present; preverb *pra*; with *an* + *at*, the *luk* of *śap* by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 2-4-72 as read]; *pra* + *anat*, the *n* of the root changed to *ṇ* by *aniteḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-4-19 as read]; since *num* is wanting, the ending follows the *śatṛ* and the ending is acute by *śaturanumo nadyajādī* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-173 as read]; *prāṇat* + *patiḥ*: in the genitive the visarga becomes *s* by *ṣaṣṭhyāḥ patiputra…* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-53 as read]); *gāḥ* (the word *go*; accusative plural; the *ā* becomes the single substitute, by *auto 'mśasoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-93 as read]; *s* → *ru* → visarga); *avindat* (root *vidḷ lābhe*; *laṅ*, third person singular, *tip*; loss of the *i* by *itaś ca*; *śa* by *tudādibhyaḥ śaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-77 as read]; *num* by *śemuc… ādīnām* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-59 as read], after the last vowel of the root; the augment *aṭ*; the form *avindat*; the relative…) *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

### Page 290 (PDF 310)

*(Running head: left 290; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 101".)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 101.5, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])**

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 101.5 concludes: *avindat* (continued: *yadvṛttānnityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read] — since the relative is related to it, no *nighāta*; since the augment *aṭ* is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable); *dasyūn* (root *dasu upakṣaye*; *yu* by *yajimaniśundhidasijanibhyo yuḥ* [Uṇ. Sū. 3-[2?]00 as read, ?]; by its being in the *vṛṣādi* class, acute on the first syllable by *vṛṣādīnāṃ ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-[2?]03 as read]; accusative plural); *adharān* (*ava* with the lengthened *a*… *adhara*, with *ru* [i.e. *r*] by *samāsapāde*…, [Pā. Sū. 8-2-[?]9 as read], and the nasal inserted before it by *ato 'ṭi nityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-3 as read], the preceding being always nasalized); *avātirat* (the root *tira*, preceded by the preverb *ava*, is used in the sense of killing; *laṅ*, third person singular; since the relative is related to it, no *nighāta*; the augment *aṭ* being acute, the word is acute on the first syllable; since the verb is acute, the preverb [*ava*] receives the *nighāta* accent by *tiṅ codāttavati* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-71 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 5 ‖* and a printed ornament.

## Rik 101.6 — printed pp. 290–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.6)**

> यः शूरेभिर्हव्यो यश्च भीरुभिर्यो धावद्भिर्ह्वयते यश्च जिग्युभिः ।
> इन्द्रं यं विश्वा भुवनाभि संदधुर्मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ६ ॥

*yaḥ śūrebhir havyo yaś ca bhīrubhir yo dhāvadbhir hvayate yaś ca jigyubhiḥ | indraṃ yaṃ viśvā bhuvanābhi saṃdadhur marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 6 ‖*

### Page 291 (PDF 311)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 13 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 291.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.6)**

> यः । शूरेभिः । हव्यः । यः । च । भीरुऽभिः । यः । धावत्ऽभिः । ह्वयते । यः । च । जिग्युऽभिः ।
> इन्द्रम् । यम् । विश्वा । भुवना । अभि । सम्ऽदधुः । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ६ ॥

*yaḥ | śūrebhiḥ | havyaḥ | yaḥ | ca | bhīru-bhiḥ | yaḥ | dhāvat-bhiḥ | hvayate | yaḥ | ca | jigyu-bhiḥ | indram | yam | viśvā | bhuvanā | abhi | saṃ-dadhuḥ | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.6)**

> य इन्द्रः शूरेभिः शौर्योपेतैः पुरुषैर्हव्यो योद्धुमाह्वातव्यः । यश्च भीरुभिर्भयशीलैः कातरैः पुरुषैः सहायार्थमाह्वातव्यः । अपि च य इन्द्रो धावद्भिः पराजयेन पलायमानैर्ह्वयते रक्षार्थमाहूयते । यश्च जिग्युभिः प्राप्तजयैराहूयते । यं चेन्द्रं विश्वा भुवना सर्वाणि भूतजातानि स्वेषु स्वेषु कार्येष्वभि संदधुः । अभिमुख्येन स्थापयन्ति । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायोप्ययामहे ॥ शूरेभिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति भिस ऐसभावः । हव्यः । ह्वयतेरचो यदिति यत् । ह्न इत्यनुवृत्तौ बहुलं छन्दसीति सम्प्रसारणम् । गुणे धातोस्तन्निमित्तस्यैव वेत्यक्वादेशः । भीरुभिः । भियः क्रुक्लुकनौ । उ. २-४१ [?] । इति क्रुप्रत्ययः । धावद्भिः । धावु गतौ । सर्तेर्वेगितायां शपि पाघ्रेत्यादिना धावादेशः । शपः पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वम् । शतुश्च लसार्वधातुकस्वरेण धातुस्वरः शिष्यते । जिग्युभिः । जि जये । लिटः क्वसुः । द्विर्वचने सन्यटोर्जेर्गिरित्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य जकारस्य कुत्वम् । भस्य यस्यादित्वेन भत्वाद्वसोः सम्प्रसारणमिति सम्प्रसारणम् । छान्दसोऽन्त्यलोपः ॥
> *ya indraḥ śūrebhiḥ śauryopetaiḥ puruṣair havyo yoddhum āhvātavyaḥ | yaś ca bhīrubhir bhayaśīlaiḥ kātaraiḥ puruṣaiḥ sahāyārtham āhvātavyaḥ | api ca ya indro dhāvadbhiḥ parājayena palāyamānair hvayate rakṣārtham āhūyate | yaś ca jigyubhiḥ prāptajayair āhūyate | yaṃ cendraṃ viśvā bhuvanā sarvāṇi bhūtajātāni sveṣu sveṣu kāryeṣv abhi saṃdadhuḥ | abhimukhyena sthāpayanti | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyopyayāmahe ‖ śūrebhiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti bhisa aisabhāvaḥ | havyaḥ | hvayater aco yad iti yat | hna ity anuvṛttau bahulaṃ chandasīti samprasāraṇam | guṇe dhātos tannimittasyaiva vety akvādeśaḥ [?] | bhīrubhiḥ | bhiyaḥ krukluknau | U. 2-41 [?] | iti krupratyayaḥ | dhāvadbhiḥ | dhāvu gatau | sarter vegitāyāṃ śapi pāghretyādinā dhāvādeśaḥ | śapaḥ pittvād anudāttatvam | śatuś ca lasārvadhātukasvareṇa dhātusvaraḥ śiṣyate | jigyubhiḥ | ji jaye | liṭaḥ kvasuḥ | dvirvacane sanyaṭor jer giḥ ity abhyāsād uttarasya jakārasya kutvam | bhasya yasyāditvena bhatvād vasoḥ samprasāraṇam iti samprasāraṇam | chāndaso 'ntyalopaḥ ‖*

"That Indra who is to be called, for fighting, by heroes (*śūrebhiḥ*), men endowed with valour; and who is to be called for help by cowards (*bhīrubhiḥ*), men of fearful nature. And that Indra who is called for protection by those who run away (*dhāvadbhiḥ*), fleeing from defeat; and who is called by those who have won victory (*jigyubhiḥ*). And that Indra whom all the worlds, all beings, *abhi saṃdadhuḥ* — set before them, each in its own work. Him, the Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: no* ais *in the instrumental plural by* bahulaṃ chandasi*;* havya *(root* hve *with* yat *and* samprasāraṇa*);* bhīru *(root* bhī *with* kru *by an Uṇādi rule [Uṇ. Sū. 2-41, as read, ?]);* dhāvat *(root* dhāv *'to go', with the substitution* dhāva *for* sṛ *in the sense of speed);* jigyu *(root* ji *with* kvasu *in the* liṭ*, with* kutva *of the* j *after the reduplicative, and* samprasāraṇa*). Several words are clotted and marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*yaḥ* — which Indra; *śūrebhiḥ* — by men of valour; *havyaḥ* — is called (for help in battle); *yaḥ ca* — and which Indra; *bhīrubhiḥ* — by men of fearful nature (is called); *yaḥ* — who; *dhāvadbhiḥ* — by those who run from defeat; *hvayate* — is called (for protection); *yaḥ ca* — and which Indra; *jigyubhiḥ* — by those who have obtained victory (is called); *yam indram* — which Indra; *viśvā bhuvanā* — all beings; *abhi saṃdadhuḥ* — in their own work-times set facing themselves; *marutvantam* — that Indra together with the Maruts; *sakhyāya* — to make friendship (with us); *havāmahe* — we call."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra, whom the men of valour, the men of fearful nature, those who run from defeat, and those who have gained victory alike call, in the same way, for help and for protection; and whom all beings, each in its own time of work, keep before them — such an Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Who is to be invoked by the brave and by the timid, by the vanquished and by victors, and whom all beings place before them (in their rites) : we invoke to become our friend, Indra, attended by the Maruts.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.6 (Kannada)**

"*Indra* — brave heroes, fit to fight, call him to help them in battle; cowards, unable to fight, call him to give them suitable help; the afflicted call him that he give them protection; and those who have fought and won, to offer him their worship in joy: they each, in a different way, pray to Indra and call him. In this way, the prayer is that Indra, who has the power to give all kinds of help, may be our friend too. Because this manifold power of Indra and his universally facing wealth are well known in the world, the strong call upon him for help, and the weak for protection."

> तदस्येदं पश्यता भूरि पुष्टं श्रदिन्द्रस्य धत्तन वीर्याय ।
> *tad asyedaṃ paśyatā bhūri puṣṭaṃ śrad indrasya dhattana vīryāya |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-103-5 as read [?])

> वृक्षस्य नु ते पुरुहूत वया व्यूतयो रुरुहुरिन्द्र पूर्वीः ।
> *vṛkṣasya nu te puruhūta vayā vy ūtayo ruruhur indra pūrvīḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-24-1 as read [?])

"— in Ṛks such as these, Indra's valour is most nourishing, abundant and many-sided: therefore the protections that go with that valour are of many kinds. As the branches of a tree spread in many directions, so Indra's protections spread in many directions *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

"[— spread in many directions]. That Indra, with such a power of protection, [is called] not only as the friend of his devotees, but most dear, 'as a father cares for his devotees' — this too is well known in the world:"
