"— just as a guide is a protector for those who travel on the road, so, 'be a protector for us, protect us from dangers and give us happiness': since many such manifold prayers are found in many places, in this Ṛk too it is described that [Indra] is called *śūrebhiḥ*, *bhīrubhiḥ*, *dhāvadbhiḥ*, *jigyubhiḥ*.

*Jigyubhiḥ* — *prāptajayaiḥ*: they call, praying to Indra to offer worship also — those who have won victory.

*Abhi saṃdadhuḥ* — *abhimukhyena sthāpayanti*: 'they set [him] facing'; *tasya tasya abhilaṣitasya dānārthaṃ dhyāyanti*: [Skandasvāmin:] 'they meditate on him for the sake of giving each one's desired thing'. For the fulfilment of their respective particular wishes, they set Indra facing themselves, and offer meditation and worship; since each has his own desire, all beings worship Indra *(viśvā bhuvanā)*."

Sū. 7-3-78 as read] the substitute *dhau* for the root before *śap*, which is *ārdhadhātuka*-like; with *dhau* + *a* + *at*, *āv*-substitution for *au*; *pararūpa* by *ato guṇe* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-97 as read]; the word *dhāvat*; since *śap* is *pit*, unaccented; since the root has *a*-ending *upadeśa*, the *lasārvadhātuka* affix [*at*] is unaccented by *tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 as read]; the root keeps its final acute); *jigyubhiḥ* (root *ji jaye*; *kvasu* by *kvasuś ca* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-57 as read]; the word *jigyus*; since it has *bha*-status before *bhis* by *ayasmayādīni chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 1-4-20 as read], *samprasāraṇa* of the *v* of *vasu* by *vasoḥ samprasāraṇam* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-131 as read]; Vedic loss of *s*; the form *jigyubhiḥ*); *viśvā bhuvanā* (in the neuter plural, *śi*, loss of *i* by *śeś chandasi bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 as read]); *saṃdadhuḥ* (root *dhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*; *liṭ*, third person plural; since the relative is related to it, no *nighāta*; final acute by the affix; the preverb *sam* is unaccented by *tiṅ codāttavati* [Pā. ## Rik 101.7 — printed pp. 295–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.7)**

> रुद्राणामेति प्रदिशा विचक्षणो रुद्रेभिर्योषा तनुते पृथु ज्रयः ।
> इन्द्रं मनीषा अभ्यर्चति श्रुतं मरुत्वन्तं सख्याय हवामहे ॥ ७ ॥

*rudrāṇām eti pradiśā vicakṣaṇo rudrebhir yoṣā tanute pṛthu jrayaḥ | indraṃ manīṣā abhy arcati śrutaṃ marutvantaṃ sakhyāya havāmahe ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.7)**

> रुद्राणाम् । एति । प्रऽदिशा । विऽचक्षणः । रुद्रेभिः । योषा । तनुते । पृथु । ज्रयः ।
> इन्द्रम् । मनीषा । अभि । अर्चति । श्रुतम् । मरुत्वन्तम् । सख्याय । हवामहे ॥ ७ ॥

*rudrāṇām | eti | pra-diśā | vi-cakṣaṇaḥ | rudrebhiḥ | yoṣā | tanute | pṛthu | jrayaḥ | indram | manīṣā | abhi | arcati | śrutam | marutvantam | sakhyāya | havāmahe ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.7)**

> विचक्षणः सूर्यात्मना प्रकाशमान इन्द्रो रुद्राणां रुद्रपुत्राणामध्यात्मं प्राणरूपेण वर्तमानानां मरुतां । यद्वा । रोदयित्रृणां प्राणानां । प्राणा हि शरीरान्निर्गताः सन्तो बन्धुजनान्रोदयन्ति । प्रदिशा प्रदेशनेन मनुष्येभ्यः प्रदानेन सहैति । अन्तरिक्षे गच्छति । तथा चाम्नायते । योऽसौ तपन्नुदेति स सर्वेषां भूतानां प्राणानादायोदेतीति । तै. आ. १-[?]४-१ [?] इति । अपि च रुद्रेभिरधिभूतं वर्तमानैः रुद्रपुत्रैर्मरुद्भिर्योषा माध्यमिका वाक् पृथु विस्तीर्णं ज्रयो वेगं तनुते । विस्तारयति । प्रसङ्गादत्र मरुतां स्तुतिः । तैर्मरुद्भिः सह वर्तमानं श्रुतं प्रख्यातं सूर्यात्मानमिन्द्रं मनीषा स्तुतिलक्षणा वाक् अभ्यर्चति । अभिमुखेन स्तौति । तं मरुत्वन्तमिन्द्रं सख्यायाह्वयामहे ॥ प्रदिशा । दिश अतिसर्जने । सम्पदादिलक्षणो भावे क्विप् । ज्रयः । जि ज्रि अभिभवने । ज्रीयतेऽभिभूयतेऽनेनेति ज्रयो वेगः । करणेऽसुन् । मनीषा । ईषाक्षादित्वात्प्रकृतिभावः ॥
> *vicakṣaṇaḥ sūryātmanā prakāśamāna indro rudrāṇāṃ rudraputrāṇām adhyātmaṃ prāṇarūpeṇa vartamānānāṃ marutām | yadvā | rodayitṝṇāṃ prāṇānām | prāṇā hi śarīrān nirgatāḥ santo bandhujanān rodayanti | pradiśā pradeśanena manuṣyebhyaḥ pradānena sahaiti | antarikṣe gacchati | tathā cāmnāyate | yo 'sau tapann udeti sa sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇān ādāyodetīti | Tai. Ā. 1-[?]4-1 [?] iti | api ca rudrebhir adhibhūtaṃ vartamānaiḥ rudraputrair marudbhir yoṣā mādhyamikā vāk pṛthu vistīrṇaṃ jrayo vegaṃ tanute | vistārayati | prasaṅgād atra marutāṃ stutiḥ | tair marudbhiḥ saha vartamānaṃ śrutaṃ prakhyātaṃ sūryātmānam indraṃ manīṣā stutilakṣaṇā vāk abhy arcati | abhimukhena stauti | taṃ marutvantam indraṃ sakhyāyāhvayāmahe ‖ pradiśā | diśa atisarjane | sampadādilakṣaṇo bhāve kvip | jrayaḥ | ji jri abhibhavane | jrīyate 'bhibhūyate 'neneti jrayo vegaḥ | karaṇe 'sun | manīṣā | īṣākṣādittvāt prakṛtibhāvaḥ ‖*

"*Vicakṣaṇaḥ* — Indra, shining in the form of the sun, goes together with the *rudras*, the sons of Rudra: the Maruts who are present within the individual (*adhyātma*) in the form of the vital breaths (*prāṇa*); or, with the breaths that make [people] weep (*rodayitṝ*): for, when the breaths leave the body, they make the kinsmen weep. *Pradiśā* — by indication, by giving to men: he goes with [that] to the mid-air. As the scripture says, 'The one who rises yonder, heating, rises taking up the breaths of all beings' (*Tai. Ā.* 1-[?]4-1 as read [?]). And *rudrebhiḥ*, with the sons of Rudra, the Maruts who are present in the cosmic [*adhibhūta*] sense, *yoṣā*, speech of the middle region, *pṛthu* — wide, *jrayaḥ* — speed — *tanute*: it spreads. Here, by occasion, the Maruts are praised. That Indra, who is famed, who has the form of the sun, accompanied by those Maruts — *manīṣā*, speech having the character of praise, *abhy arcati* — praises, facing him. Him, Indra with the Maruts, we call to be our friend."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* pradiśā *(root* diś *'to give out', with* kvip *as in the class of* sampad*);* jraya *(root* ji/jri *'to overcome', 'that by which one is overcome': speed, with* asun *as instrument);* manīṣā *(no change of the stem, as of the class* īṣākṣa*…).)*

### Page 296 (PDF 316)

*(Running head: left 296; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 101".)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*vicakṣaṇaḥ* — (in the form of the sun) Indra who shines; *rudrāṇām* — (who are in the form of the breath in all living beings) the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, [or the breaths that cause weeping]; *pradiśā* — by causing [him] to join (all living beings); *eti* — [he] goes about in the mid-air; *rudrebhiḥ* — (in the form of breath) with the Maruts (by their help); *yoṣā* — the speech of men; *pṛthu* — widely; *jrayam* — and swiftly; *tanute* — spreads; *śrutam* — the famous; *indram* — Indra; *manīṣā* — speech having the form of praise; *abhy arcati* — praises facing [him]; *marutvantam* — that Indra, together with the Maruts; *sakhyāya* — to make friendship (with us); *havāmahe* — we call."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra, who shines, goes about in the mid-air in the form of the sun, by giving the Maruts, who are in the form of breath, to all living beings. By the help of the Maruts, the speech of men spreads widely and swiftly. The speech that has the form of praise stands facing the famous Indra and praises him. That Indra, together with the Maruts, we call to make friendship with us."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> The radiant Indra proceeds (along the firmament) with the manifestation of the Rudras : through the Rudras, speech spreads with more expansive celerity, and praise glorifies the renowned Indra ; him, attended by the Maruts, we invoke to be come [sic] our friend.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.7 (Kannada)**

"*Vicakṣaṇaḥ rudrāṇāṃ pradiśā eti* — *sūryātmanā prakāśamānaḥ indraḥ rudraputrāṇām adhyātmaṃ prāṇarūpeṇa vartamānānāṃ marutāṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ pradānena saha antarikṣe āgacchati*: Indra, shining in the form of the sun, comes in the mid-air by giving to all living beings the Maruts, the sons of Rudra, who are in the form of breath — this is Sāyaṇa's explanation. Skandasvāmin:"

> प्रदिशा इत्येतस्य आदेशेन वचनेन एति गच्छति अथवा रुद्र इति स्तोतृनाम स्तोतॄणाम् आदेशेन गच्छति । आयः स्तोतृगणानां प्रार्थनावाक्यम् इव अत्र अत्र गच्छति ।
> *pradiśā ity etasya ādeśena vacanena eti gacchati athavā rudra iti stotṛnāma stotṝṇām ādeśena gacchati | ayaḥ stotṛgaṇānāṃ prārthanāvākyam iva atra atra gacchati |*
> (Skandasvāmin, as read; the last clause is clotted [?])

"— [that is: 'by *pradiśā*, by the order, the word; he goes; or *rudra* is a name of praisers; he goes at the order of the praisers']: as he explains, he goes everywhere as at the words of prayer of the praisers. If we look at the meaning of the previous Ṛk, since each one prays to Indra, Indra, who is the friend of all, must go [and answer] when he has accepted the prayer of each. And since the word *rudra* is read among the [names of the] *stotṛ* — *rebhaḥ, jaritā, kāruḥ* and the rest — twenty-three [as read, ?] — and since the sense of the previous Ṛk is here also, this meaning too is acceptable. But the explanation of *rudra* as Maruts is the natural one. And since Indra and the Maruts have constant companionship (see the first part [of this edition], p. 1[?]3-3), and since they have a close relation, the first meaning, that he goes about in the mid-air together with the Maruts as they wish, is right. How Indra, in the form of the sun, gives to all beings the vital breath in the form of wind will be discussed later.

*Vicakṣaṇaḥ* — *paṇḍitaḥ* says Skandasvāmin; *sūryātmanā prakāśamānaḥ* says Sāyaṇa. Since the word *vicakṣaṇa* has [the sense 'wise'] in all the Saṃhitā sentences, and since Sāyaṇa too, for this word in the remaining places, [has given] *prājña*, *sarvajña* —"

### Page 297 (PDF 317)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 13 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 297.)*

"— that is —"

> त्वं नो गोपाः पथिकृद्विचक्षणस्तव व्रताय मतिभिर्जरामहे ।
> *tvaṃ no gopāḥ pathikṛd vicakṣaṇas tava vratāya matibhir jarāmahe |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-[?]3-6 as read [?])

> वैश्वानर तव धामान्या चके येभिः स्वर्विदभवो विचक्षण ।
> *vaiśvānara tava dhāmāny ā cake yebhiḥ svar vid abhavo vicakṣaṇa |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-[?]-10 as read [?])

> प्र ते बभ्रू विचक्षण शंसामि गोषणो नपात् ।
> *pra te babhrū vicakṣaṇa śaṃsāmi goṣaṇo napāt |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-[?]2-[?]2 as read [?])

"— since in many Ṛks like these the word *vicakṣaṇa* is given the meaning *prājña* ('wise'), and since this meaning is accepted here too, the meaning given by Skandasvāmin is the right one.

*Yoṣā* — *mādhyamikā vāk*, says Sāyaṇa; and *somāhutilakṣaṇā*, says Skandasvāmin.

*Jrayaḥ* — since *vartate, ayate* and the like are read among the [twenty-two, as read, ?] names of verbs of movement, the word *jraya* means 'movement'. Here a swift movement is meant. To show the swiftness of movement, which has a distinguishing quality even among movements, the word *jraya* has been used in many places. For example —"

> आधीवासं परि मातू रिहन्नहं तुविग्रेभिः सत्वभिर्याति वि ज्रयः ।
> *ādhīvāsaṃ pari mātū rihann aha tuvigrebhiḥ satvabhir yāti vi jrayaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-140-[?] as read [?])

"— here the speed with which the forest-fire spreads is described."

### Page 298 (PDF 318)

*(Running head: left 298; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 101".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 101.7, continued from p. 297 (Kannada)**

> प्रति भद्रा अदृक्षत गवां सर्गा न रश्मयः । ओषा अप्रा उरु ज्रयः ।
> *prati bhadrā adṛkṣata gavāṃ sargā na raśmayaḥ | oṣā aprā uru jrayaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-5[2?]-[?] as read [?])

"— in this [Ṛk], though the word *jraya* is given the meaning 'splendour' as of a great brightness, the intention is a splendour having the speed that destroys Rākṣasas and the like. In the same way here also the sense may be said to be 'swift going'.

*Yoṣā pṛthu jrayaṃ tanute* — [*marudbhiḥ saha yajñaṃ prati gacchate indrasya*] *pipāsitā somāhutiḥ vistīrṇam asi vegaṃ vistārayatīty arthaḥ* [as printed, partly clotted [?]]: 'the Soma-oblation, desired by Indra, spreads and goes with great speed': that is the intention — the Soma-oblation desired by Indra spreads widely, and goes extremely swiftly.

If the word *yoṣā* is explained as *mādhyamikā vāk*, 'the speech of the middle region', then here it is, by occasion, praise of the Maruts: this is Sāyaṇa's intention.

*Manīṣā* — speech in the form of praise."

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.7)** *(grammar pages, pp. 298–299, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *eti* (root *iṇ gatau*, *adādi*; *laṭ*, third person singular, *tip*; *luk* of *śap* by *adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 2-4-72 as read]; *guṇa* of the root's *i*, since *tip* is the cause; the form *eti*; since it stands at the beginning of the pāda no *nighāta*… [as printed: *nighāta* accent because *ati*… follows a non-verb]); *pradiśā* (root *diśa atisarjane*; *kvip* in the sense of the action by *sampadādibhyaḥ kvip* [vārttika, Pā. 3-3-[10?]8 as read]; total loss of the affix; the word *diś*; compounded with *pra*, the accent of the last member by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]; instrumental singular); *vicakṣaṇaḥ* (root *cakṣiṅ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; *yuc* by [a rule on agent and the like]; *ana* for *yu* by *yuvoranākau* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; *ṇ* by *āṭkupvāṅ…* [Pā. Sū. 8-4-2 as read]; final acute by *citaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]; *vi* being a preverb, the accent of the last member as before); *rudrebhiḥ* (by *bahulaṃ chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-10 as read] the *ais* is optional, so does not come here; *e* [by *bahuvacane jhaly et*]); *tanute* (root *tanu vistāre*; *laṭ*, third person singular; *nighāta*).

The grammar of Rik 101.7 concludes: *jrayaḥ* (root *ji jri abhibhave*; *jrīyate 'bhibhūyate 'neneti jrayaḥ vegaḥ*; *asun* in the sense of the instrument; *guṇa* because of the affix; *ay*-substitution; the word *jrayas*; since the affix is *nit*, acute on the first syllable by *ñnityādir nityam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-197 as read]); *manīṣā* + *abhi* (the lengthening of the same-class vowel would be expected here; but since *īṣākṣa…* is in the class, the stem remains unchanged in the Saṃhitā, by *prakṛtibhāva*). ## Rik 101.8 — printed pp. 299–[?] *(the first of the four Triṣṭubh Ṛks)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.8)**

> यद्वा मरुत्वः परमे सधस्थे यद्वावमे वृजने मादयासे ।
> अत आ याह्यध्वरं नो अच्छा त्वाया हविश्चकृमा सत्यराधः ॥ ८ ॥

*yad vā marutvaḥ parame sadhasthe yad vāvame vṛjane mādayāse | ata ā yāhy adhvaraṃ no acchā tvāyā haviś cakṛmā satyarādhaḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.8)**

> यत् । वा । मरुत्वः । परमे । सधऽस्थे । यत् । वा । अवमे । वृजने । मादयासे ।
> अतः । आ । याहि । अध्वरम् । नः । अच्छ । त्वाऽया । हविः । चकृम । सत्यऽराधः ॥ ८ ॥

*yat | vā | marutvaḥ | parame | sadha-sthe | yat | vā | avame | vṛjane | mādayāse | ataḥ | ā | yāhi | adhvaram | naḥ | accha | tvā-yā | haviḥ | cakṛma | satya-rādhaḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

### Page 300 (PDF 320)

*(Running head: left 300; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 100" [as the numeral reads; 101 is meant [?]].)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.8)**

> हे मरुत्वो मरुद्भिर्युक्तेन्द्र परमे उत्कृष्टे सधस्थे सहस्थाने गृहे यद्वा यदि वा मादयासे तृप्तो वर्तसे । यद्वा यदि वावमे अर्वाचीनेऽवृजने वृज्यते रिक्तीक्रियतेऽस्मिन्निमित्ति वृजनं गृहं तस्मिन्मादयासे । अतोऽस्माद्उभयविधात्स्थानान्नोऽस्माकमध्वरं यज्ञमच्छाभिमुख्येनायाहि । आगच्छ । हे सत्यराधः सत्यधन त्वाया त्वामात्मन इच्छन्तः हविश्चकृम । कृतवन्तः ॥ मरुत्वः । मतुवसोरुरिति सम्बुद्धौ नकारस्य रुत्वम् । सधस्थे । सुपि स्थ इति कप्रत्ययः । सध मादस्थयोश्छन्दसीति सहस्य सधादेशः । मादयासे । मद तृप्तियोगे । चुरादिराकृतिगणः [?] । लेट्यडागमः । त्वाया । त्वामात्मन इच्छन्ति । सुप आत्मनः क्यच् । प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्चेति मपर्यन्तस्य त्वादेशः । व्यत्ययेन दकारस्यात्वम् । अ प्रत्ययादिति ककार[प्रत्ययः] । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया लुक् ॥
> *he marutvo marudbhir yuktendra parame utkṛṣṭe sadhasthe sahasthāne gṛhe yad vā yadi vā mādayāse tṛpto vartase | yad vā yadi vāvame arvācīne 'vṛjane vṛjyate riktīkriyate 'sminn iti vṛjanaṃ gṛhaṃ tasmin mādayāse | ato 'smād ubhayavidhāt sthānān no 'smākam adhvaraṃ yajñam acchābhimukhyenāyāhi | āgaccha | he satyarādhaḥ satyadhana tvāyā tvām ātmana icchantaḥ haviś cakṛma | kṛtavantaḥ ‖ marutvaḥ | matuvasor ur iti sambuddhau nakārasya rutvam | sadhasthe | supi stha iti kapratyayaḥ | sadha mādasthayoś chandasīti sahasya sadhādeśaḥ | mādayāse | mada tṛptiyoge | curādir ākṛtigaṇaḥ [?] | leṭy aḍāgamaḥ | tvāyā | tvām ātmana icchanti | supa ātmanaḥ kyac | pratyayottarapadayoś ceti mapayantasya tvādeśaḥ | vyatyayena dakārasyātvam | a pratyayād iti kakāra[pratyayaḥ] | supāṃ suluk iti tṛtīyāyā luk ‖*

"O Marutvān, Indra joined with the Maruts! Whether you are *mādayāse* — satisfied, remain delighted — in the supreme, excellent *sadhastha*, the place where [gods] sit together, the house; or whether you are so in the lower, nearer *vṛjana* — *vṛjyate*, 'that in which one empties': the house — from either of these two kinds of place come, *acchā* — facing — to our sacrifice, *adhvaram*. Come. O *satyarādhaḥ*, one whose wealth is true! We, *tvāyā* — desiring you for ourselves — have made the oblation (*cakṛma*)."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read:* marutvaḥ *(the vocative, with* ru *for the* n *by* matuvasoḥ ru sambuddhau…*);* sadhastha *(a* ka *affix after* stha *with a preceding member; the substitute* sadha *for* saha *by* sadha mādasthayoś chandasi*);* mādayāse *(the root* mad *in the sense of satisfaction, a* curādi *[open class?, as read [?]], the* leṭ *with* aḍāgama*);* tvāyā *(denominative* kyac *after 'you'; the substitution of* tva *for the stem up to* m*; the* ā *in place of the final* d *by* vyatyaya*;* ka *affix; the loss of the third-case ending by* supāṃ suluk…*). Some clauses are clotted and marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*marutvaḥ* — O Indra, together with the Maruts; *parame* — in the excellent (supreme); *sadhasthe* — place of residence, in the house; *yat vā* — or; *avame* — in the not-excellent; *vṛjane* — in the house; *mādayāse* — (while you remain) satisfied; *yat vā* — or; *ataḥ* — from those two kinds of residence; *naḥ* — our; *adhvaram* — (for) the sacrifice; *acchā* — facing; *ā yāhi* — be pleased to come; *satyarādhaḥ* — O giver of true wealth, Indra; *tvāyā* — desiring your coming; *haviḥ* — oblations; *cakṛma* — we have offered."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, together with the Maruts! Whether you remain satisfied in a residence of the excellent kind or in one that is not excellent — from either of these two kinds of residence, be pleased to come to our sacrifice, facing us. O Indra, giver of true wealth, desiring your coming, we have offered you oblations."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Attended by the winds, giver of true wealth, whether you may be pleased (to dwell) in a stately mansion or in a lowly dwelling, come to our sacrifice : desirous of your presence we offer you oblations.

### Page 301 (PDF 321)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 13 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 301.)*

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.8 (Kannada)**

"For Indra's favour, wealth is not the chief thing. Since devotion and faith are the chief, the prayer is made that Indra be gracious to the sacrifice of one who offers oblations with devotion, whether he is in an excellent house or not in an excellent house.

*Sadhasthe* — *sahasthāne* (*Ni.* 3-[?]1 as read [?]): since all [sit] together, it is a place common to others: *gṛhe*, 'in the house'. Skandasvāmin: *saha tiṣṭhanty asmin devatāḥ sa sadhastho yajñaḥ* — 'the one in which the gods stand together, that is *sadhastha*: the sacrifice' — he says that, since all the deities sit together, it is a sacrifice. Likewise, *vṛjane* — Sāyaṇa explains as 'house', and Skandasvāmin as *varjite doṣaiḥ* — 'the sacrifice that is free of faults'. Then the senses of *parame* and *avame* also differ. If it is explained as 'house': *parame gṛhe*, *avame gṛhe*, 'in an excellent house' and 'in a house that is not excellent'; if as 'sacrifice': *parame yajñe*, *avame yajñe*: 'those who take part in a sacrifice being carried out far away, and those who take part in a sacrifice being carried out near' — the intention is: 'come also to our sacrifice'.

*Satyarādhāḥ* — *satyasādhanaḥ*: one who gives true wealth to the sacrificers; the epithet *satyarādhāḥ* is given to Indra: 'one who has wealth in the form of truth, which gives it'."

> स वृत्रहत्ये हव्यः स ईड्यः स सुष्टुत इन्द्रः सत्यराधाः ।
> *sa vṛtrahatye havyaḥ sa īḍyaḥ sa suṣṭuta indraḥ satyarādhāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-24-2 as read [?])

> तिरश्चिदर्यः सवना पुरूण्यांगूषेभिर्गृणानः सत्यराधाः ।
> *tiraś cid aryaḥ savanā purūṇy āṃgūṣebhir gṛṇānaḥ satyarādhāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-3[?]-1 as read [?])

> शंसेदुक्थं सुदानव उत द्युक्षं यथा नरः । चकृमा सत्यराधसे ॥
> *śaṃsed uktham sudānava uta dyukṣaṃ yathā naraḥ | cakṛmā satyarādhase ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-3[?]-[?] as read [?])

"— in all the Ṛks in which the epithet *satyarādhas* appears [except the Ṛk 5-40-2 (*Ni.* 5-[?]0)], it praises Indra, as an epithet, for his wealth and for his generosity.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.8)** *(grammar page, begun at the foot of p. 301, noted briefly)*

Grammar page, noted briefly. It begins with *marutvaḥ* (*marut asya asti iti marutvān*; *matup* by *tadasyāsty asmin…* [Pā. Sū. 5-2-94 as read]; *m* → *v* by *jhayaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-10 as read]; in the vocative, *ru* for the *n* by *matuvasor ru sambuddhau chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-1 as read]; visarga) and continues on the next page.

### Page 302 (PDF 322)

*(Running head: left 302; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 101".)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 101.8, continued from p. 301 (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])**

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 101.8 continues: *sadhasthe* (root *ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*; *ka* by *supi sthaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-4 as read], when the first member is a subanta; loss of the *ā* of the root by *ato lopa iṭi ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-64 as read]; the substitute *sadha* for *saha* by *sadhamādasthayoś chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-96 as read] before a form of the root *sthā* [and *mad*]; the form *sadhastha*; locative); *vṛjane* (root *vṛjī varjane*; *lyuṭ* in the sense of the locus; *ana* for *yu* by *yuvoranākau* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; no *guṇa* of the penult by the statement *saṃjñāpūrvako vidhir anityaḥ*; acute on the middle syllable by the affix); *mādayāse* (root *mada tṛptiyoge*, *curādi*; since the root has an *anubandha* *ṅ*-like marker [*anudāttetva*], it is regularly *ātmanepada*; *ṇic* in its own sense by *satyāpapāśarūpavīṇātūlaślokasenālomatvacavarmavarṇacūrṇacurādibhyo ṇic* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-25 as read]; *guṇa*/*vṛddhi* of the root's penult by *ata upadhāyāḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 as read]; the *ṇic*-ended *mādi*, then *leṭ*, second person singular, *thās* by *thāsaḥ se* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-80 as read], *aṭ* by *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; *śap*; *guṇa* of the *ṇic*; *ay*-substitution; the form *mādayāse*; since the relative is related to it, no *nighāta* by *yadvṛttānnityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; by the accent of *ṇic*, the vowel after the *d* is acute); *yāhi* (root *yā prāpaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person singular; the preverb *ā* is unaccented because it stands before a verb); *tvāyā* (explained as 'wishes you for himself', *kyac* by *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 as read]; with *yuṣmad* + *ya*, by *pratyayottarapadayoś ca* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-98 as read], *tva* for the stem up to *m*; *ā* for the *d* by *vyatyaya*; the word, ending in *kyac*, takes the name of a root by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ*; for it *a* by *apratyayāt* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-102 as read]; loss of the *a*; in the feminine *ṭāp* by *ajādyatas ṭāp* [Pā. Sū. 4-1-4 as read]; then, the third-case ending following, the loss of the ending by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]); *satyarādhaḥ* (*satyaṃ rādhaḥ dhanaṃ yasya saḥ*; the vocative with its accent: the *nighāta* by *āmantritasya ca* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-19 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 8 ‖* and a printed ornament.

> अध । नियुत्वः । सऽगणः । मरुत्ऽभिः । अस्मिन् । यज्ञे । बर्हिषि । मादयस्व ॥ ९ ॥

*tvā-yā | indra | somam | susuma | su-dakṣa | tvā-yā | haviḥ | cakṛma | brahma-vāhaḥ | adha | niyutvaḥ | sa-gaṇaḥ | marut-bhiḥ | asmin | yajñe | barhiṣi | mādayasva ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.9)**

> हे सुदक्ष शोभनबलेन्द्र त्वायो त्वत्कामनया सोमं सुषुम । अभिषुतवन्तो वयम् । हे ब्रह्मवाहो ब्रह्मणा मन्त्ररूपेण स्तोत्रेणोह्यमान प्राप्यमाणेन्द्र त्वाया त्वत्कामनयोहवनीये पुरोडाशलक्षणं हविश्चकृम । कृतवन्तः । हे नियुत्वः नियुतोऽश्वाः तद्वन्निन्द्र अधानन्तरं मरुद्भिः सप्तगणरूपैर्देवैः सगणो गणसहितः सन्नस्मिन्वर्तमाने यज्ञे बर्हिष्यास्तीर्णे दर्भ उपविश्य मादयस्व तृप्तो भव ॥ सुषुमा । षुञ् अभिषवे । लिटि क्रादिनियमप्राप्तस्येटोऽनित्यमागममुशासनमिति वचनादभावः ॥
> *he sudakṣa śobhanabalendra tvāyā tvatkāmanayā somaṃ suṣuma | abhiṣutavanto vayam | he brahmavāho brahmaṇā mantrarūpeṇa stotreṇohyamāna prāpyamāṇendra tvāyā tvatkāmanayohavanīye puroḍāśalakṣaṇaṃ haviś cakṛma | kṛtavantaḥ | he niyutvaḥ niyuto 'śvāḥ tadvann indra adhānantaraṃ marudbhiḥ saptagaṇarūpair devaiḥ sagaṇo gaṇasahitaḥ sann asmin vartamāne yajñe barhiṣy āstīrṇe darbha upaviśya mādayasva tṛpto bhava ‖ suṣumā | ṣuñ abhiṣave | liṭi krādiniyamaprāptasyeṭo 'nityam āgamam uśāsanam iti vacanād abhāvaḥ ‖*

"O *sudakṣa* — you of excellent strength! Indra, *tvāyā* — desiring you — we have pressed (*suṣuma*) the Soma. O *brahmavāhaḥ* — you who are borne, brought, by the *brahma*, the praise in the form of a mantra; Indra! *tvāyā* — desiring you — we have made, on the *āhavanīya* [fire], the oblation, in the form of the *puroḍāśa* cake. O *niyutvaḥ* — you who have *niyuts*, horses, Indra: thereafter, *sagaṇaḥ* — accompanied by your band — with the Maruts, the gods who are in the form of seven groups, in this sacrifice now going on, seated on the *barhis*, the spread-out *darbha* grass, *mādayasva* — be satisfied."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* suṣumā *(root* ṣuñ *'to press', with the* liṭ*, and the absence of the augment* iṭ*, which the rule of* kradi *would give, by the statement that the augment's teaching is not invariable).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)** *(begun at the foot of p. 303; continues on p. 304)*

"*sudakṣa* — O Indra, of excellent strength; *tvāyā* — desiring (your help); *somam* — the Soma juice; *suṣuma* — we have pressed and offered; *brahmavāhaḥ* — O Indra, worthy to be attained by praise;"

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, of excellent strength, desiring your help we have pressed and offered the Soma juice for you. O Indra, worthy to be approached by the means of praise, as one who loves praise, desiring your help we have offered you oblations. O Indra, who have horses yoked, together with the Maruts, in a company, sit on the *darbha* seats in this sacrifice now being performed and be satisfied."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Desirous of you, Indra, who are possessed of excellent strength, we pour forth to you libations : desirous of you, who are obtained by prayer, we offer you oblations ; therefore, do you, who are possessed of horses, sit down with pleasure upon the sacred grass, attended by the Maruts, at this sacrifice.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 101.9 (Kannada)**

"*Sudakṣa* — *śobhanabala*: of excellent strength. In the address 'Indra, who have excellent strength', Indra's extraordinary strength is made known. In the Ṛk 15 of the previous sūkta [Sūkta 100]:"

> न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता आपश्चन शवसो अन्तमापुः । स प्ररिक्वा त्वक्षसा क्ष्मो दिवश्च मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विन्द्र ऊती ॥
> *na yasya devā devatā na martā āpaś cana śavaso antam āpuḥ | sa prarikvā tvakṣasā kṣmo divaś ca marutvān no bhavatv indra ūtī ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-100-15; Rik 15 of Sūkta 100)

"— the description that neither the gods nor heaven and earth could come near your strength; and —"

> विश्वे ते इन्द्र वीर्यं देवा अनु क्रतुं ददुः ।
> *viśve te indra vīryaṃ devā anu kratuṃ daduḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-6-3 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 280)

"— in Ṛks like these, all the gods praised and followed Indra's strength and valour; and so, in many other contexts, the praise of the greatness of Indra's prowess is understood; and this address *sudakṣa* here makes known that point."

### Page 305 (PDF 325)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 13 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 305. A printer's signature "20 · VOLUME 8" stands at the foot.)*

"*Brahmavāhaḥ* — *brahmaṇā mantrarūpeṇa stotreṇohyamāna prāpyamāṇendra*: 'borne, attained, by praise in the form of a mantra': it shows the need for praise, in order to obtain Indra's favour, as one fit to be attained by praise. Although for the other deities too praise is essential, since they too must be pleased by praise, the epithet *brahmavāha* has been used in the sense of Indra alone."

> इमा ब्रह्म ब्रह्मवाहः क्रियन्त आ बर्हिः सीद ।
> *imā brahma brahmavāhaḥ kriyanta ā barhiḥ sīda |*

> सुनोतेन पचत ब्रह्मवाहसे पुरुष्टुताय प्रतरं दधातन ।
> *sunotena pacata brahmavāhase puruṣṭutāya prataraṃ dadhātana |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 3-5[?]-1 as read [?])

> सखायो ब्रह्मवाहसेऽर्चत प्र च गायत ।
> *sakhāyo brahmavāhase 'rcata pra ca gāyata |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-45-4 as read [?])

"— in these Ṛks, and so in 3-3[?]-?; 6-2[?]-?; 6-4[?]-? and many others, the word *brahmavāha* is an epithet of Indra alone.

*Tvāyā* — *tvām ātmana icchati*: [the sense] 'wishing you to be one who belongs to us' is a desire. This is a special formation. In all places where the sense *tvatkāmanayā* — 'out of desire for you' — occurs, this word is used; it is used in this sense in many Ṛks, such as 1-[?]-[?], 3-[?]-[?], 8-2-[?], 8-[?]-[?] and so on.

*Niyutvaḥ* — *niyutaḥ aśvāḥ tadvann indra*: *niyut* means horses: 'the one who has horses': an epithet of Indra. In general, this epithet is used chiefly of Vāyu, and in some places also of the deities Indra and Varuṇa. To show that *niyut* means 'Vāyu's horses', the Nirukta-author quotes the Ṛk"

> विशामकोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा स्वस्तये नियुत्वान् ।
> *viśām ko ruṣasaḥ pūrvahūtau vāyuḥ pūṣā svastaye niyutvān |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-34-3 as read [?]; the first words clotted in print [?])

"— and explains: *niyutvān — niyuto 'syāśvāḥ* [(*Ni.* 5-[?]2 as read [?])]: 'the *niyuts* are the horses of this Vāyu'. But the epithet *niyutvān* is used also of the deities Indra and Varuṇa."

> अधा नियुत्व उभयस्य नः पिब शुचिं सोमं गवाशिरम् ।
> *adhā niyutva ubhayasya naḥ piba śuciṃ somaṃ gavāśiram |*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 101.9)** *(grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: *tvāyā* — explained in the previous mantra [Rik 101.8]; *suṣuma* (root *ṣuñ abhiṣave*; *liṭ*, first person plural; *ma* for the ending by *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus…* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-82 as read]; doubling of the root; though by *kṛsṛbhṛ…* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-13 as read] the augment *iṭ* is ruled out [being restricted to those roots], properly *iṭ* should come here; but by the statement *āgamaśāsanam anityam* the augment *iṭ* does not come; *ṣ* for the *s* of the root by *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-59 as read]; since the verb is at the beginning of the pāda [as the print puts it], no *nighāta* because …); *cakṛma* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *liṭ*, first person plural; since *kryādi*'s rule applies, no augment *iṭ*; *nighāta* of the finite verb); *niyutvaḥ* (*niyutaḥ aśvāḥ asya santi iti niyutvān*; *matup* by *tadasyāsty asmin* [Pā. Sū. 5-2-94 as read]; *m* → *v* by *jhayaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-10 as read]; in the vocative, *ru* for the *n* by *matuvasoru sambuddhau chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-1 as read]; visarga); *adhā* (the word *atha*; *dh* for *th* by Vedic letter-interchange; the lengthening of the vowel in the Saṃhitā by *dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-135 as read]); *mādayasva* (root *mada tṛptiyoge*, *curādi*; *nityaṃ ātmanepade*; *loṭ*, second person singular, *thās*, *sa* by *thāsaḥ se*; *va* by *sevāsitasi…* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-91 as read] — print: *savābhyāṃ vāmau*, i.e. *sevābhyāṃ vāmau*…, [Pā. Sū. 3-4-91 as read, ?]; *śap*; *guṇa* of *ṇic*; *ay*-substitution; since the verb has accent on the last syllable, *nighāta*). The Rik is closed with *‖ 9 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

> मादयस्व हरिभिर्ये त इन्द्र वि ष्यस्व शिप्रे वि सृजस्व धेने ।
> आ त्वा सुशिप्र हरयो वहन्तूशन्हव्यानि प्रति नो जुषस्व ॥ १० ॥

*mādayasva haribhir ye ta indra vi ṣyasva śipre vi sṛjasva dhene | ā tvā suśipra harayo vahantūśan havyāni prati no juṣasva ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.10)**

> मादयस्व । हरिऽभिः । ये । ते । इन्द्र । वि । स्यस्व । शिप्रे इति । वि । सृजस्व । धेने इति ।
> आ । त्वा । सुऽशिप्र । हरयः । वहन्तु । उशन् । हव्यानि । प्रति । नः । जुषस्व ॥ १० ॥

*mādayasva | hari-bhiḥ | ye | te | indra | vi | ṣyasva | śipre iti | vi | sṛjasva | dhene iti | ā | tvā | su-śipra | harayaḥ | vahantu | uśan | havyāni | prati | naḥ | juṣasva ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.10)**

> हे इन्द्र हरिभिरश्वैः सह मादयस्व । तृप्तो भव । ये ते तव स्वभूतास्तदर्थं शिप्रे हनू संहते वि ष्यस्व । सोमपानार्थं विवृते कुरु । तथा धेने सास्नासाधनभूते जिह्वोपजिह्विके वि सृजस्व । सोमपानार्थं विश्लिष्टे कुरु । हे सुशिप्र शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । शोभनशिप्रेन्द्र त्वा त्वां हरय उशा आ वहन्तु । अस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रापयन्तु । त्वं जोषन् अस्माकं कामयमानो नोऽस्माकं हव्यानि हवींषि प्रति जुषस्व । प्रत्येकं सेवस्व । मोदासि [?] ॥ वि ष्यस्व । षो अन्तकर्मणि । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदम् । दिवादित्वात् श्यन् । ओतः श्यनि । पा. ७-३-७१ । इत्योकारलोपः । उपसर्गात्सुनोतीति षत्वम् ॥
> *he indra haribhir aśvaiḥ saha mādayasva | tṛpto bhava | ye te tava svabhūtās tadarthaṃ śipre hanū saṃhate vi ṣyasva | somapānārthaṃ vivṛte kuru | tathā dhene sāsnāsādhanabhūte jihvopajihvike vi sṛjasva | somapānārthaṃ viśliṣṭe kuru | he suśipra śipre hanū nāsike vā | śobhanaśipreṇdra tvā tvāṃ harayo 'śvā ā vahantu | asmadīyaṃ yajñaṃ prāpayantu | tvaṃ joṣan asmākaṃ kāmayamāno no 'smākaṃ havyāni havīṃṣi prati juṣasva | pratyekaṃ sevasva | modāsi [?] ‖ vi ṣyasva | ṣo antakarmaṇi | vyatyayenātmanepadam | divāditvāt śyan | oataḥ śyani | Pā. 7-3-71 | ity okāralopaḥ | upasargāt sunotīti ṣatvam ‖*

"O Indra! *mādayasva* — be satisfied — together with the *haribhiḥ*, your steeds. *Ye te* — your own [horses, who are of your nature] — for them, *vi ṣyasva* — open wide your two jaws (*śipre*), which are joined: make them open for the drinking of Soma. And *dhene* — the tongue and the uvula, which serve as the means of swallowing — *vi sṛjasva*: set them wide apart, for the drinking of Soma. O *suśipra* — you of the beautiful jaws or nose! — may your horses (*harayaḥ*), *uśan* — desiring — bring you [here] to our sacrifice. You, *joṣan*, wishing us well, *prati juṣasva* — take, one by one, our oblations."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* vi ṣyasva *(root* ṣo *'to end', middle voice by* vyatyaya*;* śyan *of the* divādi *class; loss of* o *by* oataḥ śyani *[Pā. Sū. 7-3-71];* ṣ *by* upasargāt sunoti…*).)*

"*indra* — O Indra; *ye te* — those [horses] which have attained your very nature; *haribhiḥ* — with those horses; *mādayasva* — be satisfied; *śipre* — [your] jaws —"

"— since the Nirukta-author has said that the word *śipra* means either the jaws or the nose, Sāyaṇa too has said here that either of the two may be taken. > अग्निभ्राजसो विद्युतो गभस्त्योः शिप्राः शीर्षसु वितता हिरण्ययीः ।
> *agnibhrājaso vidyuto gabhastyoḥ śiprāḥ śīrṣasu vitatā hiraṇyayīḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-54-11 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk, for the word *śipra*, Sāyaṇa has given *uṣṇīṣamayyaḥ*, 'made of turbans', and the print adds 'Turban'.

In the whole, it appears that the word *śipra* may be explained also for the words *śiprin* and the like that are derived from this word, in the manner set out below. If this word is used in the dual, then the meaning is 'jaws', as in the Ṛks 1-100-10 [as read, i.e. Rik 10 of the present sūkta?], 3-3[?]-?, 5-36-2, 8-[?]-?, 10-[?]-[?], 10-1[?]-5 and the rest. *Śiprin*, then, as an epithet, is of Indra alone, 'one who has jaws or a nose'. In the Ṛks 1-3[?]-2, 1-[?]-1, 3-3[?]-10 and the like, it is an epithet of Indra: 'the one who has *śipra*'; and —"

> पीवोअश्वाः शुचद्रथा हि भूताऽयःशिप्रा वाजिनः सुनिष्काः ।
> *pīvo-aśvāḥ śucadrathā hi bhūtāyaḥśiprā vājinaḥ suniṣkāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 5-5[?]-2 as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk *ayaḥśiprāḥ* is an epithet of the Ṛbhus. Here it may mean 'visors made of iron'; or, as Sāyaṇa explains, *ayovat sārabhūtaśiprāḥ*: 'those who have jaws as strong as iron'.

In the present Ṛk, in the address *suśipra*, 'Indra, with beautiful jaws or nose', Indra is addressed. The expression *śipre vi ṣyasva* means 'open the two jaws': the intention is 'open your jaws for the drinking of Soma'."

## Rik 101.11 (the last Rik of Sūkta 101) — printed pp. 310–312

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 101.11)**

> मरुत्स्तोत्रस्य वृजनस्य गोपा वयमिन्द्रेण सनुयाम वाजम् ।
> तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ ११ ॥

*marutstotrasya vṛjanasya gopā vayam indreṇa sanuyāma vājam | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 101.11)**

> मरुत्ऽस्तोत्रस्य । वृजनस्य । गोपाः । वयम् । इन्द्रेण । सनुयाम । वाजम् ।
> तत् । नः । मित्रः । वरुणः । मामहन्ताम् । अदितिः । सिन्धुः । पृथिवी । उत । द्यौः ॥ ११ ॥

*marut-stotrasya | vṛjanasya | gopāḥ | vayam | indreṇa | sanuyāma | vājam | tat | naḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | māmahantām | aditiḥ | sindhuḥ | pṛthivī | uta | dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 101.11)**

> मरुत्स्तोत्रस्य । मरुद्भिः सह स्तोत्रं यस्य स मरुत्स्तोत्रः । तस्य वृजनस्य शत्रूणां क्षेप्तॄरिन्द्रस्य सम्बन्धिनो गोपा गोपायनीया रक्षणीया वयं तेनेन्द्रेण वाजमन्नं सनुयाम । लभेमहि । यदेतदस्माभिः प्रार्थितं नोऽस्मदीयं तन्मित्रादयो द्यावापृथिव्यौ च मामहन्ताम् । पूजितं कुर्वन्तु ॥ वृजनस्य । वृजी वर्जने । कैवृजिमन्दिनिधाभ्यः [?] कुरिति कुप्रत्ययः ॥
> *marutstotrasya | marudbhiḥ saha stotraṃ yasya sa marutstotraḥ | tasya vṛjanasya śatrūṇāṃ kṣeptṝr indrasya sambandhino gopā gopāyanīyā rakṣaṇīyā vayaṃ tenendreṇa vājam annaṃ sanuyāma | labhemahi | yad etad asmābhiḥ prārthitaṃ no 'smadīyaṃ tan mitrādayo dyāvāpṛthivyau ca māmahantām | pūjitaṃ kurvantu ‖ vṛjanasya | vṛjī varjane | kaivṛjimandinidhābhyaḥ [?] kur iti kupratyayaḥ ‖*

"*Marutstotrasya* — one whose praise is together with the Maruts is *marutstotra*; of that Indra — *vṛjanasya* — who casts away the enemies [*kṣeptṝ*] — we, who are his to be protected (*gopāḥ*), by that Indra *vājam* — food — may we obtain (*sanuyāma*). What we have prayed for in this, our [prayer] — may Mitra and the rest, and heaven and earth, honour it: may they make it honoured."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* vṛjana *(root* vṛj *'to avoid', with an Uṇādi* ku*-affix; the list of roots is clotted [?]).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*marutstotrasya* — [of him] who accepts praise together with the Maruts; *vṛjanasya* — of Indra, the destroyer of enemies; *gopāḥ* — who are fit for his protection; *vayam* — we; *indreṇa* — by that Indra; *vājam* — food; *sanuyāma* — may we obtain; *naḥ* — our; *tat* — (that prayed-for) food; *mitraḥ* — Mitra; *varuṇaḥ* — and Varuṇa; *aditiḥ* — Aditi; *sindhuḥ* — the deity presiding over the sea; *pṛthivī* — the earth; *uta* — and; *dyauḥ* — the heavenly world; *māmahantām* — may [they] make [it] honoured (and guard it)."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"We who are fit for the protection of Indra, who accepts praise together with the Maruts and who destroys enemies, may obtain food from that Indra. May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, the deity presiding over the sea, the earth and the heavenly world guard that food which we have prayed for."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Protected by that destroyer of (foes), who is united in praise with the Maruts, we may receive sustenance from Indra ; and may Mitra, Varuna, Aditi,—ocean, and heaven, preserve it to us.

"*Marutstotrasya* — *marudbhiḥ saha stotraṃ yasya sa marutstotraḥ tasya*: to Indra, who accepts praise together with the Maruts.

*Vṛjanasya* — *śatrūṇāṃ kṣeptur indrasya*: of Indra, who casts away and destroys the enemies; *vṛjana* means 'crooked', 'deceit' and 'power' (*Ni.* 2-9 as read [?]); here it means 'enemies who practise deceit': enemies who play false."

## Sūkta 102

**ನೂರ ಎರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು** — *nūra eraḍaneya sūktavu*, "the hundred-and-second Sūkta" *(Kannada heading)*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 102 (Sanskrit in Kannada script; doubtful places [?]):**

> इमां ते इत्येकादशर्चं नवमं सूक्तं कुत्सस्यार्षमैन्द्रम् । अन्त्या त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा दश जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । इमां ते ऽन्त्या त्रिष्टुबिति ॥ विनियोगो लैङ्गिकः ॥
> *imāṃ te ity ekādaśarcaṃ navamaṃ sūktaṃ kutsasyārṣam aindram | antyā triṣṭup śiṣṭā daśa jagatyaḥ | tathā cānukrāntam | imāṃ te 'ntyā triṣṭub iti ‖ viniyogo laiṅgikaḥ ‖*

*(Sense: "The ninth sūkta, of eleven Ṛks, beginning* imāṃ te*, is the seer-composition of Kutsa, addressed to Indra; the last [Ṛk] is Triṣṭubh, the remaining ten Jagatī. So the Anukramaṇī: '*imāṃ te*; the last Triṣṭubh.' Its application is by the sign [i.e. by its fitness, not by a specific rule].")*

**Anuvāda (Kannada):** "*Imāṃ te* — this sūkta is the ninth sūkta in the fifteenth anuvāka. It has eleven Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa. The deity is Indra. The last Ṛk of this sūkta is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining ten Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said *imāṃ te 'ntyā triṣṭub iti*. Its application is *laiṅgika*."

*(A printer's ornament follows.)*

**॥ ओं ॥ — Om** *(printed)*

**सूक्त — १०२ — Sūkta 102** *(printed heading block, in Kannada script and numerals)*

- मण्डल १ · अनुवाक १५ · सूक्त १०२ — *Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 15, Sūkta 102.*
- अष्टक १ · अध्याय ७ · वर्ग १४, १५ — *Aṣṭaka 1, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 14, 15* (numerals as read, small [?]).
- ऋक्संख्या — ११ — *Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 11.*
- ऋषिः — कुत्स आङ्गिरसः — *Ṛṣi: Kutsa Āṅgirasa.*
- देवता — इन्द्रः — *Deity: Indra.*
- छन्दः — १-१० जगती । ११ त्रिष्टुप् — *Metre: Ṛks 1–10 Jagatī; 11 Triṣṭubh.*

*imām | te | dhiyam | pra | bhare | mahaḥ | mahīm | asya | stotre | dhiṣaṇā | yat | te | ānaje | tam | ut-save | ca | pra-save | ca | sasahim [as printed; Saṃhitā* sāsahim*] | indram | devāsaḥ | śavasā | amadan | anu ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.1)**

> हे इन्द्र महो महतस्ते तवेमामिदानीं क्रियमाणां महीं महतीमात्यन्तोत्कृष्टां धियं स्तुतिं प्रभरे । प्रकर्षेण सम्पादयामि । ते तव धिषणा त्वदीया बुद्धिरस्य मम स्तोतुः स्तोत्रे स्तुतौ यद्यस्मादानजे आक्ता संश्लिष्टासीत् । तस्मात्तव प्रियां स्तुतिं करोमीत्यर्थः । उत्तरार्धर्चः परोक्षकृतः । ससहिं शत्रूणामभिभवितारं पूर्वोक्तं तमिन्द्रं देवासः कर्मसु दीव्यन्त ऋत्विजः शवसा स्तुतिभिः कीर्तनबलेनानुमदन् । अनुक्रमेण हर्षं प्रापयन् । किमर्थम् । उत्सवे चोत्क्षेपणार्थमभिवृद्ध्यर्थं प्रसवे च धनानां वृष्ट्युदकानां वोत्पत्त्यर्थं च ॥ आनजे । अञ्जू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकान्तिगतिषु । अस्मात्कर्मणि लिट् । द्विर्वचनहलादिशेषौ । अत आदेरित्यभ्यासस्यात्वम् । तस्मान्नुट् द्विहलः । पा. ७-४-७१ । इति नुट् । व्यत्ययेनोपधानकारलोपः । उत्सवे । प्रसवे । सू प्रेरणे । ऋदोरबिति भावेऽप् । निमित्तात्कर्मसंयोगे । पा. २-३-३६ [?] । इति सप्तमी । धात्वादिसूत्रपदांकोदात्तत्वम् [?] । ससहिम् । षह अभिभवे । आद्यगमहन इत्यैत्र्योत्सर्गाच्छन्दसीति वचनात्किप्रत्ययः । लिड्वद्भावाद्द्विर्वचनम् । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायामभ्यासस्य दीर्घत्वम् । अमदन् । मदी हर्षे । हेतुमति णिच् । मदी हर्षग्लपनयोरिति घटादिषु पाठान्मितां ह्रस्व इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । छन्दस्युभयथेति शप आर्धधातुकत्वाण्णेरनिटीति णिलोपः ॥
> *he indra maho mahatas te tavemām idānīṃ kriyamāṇāṃ mahīṃ mahatīm atyantotkṛṣṭāṃ dhiyaṃ stutiṃ pra bhare | prakarṣeṇa sampādayāmi | te tava dhiṣaṇā tvadīyā buddhir asya mama stotuḥ stotre stutau yad yasmād ānaje āktā saṃśliṣṭāsīt | tasmāt tava priyāṃ stutiṃ karomīty arthaḥ | uttarārdharcaḥ parokṣakṛtaḥ | sasahiṃ śatrūṇām abhibhavitāraṃ pūrvoktaṃ tam indraṃ devāsaḥ karmasu dīvyanta ṛtvijaḥ śavasā stutibhiḥ kīrtanabalenānumadan | anukrameṇa harṣaṃ prāpayan | kimartham | utsave cotkṣepaṇārtham abhivṛddhyartham prasave ca dhanānāṃ vṛṣṭyudakānāṃ votpattyartham ca ‖ ānaje | añjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāntigatiṣu | asmāt karmaṇi liṭ | dvirvacanahalādiśeṣau | ata āder ity abhyāsasyātvam | tasmān nuṭ dvihalaḥ | Pā. 7-4-71 | iti nuṭ | vyatyayenopadhānakāralopaḥ | utsave | prasave | sū preraṇe | ṛdor ap iti bhāve 'p | nimittāt karmasaṃyoge | Pā. 2-3-36 [?] | iti saptamī | dhātvādisūtrapadāṃkodāttatvam [?] | sasahim | ṣaha abhibhave | ādyagamahana ity airtryotsargāc chandasīti vacanāt kipratyayaḥ | liḍvadbhāvād dvirvacanam | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyām abhyāsasya dīrghatvam | amadan | madī harṣe | hetumati ṇic | madī harṣaglapanayor iti ghaṭādiṣu pāṭhān mitāṃ hrasva iti hrasvatvam | chandasy ubhayatheti śapa ārdhadhātukatvāṇ ṇer aniṭīti ṇilopaḥ ‖*

"O Indra! *te* — of you, *mahaḥ* — the great — I bring forth (*pra bhare*, 'I accomplish with force') this praise (*dhiyam*), now being made, *mahīm* — mighty, exceedingly excellent. *Yat* — because your *dhiṣaṇā*, your understanding, *ānaje* — has been attached, has been joined to, *asya stotre* — to this praise of me, the praiser, for that reason, the sense is, I make a praise dear to you. The latter half of the Ṛk is in the third person [*parokṣakṛta*]: *tam indram* — that Indra spoken of before, *sasahim* — the overcomer of enemies — the *devāsaḥ*, the priests who shine in the rites, *śavasā* — by their praises, by the strength of their proclaiming — *anu amadan* — made him glad one after another. For what purpose? For *utsava* — for lifting up, for increase — and for *prasava* — for the production of wealth or of rain-waters."

Sū. 7-4-71 as read, ?]);* utsave/prasave *(root* sū *'to impel', with* ap*; the locative of the purpose [Pā. Sū. 2-3-36, as read [?]]);* sasahi *(root* ṣah *with* ki *and the doubling as if* liṭ*, lengthened in the Saṃhitā by* anyeṣām api dṛśyate*);* amadan *(root* mad *with the causative* ṇic*; shortening of the penult by* mitāṃ hrasvaḥ*; loss of* ṇi*). Several rule-names and the clause on accent are clotted and marked [?].)*

### Page 315 (PDF 335)

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*(indra — O Indra)*; *te* — your; *dhiṣaṇā* — mind; *asya* — this, of the praiser, which is my; *stotre* — in praise; *yat* — for which reason; *ānaje* — [has been] merged (with reverence); *mahaḥ* — of the great-souled; *te* — your; *mahīm* — extremely excellent; *imāṃ dhiyam* — this praise; *pra bhare* — I make, exceedingly; *sasahim* — one who conquers enemies; *tam indram* — that Indra; *devāsaḥ* — the priests who shine in the sacrificial acts; *utsave ca* — for their elevation; *prasave ca* — and for wealth such as (rain-water); *śavasā* — by the strength of praise; *anu amadan* — made glad in succession."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, because your mind is merged in reverence in this my praise, which makes you glad, I make this praise, extremely excellent, and offer it to you, the great-souled. The priests who shine in the sacrificial acts, by the strength of their praise, made glad one after another that Indra who conquers enemies, for their own elevation and for wealth such as rain-water."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> I address to you, who are mighty, this excellent hymn, because your understanding has been gratified by my praise : the gods have successively delighted that victorious Indra with the power (of praise) for the sake of prosperity and wealth.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.1 (Kannada)**

"*Dhiyam* — though the word *dhī* is read among the thirteen names of intelligence (*prajñā*) (*Ni.* 3-[?]9 as read [?]), here the bhāṣya-author has given for this word the meaning *stotra*, 'praise'.

*Utsave prasave* — *sū preraṇe*: *utsavārtham abhivṛddhyartham* — for the sake of increase, for prosperity, or for the increase of wealth (*śrī*)."

### Page 316 (PDF 336)

*(Running head: left 316; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

"*Sasahim* — *ṣaha abhibhave*; *śatrūṇām abhibhavitāram*: one who overcomes, defeats the enemies.

*Devāsaḥ* — though the general sense of this word is 'deities', the bhāṣya-author here explains: *karmasu dīvyanta ity devā ṛtvijaḥ* — 'those who shine in the rites are *devāḥ*, priests': that is, since they shine, taking the chief place in the sacrificial and other acts, he has explained *devāḥ* or *devāsaḥ* as 'priests'. When Yāska gives the general sense of the word *deva*, he says: *devo dānād vā dīpanād vā dyotanād vā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā* — 'the *deva* is the giver, or the shining one, or the illuminating one, or the one who is in heaven': the sense is 'one who gives, who shines, or who is in heaven'. The bhāṣya-author, in the Ṛk"

> स्वग्नयो हि वार्यं देवासो दधिरे च नः ।
> *svagnayo hi vāryaṃ devāso dadhire ca naḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-[?]4-8 as read [?])

"— and in Ṛks like it, has explained the word *devāsaḥ* as the priests themselves: *devāso dīpyamānā ṛtvijaḥ*.

*Śavasā* — though the word *śavas* is read among the twenty-eight names of strength (*Ni.* 2-9 as read [?]), here the bhāṣya-author has given the meaning *śavasā stutibhiḥ kīrtanabalena*: 'by the strength that arises from doing the praise and the like'.

The first half of the Ṛk here addresses Indra directly and praises him: this kind of praise is called *pratyakṣakṛta*. The second half speaks of Indra generally, without address, as if he were not before us: this kind of praise is called *parokṣakṛta*. On this matter Yāska has explained thus —"

> तद्यानि नामानि प्राधान्यस्तुतीनां देवतानां तद्दैवतमित्याचक्षते । यत्कामा ऋषिर्यस्यां देवतायामार्थपत्यमिच्छन्स्तुतिं प्रयुङ्क्ते तद्दैवतः स मन्त्रो भवति । ताः त्रिविधा ऋचः परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृता आध्यात्मिकाश्च । तत्र परोक्षकृताः सर्वाभिर्नामविभक्तिभिर्युज्यन्ते प्रथमपुरुषैश्चाख्यातस्य । अथ प्रत्यक्षकृता मध्यमपुरुषयोगास्त्वमिति चैतेन सर्वनाम्ना । परोक्षकृताः प्रत्यक्षकृताश्च मन्त्रा भूयिष्ठा अल्पश आध्यात्मिकाः ॥
> *tad yāni nāmāni prādhānyastutīnāṃ devatānāṃ tad daivatam ity ācakṣate | yatkāmā ṛṣir yasyāṃ devatāyām ārthapatyam icchan stutiṃ prayuṅkte taddaivataḥ sa mantro bhavati | tāḥ trividhā ṛcaḥ parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtā ādhyātmikāś ca | tatra parokṣakṛtāḥ sarvābhir nāmavibhaktibhir yujyante prathamapuruṣaiś cākhyātasya | atha pratyakṣakṛtā madhyamapuruṣayogās tvam iti caitena sarvanāmnā | parokṣakṛtāḥ pratyakṣakṛtāś ca mantrā bhūyiṣṭhā alpaśa ādhyātmikāḥ ‖*
> (*Nirukta*, Daivatakāṇḍa, adhyāya 7, khaṇḍa 1–3 [as printed: "adhyāya 7, khaṇḍa 1-3"]; the Sanskrit is given as read, some words clotted [?])

"— that is: among mantras there are many kinds, according to the sense: mantras of deities, mantras of praise, mantras of blessing, oath, curse, ... [the print lists:] *śapatha*, *abhiśāpa*, *kaśmīdbhāva*, *paridevanā*, *nindā*, *praśaṃsā*. *Daivata mantra* means a mantra that describes the greatness of deities; *stuti* means praise: a mantra that contains prayers; *āśīḥ* means blessing, a mantra that wishes for a good end; *śapatha* means a vow, *abhiśāpa* a curse, *kaśmīdbhāva* an account of an event or of the truth of a thing, *paridevanā* a lament, *nindā* blame, *praśaṃsā* praise, [dānastuti] and the like.

Among the many kinds mentioned above, the Ṛks that are *daivata* ('addressed to a deity') are of three kinds: *parokṣakṛta*, *pratyakṣakṛta* and *ādhyātmika*. *Parokṣakṛta* — since the deity who is praised is not before one, mantras that use, in praising, in the proper names and the verbs of that deity, the third person (*third person both in subject and predicate* — English in the original). *Pratyakṣakṛta* — Ṛks that praise, addressing the deity to be praised as if he were visibly present, with words such as 'you', 'your' in the second person (*Second person* — English in the original). *Ādhyātmika* — mantras that praise by using the first person (*First person* — English in the original). Of these three kinds of mantras, the *parokṣakṛta* and the *pratyakṣakṛta* are the more numerous; the *ādhyātmika* mantras are only a few. In accordance with this order, in a Ṛk of the present kind, the first half of the Ṛk is *pratyakṣakṛta* and the second half is *parokṣakṛta*."

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 102.1, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])**

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 102.1 concludes: *ānaje* (continued: since *yat* is related to it, the *nighāta* is prevented by *yadvṛttānnityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read], and by the accent of the affix the word is acute on the last syllable); *utsave* (*prasave*; root *sū preraṇe*; *ap* in the sense of the action by *ṛdor ap* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-57 as read]; *guṇa* of the root vowel by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-84 as read]; *av*-substitution; the locative *saptamī* by the statement that, since it is connected with the [fruit of the] action, a word expressing the cause takes the seventh case, *nimittāt karmayoge* [vārttika under Pā. Sū. 2-3-36 as read, ?]; the accent of the last member of the compound by *thāthaghañktājabitrāṇām* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-144 as read]); *sasahim* (root *ṣaha abhibhave*; *ki* by *ādṛgamahanajanaḥ kikinau liṭ ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-171 as read], by the rule *utsargaś chandasi* — hence it comes here too; *liṭ* said to be as if present, so doubling of the root; *ādihalśeṣa*; lengthening of the reduplicative by *anyeṣām api dṛśyate* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-137 as read]; final acute by the affix; accusative singular); *devāsaḥ* (the word *deva*, *jas* following; the augment *asuk* by *ājjaser asuk* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-50 as read]); *amadan* (root *madī harṣe*; since the causative sense is shown, *ṇic* by *hetumati ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-26 as read]; *vṛddhi* of the penult by *ata upadhāyāḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-116 as read]; because the root *madī harṣaglapanayoḥ* is read among the *ghaṭādi* verbs, it is called *mit*, and the shortening of the penult by *mitāṃ hrasvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-92 as read]; *laṅ*, third person plural, *jhi* → *anta* [*an* with loss]; loss of the *i* by *itaś ca*; loss of *t* by *saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ*; *śap*; *śap* is *ārdhadhātuka* in the Veda by *chandasy ubhayathā* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-117 as read], hence loss of *ṇi* by *ṇer aniṭi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-51 as read]; *nighāta* accent). The Rik is closed with *‖ 1 ‖* and a printed ornament.

## Rik 102.2 — printed pp. 319–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.2)**

> अस्य श्रवो नद्यः सप्त बिभ्रति द्यावाक्षामा पृथिवी दर्शतं वपुः ।
> अस्मे सूर्याचन्द्रमसाभिचक्षे श्रद्धे कमिन्द्र चरतो वितर्तुरम् ॥ २ ॥

*asya śravo nadyaḥ sapta bibhrati dyāvākṣāmā pṛthivī darśataṃ vapuḥ | asme sūryācandramasābhicakṣe śraddhe kam indra carato vitarturam ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.2)**

> अस्य । श्रवः । नद्यः । सप्त । बिभ्रति । द्यावाक्षामा । पृथिवी । दर्शतम् । वपुः ।
> अस्मे इति । सूर्याचन्द्रमसा । अभिऽचक्षे । श्रद्धे । कम् । इन्द्र । चरतः । विऽतर्तुरम् ॥ २ ॥

*asya | śravaḥ | nadyaḥ | sapta | bibhrati | dyāvākṣāmā | pṛthivī | darśatam | vapuḥ | asme iti | sūryācandramasā | abhi-cakṣe | śraddhe | kam | indra | carataḥ | vi-tarturam ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.2)**

> अस्येन्द्रस्य श्रवो यशः कीर्तिं सप्त इमं मे गङ्गे इत्यस्यामृचि प्राधान्येन प्रतिपादिता गङ्गाद्याः सप्तसंख्याका नद्यो बिभ्रति । धारयन्ति । वृत्रहननेनेन्द्रस्य यद्वृष्टेः प्रदातृत्वं तत्प्रभूतजलोपेता नद्यः प्रकटयन्तीत्यर्थः । अपि च द्यावाक्षामा द्यावापृथिव्यौ । पृथिवीत्यन्तरिक्षनाम । अन्तरिक्षं चास्य सूर्यात्मना वर्तमानस्येन्द्रस्य दर्शतं सर्वैः प्राणिभिर्दर्शनीयं वपुः । रूपनामैतत् । प्रकाशात्मकं रूपं धारयन्ति । किंच हे इन्द्र अस्मे अस्माकमभिचक्षे द्रष्टव्यानां पदार्थानामाभिमुख्येन प्रकाशनार्थं श्रद्धे कं श्रद्धार्थं । चक्षुषा दृष्टे हि वस्तुनीदं सत्यमिति श्रद्धोत्पद्यते । कमित्येतत्पादपूरणम् । तदुभयार्थं सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वितर्तुरं परस्परव्यतिहारेण तरणं पुनःपुनर्गमनं यथा भवति तथा चरतः । वर्तेते । त्वमेव तद्रूपः सन्वर्तस इत्यर्थः ॥ अस्य । ऊदिदमिति विभक्ते-
> *asyendrasya śravo yaśaḥ kīrtiṃ sapta imaṃ me gaṅge ity asyām ṛci prādhānyena pratipāditā gaṅgādyāḥ saptasaṃkhyākā nadyo bibhrati | dhārayanti | vṛtrahananendrasya yad vṛṣṭeḥ pradātṛtvaṃ tatprabhūtajalopetā nadyaḥ prakaṭayantīty arthaḥ | api ca dyāvākṣāmā dyāvāpṛthivyau | pṛthivīty antarikṣanāma | antarikṣaṃ cāsya sūryātmanā vartamānasyendrasya darśataṃ sarvaiḥ prāṇibhir darśanīyaṃ vapuḥ | rūpanāmaitat | prakāśātmakaṃ rūpaṃ dhārayanti | kiṃca he indra asme asmākam abhicakṣe draṣṭavyānāṃ padārthānām ābhimukhyena prakāśanārthaṃ śraddhe kaṃ śraddhārthaṃ | cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭe hi vastunīdaṃ satyam iti śraddhotpadyate | kam ity etat pādapūraṇam | tad ubhayārthaṃ sūryācandramasau vitarturaṃ parasparavyatihāreṇa taraṇaṃ punaḥpunargamanaṃ yathā bhavati tathā carataḥ | vartete | tvam eva tadrūpaḥ san vartasa ity arthaḥ ‖ asya | ūḍidam iti vibhakte-* *(the line continues on p. 320)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*asya* — of this Indra; *śravaḥ* — the fame; *sapta nadyaḥ* — the seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, too; *bibhrati* — make known (and carry); *dyāvākṣāmā* — heaven and earth; *pṛthivī* — the mid-air too; *darśatam* — [which in the form of the sun] charms all minds, becoming visible; *vapuḥ* — [Indra's] shining form; *prakāśayanti* — make manifest; *indra* — O Indra; *asme* — for us; *abhicakṣe* — in order that everything may become visible; *śraddhe tam* — and (after they have become visible) in order to produce faith in them; *vitarturam* — [their] eternal course, in the form of going and coming by their own movement; *carataḥ* — the sun and the moon and all the rest perform."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"The seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, bear and make known the fame of Indra. Heaven and earth and the mid-air make manifest the form of that Indra, shining in the form of the sun, charming all minds. O Indra, so that all things may become visible to us, and so that faith may be produced in them once they have become visible, the sun, the moon and all the rest also carry out their works, going and coming in their eternal course."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> The seven rivers display his glory ; heaven and earth, and sky display his visible form : the sun and moon, Indra, perform their revolutions, that we may see, and have faith in what we see.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.2 (Kannada)**

"*Śravaḥ* — *śravaḥ* means fame: '*śravaś ca praśaṃsāṃ ca*' [as read]: the Nirukta saying (*Ni.* 4-[?]2 as read [?]).

*Asya śravo nadyaḥ sapta bibhrati* — here 'the seven rivers' means the seven rivers named in the Ṛk *imaṃ me gaṅge* (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-75-5 as read [?]): Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, Parūṣṇī, Asiknī and Marudvṛdhā. These seven rivers hold up the fame of Indra. That is, Indra, having pierced the clouds and checked the downpour of rain on the earth, killed Vṛtra and caused the rain-water to fall on the earth; by that water the seven rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, fill with abundant water and flow, making manifest Indra's brave deeds, such as the slaying of Vṛtra, and so spread his fame: that is the chief intention. The matter of the slaying of Vṛtra as the cause for these rivers is supported by the Ṛks"

> अपामतिष्ठद्धरुणह्वरं तमोऽन्तर्वृत्रस्य जठरेषु पर्वतः ।
> अभीमिन्द्रो नद्यो वव्रिणा हिता विश्वा अनुष्ठाः प्रवणेषु जिघ्नते ॥
> *apām atiṣṭhad dharuṇahvaraṃ tamo 'ntar vṛtrasya jaṭhareṣu parvataḥ | abhīm indro nadyo vavriṇā hitā viśvā anuṣṭhāḥ pravaṇeṣu jighnate ‖*

> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-62-6 as read [?])

*(Glosses, mine and tentative: "The darkness, hard to cross, stood in the waters, within the bellies of Vṛtra, the mountain; Indra, the nadis fastened by the obstructor, all in the declivities he struck"; "That is the most sacrificial deed of this wonderful [god], the most beautiful of his works: when, in the recess, the four rivers, honey-streaming, he made swell".)*

"— [and others] support this.

*Dyāvākṣāmā* — since *gauḥ, gmā* and the like, the first of the twenty-one names of the earth (*pṛthivī*), include the word *kṣāmā* (*Ni.* 1-1[?] as read [?]), *dyāvākṣāmā* means heaven and earth: the heavenly world and the earth.

*Pṛthivī* — since the word *pṛthivī* is read among the sixteen names of the mid-air beginning with *ambara*, *viyat* [as read, ?], *pṛthivī* means the mid-air. Therefore, in the words *dyāvākṣāmā pṛthivī* said here, the three — earth, mid-air, heaven — are meant.

*Darśataṃ vapuḥ* — *darśanīyaṃ rūpam*: 'a form fit to be seen', a beautiful form. Earth, mid-air and heaven, making manifest the beautiful form of Indra who illumines the world in the form of the sun, spread his greatness: that is the chief intention."

**Special Topics of Rik 102.2, continued from p. 321 (Kannada)**

"*Abhicakṣe, śraddhe* — since we see with the eyes, the belief arises that such things are true. Therefore, the sun and moon, which every day, rising and setting again and again, become visible to us, always appear to our eyes, so that we may directly have faith in the greatness of Indra. For us men, among the things that appear to our eyes — that is, among mountains, rivers, trees and the like — the belief arises naturally that they are true; in the worlds such as heaven, which do not appear to the eyes, there is not so much belief. Therefore the sun and moon appear to our eyes every day. Since Indra himself has established them in the mid-air, whenever we look at the sun and moon the greatness of Indra comes within the range of our memory. Though we cannot see Indra's greatness directly, by looking at the sun and moon, which are visible to us, we can easily infer and understand him: this is the chief intention.

*Kam* — Yāska, on this word —"

"O Maghavan, wealthy Indra! For *sātaye* — for our gaining of wealth — *tam sma* — that very chariot — *prāva*: send forth, set in motion. O Indra, much praised (*puruṣṭuta*) by our minds, by our understanding! Your own, *jaitram* — victorious — chariot, which, in *saṃgame*, in the meeting with enemies, in battle (*ājā*), we *anumadāma* — we praise in succession. And, O Maghavan, to us, *tvāyadbhyaḥ* — who desire you — give *śarma*, happiness."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* ava *(the root* av *as a verb of motion here);* saṃgama *(*ap *in the sense of the object by* grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca*, with the accent of the last member);* ājā *(the locative ending replaced by* ḍā*);* tvāyat *(denominative* kyac *with* tva *for the stem as before, then* śatṛ*, and the single-substitute accent).)*

### Page 325 (PDF 345)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 14 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 325.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*maghavan indra* — O Indra, endowed with wealth; *sātaye* — (to us) for the gaining of wealth; *tam sma rathaṃ* — that chariot of yours; *prāva* — send quickly; *naḥ* — our; *manasā* — with mind (cordial); *puruṣṭuta* — O Indra, praised by us many times; *te* — your; *jaitraṃ* — which brings victory; *yam* — which chariot; *saṃgame* — which confronts enemies; *ājā* — [when] battle has come; *anumadāma* — we rejoice (seeing it in the field of battle); *maghavan* — O Indra, endowed with wealth; *tvāyadbhyaḥ* — to us who desire your help; *naḥ* — to us; *śarma* — happiness; *yaccha* — give."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, endowed with wealth! Send your chariot quickly, so that we may gain wealth. We praise you many times with cordial mind. And as soon as we see, in the field of battle, your victorious chariot, which confronts the enemies when battle has come, we rejoice that victory is assured to us. O Indra, endowed with wealth, give happiness to us who desire your help."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Maghavan, despatch your chariot to bring us wealth ; that victorious car, which, Indra, who are much praised by us in time of war, we rejoice to behold in battle : O, Maghavan, grant happiness to those who are devoted to you.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.3 (Kannada)**

"*Sma* — for the sake of the metre, the final letter of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text. The word means *eva*, 'just': *tam sma* — *tam eva*, 'that very one'.

*Pra ava* — *ava rakṣaṇagatikāntī…*: since the root *av* has many senses, such as protection, [Sāyaṇa] says that here the sense of motion is to be taken. So *prāva* means 'send, dispatch'.

*Saṃgame ājā* — *śatrubhiḥ saha saṃgamane ājā yuddhe*: in the battle in which one meets enemies: in the battle that brings one face to face with enemies."

### Page 326 (PDF 346)

*(Running head: left 326; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

**Special Topics of Rik 102.3, concluded from p. 325 (Kannada)**

"*Manasā puruṣṭuta* — *asmākaṃ buddhyā* — 'with our understanding', that is, with the mind, with faith, praised many times.

*Tvāyadbhyaḥ* — *tvāṃ kāmayamānebhyo no 'smākam*: to us who desire you (Indra). This word occurs in the Ṛgveda only in this Ṛk; it is not found in the Mantras elsewhere either.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.3)** *(grammar pages, pp. 326–327, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *ava* (the root *ava rakṣaṇādiṣu*, used here in the sense of motion; *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip*; *hi* for it; *śap*; loss of the *hi* by *ato heḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-105 as read]; since the verb stands at the beginning of the foot, the *nighāta* accent comes); *sātaye* (fixed by *nipātana* as acute on the last syllable by *ūtiyūti…* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-97 as read]; dative singular); *anumadāma* (root *madī harṣaglepanayoḥ* [as printed; *harṣaglapanayoḥ*]; *loṭ*, first person plural; because *yat* is related to it, the *nighāta* is prevented by *yadvṛttānnityam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-66 as read]; since *śap* is *pit*, it is unaccented; the *lasārvadhātuka* affix is unaccented by *tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāl lasārvadhātukam anudāttam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-186 as read], so the root's accent remains; the preverb *anu* receives the unaccented tone by *tiṅ codāttavati* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-71 as read]); *saṃgame* (root *gamḷ gatau*; *ap* in the sense of the object by *grahavṛdṛniścigamaś ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-58 as read]; the accent of the last member by *thāthaghañktājabitrāṇām* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-144 as read]; locative singular); *ājā* (the word *āji*, in the locative singular: the ending replaced by *ḍā* by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]; because of *ḍit*, loss of the *ṭi*-part); *tvāyadbhyaḥ* (*tvām ātmana icchati tvāyati*; *kyac* by *supa ātmanaḥ kyac* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-8 as read] after the word *yuṣmad*; *tva* for the stem up to *m* by *pratyayottarapadayoś ca* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-98 as read]; *ā* for the *d* by *vyatyaya*; the *kyac*-ending form takes the name of a root by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-32 as read]; *śatṛ* in the sense of the present; since the root has *a*-ending *upadeśa*, the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented and, the single substitute with the *a* of *kyac* by *ato guṇe*, the substitute is acute by *udāttenoodāttaḥ*, i.e. *ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-5 as read]; dative plural); *yaccha* (root *dāṇ dāne*; *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip*; *hi* for *sip* by *serhyapicca* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-87 as read]; *śap*; *pāghrādhmā…* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-78 as read]: *yaccha* substituted for the stem)" *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

## Rik 102.4 — printed pp. 327–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.4)**

> वयं जयेम त्वया युजा वृतमस्माकमंशमुदवा भरेभरे ।
> अस्मभ्यमिन्द्र वरिवः सुगं कृधि प्र शत्रूणां मघवन्वृष्ण्या रुज ॥ ४ ॥

*vayaṃ jayema tvayā yujā vṛtam asmākam aṃśam ud avā bhare-bhare | asmabhyam indra varivaḥ sugaṃ kṛdhi pra śatrūṇāṃ maghavan vṛṣṇyā ruja ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.4)**

> वयम् । जयेम । त्वया । युजा । वृतम् । अस्माकम् । अंशम् ।
> उत् । अव । भरेऽभरे ।
> अस्मभ्यम् । इन्द्र । वरिवः । सुऽगम् । कृधि । प्र । शत्रूणाम् । मघऽवन् । वृष्ण्या । रुज ॥ ४ ॥

*vayam | jayema | tvayā | yujā | vṛtam | asmākam | aṃśam | ut | ava | bhare-bhare | asmabhyam | indra | varivaḥ | su-gam | kṛdhi | pra | śatrūṇām | magha-van | vṛṣṇyā | ruja ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.4)**

> हे इन्द्र युजास्माभिर्युक्तेन सहायभूतेन त्वया वृतमावरणीयं शत्रुं वयं स्तोतारो जयेमु । अभिभवेम । अपि च भरेभरे संग्रामे संग्रामेऽस्माकमंशमस्मदीयं भागमुदव । शत्रुकृतपीडापरिहारेणोत्कृष्टं रक्ष । तथा हे इन्द्र वरिवो धनमस्मभ्यं सुगं सुगमनं सुप्रापं कृधि । कुरु । तथा हे मघवन् शत्रूणामस्मद्द्वेषकारिणां वृष्ण्या वृष्ण्यानि वीर्याणि प्र रुज । प्रभङ्गि । बाधस्वेत्यर्थः ॥ वृतं । वृङ् वरणे । क्विप्च्छन्दसि क्विप् । तुगागमः । सुगं । सुदुरोरधिकरण इति गमेर्डप्रत्ययः । कृधि । श्रुशृणुपृकृवृभ्य इति हेर्धिः । रुज । रुजो भङ्गे । तौदादिकः ॥
> *he indra yujāsmābhir yuktena sahāyabhūtena tvayā vṛtam āvaraṇīyaṃ śatruṃ vayaṃ stotāro jayemu | abhibhavema | api ca bhare-bhare saṃgrāme saṃgrāme 'smākam aṃśam asmadīyaṃ bhāgam udava | śatrukṛtapīḍāparihāreṇotkṛṣṭaṃ rakṣa | tathā he indra varivo dhanam asmabhyaṃ sugaṃ sugamanaṃ suprāpaṃ kṛdhi | kuru | tathā he maghavan śatrūṇām asmaddveṣakāriṇāṃ vṛṣṇyā vṛṣṇyāni vīryāṇi pra ruja | prabhaṅgi | bādhasvety arthaḥ ‖ vṛtam | vṛṅ varaṇe | kvip chandasi kvip | tugāgamaḥ | sugam | sudurorādhikaraṇa iti gamer ḍapratyayaḥ | kṛdhi | śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhya iti herdhiḥ | ruja | rujo bhaṅge | taudādikaḥ ‖*

*(The print's text is read as given;* kvip chandasi kvip *is the print's wording, perhaps for* kvip ca chandasi *[?].)*

"O Indra, we, the praisers, with you as our ally (*yujā*), united with us, would conquer (*jayema*) the enemy who is *vṛtam* — who is to be surrounded, [or] who besets us. And in battle after battle, *udava* — protect excellently — our portion, what belongs to us, by removing the oppression done by enemies. Likewise, O Indra, make *varivas*, wealth, *sugam* — easy to reach, easy to obtain — for us. And, O Maghavan, *pra ruja* — break, crush — the powers of the enemies who bear us hatred: oppress them, that is the sense."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized: the form* vṛta *(root* vṛ *'to choose, to cover', with* kvip *and the augment* tuk*);* suga *(root* gam *with* ḍa *when preceded by* su/dur *in the sense of the locus);* kṛdhi *(*dhi *for* hi *after* śru, śṛ, pṛ, kṛ, vṛ*);* ruja *(root* ruj *'to break', of the* tudādi *class).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*indra* — O Indra; *yujā* — (as our helper) joined with us; *tvayā* — by your help; *vṛtam* — [the enemy] who besets us; *vayam* — we (your devotees); *jayema* — may we conquer; *bhare-bhare* — in every battle; *asmākam* — our own; *aṃśam* — portion; *udava* — protect excellently; *indra* — O Indra; *varivaḥ* — wealth; *asmabhyam* — for us; *sugam* — easy to reach; *kṛdhi* — make; *maghavan* — O Indra, rich in wealth; *śatrūṇām* — of enemies; *vṛṣṇyā* — strengths; *pra ruja* — cause to be destroyed."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, by your help, with you united with us, may we conquer the enemy who besets us. In every battle protect our portion so that the enemies' oppression does not reach it. O Indra, make wealth easy for us to reach. And, O Indra, rich in wealth, cause the strength of our enemies to be destroyed."

### Page 328 (PDF 348)

*(Running head: left 328; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

**English Translation (as printed)**

> May we, having you for our ally, overcome our adversaries in every encounter ; defend our portion ; render riches easily attained by us ; enfeeble, Maghavan, the vigour of our enemies.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.4 (Kannada)**

"*Vayaṃ jayema tvayā yujā vṛtam* — *vṛṅ varaṇe*: 'to cover, to enclose': the intention is that, by your help, we may conquer the enemy who comes and encloses us for the sake of fighting.

*Asmākam aṃśam ut ava bhare bhare* — protect our portion, that is, our houses and the like, our wealth, our sovereignty and other things that belong to us, so that they do not fall under the power of enemies in each battle. Since the word *bhare* is read twice, it suggests the sense 'in every battle'."

### Page 329 (PDF 349)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 14 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 329.)*

"*Varivaḥ* — since *maghaṃ, reknaḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-eight names of wealth, the word *varivas* is also read there (*Ni.* 2-[?] as read [?]): *varivaḥ* means wealth.

*Sugaṃ kṛdhi* — make wealth easy to obtain for us.

*Vṛṣṇyā* — heroism, or valour.

*Ruja* — *rujo bhaṅge*: 'to break': *bhagnaṃ māḍu*, *nāśavāḍu*: break, destroy: *śatrūṇāṃ vṛṣṇyā pra ruja*: check the valour (the pride) of the enemies: that is the intention.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.4)** *(grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: *jayema* (root *ji jaye*; *vidhiliṅ*, first person plural, *mas*; loss of the *s* by *nityaṃ ṅitaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-99 as read]; *yāsuṭ* by *yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣūdātto ṅicca* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-103 as read]; *śap*; *guṇa* of the root vowel; *ay*-substitution; *iy*-substitution for *yās* by *ato yeyaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-80 as read]; loss of *y* by *lopo vyor vali* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-66 as read]; *nighāta*); *yujā* (root *yujir yoge*; *kvip* by *kvip ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-76 as read]; in the instrumental, acute on the ending by *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-168 as read]); *bhare-bhare* (the doubling by *nityavīpsayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-4 as read]; the latter, by *tasya parām āmreḍitam* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-2 as read], gets the name *āmreḍita*; it is unaccented by *anudāttaṃ ca* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-3 as read]); *vṛtam* (root *vṛṅ varaṇe*; *kvip* by *kvip ca*; since the affix is *kit*, no *guṇa*; *tuk* by *hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-71 as read]; accusative singular); *sugam* (root *gamḷ gatau*, with *su* as the preceding word, *ḍa* by *sudurosādhikaraṇe* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-48 as read]; by the force of its being *ḍit*, loss of the *ṭi*-part of the root; final acute by the affix); *kṛdhi* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*; *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip*; *hi* for it by *serhyapicca* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-87 as read]; by *śruśṛṇupṛkṛvṛbhyaś chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-102 as read] the substitute *dhi* for *hi*; *nighāta* accent at the end of the verb)" *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

### Page 331 (PDF 351)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 14 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 331.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.5)**

> हे धनानां धर्तर्गोहिरण्यादिरूपाणां द्रव्याणां धारयितरिन्द्र विपन्यवः स्तोतारः । स्तोतृनामैतत् । स्तोतार इमे जना अवसा रक्षणेन हेतुना त्वा त्वां हवमाना आह्वयन्तो नाना हि । विभिन्नाः खलु । तेषां मध्येऽस्माकं स्माकमेव सातये धनदानाय रथमातिष्ठ । आरोह । हे इन्द्र निभृतमव्याकुलं तव मनश्चित्तं जैत्रं हि । जयशीलं खलु । शत्रूञ्जित्वास्मभ्यं धनं दातुं समर्थमित्यर्थः ॥ सातये । षणु दाने । स्त्रिनि जनसनखनां सन्झलोरिति आत्त्वं ॥
> *he dhanānāṃ dhartar gohiraṇyādirūpāṇāṃ dravyāṇāṃ dhārayitar indra vipanyavaḥ stotāraḥ | stotṛnāmaitat | stotāra ime janā avasā rakṣaṇena hetunā tvā tvāṃ havamānā āhvayanto nānā hi | vibhinnāḥ khalu | teṣāṃ madhye 'smākaṃ smākam eva sātaye dhanadānāya ratham ātiṣṭha | āroha | he indra nibhṛtam avyākulaṃ tava manaś cittaṃ jaitraṃ hi | jayaśīlaṃ khalu | śatrūñ jitvāsmabhyaṃ dhanaṃ dātuṃ samarthām ity arthaḥ ‖ sātaye | ṣaṇu dāne | strini janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ ity ātvaṃ ‖*

*(The print's* smākam eva *is read as* asmākam eva *[?];* strini *is the print's, perhaps* ktini *[?].)*

"O *dhartaḥ*, upholder, bearer, of wealth in the form of cows, gold and the like! Indra! *Vipanyavaḥ* — praisers (this is a name for praisers); these praising people, for the sake of protection (*avasā*), calling you, are *nānā* — indeed varied, different. Among them, for our own sake, for the giving of wealth, mount your chariot, ascend. O Indra, your mind is *nibhṛtam* — undisturbed — *jaitram* — victorious, indeed: able, having conquered the enemies, to give wealth to us: that is the sense."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*dhanānām* — of wealth (in the form of cows, gold and the like); *dhartaḥ* — O Indra, the upholder; *vipanyavaḥ* — (your) devotees; *ime janāḥ* — these people (in the company of these people); *avasā* — with the object of obtaining protection; *tvā* — you; *havamānāḥ* — calling; *nānā hi* — are many (among them); *asmākaṃ sma* — for us; *sātaye* — for the giving of wealth; *ratham* — the chariot; *ā tiṣṭha* — mount; *indra* — O Indra; *nibhṛtaṃ* — undisturbed (smiling); *tava* — your; *manaḥ* — mind; *jaitraṃ hi* — is it not indeed victorious?"

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, upholder of wealth in the form of cows, gold and the like! Many are those in the company of these your devotees who call you with the object of obtaining protection. Among all of them, mount your chariot in order to give wealth to us in particular. O Indra, is not your smiling mind victorious?"

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Many are the men who call upon you for your protection : mount your car to bring wealth to us, for your mind, Indra, is composed, and resolved on victory.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.5 (Kannada)**

"*Vipanyavaḥ* — since *vipraḥ, ugraḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-four [as read, ?] names of the wise (*medhāvin*), the word *vipanyavaḥ* is read there too (*Ni.* 3-[?]9 as read [?]); the sense of this word is 'intelligent'. The bhāṣya-author says 'praisers'."

### Page 332 (PDF 352)

*(Running head: left 332; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

"*Nānā hi tvā havamānā janā ime vipanyavaḥ* — now, gathered here, those who call you and praise you are of many kinds: that is, their wishes are of many kinds. All of them call you and praise you, each for his own protection and each for the desired object he wants.

*Dhanānāṃ dhartaḥ* — one who holds cows, gold and other wealth: that is, one who has them at hand in order to give them to praisers, one who holds them in his hand.

*Asmākaṃ sātaye* — we also are among the praising people. What we need is wealth.

*Rathaṃ ā tiṣṭha* — mount (and set out in) the chariot (quickly), in order to give us wealth.

*Jaitraṃ hi indra nibhṛtaṃ manas tava* — O Indra, your mind is undisturbed, set only on victory: that is the intention.

It treats: *havamānāḥ* (root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *śānac* in the sense of the present; *samprasāraṇa* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; the single substitute by *samprasāraṇāc ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-108 as read]; *śap*; *guṇa* of the *u* because of it; *av*-substitution; *muk* to a stem ending in *a* by *āne muk* [Pā.
