**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*(indra — O Indra)*; *bāhū* — your two arms; *gojitā* — which conquer [enemies] and win cows; *amitakratuḥ* — [your] knowledge is unmeasured; *simaḥ* — [you are] most excellent; or one who binds enemies; *karman karman* — in every sacrificial act; *śatamūtiḥ* — endowed with a hundred kinds of protection; *khajaṅkaraḥ* — the maker of war; *akalpaḥ* — independent, not subject to the control of others; *indraḥ* — Indra; *ojasā* — of the strength [of all beings]; *pratimānam* — the type, the standard; *atha* — for that very reason; *siṣāsavaḥ* — men who desire to obtain wealth; *janāḥ* — people; *vi hvayante* — call [Indra] in many ways."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, your two arms conquer enemies and win cows. Your knowledge is unbounded. You are most excellent; you are endowed with a hundred kinds of protection in every sacrificial act; you are the maker of war; you are independent, not subject to the control of others. Indra is the standard of the strength of all beings. For that reason men who desire wealth pray to Indra and call him in many ways."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Your arms are the winners of cows, your wisdom is unbounded, you are most excellent, the granter of a hundred aids in every rite : the author of war, Indra is uncontrolled ; the type of strength ; therefore men, who are desirous of wealth, invoke him in various ways.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.6 (Kannada)**

"*Gojitā* — *śatrūṇāṃ parājayena gavāṃ lambhayitārau* | *gā jayata iti gojitau*: the hands of Indra, who has the capacity, in battle, to defeat the enemies and win the cows that are with them."

### Page 335 (PDF 355)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 14 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 335.)*

"*Amitakratuḥ* — here the word *kratu* has the sense of knowledge (*Ni.* 4-[?]3 as read [?]): one whose knowledge is unmeasured; there is no end to Indra's knowledge anywhere: the intention is that he is exceedingly wise.

*Simaḥ* — *ṣiñ bandhane*: *śreṣṭhaḥ*, 'most excellent': 'the most excellent one'. This word is found in the Ṛgveda —"

> तमित्पृच्छन्ति न सिमो वि पृच्छति स्वेनेव धीरो मनसा यदग्रभीत् ।
> *tam it pṛcchanti na simo vi pṛcchati svenēva dhīro manasā yad agrabhīt |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-145-1 as read [?])

> सिमु उक्ष्णोऽवसृष्टाः अदन्ति स्वयं बलानि तन्वः शृणानाः ।
> *simu ukṣṇo 'vasṛṣṭāḥ adanti svayaṃ balāni tanvaḥ śṛṇānāḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-28-[?] as read [?]; the print's first word clotted [?])

> यदेदयुक्त हरितः सधस्थादाद्रात्री वासस्तनुते सिमस्मै ।
> *yad edayukta haritaḥ sadhasthād ād rātrī vāsas tanute simasmai |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-115-[?] as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these. In these places the bhāṣya-author has given for the word *simu* the meaning 'all'. And *tathā ca śāṭyāyanakam* — *simu iti vai śreṣṭham ācakṣata iti*: 'as in the Śāṭyāyanaka, "they call the best *simu*"'. And *yadvā simaḥ śatrūṇāṃ bandhakaḥ*: 'or *sima* is the binder of enemies': the Śāṭyāyanins (the Sāmavedins) say that the word *simu* gives the sense 'most excellent'. Or, since the word *sima* is derived from the root *ṣiñ* with the sense 'to bind', the bhāṣya-author says the meaning is 'one who binds the enemies'. In this context *simaḥ* may also be taken as 'the most excellent among all men'.

*Karman karman* — in every act, in every sacrificial act; since the word *karman* is read twice, this means 'in every act': in the act performed by each praiser.

*Khajaṅkaraḥ* — *khaja manthe*: *khajati mathnāti puruṣān iti khajaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ* | *tasya kartā*: since the root *khaj* has the sense 'to churn, to oppress', *khaja* means the war that oppresses and harms men: *khajaṅkara* is the one who fights the enemies.

*Akalpaḥ* — *kalpenānyena rahitaḥ* | *advitīyaḥ* | *svatantra ity arthaḥ*: 'without any other [to compare]; without a second; independent'. Since no one is equal to him, he is without a second, or independent.

*Śatamūtiḥ* — *bahuvidharakṣaṇopetaḥ*: one who gives many kinds of protection to those who praise him. The word *śata* may be taken here in the sense 'many'.

*Pratimānam ojasā* — *sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām yad ojo balam asti tena sarveṇa pratimānaṃ pratinidhitvena mīyamānaḥ*: 'measured, as the representative of all the strength that there is in all living beings': whatever strength or capacity is in all beings, all of that is united in Indra" *(the sentence continues on p. 336)*

### Page 336 (PDF 356)

*(Running head: left 336; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

"[— all of that is united in Indra.] The strength of Indra alone is equal to the total strength and capacity of all living beings: that is the intention.

*Siṣāsavaḥ* — *vana ṣaṇa sambhaktau* | *dhanaṃ labdhukāmāḥ*: people who wish for wealth and the like.

*Janā vi hvayante* — *vividham āhvayanti*: 'they call in various ways': with praises and the like, and with the performance of sacrificial acts, they call Indra.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.6)** *(grammar pages, pp. 336–337, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *gojitā* (*gā jayataḥ iti gojitau*; the case-ending replaced by *ā* by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]); *bāhū* (*bādhata iti bāhuḥ*; the affix *ku* after the root *bādh* by *ārtidṛśikamibhyaḥ…* [Uṇ. Sū. 1-[?]2 as read, ?]; *h* for *dh*; final acute by the affix; dual); *amitakratuḥ* (*amitāḥ kratavaḥ yasya saḥ*; the accent of the first member by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 as read]); *simaḥ* (root *ṣiñ bandhane*; the Uṇādi affix *mak*; since it is *kit*, no *guṇa*; final acute by the affix); *karman karman* (the doubling by *nityavīpsayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-4 as read]; the latter, taking the name *āmreḍita*, is unaccented by *anudāttaṃ ca* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-3 as read]; the locative ending dropped by *supāṃ suluk…*); *khajaṅkaraḥ* (root *khaja manthe*; *ac* of the *pacādi* class by *nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-134 as read]; *khaja*; and by the *ca* of *kṣemapriyamadre 'ṇ ca* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-44 as read], which gathers what is not stated, *khac* after the root *ḍukṛñ* when *khaja* is the preceding word; *guṇa* of the root vowel because of the affix; *raparatva*; since it ends in a *kit* affix [*khac* is *khit*] the augment *mum* by *arurdviṣadajantasya mum* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-67 as read]; the form *khajaṅkara*; the accent of the last member by *gatikārakopapadāt kṛt* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-139 as read]); *akalpaḥ* (*na vidyate kalpo yasya saḥ akalpaḥ*; the accent of the last member by *nañsubhyām* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-172 as read])."

Sū. 7-2-49 as read], it being optional; *ā* for the nasal by *janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-42 as read]; the doubling of the root by *sanyaṅoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-9 as read]; shortening in the reduplicative by *hrasvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-4-59 as read]; *i* by *sanyataḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-4-79 as read]; *ṣ* for *s* by *ādeśapratyayayoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-3-59 as read]; the *san*-ending form takes the name of a root by *sanādyantā dhātavaḥ*; then *u* by *sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-168 as read]; loss of the *ā* of *san* [i.e. of the final *a*] by *ato lopaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-48 as read]; the form *siṣāsu*; since the *u*-affix is *sit-*like [as printed], the accent of the stem remains; nominative plural); *hvayante* (root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *laṭ*, third person plural; since a verb follows an indeclinable [*vi*], *nighāta*). ## Rik 102.7 — printed pp. 337–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.7)**

> उत्ते शतान्मघवन्नुच्च भूयस उत्सहस्राद्रिरिचे कृष्टिषु श्रवः ।
> अमात्रं त्वा धिषणा तित्विषे मह्यधा वृत्राणि जिघ्नसे पुरंदर ॥ ७ ॥

*ut te śatān maghavann ucca bhūyasa ut sahasrād ririce kṛṣṭiṣu śravaḥ | amātraṃ tvā dhiṣaṇā titviṣe mahy adhā vṛtrāṇi jighnase puraṃdara ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.7)**

> हे मघवन् धनवन्निन्द्र कृष्टिषु स्तोत्रषु मनुष्येषु त्वया दीयमानं श्रवो यदन्नमस्ति तच्छतात् शतसंख्याकाद्धनादुद्रिरिचे । उद्रिक्तमधिकं भवति । अपि च भूयसः शतसंख्याकादपि बहुतराद्धनादुद्रिरिचे । अधिकं भवति । किं बहुना । सहस्रात्संख्याकादपि वृत्युद्रिरिचे । त्वया दत्तं तदन्नमक्षयमित्यर्थः । अपि चामात्रं मात्रायेयत्तया रहितं परिगणितुमशक्यं सर्वैर्गुणैरधिकं त्वां मही महती धिषणास्मदीया स्तुतिलक्षणा वाक् तित्विषे । दीपयति । त्वत्सम्बन्धिनो गुणान्प्रकाशयति । हे पुरंदर शत्रूणां पुरां दारयितरिन्द्र अध स्तुत्यनन्तरं वृत्राण्यावरकान् शत्रूञ्जिघ्नसे । हंसि विनाशयसि ॥ रिरिचे । रिचिर् विरेचने । कर्मणि लिट् । तित्विषे । त्विष दीप्तौ । जिघ्नसे । हन्तेर्लेटि व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । लेटोऽडाटाविति अडागमः । बहुलं छन्दसीति शपः श्लुः । गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । स्थानिवद्भावाद्द्विर्वचनादि । बहुलं छन्दसीत्यभ्यासस्येत्वम् । पुरंदर । पूःसर्वयोर्दारिसहोः । पा. ३-२-४१ । इति खच् । खचि ह्रस्वः । पा. ६-४-९४ । इति ह्रस्वत्वम् । वाचंयमपुरंदरौ च । पा. ६-३-६९ । इति निपातनादमम् ॥

*(The print's* vṛty *in* sahasrāt saṃkhyākād api vṛty ud ririce *is clotted; probably* vṛtyā [?].)*

"O Maghavan, wealthy Indra! The *śravaḥ* — the food — that is given by you among the *kṛṣṭiṣu* — among men, the praisers — *ud ririce* — exceeds, is greater than, [food worth] a hundred. And more: it exceeds even what is more than a hundred. What need to say more? It exceeds even [food] in the thousands: that food given by you is inexhaustible. Furthermore, *amātram* — measureless, unlimited, impossible to reckon, surpassing in all qualities — you, *mahī dhiṣaṇā*, our great speech in the form of praise, *titviṣe* — makes bright, makes your qualities manifest. O *puraṃdara* — breaker of enemies' cities — Indra, thereafter, after the praise, you destroy the *vṛtrāṇi* — the enemies who obstruct."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read:* ririce *(root* ric *in the passive* liṭ*);* titviṣe *(root* tviṣ *'to shine');* jighnase *(*leṭ *of* han *with the middle voice by* vyatyaya*,* aḍāgama*, loss of the penult by* gamahana…*, doubling, and* i *in the reduplicative);* puraṃdara *(*khac *after* dṛ *when* pur *precedes, by* pūḥsarvayor dārisahoḥ *[Pā. Sū. 3-2-41, as read]; shortening before* khac*; the augment* am *by* vācaṃyamapuraṃdarau ca *[Pā. Sū. 6-3-69, as read]).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*maghavan* — O Indra, rich in wealth; *kṛṣṭiṣu* — to men (your devotees); *te* — your (the one you give with your favour); *śravaḥ* — food; *śatāt* — than what a hundred people need; *ut ririce* — is greater; *bhūyasaḥ* — than even that, a number exceeding it; *ut* — is greater; *ca* — and; *sahasrāt* — than what a thousand people need; *ut* — is greater; *amātraṃ* — (beyond men's reckoning) *tvā* — you; *mahī* — great; *dhiṣaṇā* — (our) speech in the form of praise; *titviṣe* — makes manifest; *puraṃdara* — O Indra, destroyer of the cities of enemies; *adha* — after (our) praise; *vṛtrāṇi* — the enemies who obstruct; *jighnase* — you destroy."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, rich in wealth, the food that you give with favour to your devotees among men is greater than what a hundred people need; it is greater than that, greater than the number that a thousand people need. Beyond men's reckoning, our great praise makes manifest and makes you shine. O destroyer of the cities of enemies, after our praise you destroy all our enemies by [your] extraordinary power."

### Page 339 (PDF 359)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 14 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 339.)*

**English Translation (as printed)**

> The food, Maghavan, (which is to be given by you) to men, may be more than sufficient for a hundred, or for more, even, than a thousand : great praise has glorified you, who are without limit, whereupon you destroy your enemies.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.7 (Kannada)**

"*Śravaḥ* — since *śravaḥ*, *andhaḥ*, *vājaḥ* and the like are read among the twenty-eight names of food, *śravaḥ* means *annam*, 'food' (*Ni.* 2-[7?] as read [?]).

*Kṛṣṭiṣu (tvayā dattaṃ yac chravastat) bhūyasaḥ sahasrāt ut ririce* — the food given by Indra to men — a hundred portions, still more, even a thousand portions more — grows in plenty: that is, it does not quickly come to an end. Therefore.

*Amātram* — *mātrāyeyattayā rahitaṃ parigaṇitum aśakyaḥ sarvair guṇair adhikam*: 'of whom no measure can be made; surpassing in all qualities': one who is so many-sidedly endowed with qualities that one cannot say 'this much': greater than all. To you who are such an Indra —

*Mahī dhiṣaṇā titviṣe* — this great, or extensive, speech in the form of praise, which we make, makes your surpassing qualities manifest: that is, 'we praise your excellent qualities at length'.

*Adha* — for the sake of the metre, the final letter of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text. *Adha* means *anantaram*, 'afterwards'.

*Adha vṛtrāṇi jighnase puraṃdara* — the prayer: 'after we have praised, destroy our enemies'.

*Puraṃdara* — *śatrūṇāṃ purāṃ dārayitar indra*: 'breaker of enemies' cities'. Concerning Indra's destroying the cities of the Dasyus, Śambara and the others —"

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.7)** *(grammar pages, pp. 340–341, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *ririce* (root *ricir virecane*; *liṭ* in the passive; the middle-voice affix by *bhāvakarmaṇoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 1-3-13 as read]; third person singular, *ta*; *eś* for it by *liṭas tajhayor eśirec* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-81 as read]; doubling of the root; *halādiśeṣa*; the form *ririce*; since it stands at the beginning of the foot [as printed: *ati…*], *nighāta*)" *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

### Page 341 (PDF 361)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 14 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 341.)*

The grammar of Rik 102.7 continues: *kṛṣṭiṣu* (root *kṛṣa vilekhane*; *ktic* by *ktic ktau ca saṃjñāyām* [Pā. Sū. 3-3-174 as read]; *ṭ* for the *t* of the affix by the *ṣṭutva* rule; acute on the last syllable by the affix; locative plural); *amātram* (*na vidyate mātrā yasya saḥ amātraḥ* — 'he whose measure does not exist'; the accent of the last member by *nañsubhyām* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-172 as read]); *titviṣe* (root *tviṣa dīptau*; *liṭ*, third person singular; *nighāta* at the end of the verb); *mahī* (in the Saṃhitā, from *mahatī*, the loss of *t* by *vyatyaya* in the Veda); *adha* (the letter-interchange, *tha* → *dha*); *jighnase* (root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *leṭ*, second person singular; the middle voice by *vyatyayo bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-85 as read], *se* for it; *aṭ* by *leṭo 'ḍāṭau* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-94 as read]; *śap* replaced by *śluḥ* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; doubling of the root by *ślau* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-10 as read]; *halādiśeṣa*; *ku*-to-*c*… *kuhoś cuḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-4-62 as read]; loss of the penult *a* by *gamahanajanakhanaghasāṃ lopaḥ kṅity anaṅi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-98 as read]; *i* for the *a* of the reduplicative by *abhyāsāc ca* [Pā. Sū. 7-3-55 as read]; *nighāta*); *puraṃdara* (root *dṝ vidāraṇe*; *khac* by *pūḥsarvayor dārisahoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-41 as read]; after the *ṇic*-ended form *dāri* [as printed], shortening of the penult before *khac* by *khici hrasvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-94 as read]; by *vācaṃyamapuraṃdarau ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-69 as read] the augment *am* is made by *nipātana*; in the vocative, the *nighāta* by *āmantritasya ca* [Pā. Sū. 8-1-19 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 7 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

## Rik 102.8 — printed pp. 342–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.8)**

> त्रिविष्टिधातु प्रतिमानमोजसस्तिस्रो भूमीर्नृपते त्रीणि रोचना ।
> अतीदं विश्वं भुवनं ववक्षिथाशत्रुरिन्द्र जनुषा सनादसि ॥ ८ ॥

*triviṣṭidhātu pratimānam ojasas tisro bhūmīr nṛpate trīṇi rocanā | atīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vavakṣithāśatrur indra januṣā sanād asi ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.8)**

> त्रिविष्टिऽधातु । प्रतिऽमानम् । ओजसः । तिस्रः । भूमीः । नृऽपते । त्रीणि । रोचना ।
> अति । इदम् । विश्वम् । भुवनम् । ववक्षिथ । अशत्रुः । इन्द्र । जनुषा । सनात् । असि ॥ ८ ॥

*triviṣṭi-dhātu | prati-mānam | ojasaḥ | tisraḥ | bhūmīḥ | nṛ-pate | trīṇi | rocanā | ati | idam | viśvam | bhuvanam | vavakṣitha | aśatruḥ | indra | januṣā | sanāt | asi ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.8)**

> हे नृपते नृणां पालयितरिन्द्र त्वमोजसः सर्वेषां प्राणिनां बलस्य प्रतिमानं प्रतिधिरसि । कीदृशं प्रतिमानम् । त्रिविष्टिधातु । धातुशब्दो रज्जुभागवचनः । यथा त्रिधातु पञ्चधातु वा शुल्वं करोतीति । यथा त्रिविष्टिस्त्रिगुणिता रज्जुर्दृढीयसी एवमिन्द्रोऽपि दृढतर इत्यर्थः । किंच त्वं तिस्रो भूमीरस्त्रीन् लोकान् त्रीणि रोचना त्रीणि तेजांसि दिव्यादिशाख्यमन्तरिक्षे वैद्युतरूपमग्निं पृथिव्यामाहवनीयादिरूपेण वर्तमानं पार्थिवमग्निं एवं त्रीन् लोकान् त्रीणि तेजांसि चाति ववक्षिथ । अतिशयेन वोढुमिच्छसि । अपि चेदं विश्वं सर्वं भुवनं भूतजातं चातिवोढुमिच्छसि । सर्वस्य जगतः पालनेन त्वमेव सर्वेषां निर्वाहको भवसीत्यर्थः । यस्माद्धे इन्द्र त्वं सनाच्चिरकालादारभ्य जनुषा जन्मना जन्मप्रभृत्यशत्रुः सपत्नरहितोऽसि ॥ त्रिविष्टिधातु । त्रिधा त्रिप्रकारेण विष्टया प्रवेशनेन विधीयते क्रियते इति त्रिविष्टिधातुस्त्रिगुणिता रज्जुः । विश प्रवेशने । स्त्रियां क्तिन् । ... [see p. 343]
> *he nṛpate nṛṇāṃ pālayitar indra tvam ojasaḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ balasya pratimānaṃ pratidhir asi | kīdṛśaṃ pratimānam | triviṣṭidhātu | dhātuśabdo rajjubhāgavacanaḥ | yathā tridhātu pañcadhātu vā śulvaṃ karotīti | yathā triviṣṭis triguṇitā rajjur dṛḍhīyasī evam indro 'pi dṛḍhatara ity arthaḥ | kiṃca tvaṃ tisro bhūmīr astrīn lokān trīṇi rocanā trīṇi tejāṃsi divyādiśākhyam antarikṣe vaidyutarūpam agniṃ pṛthivyām āhavanīyādirūpeṇa vartamānaṃ pārthivam agniṃ evaṃ trīn lokān trīṇi tejāṃsi cāti vavakṣitha | atiśayena voḍhum icchasi | api cedaṃ viśvaṃ sarvaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhūtajātaṃ cātivoḍhum icchasi | sarvasya jagataḥ pālanena tvam eva sarveṣāṃ nirvāhako bhavasīty arthaḥ | yasmāddhe indra tvaṃ sanāc cirakālād ārabhya januṣā janmanā janmaprabhṛty aśatruḥ sapatnarahito 'si ‖ triviṣṭidhātu | tridhā triprakāreṇa viṣṭyā praveśanena vidhīyate kriyate iti triviṣṭidhātus triguṇitā rajjuḥ | viśa praveśane | striyāṃ ktin | …*

*(The print's* astrīn *in the first clause stands for* tisras trīn *or the like; read* tīn lokān *[?]; and* divyādiśākhyam *is the print's reading of a clotted phrase [?].)*

"O *nṛpate* — protector of men — Indra! You are the *pratimāna*, the counterpart, the representative, of the strength (*ojas*) of all living beings. What kind of counterpart? *Triviṣṭidhātu*: the word *dhātu* means a strand of a rope; as in 'he makes a three-stranded, five-stranded cord'. As a *triviṣṭi* — a rope of three strands — is the stronger, so Indra too is stronger: that is the sense. And more: you *ati vavakṣitha* — desire to bear exceedingly — *tisro bhūmīḥ*, the three worlds, *trīṇi rocanā*, the three lights: the fire in the form of lightning in the mid-air, the earthly fire existing on the earth in the form of the *āhavanīya* and the rest, [and the sun in heaven] — thus the three worlds and the three lights. And you desire to bear this whole world, all beings. By protecting the whole world, you alone are the sustainer of all. For, Indra, from of old (*sanāt*), by birth (*januṣā*), from your birth on, you are *aśatru* — without a rival."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*nṛpate* — O Indra, protector of men; (*tvam* — you); *triviṣṭidhātu* — like a rope of three strands, strong; *ojasaḥ* — also of the strength [of all men]; *pratimānam* — you are the type, the counterpart; (and besides) *tisraḥ bhūmīḥ* — the three worlds, also; *trīṇi rocanā* — (the sun, lightning, and fire in the form of *āhavanīya*, etc.) these three lights, also; *ati vavakṣitha* — you desire to bear exceedingly (you are able); *idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanam* — all this world of beings also (you are able to bear); *indra* — O Indra; (*tvam* — you); *januṣā sanāt* — from birth, always (for a very long time) [*sanāt januṣā* — from before your birth, for a very long time]; *aśatruḥ* — without enemies; *asi* — you are."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, protector of men! As a rope woven of three strands is strong, so you are the counterpart of the strength of all men. And you desire to bear exceedingly the three worlds and the three lights, and you are able. You are able to bear together all this world of beings. O Indra, from your birth, and for a very long time, you are without an enemy who competes with you."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> Strong as a thrice-twisted rope, you are the type of strength ; protector of men, that are more than able to sustain the three spheres, the three luminaries, and all this world of beings, Indra, who have from birth ever been without a rival.

### Page 344 (PDF 364)

*(Running head: left 344; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.8 (Kannada)**

"*Idam uktaṃ bhavati* — [Sāyaṇa:] *sakalalokeṣu eteṣv ime ca bhuvane yatra sarveṣāṃ vastūnāṃ balam asti tasya triguṇaṃ balaṃ tvayi bhavatīti bhāvaḥ* | *imāś ca ye lokās tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo 'pi tvaṃ mahīyān bhavasi* | *ataḥ kāraṇān na ko 'pi tava śatruḥ kvāpi bhavatīti ca*: that is: in all the worlds, in these worlds, in all things and in all living beings and men, whatever strength and capacity there is, thrice that is in you, Indra; you are greater than all these worlds. Therefore you have no enemy anywhere, ever: that is the intention.

*Triviṣṭidhātu* — *dhātuśabdo rajjubhāgavacanaḥ* | *tridhā triprakāreṇa viṣṭyā praveśanena vidhīyate kriyata iti triviṣṭidhātus triguṇitā rajjuḥ* | *yathā tridhātu pañcadhātu vā śulvaṃ karotīti* | *yathā triviṣṭis triguṇitā rajjur dṛḍhīyasī evam indro 'pi dṛḍhatara ity arthaḥ*: here the word *dhātu* must be understood to mean 'rope' — 'cord'. *Tridhātu*: three separate strands are joined, and each of them is twisted together into one strand to make one cord; to make a rope, two or three such thin strands are twisted into one cord; and then three such twisted strands [of a hundred-fold? as read [?]], as before, are twisted into a stronger rope; and, further, for a still stronger and more lasting rope, three such twisted strands are joined and twisted again. A rope so made is very strong: so Indra is endowed with great strength: that is the sense. Here there is a special point in the offering of a three-strand-twisted rope as a comparison to Indra's strength. In this very Ṛk, the words *tisro bhūmīḥ* and *trīṇi rocanā* — as in a rope with three strands, one strand pervades the others in whatever way — in the same way Indra's strength and capacity pervade *tisro bhūmīḥ* — the three worlds, earth, mid-air and heaven — and *trīṇi rocanā* — shining through the three kinds of fire.

*Pratimānam ojasaḥ* — Indra's strength is the representative of the strength that is in all beings: the intention is that it is equal to the sum (the whole) of the strength [of all].

*Tisro bhūmīḥ* — *traya ime lokāḥ* | *dyauś ca pṛthivī cāntarikṣaṃ ca*: the three worlds, earth, mid-air and heaven. The words *tisro bhūmīḥ*, which indicate the three worlds —"

> तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन्त्रीरुत द्यून्त्रीणि व्रता विदथे अन्तरेषाम् ।
> *tisro bhūmīr dhārayan trīr uta dyūn trīṇi vratā vidathe antar eṣām |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-27-8 as read [?])

"— occur in Ṛks like these.

*Trīṇi rocanā* — *trīṇi tejāṃsi* | *divyādiśākhyam antarikṣe vaidyutarūpam agniṃ pṛthivyām āhavanīyādirūpeṇa vartamānaṃ pārthivam agniṃ*: the three lights: the light in the form of the sun in heaven (in the sky), the light in the form of lightning in the mid-air, and the light in the form of fire — the *āhavanīya* and the rest — on the earth: these three kinds of light. Or: the three circles of light.

*Ati idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vavakṣitha* — the whole movable world that has the form of the worlds said above — earth, mid-air, heaven — and all beings, the three kinds of luminaries, sun, lightning and fire: you, Indra, you protect and hold up all with your strength and capacity: that is the intention.

*Aśatruḥ indraḥ januṣā sanāt asi* — O Indra, since your birth you have never had a rival, anywhere. Here 'enemy' means one who stands against you, who fights you with strength. Such a mighty enemy of yours did not exist, does not exist now, and will not exist hereafter: you have unrivalled valour: that is the intention.

## Rik 102.9 — printed pp. 347–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.9)**

> त्वां देवेषु प्रथमं हवामहे त्वं बभूथ पृतनासु साससिः ।
> सेमं नः कारुमुपमन्युमुद्भिदमिन्द्रः कृणोतु प्रसवे रथं पुरः ॥ ९ ॥

*tvāṃ deveṣu prathamaṃ havāmahe tvaṃ babhūtha pṛtanāsu sāsahiḥ | sem̐ naḥ kārum upamanyum udbhidam indraḥ kṛṇotu prasave rathaṃ puraḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.9)**

> त्वाम् । देवेषु । प्रथमम् । हवामहे । त्वम् । बभूथ । पृतनासु । ससहिः ।
> सः । इमम् । नः । कारुम् । उपमन्युम् । उत्ऽभिदम् । इन्द्रः । कृणोतु । प्रऽसवे । रथम् । पुरः ॥ ९ ॥

*tvām | deveṣu | prathamam | havāmahe | tvam | babhūtha | pṛtanāsu | sasahiḥ | saḥ | imam | naḥ | kārum | upamanyum | ut-bhidam | indraḥ | kṛṇotu | pra-save | ratham | puraḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.9)**

> हे इन्द्र देवेषु प्रथमं श्रेष्ठं त्वां हवामहे । योगार्थमाह्वयामहे । तथा त्वं पृतनासु संग्रामेषु सासहिर्बभूथ । शत्रूणामभिभविताासि । उत्तरार्धः परोक्षकृतः । स इन्द्रो नोऽस्माकं कारुं स्तुतीनां कर्तारमुपमन्युमुपमन्तारं सर्वज्ञमुद्भिदं शत्रूणामुद्भेत्तारमिममेवंगुणविशिष्टं पुत्रं कृणोतु । करोतु । अपि च प्रसवे युद्धोत्पत्तावस्मदीयं रथं पुरोऽस्मभ्यो रथेभ्यः पुरतो वर्तमानं करोतु । यद्वा । कारुमित्यादीनि रथविशेषणानि । कारुं युद्धस्य कर्तारमुपमन्युमुपगतेन प्राप्तेन मन्युना क्रोधेन युक्तमुद्भिदं मार्गेऽवस्थितानां वृक्षादीनामुद्भेत्तारमतिवेगेन भङ्क्तारं ॥ बभूथ । बभूथातत्नथ जगृम्भ ववर्थेति निगम इति निपातनादिडभावः । स इमं । सोऽचि
> *he indra deveṣu prathamaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tvāṃ havāmahe | yogārtham āhvayāmahe | tathā tvaṃ pṛtanāsu saṃgrāmeṣu sāsahir babhūtha | śatrūṇām abhibhavitāsi | uttarārdhaḥ parokṣakṛtaḥ | sa indro no 'smākaṃ kāruṃ stutīnāṃ kartāram upamanyum upamantāraṃ sarvajñam udbhidaṃ śatrūṇām udbhettāram imam evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭaṃ putraṃ kṛṇotu | karotu | api ca prasave yuddhotpattāv asmadīyaṃ rathaṃ puro 'smabhyo rathebhyaḥ purato vartamānaṃ karotu | yadvā | kārum ity ādīni rathaviśeṣaṇāni | kāruṃ yuddhasya kartāram upamanyum upagatena prāptena manyunā krodhena yuktam udbhidaṃ mārge 'vasthitānāṃ vṛkṣādīnām udbhettāram ativegena bhaṅktāraṃ ‖ babhūtha | babhūthātatnatha jagṛmbha vavartheti nigama iti nipātanād iḍabhāvaḥ | sa imam | so 'ci* *(the line continues on p. 348)*

### Page 348 (PDF 368)

*(Running head: left 348; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

> […]लोपे चेत्पादपूरणमिति सुलोपः । प्रसवे । षूङ् प्राणिप्रसवे । ऋदोरप् । थाथादिनोत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वम् ॥
> *[…]lope cet pādapūraṇam iti sulopaḥ | prasave | ṣūṅ prāṇiprasave | ṛdor ap | thāthādinottarapadāntodāttatvam ‖*

"O Indra! *Prathamam* — the foremost, the most excellent — among the gods, you we call, for the sake of the sacrifice. And you have become *sāsahiḥ*, a conqueror, in battles; you are the overcomer of enemies. The second half is in the third person. That Indra — *kārum*, the maker of praises; *upamanyum*, the one who ponders closely, the all-knowing; *udbhidam*, the one who breaks up enemies — may he make our son, [one] of these qualities. And in *prasave*, in the arising of battle, may he set our chariot at the front, ahead of [other] chariots. Or [taking the epithets as of the chariot]: *kārum* — the maker of battle; *upamanyum* — joined to anger that has come upon it; *udbhidam* — one that breaks up trees and the like standing in the road, breaking them with great speed."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* babhūtha *(the absence of* iṭ *by* nipātana *in the Veda, in the list* babhūthātatnatha jagṛmbha vavartha*);* sa imam *(loss of the* su *of* saḥ*, when it fills out the foot);* prasave *(root* ṣū *with* ap*, with the accent of the last member). The words clotted in the print are marked [?].)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*(indra — O Indra)*; *deveṣu* — among gods; *prathamaṃ* — the first, or the best; *tvāṃ* — you; *havāmahe* — we call (for the sacrifice); *tvaṃ* — you; *pṛtanāsu* — in battles; *sasahiḥ* — one who defeats enemies; *babhūtha* — [you] have been; *saḥ indraḥ* — that Indra; *naḥ* — to us; *kāruṃ* — the praiser; *upamanyuṃ* — the all-knowing; *udbhidaṃ* — the destroyer of enemies; *imaṃ* — this son; *kṛṇotu* — may he favour. Or [*kāruṃ* — the maker of battle; *upamanyuṃ* — one who shows anger; *udbhidaṃ* — one who breaks up obstacles;] *imaṃ rathaṃ* — this our chariot; *prasave* — at the time when battle has begun; *puraḥ* — (before all other chariots) at the front; *kṛṇotu* — may he make."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, we call you, the best among all the gods, for the sake of the sacrifice. You defeat the enemies in battles. May that Indra favour this son of ours, who praises, who is all-knowing, who destroys enemies. Or: may he make this chariot of ours — which is the maker of battle, which shows anger, which breaks up obstacles — go at the front, ahead of all other chariots, at the times when battle has begun."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> We invoke you, Indra, the first among the gods ; you have been the victor in battles : may Indra put foremost in the battle this our chariot, which is efficient, impetuous, and the uprooter (of all impediments).

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.9 (Kannada)**

"*Tvāṃ deveṣu prathamaṃ havāmahe* — in these words, 'we call you, Indra, who are the best among all the gods'; or, when calling the gods, 'we call you first': that is the sense.

*Pṛtanāsu* — *saṃgrāmeṣu*: since *raṇaḥ, vivāk* and the like, the forty-four names of battle, include the word *pṛtanā*, *pṛtanāsu* means 'in battles' (*Ni.* 2-[?]7 as read [?])."

### Page 349 (PDF 369)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 15 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 349.)*

"*Sasahiḥ* — *śatrūṇām abhibhavitā*: one who makes the enemies be defeated. Here, for the sake of the metre, the first letter of this word is lengthened in the Saṃhitā text.

*Kārum* — since *rebhaḥ, jaritā* and the like, the nineteen names of the praiser, include the word *kāruḥ*, *kārum* means 'one who praises' (*Ni.* 3-[?]9 as read [?]). Also Yāska, on the Ṛk"

> दैव्या होतारा प्रथमा सुवाचा मिमाना यज्ञं मनुषो यजध्यै ।
> प्रचोदयन्ता विदथेषु कारू प्राचीनं ज्योतिः प्रदिशा दिशन्ता ॥
> *daivyā hotārā prathamā suvācā mimānā yajñaṃ manuṣo yajadhyai | pracodayantā vidatheṣu kārū prācīnaṃ jyotiḥ pradiśā diśantā ‖*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-110-7 as read [?])

"— in giving the derivation, says, *vidatheṣu kārū* — *yajñeṣu kartārau ṛtvijau*: 'in the sacrifices, the two priests who are the doers' — that is, he says that they are the two priests who take part in the sacrifices (*Ni.* 3-[?]1 as read [?]).

*Upamanyum* — *upamantāraṃ sarvajñam* | *yadvā upamanyum upagatena prāptena manyunā krodhena yuktam*: *upamantṛ* — one who knows all; or, the word *manyu* can also mean 'knowledge' — from the root *man* in the sense of 'to know' — [so] one who knows all, all-knowing. Or, since the word *manyu* has the sense 'anger', 'one who is full of anger' may be taken as the meaning. In this context the intention is that Indra, as he fights, is full of anger against enemies.

*Udbhidam* — *śatrūṇām udbhettāram*: one who breaks the enemies, who destroys them, who ruins them.

*Prasave* — *ṣūṅ prāṇiprasave*: the word *prasava* suggests 'to be born, to come about'. Here the sense is 'when battle has come about'.

*Indraḥ kṛṇotu prasave rathaṃ puraḥ* — on the field of battle, may our chariot be made to go ahead of the chariots of all; that is, we pray Indra that, so that we may fight against the enemies and defeat them, our chariot may be made to stand firmly in front of the enemy. In this Ṛk the first half is *pratyakṣakṛta* and the latter half *parokṣakṛta*. The explanation of *pratyakṣakṛta* and the like was given in the special topics of the first Ṛk of this sūkta (page 316).

## Rik 102.10 — printed pp. 350–[?]

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.10)**

> त्वं जिगेथ न धना रुरोधिथार्भेष्वाजा मघवन्महत्सु च ।
> त्वामुग्रमवसे सं शिशीमस्यथा न इन्द्र हवनेषु चोदय ॥ १० ॥

*tvaṃ jigetha na dhanā rurodhithārbheṣv ājā maghavan mahatsu ca | tvām ugram avase saṃ śiśīmasy athā na indra havaneṣu codaya ‖ 10 ‖*

### Page 351 (PDF 371)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 15 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 351.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.10)**

> त्वम् । जिगेथ । न । धना । रुरोधिथ । अर्भेषु । आजा । मघऽवन् । महत्ऽसु । च ।
> त्वाम् । उग्रम् । अवसे । सम् । शिशीमसि । अथ । नः । इन्द्र । हवनेषु । चोदय ॥ १० ॥

*tvam | jigetha | na | dhanā | rurodhitha | arbheṣu | ājā | magha-van | mahat-su | ca | tvām | ugram | avase | sam | śiśīmasi | atha | naḥ | indra | havaneṣu | codaya ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.10)**

> हे इन्द्र त्वं जिगेथ । शत्रूञ्जयसि । तथा धना शत्रुभ्योऽपहृतानि धनानि न रुरोधिथ । नावरुणत्सि । स्तोतृभ्यः प्रयच्छसीत्यर्थः । हे मघवन् धनवन्निन्द्र अर्भेषु अल्पेष्वाजा आजिषु संग्रामेषु महत्सु च प्रौढेषु संग्रामेषु चावसेऽस्माकं रक्षणार्थमुग्रमुद्गूर्णमधिकबलं त्वां सं शिशीमसि । स्तोत्रैस्तीक्ष्णीकुर्मः । अथानन्तरं हे इन्द्र त्वं हवनेषु युद्धार्थमाह्वानेषु सत्सु नोऽस्माञ्चोदय । संग्रामेषु प्रेरय । जयं प्रापयेत्यर्थः ॥ जिगेथ । जि जये । लिटि थलि क्रादिनियमात्प्राप्तस्येटोऽचस्तास्वत्थल्वेनिटो नित्यम् । पा. ७-२-६१ । इति प्रतिषेधः । सन्लिटोर्जेरित्यभ्यासादुत्तरस्य जकारस्य कुत्वम् । रुरोधिथ । क्रादिनियमादिट् । आजा । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या बहुवचनस्य डादेशः । शिशीमसि । शो तनूकरणे । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य श्लुः । आदेच उपदेशेऽशितीत्यात्वम् । द्विर्वचने बहुलं छन्दसीत्यभ्यासस्येत्वम् । ई हल्यघोरिति सेकारान्तादेशः । इदन्तो मसिः ॥
> *he indra tvaṃ jigetha | śatrūñ jayasi | tathā dhanā śatrubhyo 'pahṛtāni dhanāni na rurodhitha | nāvaruṇatsi | stotṛbhyaḥ prayacchasīty arthaḥ | he maghavan dhanavann indra arbheṣv alpeṣv ājā ājiṣu saṃgrāmeṣu mahatsu ca prauḍheṣu saṃgrāmeṣu cāvase 'smākaṃ rakṣaṇārtham ugram udgūrṇam adhikabalaṃ tvāṃ saṃ śiśīmasi | stotraiḥ tīkṣṇīkurmaḥ | athānantaraṃ he indra tvaṃ havaneṣu yuddhārtham āhvāneṣu satsu no 'smāñ codaya | saṃgrāmeṣu preraya | jayaṃ prāpayety arthaḥ ‖ jigetha | ji jaye | liṭi thali krādiniyamāt prāptasyeṭo 'cas tāsvat thalvenito nityam | Pā. 7-2-61 | iti pratiṣedhaḥ | sanliṭor jer ity abhyāsād uttarasya jakārasya kutvam | rurodhitha | krādiniyamād iṭ | ājā | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā bahuvacanasya ḍādeśaḥ | śiśīmasi | śo tanūkaraṇe | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya śluḥ | ādeca upadeśe 'śitīty ātvam | dvirvacane bahulaṃ chandasīty abhyāsasyetvam | ī halyagoḥ iti sekārāntādeśaḥ | idanto masiḥ ‖*

*(Reading note: the print's* ī halyagoḥ iti sekārāntādeśaḥ *is read as given; the sūtra is* ī halyaghoḥ *[?].)*

"O Indra! You *jigetha* — conquer enemies. And the *dhanā* — the riches carried off from [us by] enemies — you *na rurodhitha*, do not withhold: you give them to the praisers. O Maghavan, wealthy Indra! *Arbheṣu ājā* — in small battles — and *mahatsu ca* — in great, mature battles — for *avase*, our protection, we *saṃ śiśīmasi* — sharpen with praises — you, *ugram*, of upraised, greater strength. And then, O Indra, when there are *havaneṣu*, calls for battle, *codaya* — impel us, urge us into the battles: bring us victory: that is the sense."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* jigetha *(root* ji*; in the* liṭ *second person* thal*, the* iṭ *that* kradi*… would give is prohibited, as for* tās *[Pā. Sū. 7-2-61, as read], and* kutva *of the* j *after the reduplicative);* rurodhitha *(with* iṭ *by the* kradi *rule);* ājā *(*ḍā *for the plural ending of the locative);* śiśīmasi *(root* śo *'to sharpen';* śluḥ *for the* vikaraṇa*; the substitution* ā*; doubling;* i *in the reduplicative;* ī *by* ī halyaghoḥ *[?];* masi *with* i*).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*indra* — O Indra; *tvaṃ* — you; *jigetha* — conquer (enemies); *dhanā* — the riches taken by enemies; *na rurodhitha* — you do not withhold (you distribute to all your devotees); *maghavan* — O Indra, endowed with wealth; *arbheṣu ājā* — in small battles; *mahatsu ca* — and in great battles; *avase* — for (our) protection; *ugraṃ* — of fierce strength; *tvāṃ* — you; *saṃ śiśīmasi* — (by praises) we make sharp (make you well pleased); *atha* — afterwards; *indra* — O Indra; *havaneṣu* — when (for battle) we call; *naḥ* — us; *codaya* — urge on."

### Page 352 (PDF 372)

*(Running head: left 352; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 102".)*

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, you conquer enemies. You do not withhold the riches taken from enemies, but distribute them to all your devotees. O Indra, endowed with wealth, in small battles and in great battles, for our protection, we make you of fierce strength sharp, [that is, well pleased], with our praises. Afterwards, at the times of battle, forgive our call, come, and urge us on."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> You conquer, and withhold not the booty : in trifling or serious conflicts, we sharpen you, fierce Maghavan, for our defence ; do you therefore, inspirit us in our defiances.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 102.10 (Kannada)**

"*Arbheṣu* — *arbha* is a name for 'small'. *Arbhake avṛddhe* [Yāska] (*Ni.* 4-[?]3): 'small, not grown, not mature'.

*Arbheṣu mahatsu ca ājā* — in small contests or in great battles: that is the sense.

*Ugraṃ* — *udgūrṇam adhikabalam*: you who are valiant, or of superior strength, Indra.

*Śiśīmasi* — *stotrais tīkṣṇīkurmaḥ* | *śo tanūkaraṇe*: with praises, and so on, we praise you and make your understanding sharp.

*Havaneṣu* — this is a synonym of the words *āhava*, *yuddha*, 'battle': in battles.

Some are of the opinion that the seer made this praise to pray to Indra to obtain victory at the time when battle has come about. For in the Ṛks too, a prayer that the words connected with battle may bring victory is plainly expressed.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 102.10)** *(grammar pages, pp. 352–353, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar page, noted briefly. It treats: *jigetha* (root *ji jaye*; *liṭ*, second person singular; *thal* for *sip* by *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatususthalthusaṇalvamāḥ* [Pā. Sū. 3-4-82 as read]; by *kṛsṛbhṛvṛstudrusruśruvo liṭi* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-13 as read] the *iṭ* is fixed [as printed: *iṇ-niṣedha*…]; though it would come, by *acas tāsvat thalo nityam anito* [Pā. Sū. 7-2-61 as read] the *iṭ* is prohibited, for the root ends in a vowel)" *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

The grammar of Rik 102.10 continues: *jigetha* (continued: because the root ends in a vowel, the prohibition of *iṭ* is repeated for *thal*; doubling of the root because of *liṭ*; *k* for the *j* after the reduplicative by *sanliṭoś ceḥ* [as printed; i.e. *sanliṭoḥ jeḥ*, Pā. Sū. 7-3-57 as read]; *guṇa* by *sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*; the form *jigetha*; *nighāta*); *dhanā* (*dhanāni*; loss of *śi* by *śeś chandasi bahulam* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-70 as read]); *rurodhitha* (root *rudhir āvaraṇe*; *liṭ*, second person singular; *thal*; as before, by the rule on *kradi* the augment *iṭ* comes to *thal*; doubling of the root; *nighāta*); *ājā* (the word *āji*; the locative ending *ḍā* by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]; since *ḍit*, loss of the *ṭi*-part); *avase* (root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *asun*, which goes with all roots; acute on the first syllable, the affix being *nit*; dative singular); *śiśīmasi* (root *śo tanūkaraṇe*; *laṭ*, first person plural, *masi*; *śap* replaced by *śluḥ* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *ā* for the *o* by *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-45 as read]; doubling by *ślau* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-10 as read]; *i* in the reduplicative by *bahulaṃ chandasi* [Pā. Sū. 7-4-78 as read]; *ī* for the root's *ā* by *ī halyaghoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-113 as read], the word having the name *abhyasta*; the augment *i* to *masi* by *idanto masiḥ* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-46 as read]; *nighāta*); *atha* (the lengthening *athā* in the Saṃhitā by *nipātasya ca* [Pā. Sū. 6-3-136 as read]); *codaya* (root *cuda preraṇe*, *curādi*; *ṇic* in its own sense by *satyāpapāśa…* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-25 as read]; after the *ṇic*-ended form, *loṭ*, second person singular, *sip*, *hi* for it; *śap*; *guṇa* of *ṇic*; *ay*-substitution; *nighāta*). ## Rik 102.11 — printed pp. 354–355 *(the last Rik of Sūkta 102; Triṣṭubh)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥ — Saṃhitā-pāṭha (Rik 102.11)**

> विश्वाहेन्द्रो अधिवक्ता नो अस्त्वपरिह्वृताः सनुयाम वाजम् ।
> तन्नो मित्रो वरुणो मामहन्तामदितिः सिन्धुः पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ ११ ॥

*viśvāhendro adhivaktā no astv aparihvṛtāḥ sanuyāma vājam | tan no mitro varuṇo māmahantām aditiḥ sindhuḥ pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥ — Pada-pāṭha (Rik 102.11)**

> विश्वाहा । इन्द्रः । अधिऽवक्ता । नः । अस्तु । अपरिऽह्वृताः । सनुयाम । वाजम् ।
> तत् । नः । मित्रः । वरुणः । मामहन्ताम् । अदितिः । सिन्धुः । पृथिवी । उत । द्यौः ॥ ११ ॥

*viśvāhā | indraḥ | adhi-vaktā | naḥ | astu | apari-hvṛtāḥ | sanuyāma | vājam | tat | naḥ | mitraḥ | varuṇaḥ | māmahantām | aditiḥ | sindhuḥ | pṛthivī | uta | dyauḥ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 102.11)**

> व्याख्यातेयं रोहिच्छ्यावेति वर्गे । इन्द्रः सर्वेष्वहःसु अस्माकं पक्षपातेन वक्ता भवतु । वयं चाकुटिलगतयः सन्त इन्द्रेण दत्तमन्नं लभामहे । यदस्माभिः प्रार्थितमस्मदीयं तन्मित्रादयः पूजितं कुर्वन्तु ॥
> *vyākhyāteyaṃ rohicchyāveti varge | indraḥ sarveṣv ahaḥsu asmākaṃ pakṣapātena vaktā bhavatu | vayaṃ cākuṭilagatayaḥ santa indreṇa dattam annaṃ labhāmahe | yad asmābhiḥ prārthitam asmadīyaṃ tan mitrādayaḥ pūjitaṃ kurvantu ‖*

"This [Ṛk] was explained in the *varga* beginning *rohicchyāvā* [i.e. at Rik 100.19, where the same words occur]. May Indra, on all days, speak for us with partiality; and we, going on straight paths, receive the food given by Indra. What we have prayed for, may Mitra and the rest honour."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*viśvāhā* — at all times; *naḥ* — for us; *indraḥ* — Indra; *adhivaktā* — one who speaks words of partisanship; *astu* — may he be (and we also); *aparihvṛtāḥ* — leaving the crooked path (staying on the straight path); *vājam* — (abundant) food; *sanuyāma* — may we enjoy; *naḥ* — our; *tat* — that prayed-for desired object; *mitraḥ* — Mitra; *varuṇaḥ* — and Varuṇa; *aditiḥ* — Aditi; *sindhuḥ* — the deity presiding over the sea; *pṛthivī* — the earth; *uta* — and; *dyauḥ* — the heavenly world also; *māmahantām* — may they guard."

## Sūkta 103

**ನೂರಮೂರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು** — *nūramūraneya sūktavu*, "the hundred-and-third Sūkta" *(Kannada heading)*

**Sāyaṇa's introduction to Sūkta 103 (Sanskrit in Kannada script; doubtful places [?]):**

> तत्त इत्यष्टर्चं दशमं सूक्तं कुत्सस्यार्षमैन्द्रं त्रैष्टुभम् । तथा चानुक्रान्तम् । तत्तेऽष्टेति ॥ तृतीये छन्दोमे निष्केवल्य इदं सूक्तं निविद्धानम् । विश्वजित इति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । तत्त इन्द्रियमिति निष्केवल्यम् । आ. ८-२ [?] । इति ॥
> *tat ta ity aṣṭarcaṃ daśamaṃ sūktaṃ kutsasyārṣam aindraṃ traiṣṭubham | tathā cānukrāntam | tat te 'ṣṭeti ‖ tṛtīye chandome niṣkevalya idaṃ sūktaṃ nividdhānam | viśvajita iti khaṇḍe sūtritam | tat ta indriyam iti niṣkevalyam | Ā. 8-2 [?] iti ‖*

*(Sense, mine, from the Kannada that follows: "The tenth sūkta, of eight Ṛks, beginning* tat te*, is the seer-composition of Kutsa, addressed to Indra, in Triṣṭubh. So the Anukramaṇī: '*tat te* — eight.' In the third* chandoma *day, at the* niṣkevalya *[śastra], this sūkta is used as the* nivid*-dhāna [i.e. in place of the* nivid*]. It is set down in the section called* Viśvajit*: '*tat ta indriyam* — the* niṣkevalya*.'")*

*(A rule of dashes follows.)*

### Page 356 (PDF 376)

*(Running head: left 356; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 103".)*

**Anuvāda of Sūkta 103 (Kannada)**

"*Tat te indriyam* — this sūkta is the tenth sūkta in the fifteenth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Kutsa. The deity is Indra. The metre is Triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said, beginning, *tat te 'ṣṭā*. In the third *chandoma* day, when the mantras of the Niṣkevalya *śastra* are being recited, this sūkta is to be used first, as the *nivid* mantra: it is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, in the section called *Viśvajit*, by the aphorism *tat ta indriyam iti niṣkevalyam* (*Ā.* 8-2 as read)."

*(A rule of dashes follows.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 103.1)**

> हे इन्द्र ते त्वदीयं परमुत्कृष्टं तत्प्रसिद्धमिदं वर्तमानमिन्द्रियं बलं पुरा पूर्वस्मिन्काले कवयः क्रान्तदर्शिनः स्तोतारः पराचैः पराचीनं पराङ्मुखं । यद्वा । पराचैः पराञ्चनैः पराग्गमनैर्युक्तं । यद्वाभिमुखमेवाधारयन्त । धृतवन्तः । अपि चास्येन्द्रस्यान्यदेकमिदमग्न्याख्यं ज्योतिः क्षमा क्षमायां भूमौ वर्तते । अन्यदपरमेकं सूर्याख्यं दिवि द्युलोके । ईं तदिदमुभयविधमिन्द्रस्य ज्योतिः संपृच्यते । परस्परं सं युज्यते । रात्र्यादित्यादिनिन्द्रेण [?] संयुक्तो भवति । अग्निं वाऽऽदित्यः सायं प्रविशति । तस्मादग्निर्दोरात्रस्कृतं दद्दृश इति श्रुतेः । अहनि त्वग्निः सूर्येण संगच्छते । उद्यन्तं वाऽऽदित्यमग्निरनुसमारोहति । तस्माद्धूम एवाग्नेर्दिवा ददृश इति श्रुतेः । तै. ब्रा. २-१-२-१० [?] । अनयोः परस्परसंगमने दृष्टान्तः । समनेव केतुः । समनशब्दः संग्रामवाची । यथा समने संग्रामे युध्यमानयोरुभयोः केतुर्ध्वजो ध्वजान्तरेण संयुज्यते तद्वत् ॥ इन्द्रियं । इन्द्रस्य लिङ्गं बलं । इन्द्रियमिन्द्रमिति घच्छत्ययान्तो निपात्यते । पराचैः । अव्ययमेतत् उच्चैर्नीचैरिति यथा । यास्कस्त्वाह । पराचैः पराञ्चनैः । नि. ११-[?]२ । इति । क्षमा । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या लुक् । ईमो मलोपः सांहितिकश्छान्दसः । समनेव । षम ष्टम अवैक्लव्ये । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते । पा. ३-२-१७८ । इति युच् । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्या आकारः । इवेन विभक्त्यलोपः पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं चेति समासः ॥
> *he indra te tvadīyaṃ param utkṛṣṭaṃ tat prasiddham idaṃ vartamānam indriyaṃ balaṃ purā pūrvasmin kāle kavayaḥ krāntadarśinaḥ stotāraḥ parācaiḥ parācīnaṃ parāṅmukhaṃ | yadvā | parācaiḥ parāñcanaiḥ parāggamanair yuktaṃ | yadvābhimukham evādhārayanta | dhṛtavantaḥ | api cāsyendrasyānyad ekam idam agnyākhyaṃ jyotiḥ kṣamā kṣamāyāṃ bhūmau vartate | anyad aparam ekaṃ sūryākhyaṃ divi dyuloke | īṃ tad idam ubhayavidham indrasya jyotiḥ saṃpṛcyate | parasparaṃ saṃ yujyate | rātryādityād indreṇa [?] saṃyukto bhavati | agniṃ vā''dityaḥ sāyaṃ praviśati | tasmād agnir dorātraskṛtaṃ dadṛśa iti śruteḥ | ahani tv agniḥ sūryeṇa saṃgacchate | udyantaṃ vā''dityam agnir anusamārohati | tasmād dhūma evāgner divā dadṛśa iti śruteḥ | Tai. Brā. 2-1-2-10 [?] | anayoḥ parasparasaṃgamane dṛṣṭāntaḥ | samaneva ketuḥ | samanaśabdaḥ saṃgrāmavācī | yathā samane saṃgrāme yudhyamānayor ubhayoḥ ketur dhvajo dhvajāntareṇa saṃyujyate tadvat ‖ indriyam | indrasya liṅgaṃ balam | indriyam indram iti ghacchatyayānto nipātyate | parācaiḥ | avyayam etat uccair nīcair iti yathā | yāskas tv āha | parācaiḥ parāñcanaiḥ | Ni. 11-[?]2 | iti | kṣamā | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā luk | īmo malopaḥ sāṃhitikaś chāndasaḥ | samaneva | ṣama ṣṭama avaiklavye | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate | Pā. 3-2-178 | iti yuc | supāṃ suluk iti saptamyā ākāraḥ | ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ceti samāsaḥ ‖*

*(The print's* rātryādityād indreṇa saṃyukto bhavati *is clotted and read as given [?];* ghacchatyayānto *is the print's reading of the rule-name for* indriya *[?].)*

"O Indra! That famed, excellent *indriya* of yours — [your] strength, which is present now — in former times the *kavayaḥ*, the far-seeing praisers, *adhārayanta* — upheld, [as] *parācaiḥ*, turned away [or: with turning-away goings; or: facing]. And, of this Indra, one light, called fire, is on the earth (*kṣamā*); another, called the sun, in heaven. These two kinds of light of Indra *sam pṛcyate* — are joined together. As the scripture says, 'In the evening the sun enters the fire; therefore the fire is seen as the work of day and night [? as read]'; 'by day the fire joins the sun; the fire mounts after the rising sun; therefore it is the smoke of the fire that is seen by day' (*Tai. Brā.* 2-1-2-10 as read [?]). A comparison for their joining one another: *samaneva ketuḥ* — the word *samana* means battle: as in battle, between two who fight, the banner of one joins the other's banner, so [these two lights]."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized:* indriya *(= 'the sign of Indra': strength; the suffix* gha*/*cha *fixed by* nipātana*);* parācaiḥ *(an indeclinable, like* uccaiḥ, nīcaiḥ*; Yāska:* parācaiḥ parāñcanaiḥ *[Ni. 11-?2, as read, ?]);* kṣamā *(the locative ending dropped);* ī *(loss of the* m*, in the Saṃhitā, Vedic);* samana *(root* ṣam/ṣṭam *'to be unagitated' with* yuc *by* anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate *[Pā. Sū. 3-2-178, as read]; the compound with* iva*).)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha of Rik 103.1, continued from p. 357 (Kannada)**

"[*purā* —] in former times; *kavayaḥ* — the far-seeing praisers; *parācaiḥ* — (as one that was not hostile to the gods) as if facing away (as if facing the enemies); *adhārayanta* — they upheld [it] and understood [it]; *asya* — of this Indra; *anyat* — one portion; *idam* — the light called Agni; *kṣamā* — on the earth; *anyat* — another portion; the light called the sun; *divi* — in the mid-air [heaven]; (thus) *īm* — both these kinds of light of Indra; *samanā* — in the field of battle; *ketuḥ iva* — like the banners (of the two sides); *saṃ pṛcyete* — join together."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"O Indra, in former times the far-seeing praisers understood your excellent, well-known, visible strength, as if they were always ready for battle [against the enemy]. A portion of Indra, the light called Agni on the earth, and another portion, the light called the sun, spreading in the mid-air, join together as the banners of the two sides do when they come together in the field of battle: by day Agni joins the sun, and by night the sun joins Agni."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> The sages have formerly been possessed of this your supreme power, Indra, as if it were present with them, one light of whom shines upon the earth, the other in heaven, and both are in combination with each other, as banner (mingles with banner) in battle.

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 103.1 (Kannada)**

"*Indriyam* — *balam*, 'strength'. In this Ṛk, Sāyaṇa has given for the word *indriya* the meaning 'strength'; Skandasvāmin has given 'strength or wealth'. The Nirukta-author has included this word among the twenty-eight names of wealth beginning *maghaṃ, reknaḥ* (*Ni.* 2-[?] as read [?]). Whether as strength, as wealth, or as any other meaning, since it is connected with Indra, the sense of *indriya* or the derivation of the word is known from many sentences of the Ṛksaṃhitā. Besides these two meanings, it is also understood that it is suited to being offered to Indra and that it gives satisfaction to Indra."

> स इद्वने नमस्युभिर्वचस्यते चारु जनेषु प्रब्रुवाण इन्द्रियम् ।
> *sa id vane namasyubhir vacasyate cāru janeṣu prabruvāṇa indriyam |*

> *māntarāṃ bhujam ā rīriṣo naḥ śraddhitaṃ te mahata indriyāya |*

### Page 360 (PDF 380)

*(Running head: left 360; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 103".)*

"— in Ṛks like these, *indriya* is also given the sense 'wealth, sovereignty (*aiśvarya*)'. Thus, as the word *indriya* has derivations according to the context, with the different meanings that arise in each place, the sense of strength, or wealth, may be given in this Ṛk, suited to the context.

*Parācaiḥ* — this word has been explained with a distinct sense by the bhāṣya-author. After first giving a meaning of his own, he afterwards cites the derivation in the Nirukta: *parācaiḥ parācīnena parāṅmukham* — he first explains 'turned away, with the face turned', and afterwards '*parācaiḥ parāñcanaiḥ parāgamanair yuktam*' — 'joined with turning away': and so he has told also the Nirukta-author's derivation, that it means 'joined with the going away' (*Ni.* 11-[?]2 as read [?]). The Nirukta-author, in the Ṛk of the tenth *maṇḍala* —"

> किमिच्छन्ती सरमा प्रेदमानड् दूरे ह्यध्वा जगुरिः पराचैः ।
> *kim icchantī saramā predam ānaḍ dūre hy adhvā jaguriḥ parācaiḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 10-108-[?] as read [?])

"— in explaining this Ṛk he explains *parācaiḥ* as '*parāñcanair gatiḥ*', and Durgācārya has given the explanation of *parāmukhaiḥ añcanair gamanaiḥ ayito gataḥ*, *viprakṛṣṭo devanivāsāt* — 'gone by goings that are turned away; far from the abode of the gods' [as read, ?]. On the whole, it appears that the meaning to be taken is 'facing away': that is, that Indra's power was always, from the world of the gods, turned away from [the gods] and facing the enemies; that it was always turned against enemies and was intent on [their] conquest. Likewise —"

> बाधस्व दूरे निर्ऋतिं पराचैः कृतं चिदेनः प्र मुमुग्ध्यस्मत् ।
> *bādhasva dūre nirṛtiṃ parācaiḥ kṛtaṃ cid enaḥ pra mumugdhy asmat |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-[?]4-9 as read [?])

> आरे बाधेथां निर्ऋतिं पराचैरस्मे भद्रा सौश्रवसानि सन्तु ।
> *āre bādhethāṃ nirṛtiṃ parācair asme bhadrā sauśravasāni santu |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-[?]4-3 as read [?])

"— in all Ṛks like these, 'turned away' is the apt meaning for the context. But in the Ṛk at hand it is hard to establish the sense definitely. As said above, the point may be made that Indra's strength has always been facing the enemies, away from the world of the gods.

*Kavayaḥ adhārayanta* — *stotāraḥ dhṛtavantaḥ*: 'the praisers understood that Indra's power was ever facing the enemies': that is the sense.

*Kṣamed am anyad divy anyat* — *idam agnyākhyaṃ jyotiḥ kṣamā bhūmau vartate* | *anyad asyaikaṃ sūryākhyaṃ dyuloke*: the fire-like light of Indra on earth, and the sun-like light in the mid-air, spreading" *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

### Page 361 (PDF 381)

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 16 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 361.)*

"— as described in the passage *udyantaṃ vā ādityam agnir anusamārohati* (*Tai. Brā.* 2-1-2-10 as read [?]), by day the fire joins the sun, and by night the sun joins the fire: so it is described.

*Samanā iva ketuḥ* — *samanaśabdaḥ saṃgrāmavācī* (*Ni.* 2-[?]7 as read [?]): *yathā samane saṃgrāme yudhyamānayor ubhayor dhvajau dhvajāntareṇa saṃyujyate tadvat*: *samana* means battle. As in battle the two banners join each other, so — this simile is applied to the joining of the sun and fire. The words that carry the simile, *samanā iva*, are used also in some other places, but their sense differs there; it must be noted. The reason is the difference of accent: the foot order *sa-ma-nā iva* is used in this Ṛk only. As for the rest —"

> अभि प्रवन्त समनेव योषाः कल्याण्यः स्मयमानासो अग्निम् ।

> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 6-[?]3-[?] as read [?])

> समनेव वपुष्यतः कृणवन्नानुषा युगा ।

> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 8-[?]-[?] as read [?])

"— in these Ṛks *samanā iva* in the order is for *samānamanaskā yoṣitā iva* — 'like women with the same mind': 'like women of one mind': so the sense of *samana* here is not 'battle'. In the Ṛk in question only, *samana* means 'battle'.

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *indriyam* (*indrasya liṅgaṃ balam indriyam*; *indriyam indraliṅgam indradṛṣṭam indrasṛṣṭam indrajuṣṭam indradattam iti vā* [Pā. Sū. 5-2-93 as read], by *nipātana* ending in the affix *gha* [*cha*, as printed]; final acute by the affix by *citaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-163 as read]); *parācaiḥ* (like *uccaiḥ, nīcaiḥ*, an indeclinable; Yāska says it so: *parācaiḥ parāñcanaiḥ* [*Ni.* 11-?2 as read, ?]); *adhārayanta* (root *dhṛṅ avasthāne*; because the causative sense is shown, *ṇic*; after the *ṇic*-ended form, *laṅ*, third person plural; since it is at the beginning of the foot [as printed] no *nighāta*; since the augment *aṭ* is acute, the word is acute on the first syllable)" *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Rik 103.1, concluded (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])**

Grammar page, noted briefly. The grammar of Rik 103.1 concludes: *kṣamā* (the locative ending, following, is dropped by *supāṃ suluk…* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-39 as read]); *divi* (the ending acute by *ūḍidaṃpadādi…* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); *īm* (in the Saṃhitā, Vedic loss of the other *m*); *samaneva* (root *ṣama ṣṭama avaiklavye*; *yuc* by *anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyate* [Pā. Sū. 3-2-178 as read]; *ana* for *yu* by *yuvoranākau* [Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 as read]; *s* for the initial *ṣ* of the root; the locative ending following, replaced by *ā* by *supāṃ suluk…*; the form *samanā*; *samanā iva* — *samaneva*; the loss of the ending [of the first member] before *iva* and the accent of the first member by *ivena vibhaktyalopaḥ pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ca* [vārttika, as read], so the compound). The Rik is closed with *‖ 1 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 103.2)**

> स इन्द्रः पृथिवीमसुरैः पीडितां भूमिं धारयत् । धृतवान् । पीडारहितत्वेन स्थितामकरोदित्यर्थः । तदनन्तरं पप्रथच्च । तां भूमिं विस्तीर्णामकरोत् । अपि च वज्रेणायुधेन हन्तव्यान्वृत्रादीन्हत्वापो वृष्ट्युदकानि निः ससर्ज । मेघान्निर्गमयामास । एतदेव स्पष्टीक्रियते । अहिमन्तरिक्षे वर्तमानं मेघमहन् । वज्रेण वर्षणार्थमताडयत् । रौहिणं । रौहिणो नाम कश्चिदसुरः । तं च व्यभिनत् । व्यदारयत् । अपि च मघवा धनवानिन्द्रः शचीभिरात्मीयैर्युद्धकर्मभिर्व्यंसं विगतभुजं वृत्रासुरमहन् । अवधीत् ॥ पप्रथत् । प्रथं करोति प्रथयति । तत्करोतीति णिच् । नानिष्ठवत्वातिपदिकस्य कार्यं । पा. ६-४-१५३-१ । इति वचनाद्र ऋतो हलादेर्लघोः । पा. ६-४-१६१ । इति ऋकारस्य रत्वम् । टेरिति टिलोपः । तस्य स्थानिवद्भावाद्द्वुद्भ्यभावः । प्रथयतेर्लुङ् चङि णिलोपे । द्विर्वचने चङ्यन्यतरस्याम् । पा. ६-१-११३ । इति चङः पूर्वस्योदात्तत्वम् । न णिलोपस्य स्थानिवत्त्वं न पदान्तेत्यादिना स्वरनिधिं प्रति तन्निषेधात् । पूर्वपदस्यासमानवाक्यस्थत्वान्निघाताभावः ॥
> *sa indraḥ pṛthivīm asuraiḥ pīḍitāṃ bhūmiṃ dhārayat | dhṛtavān | pīḍārahitatvena sthitām akarod ity arthaḥ | tadanantaraṃ paprathac ca | tāṃ bhūmiṃ vistīrṇām akarot | api ca vajreṇāyudhena hantavyān vṛtrādīn hatvāpo vṛṣṭyudakāni niḥ sasarja | meghān nirgamayām āsa | etad eva spaṣṭīkriyate | ahim antarikṣe vartamānaṃ megham ahan | vajreṇa varṣaṇārtham atāḍayat | rauhiṇaṃ | rauhiṇo nāma kaścid asuraḥ | taṃ ca vyabhinat | vyadārayat | api ca maghavā dhanavān indraḥ śacībhir ātmīyair yuddhakarmabhir vyaṃsaṃ vigatabhujaṃ vṛtrāsuram ahan | avadhīt ‖ paprathat | prathaṃ karoti prathayati | tat karotīti ṇic | nāniṣṭhavatvātipadikasya kāryam | Pā. 6-4-153-1 | iti vacanād ra ṛto halāder laghoḥ | Pā. 6-4-161 | iti ṛkārasya ratvam | ṭer iti ṭilopaḥ | tasya sthānivadbhāvād dvudbhyabhāvaḥ | prathayater luṅ caṅi ṇilope | dvirvacane caṅy anyatarasyām | Pā. 6-1-113 [?] | iti caṅaḥ pūrvasyodāttatvam | na ṇilopasya sthānivattvaṃ na padāntety ādinā svaranidhiṃ prati tanniṣedhāt | pūrvapadasyāsamānavākyasthatvān nighātābhāvaḥ ‖*

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read: the form* paprathat *(the denominative* ṇic *'to make wide', the substitution* ra *for the* ṛ *of* pṛthu *by* ra ṛto halādeḥ laghoḥ *[Pā. Sū. 6-4-161, as read], loss of* ṭi*, the aorist* luṅ *with* caṅ*, the doubling, and the accent of the reduplicative by a rule that the print gives as* Pā. 6-1-113 [?]). The sūtra numerals and some clauses are clotted and marked [?].)*

"That Indra *dhārayat* — upheld, held up — the earth, the land oppressed by the Asuras: the sense is that he made it stand free of oppression. Thereafter he *paprathat ca* — he made that earth wide. And further, having struck with the thunderbolt, the weapon, those to be struck, Vṛtra and the rest, he *niḥ sasarja* — let loose, brought out — the *apaḥ*, the rain-waters, from the clouds. This is made plain: he struck the cloud, *ahi*, that was in the mid-air, with the thunderbolt, for the sake of rain. *Rauhiṇam* — Rauhiṇa is the name of a certain Asura; him too he *vyabhinat* — split. And Maghavā, wealthy Indra, with his *śacībhiḥ* — his own warlike deeds — *ahan* — killed — the *vyaṃsa* — the armless — Vṛtra the Asura."

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*saḥ* — Indra; *pṛthivīṃ* — the earth (oppressed by Asuras); *dhārayat* — raised [and] held (and saved it from harm); *paprathat ca* — and made [the earth] spread widely; *vajreṇa* — with the thunderbolt; *hatvā* — having killed (Vṛtra and the rest); *apaḥ* — the waters (the rain-waters and the like); *niḥ sasarja* — let out from the clouds; *ahiṃ* — the cloud in the mid-air; *ahan* — struck; *rauhiṇaṃ* — the Asura named Rauhiṇa; *vy abhinat* — split; *maghavā* — Indra, endowed with wealth; *śacībhiḥ* — by his (battle) deeds; *vyaṃsaṃ* — Vṛtra the Asura, who was deprived of arms; *ahan* — killed."

**॥ भावार्थः ॥ — Bhāvārtha (Kannada)**

"Indra raised up the earth, which was oppressed by Asuras, saved it from harm, and made the earth spread widely. Killing Vṛtra and the rest with the thunderbolt, he let out the rain-waters and the like from the clouds. He struck, with the thunderbolt, the cloud in the mid-air. He split the Asura named Rauhiṇa. Indra, endowed with wealth, by his battle deeds killed Vṛtra the Asura, who was deprived of arms."

**English Translation (as printed)**

> He upholds, and has spread out, the earth ; having struck (the clouds), he has extricated the waters ; he has slain Ahi, he has pierced Rauhina, he has destroyed, by his prowess, the mutilated (Vritra).

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ — Special Topics of Rik 103.2 (Kannada)**

"*Saḥ pṛthivīṃ dhārayat* — the intention is that Indra protected the earth, which had been oppressed by the Asuras. The exploits of Indra's daring are here described, by which he destroyed the Rākṣasas and the like who were producing obstacles that held back rain-water and the like and were causing harm to the world, and so made the earth safe. [Sāyaṇa:] *asuraiḥ pīḍitāṃ bhūmiṃ dhṛtavān* | *pīḍārahitatvena sthitām akarod ity arthaḥ*: so Sāyaṇa explains."

> आधारयत्पृथिवीं विश्वधायसमस्तभ्नान्मायिया द्यामवस्रसः ।
> *ādhārayat pṛthivīṃ viśvadhāyasam astabhnān māyayā dyām avasrasaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-1[?]-[?] as read [?])

"— as in this Ṛk, it is well known that Indra, by his strength and by his wisdom, held and protected the earth, the support of all. And as to his deeds, which are the benefactors of the world —

*Vajreṇa hatvā apaḥ niḥ sasarja* — he destroyed the enemy in the form of the cloud, which causes obstruction to all, and let loose the rain that is the greatest benefactor of the life of the people. He made the flood flow. He gave the world the wealth of water. And —

*Ahiṃ ahan* — the word *ahi* is read among the names of cloud (*Ni.* 1-[?]0 as read [?]) and among the names of water (*Ni.* 1-[?]2 as read [?]); here it must be taken in the sense of 'cloud'. The Nirukta-author, quoting the Ṛk"

> दासपत्नीरहिगोपा अतिष्ठन्निरुद्धा आपः पणिनेव गावः ।
> *dāsapatnīr ahigopā atiṣṭhan niruddhā āpaḥ paṇineva gāvaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-32-11 as read [?])

"— in explaining the derivation of the word *ahi*, gives the meaning 'cloud' and says *āhanti ayanāt* (*Ni.* 2-[?]2): 'since it moves in the mid-air, the cloud has the name *ahi*'. Here too Sāyaṇa has said *antarikṣe vartamānaṃ meghaṃ*: 'the cloud that is in the mid-air'. And"

*(Running head: left "A. 1 A. 7 Va. 16 [?]"; centre "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; right 365.)*

"— [the Nirukta-author]: *ayam api itaro hīr etasmād eva nirhṛsitopasargaḥ āpnotīti* (*Ni.* 3-[?]2 as read [?]): 'this other *ahi*, too, comes from the root *han*, which has the sense "to go", with the preverb *ā* added, and, after a shortening [of the preverb], it is *ahi*, with the sense *sarpaṇa*, "creeping"'. Besides this, *yo 'hiḥ sa budhnyaḥ budhnam antarikṣaṃ tan nivāsāt* (*Ni.* 10-[?]4 as read [?]): 'because he dwells in the mid-air, which is *budhna*, the *ahi* is called *budhnya*': the Nirukta-author has shown that, because [the cloud] dwells in such a mid-air, it also gets the name *budhnya*. Explaining this same meaning, the author of the Bṛhaddevatā also says —"

> आहिराहन्ति मेघान्स इति वा तेषु मध्यमः । योऽहिः स बुध्न्ये बुध्ने हि सोऽन्तरिक्षेऽभिजायते ॥
> *āhir āhanti meghān sa iti vā teṣu madhyamaḥ | yo 'hiḥ sa budhnye budhne hi so 'ntarikṣe 'bhijāyate ‖*
> (*Bṛ. De.* 3-[?]4-[?] as read [?])

"The *ahi* goes forward resting on the clouds, or moves among them; since he is born in the deep mid-air, he too is named *budhnya*: this is the derivation given for the word *ahi*. In this sense *ahi* may mean a serpent, or an Asura. Besides these meanings — the cloud, the Asura who moves in the deep mid-air, or the serpent — the word is used as an epithet of Vṛtra the Asura, and also in the form of a synonym."

> त्वं प्रति प्रवत आशयानमहिं वज्रेण मघवन्वि वृश्चः ।
> *tvaṃ prati pravata āśayānam ahiṃ vajreṇa maghavan vi vṛścaḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-1[?]-[?] as read [?])

"— in Ṛks like these *ahiṃ* means 'the Asura named Vṛtra', that is, in the sense of a synonym of Vṛtra. In the thirty-second sūkta of the first maṇḍala, *ahi* means everywhere the cloud that spreads, stopping the water. In the present Ṛk also, as Sāyaṇa says, the meaning is *megha*, 'cloud'. Skandasvāmin has said *ahināmānam asuram*, but for this context the meaning 'cloud' is the more fitting.

*Rauhiṇam* — the word *rauhiṇa* is read also among the names of cloud (*Ni.* 1-[?]1 as read [?]); here the meaning is *rākṣasa*. Likewise —"

> यो रौहिणमस्फुरद्वज्रबाहुर्द्यामारोहन्तं स जनास इन्द्रः ।
> *yo rauhiṇam asphurad vajrabāhur dyām ārohantaṃ sa janāsa indraḥ |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 2-1[?]-[?] as read [?])

"— in this Ṛk too the meaning is *rākṣasa*. In the Ṛksaṃhitā this Asura's name occurs in two places only.

*Vyaṃsam ahan* — [Sāyaṇa] has explained *vyaṃsa* as a synonym of an Asura, 'he killed the Asura named Vyaṃsa'. The word *vyaṃsa* in all places but one or two is an epithet of Vṛtra."

**Special Topics of Rik 103.2, concluded from p. 365 (Kannada)**

> अहन्वृत्रं वृत्रतरं व्यंसमिन्द्रो वज्रेण महता वधेन ।
> *ahan vṛtraṃ vṛtrataraṃ vyaṃsam indro vajreṇa mahatā vadhena |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-32-5 as read [?]; as quoted on p. 274)

> यो व्यंसं जाहृषाणेन मन्युना यः शम्बरं यो अहन्पिप्रुमव्रतम् ।
> *yo vyaṃsaṃ jāhṛṣāṇena manyunā yaḥ śambaraṃ yo ahan pipruṃ avratam |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 1-101-2; Rik 2 of the preceding sūkta)

"— in Ṛks like these, the word *vyaṃsa*, which occurs there, is explained as an epithet of Vṛtra, 'Vṛtra, whose arms have gone'. In the same way, in 2-1[?]-?; 3-3[?]-3 [as read [?]] and others also, it means Vṛtra, who is without arms.

> ममच्छ न ते मघवन्व्यंसो निविविध्वाँ अप हनू जघान ।
> *mamac chana te maghavan vyaṃso nividhvām̐ apa hanū jaghāna |*
> (*Ṛ. Saṃ.* 4-1[?]-[?] as read [?]; the first words clotted in print [?])

"— in this Ṛk, too, here, *vyaṃsanāmā asuraḥ*, *vyaṃsanāmānam asuram*, the Asura named Vyaṃsa, is a synonym of 'Asura'. [Sāyaṇa] uses it in the company of Asuras such as Pipru, Śuṣṇa and Namuci, and the mention of his name is in the manner [of those]. But, as with Ahi, Vṛtra and the rest, the description of his fearsome form is not much amplified.

*Śacībhiḥ* — since the word *śacī* is read among the names of action (*Ni.* 2-1) and also among the names of intelligence (*Ni.* 3-[?]9), here it means either 'by Indra's extraordinary deeds' or 'by [his] intelligences'.

*Maghavā* — *dhanavān indraḥ*: since the word *magha* is read among the names of wealth (*Ni.* 2-9), *maghavā* means Indra, endowed with wealth: the natural sense. As the word *maghavat* may be construed [also] as 'a performer of sacrifice', this is shown further on, in its context. Here, since it is a synonym of Indra, and since the exploits of Indra, fighting with the Asuras and others, are being described, it would not be wrong to say that *maghavā* means Indra who is joined with Viṣṇu. Because, when Indra fights the Asuras and others, he gets the help of Viṣṇu, and because for Viṣṇu the name *makha* is well known, there is the authority of Śruti for saying this in such contexts:

> स उ एव मखः स विष्णुः । तेते इन्द्रो मखवान्भवन्मखवान्ह वै तं मघवानित्याचक्षते परोक्षं परोक्षकामा हि देवाः ।
> *sa u eva makhaḥ sa viṣṇuḥ | tete indro makhavān abhavan makhavān ha vai taṃ maghavān ity ācakṣate parokṣaṃ parokṣakāmā hi devāḥ |*
> (*Śat. Brā.* 1[4?]-1-1-1[?] as read [?]; some words clotted in print [?])

"— since Viṣṇu is *makha*, and Indra is *makhavān*, 'one who has Makha', it is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa that the gods, being fond of the indirect, call him *maghavān*."

> इन्द्राविष्णू दृंहिताः शम्बरस्य नव पुरो नवतिं च श्नथिष्टम् ।

"— in Ṛks like these it is said in many places that Indra and Viṣṇu together destroyed the Asuras. **॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (Rik 103.2)** *(grammar pages, pp. 367–368, noted briefly; numerals small and doubtful [?])*

Grammar pages, noted briefly. They treat: *dhārayat* (root *dhṛṅ avasthāne*; after the *ṇic*-ended form, *laṅ*, third person singular; the augment *aṭ* does not come, by *bahulaṃ chandasy māṅyoge 'pi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-75 as read]; *nighāta* at the end of the verb); *pṛthivīm* (the word *pṛthivī* ends in the affix *ṅīṣ*, so acute on the last syllable; with *am*, by *ami pūrvaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-107 as read] the single substitute prior form; the substitute is acute by *udāttenodāttaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-5 as read]); *paprathat* (*pṛthuṃ karoti prathayati*; *ṇic* by the vārttika *tatkaroti tadācaṣṭe*; by the statement *nāniṣṭhavatvātipadikasya kāryam* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-153 vārttika 1, as read], the *iṣṭhan*-type rule on the *a*-ending stem applies even to the *ṇic*-ending form; then *ra ṛto halāder laghoḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-161 as read] for the *ṛ*, *ra*; loss of *ṭi* by *ṭeḥ* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-143 as read]; no *guṇa* of the penult, since a *ṇic*-based [*sthānivadbhāva*] under *aci ñiṇiti…* [as read, ?]; the form *prathi*, called a root; *luṅ*, third person singular, *tip*; loss of *i* by *itaś ca*; *caṅ* by *ṇiśrisrubhyaḥ kartari caṅ* [Pā. Sū. 3-1-48 as read]; doubling of *caṅ*-root by *caṅi* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-11 as read]; *halādiśeṣa*; loss of *ṇi* by *ṇer aniṭi* [Pā. Sū. 6-4-51 as read]; the accent of the reduplicative's former part by *caṅy anyatarasyām* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-218 as read]; the question whether the *ṇi*-loss counts as present is answered by *na padāntadvirvacana…* [Pā. Sū. 1-1-58 as read] in respect of accent; here, though *pṛthivīm* is the preceding word, since it is in another sentence [*vākyāntaragata*], the *nighāta* does not come by *samānavākye nighātayuṣmadasmadādeśāḥ* [as read]); *sasarja* (root *sṛja visarge*; *liṭ*, third person singular; since a verb follows an indeclinable, the *nighāta*)" *(the grammar continues on the next page)*

### Page 368 (PDF 388)

*(Running head: left 368; centre "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā"; right "Maṃ. 1 A. 15 Sū. 103".)*

The grammar of Rik 103.2 concludes: *apaḥ* (the word *ap*; accusative plural; the ending acute by *ūḍidaṃpadādi…* [Pā. Sū. 6-1-171 as read]); *ahan* (root *han hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *laṅ*, third person singular; since it stands at the beginning of the foot no *nighāta*; the augment *aṭ* being acute, the word is acute on the first syllable); *abhinat* (root *bhidir vidāraṇe*; *laṅ*, third person singular; though *ahim* before it precedes a finite verb [*atiṅanta*], since it belongs to another sentence the *nighāta* does not come; acute on the first syllable); *vyaṃsam* (*vigataḥ aṃśaḥ yasya saḥ vyaṃsaḥ*, a *bahuvrīhi*; the accent of the first member by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* [Pā. Sū. 6-2-1 as read]; *yaṇ* for *i* of *vi* before the vowel; since *yaṇ* has come in the place of an acute, the following unaccented vowel receives the *svarita* by *udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svaritaḥ* [Pā. Sū. 8-2-4 as read]). The Rik is closed with *‖ 2 ‖* and a rule of dashes.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ — Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Rik 103.3)**

> जातोभर्मा । जातू इत्यशनिमाचक्षते । भर्मायुधम् । अशनिरूपमायुधं यस्य स तथोक्तः । यद्वा । जातानां प्रजानां भर्ता । ओज ओजसा बलेन निष्पाद्यं कार्यं श्रद्दधानः । आदरातिशयेन कामयमानः । एवंभूतः स इन्द्रो दासीर्दस्युसम्बन्धिनीः पुरः पुराणि विभिन्दन् विनाशयन्व्यचरत् । विविधमगच्छत् । हे वज्रिन्वज्रवन्निन्द्र विद्वान् स्तुतीर्विजानंस्त्वमस्य स्तोतुर्दस्यवे उपक्षयकारिणे शत्रवे हेतिमायुधं विसृजेति शेषः । अपि च हे इन्द्र आर्यं सहः । आर्या विद्वांसः स्तोतारः । तदीयं बलं वर्धय । अतिवृद्धं कुरु । तथा द्युम्नं तदीयं यशश्च प्रवर्धय ॥ जातोभर्मा । जनी प्रादुर्भावे । अन्येष्वपि दृश्यत इति दृशिग्रहणस्य सर्वोपाधिव्यभिचारार्थत्वात्केवलादपि डप्रत्ययः । जांस्त्रवर्तीति जातुः । तुर्वी हिंसार्थः । क्विपि रालोप इति वलोपः । ब्रियते इति भर्म । अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति मनिन् । जातोर्भर्म यस्य । छान्दसो रेफफलोपः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । पक्षान्तरे तु जनेर्निष्ठा । जनसनखनामित्यात्त्वं । जातं सर्वं भर्म भर्तव्यं येन । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । वर्णव्यापत्त्या ऽकारस्य ऊकारः ॥
> *jātobharmā | jātū ity aśanim ācakṣate | bharmāyudham | aśanirūpam āyudhaṃ yasya sa tathoktaḥ | yadvā | jātānāṃ prajānāṃ bhartā | oja ojasā balena niṣpādyaṃ kāryaṃ śraddadhānaḥ | ādarātiśayena kāmayamānaḥ | evaṃbhūtaḥ sa indro dāsīr dasyusambandhinīḥ puraḥ purāṇi vibhindan vināśayan vy acarat | vividham agacchat | he vajrin vajravann indra vidvān stutīr vijānaṃs tvam asya stotur dasyave upakṣayakāriṇe śatrave hetim āyudhaṃ visṛjeti śeṣaḥ | api ca he indra āryaṃ sahaḥ | āryā vidvāṃsaḥ stotāraḥ | tadīyaṃ balaṃ vardhaya | ativṛddhaṃ kuru | tathā dyumnaṃ tadīyaṃ yaśaś ca pravardhaya ‖ jātobharmā | janī prādurbhāve | anyeṣv api dṛśyata iti dṛśigrahaṇasya sarvopādhivyabhicārārthatvāt kevalād api ḍapratyayaḥ | jāṃstravartīti jātuḥ | turvī hiṃsārthaḥ | kvipi rālopa iti valopaḥ | bhriyate iti bharma | anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti manin | jātor bharma yasya | chāndaso rephaphalopaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | pakṣāntare tu janer niṣṭhā | janasanakhanām ity ātvaṃ | jātaṃ sarvaṃ bharma bhartavyaṃ yena | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | varṇavyāpattyā 'kārasya ūkāraḥ ‖*

*(The print's* jāṃstravartīti jātuḥ*,* rāloṣa*… and* rephaphalopaḥ *are clotted and read as given [?].)*

"*Jātobharmā* — they call the thunderbolt *jātu*; *bharma* is a weapon; he whose weapon has the form of the thunderbolt is so called; or: the sustainer (*bhartā*) of born creatures. *Oja* — *ojasā balena niṣpādyaṃ kāryam* — what is to be accomplished by strength: *śraddadhānaḥ* — desiring it with great regard. Such an Indra *vy acarat* — went about variously, *vibhindan* — breaking, destroying — the *puraḥ*, the cities, *dāsīḥ*, belonging to the Dasyus. O *vajrin* — Indra, bearer of the thunderbolt! You, *vidvān*, knowing [our] praises, [hurl] against this praiser's *dasyave*, destructive enemy, your *hetim*, weapon — [so the sentence is to be completed]. And, O Indra, *āryaṃ sahaḥ* — the *āryas* are the learned praisers; their strength — *vardhaya*, increase it, make it grow exceedingly; and also increase their *dyumnam*, their fame."

*(The grammatical tail is characterized, not fully read:* jātu *(root* jan *'to be born', with* ḍa *…; or 'the one that makes born [creatures] move' [?]), and* bharma *('what is borne', with* manin*); the compounds* jātobharman *with the accent of the first member.)*

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥ — Pratipadārtha (Kannada)**

"*jātobharmā* — [he who] has the thunderbolt as weapon; or one who is the maintainer of all born creatures; *ojaḥ* — [his own] strength; *śraddadhānaḥ* — [one who] respects with firm faith; *saḥ* — that Indra; *dāsīḥ* — belonging to the Dasyus; *puraḥ* — cities; *vibhindan* — destroying; *vyacarat* — (freely) went about; *vajrin* — O Indra, who hold the thunderbolt; *vidvān* — knowing (the greatness of the praise); *asya* — this devotee who praises; *dasyave* — against the enemy who does harm; *hetiṃ* — the weapon (hurl); *indra* — O Indra; *āryaṃ* — [that] belongs to the Āryas; *sahaḥ* — strength; *dyumnaṃ* — and fame; *vardhaya* — make them grow."
